# TO THE HONEST
## READER, GREETINGS. <note>original: "CANDIDO LECTORI S. P." The abbreviation S.P. stands for "Salutem Plurimam," a standard formal greeting wishing the reader much health and prosperity.</note>

<image-desc>Decorative square woodcut initial 'Q' containing botanical motifs and scrollwork.</image-desc>

I, who previously issued three volumes to advance the study of <term>Chemistry <note>original: "Chemicorum." At this time, alchemy and chemistry were viewed as the same pursuit—the investigation of the secrets of nature and matter.</note></term> into the public light through printing—volumes filled with various types of teachings and the <term>scholarly works <note>original: "lucubrationibus." This term literally refers to "work done by candlelight," highlighting the intense, late-night labor of the authors.</note></term> of the most esteemed men, to the significant benefit of many—now present to you, dear Reader, the Fourth Volume. This volume contains two types of writings. The first group consists of those which, although previously available to the public, were published individually at different times and in various places. Because they were scattered, they were difficult for many to obtain. In this book, I have gathered them together and combined them into a single volume so that readers who might otherwise lack them by chance can find them all collected and placed before their eyes here, offering them what they previously sought. The second type consists of very ancient manuscripts that have never been made public before and have been seen by very few—indeed, I might say none—of the people of our time. I have spared no expense or labor in acquiring and publishing these. Some of them were written in such ancient and outdated handwriting that simply deciphering them was a significant challenge for our team. In correcting or changing these, however, the hand [abstained]... <note>The text ends mid-sentence as it moves to the next page.</note>

# PREFACE

*...we have maintained, even if they sometimes displayed a certain <term>barbarity <note>original: "barbariem." This refers to non-classical or medieval Latin that does not follow the elegant rules of Cicero, often found in technical alchemical texts.</note></term> in their phrasing, or if the letters themselves introduced errors. We did this so that we might satisfy the reader and the most earnest investigator of this art, who by no means looks for elegance of speech, but rather busies himself with digging out and coming to know the truth placed in hidden locations. Every good man is also bound, in a serious matter and in any teaching of the ancients, to set down and express the author's own naked words, observing them even to the point of <term>scrupulousness <note>original: "superstitionem." Here used in the classical sense of "excessive precision" or "meticulous dread of error" rather than religious belief.</note></term>. Thus, in transcribing, reciting, or producing these opinions from any archive, he should consider it a <term>sin <note>original: "piaculum." An act requiring expiation; a grave error or crime against the integrity of the text.</note></term> to have omitted or changed even a single letter.*

*Furthermore, since I have in my hands several other chemical writings which have not yet been made public through the benefit of the press, I shall strive with all my might so that a Fifth (or perhaps more) <term>Chemical Volume <note>original: "Tomus Chemicus." The "Theatrum Chemicum" eventually expanded to six volumes, becoming the most comprehensive collection of alchemical texts ever printed.</note></term> may be published. To carry out this task, I wish to earnestly request all those who have the studies of <term>Chemical Philosophy <note>original: "Philosophiae Chemicae." A term for alchemy that emphasizes its theoretical and natural-philosophical foundations.</note></term> at heart, of whatever status or condition they may be, that if they possess writings of this kind, they kindly share them. If they can assist me in this laudable purpose of mine, let them do so, and contribute to the common good. I admit, indeed, that in such a collection, bad things are mixed with good, and many trivial and worthless things are mixed with the most serious matters—or rather, truths (as happens in all disciplines in our time) are oppressed and suffocated by falsehoods, which a prudent and wise...*

<meta>catchword: tus [completing "cordatus," meaning wise or heart-centered]</meta>

# TO THE READER

<note>This page contains the signature mark "): ( 3", which helped bookbinders assemble the pages in the correct order.</note>

...learned Reader, who glows with any vein of philosophy, will rightly discern, and properly extract gold from the dung of the <term>Sophists <note>original: "Sophistarum." In an alchemical context, "sophists" or "puffers" were charlatans who sought only to make gold through trickery, as opposed to the "true philosophers" seeking natural and spiritual secrets.</note></term>.

Finally, I wish it to be known to the Reader that, having so far expended and contributed our efforts to those things which concern <term>metallurgy <note>original: "rem metallicam." This refers to the science of mining and refining metals, a field Zetzner published in extensively, including works by Agricola.</note></term>, a *Chemicomedical Theater* shall hereafter also issue from our workshop, God willing. It will be furnished with a collection of the most excellent remedies, of which we wish to advise you. 

And meanwhile, we bid you farewell with these words, and urge you to apply yourself with all your strength to those <term>Philosophers <note>The "Philosophers" here refers to the ancient alchemical authorities who were believed to have hidden the secrets of nature in their writings.</note></term> who are never accustomed to lie. We command you to insist firmly on their footsteps in the <term>universal work <note>original: "opere universali." A reference to the "Magnum Opus" or Great Work—the process of creating the Philosopher's Stone.</note></term> (outside of which there is nothing but labor and sorrow). Farewell. Strasbourg, in the year of human salvation, 1613.

->LAZARUS ZETZNERUS.<-

# IN THE NAME OF-
## OUR LORD JESUS CHRIST,
### BEGINS THE TESTAMENT OF MASTER
### Raymond Lull, and first concerning
### Theory.

<image-desc>A large decorative drop cap 'D' featuring intricate floral and foliate scrollwork.</image-desc>

*O God, YOU WHO ARE GLORIOUSLY OMNIPOTENT, for the sake of loving, honoring, and remembering You, we begin this present art, so that it may be revealed to the sons of truth what was partially hidden from us, and so that it may serve as a completion for them of that most excellent and noble part of philosophy which we shall manifest in this, our abbreviated volume. This science concerns a transmutation <term>transmutation: the alchemical process of changing one substance—usually a base metal like lead—into another, such as gold or silver</term> that is not only perfect, but indeed most perfect, which the sophists <note>original: "sophistæ"; in an alchemical context, this refers to "puffers" or fraudulent practitioners who use deceptive tricks rather than true natural philosophy</note> can never attain, and who without cause defame this illustrious science. For this reason, we leave the aforementioned book to the sons of our doctrine by way of a testament, which we divide into three principal books: namely, Theory, Practice, and the Codicil <note>original: "Codicillum"; a small book or supplement, often serving as a final summary or practical key to a larger work</note>. These three parts are distinguished into four distinctions, which are: circular figures, definitions, mixtures, and differential applications, both for the second book on practice and for the first on theory. This book is divided into four distinctions, and they are first: circular figures, definitions, mixtures, and the different applications for the second book on practice and the first book on theory. In the name and reverence of heavenly power and wisdom, we intend to clarify for you, son of doctrine, the gift given to us through a necessary process, without which there is no full knowledge of that thing which is one, and which is composed of*

<summary>This page serves as the formal opening of Raymond Lull's alchemical "Testament," establishing its religious foundation and outlining its three-part structure of Theory, Practice, and Codicil. Lull claims to reveal a "most perfect" method of transmutation intended for true followers of philosophy, distinguishing them from fraudulent "sophists."</summary>

<keywords>Raymond Lull, Testament, alchemy, transmutation, Theory and Practice, Codicil, philosophy, sophists, circular figures</keywords>

# P R E F A C E.

*...concerning those entities which are the matter of nature <term>matter of nature: the fundamental substance or "prime matter" that alchemists believed formed the basis of all physical things</term>, which have been and are discovered through dissolutions <note>original: "dissolutiones"; the chemical process of breaking a solid down into its constituent liquid or elemental parts</note>, and which do not allow themselves to be seen in ordinary ways. And for this reason, because this doctrine of dissolution thoroughly pants, sighs, and desires the end, seeking to arrive at the point of completion, may You, eternal and supreme Power, be willing to enlighten Christians and those who believe in You, so that they may see and know the truth fashioned by the ancients <note>original: "antiquos"; likely referring to legendary figures like Hermes Trismegistus or early Greek alchemists</note>. Without this truth, this science—which is better than even the noblest part of philosophy—cannot be made whole. It is now time for us to be introduced to it, because the moment has come when we ought to*
->*set down its definitions.*<-

<summary>This page concludes the introductory prayer of the preface, emphasizing that alchemical truths are hidden from ordinary sight and require divine enlightenment to be understood. It positions alchemy as the highest form of philosophy and prepares the reader for the formal definitions of the craft.</summary>
<keywords>matter of nature, dissolution, divine illumination, philosophy, definitions, Raymond Lull, alchemy</keywords>

--- Page 16 ---
<meta>This page continues from the preface, moving from the philosophical justification of the work into the specific definitions and structure of the book. It introduces the "Lament of Nature," a common medieval allegorical device where Nature personifies the creator's grief over the misuse of her secrets.</meta>

*Concerning the definitions of this art, and the lament of nature, and what theory is, and what practice is.*
A 2

---

### CHAPTER I.

<image-desc>Ornamental woodcut drop cap 'E' depicting a figure sitting in a landscape with a tree.</image-desc>
**Real entities**, existing in their primordial and succeeding principles <note>original: "primordialibus & succedentibus principiis"; the fundamental elements and the stages of development that follow them</note>, provide the knowledge and the means of understanding the nature of bodies, as well as the intermediates and the known extremes. These are the cause of their true permutation and transmutation according to their roots, in a spherical form and permanent species through their own dispositions, insofar as they are changeable and entirely transmutable into a true and useful form of perfect things. This is done by preserving the essence as much as possible, in order to lead them to the supreme and perfect **temperament** <term>temperament: the ideal balance of the four qualities—hot, cold, moist, and dry—which alchemists believed resulted in gold or the Elixir</term>. 

But in this book, when we speak of physical discontinuity <note>original: "discontinuatione physica"; likely referring to the separation of elements or the breakdown of matter into its constituent parts</note>, we have received a mandate from the mistress and lady of nature. Because she appeared to us clearly, and opened her works to us, and showed them as they were opened. Therefore, weeping and groaning, she cried out against us, saying: "Alas, what shall I do from now on, since men strive to take and carry away my instruments from me, and they wish to plunder my secrets and uncover me? And those things which I have formed by the permission of God and my Master, they wish to dispatch me to death." 

This is the grief that **Lady Nature** spoke before her priest: "I groan and I mourn." And truly she wept so profoundly that there was no heart seeing her that was not moved by compassion, nor hindered from weeping by love for her. For the pain in her body was so great that she was driven even to spasms because of the grief and displeasure she felt for the good works she had performed in this world—so much so that she wished to abandon them and no longer cared to perform them, provided she could obtain permission from God her Master, whom she had petitioned regarding this. 

Because of this, we received a mandate that we must keep her instruments secret and guard them from the hands of her enemies. All these things we shall declare in the second book, if you are able to enter therein. Therefore, this first book is divided and partitioned into five parts and five divisions through general chapters.

Since, however, the **practice** of this part of philosophy cannot be handed down without the **theory** preceding it, we say that theory is in that part where the dispositions of transmutable and changeable bodies toward a balanced temperament are taught and demonstrated, insofar as is necessary for the perfection of our [work...]

<vocab>nature, transmutation, spherical, physical, philosophy, theory, practice, instruments</vocab>

# RAYMUNDUS LULLUS

of the mastery <note>original: "magisterii"; referring to the *Magisterium* or the "Great Work" of alchemy</note>. Practice, indeed, is that part in which the form and the mode of operating correctly is described, according to the requirements of the disposition previously known through theory. And therefore, because neither the dispositions of the aforementioned bodies, nor their natures, can be known except through the consideration of things natural, things unnatural, and things contrary to nature <note>This tripartite division—natural, unnatural, and contrary to nature—is borrowed from Galenic medicine and applied here to the "health" or "perfection" of metals</note>, we divide theory into three parts for a better understanding. This is because the dispositions of the whole changeable body, in general, are only three: namely, **temperament**, **imbalance**, and **neutrality**.

First, it must be known that **temperament** is comprised under natural things, because formally its **complexion** <term>complexion: the specific combination of the four primary qualities—hot, cold, moist, and dry—within a substance</term> is made of subtle parts joined together at once. Regarding the compositions of these parts, the philosophers have spoken at length, taking a broad view insofar as they could understand the continuation and gathering of parts when that continuity receives its own composition.

**Imbalance** <note>original: "Intemperamentum"; also translated as distemper or lack of balance</note>, however, is comprised under those things which are contrary to nature; and therefore it is called by another name, "corruption," or the distancing from true temperament, with which the whole exists and without which there is nothing.

**Neutrality**, in truth, contains the middle ground of the aforementioned parts; called by another name, it is the "ligament" of the stated extremes—namely of temperament and imbalance—or otherwise it is called the middle disposition between two contraries.

->*On the temperament of bodies, and imbalance, and neutrality;*<-
->*and on medicine, and on natural, unnatural,*<-
->*and contrary-to-nature instruments.*<-

### CAP. II.

And therefore you must observe that true **temperament** is the natural disposition of perfect bodies, through which natural actions are perfected in the perfection of the **medicine** <term>medicine: in alchemy, this refers to the Elixir or Philosopher's Stone, which "heals" base metals into gold</term>, in which they are perfected without any other medium. These actions enter through the whole, and because of this, it must be a disposition of the nature of the quality of all bodies, and not of the action.

For if a medicinal body is not well-tempered, it would entirely cease to change imperfect bodies toward that perfection which is completed with the due **projection** <term>projection: the final stage of the alchemical process where a small amount of the Elixir is "cast upon" a larger mass of molten base metal to transmute it</term>. Indeed, it is then called a "powerful temperament" only when it is fit to complete the action given to it through the complexion of its own temperament, along with the completion given to it through the known way and mode of projection. This action renders and ordains the medicine fit and capable through its own temperament. To the knowledge of this, the intention of the one who knows our work ought principally to be aimed and directed.

[...of the craftsmen] <note>The Latin text begins with "Arum," likely the end of "Artificum" (of the craftsmen) continuing from the previous page's catchword.</note> labors to determine a noble temperament through the instrument of prudent wisdom. For those considerations that do not concern temperament must in no way be applied to this matter. Nevertheless, temperament is acquired through the ingenuity of nature, or by the master's will within the **ferment** <note>original: "fermento"; in alchemy, the "ferment" is a substance that transforms the base matter into the nature of the ferment itself, much like leaven in bread</note> through the intellect, toward the unification of things pertaining to and capable of being mixed by the science and the informative art; in medicine, this constitutes a single **habit** <term>habit: a stable condition or disposition of a substance's nature</term> or several. Because temperament is the perfection of action, it is not more clearly known, nor more rightly preserved or discovered, than through the aforementioned science. Whether it be one habit or several, there is always but one single limit and mode of preserving the correct bounds to produce that end called temperament, which we wish to signify by the letter **C**.

**Imbalance** <note>original: "Intemperamentum"</note>, or the lack of temperament, is an unnatural and corruptible disposition. it arises through elemental dissolution, by which the actions of individual things and of nature are immediately corrupted, through the distancing or the instability of their temperament—which had previously come about through the continuity and binding together of its composite parts...

*On the principles of nature in a universal sense, and how all things are extracted from a confused mass <note>Original: "massa confusa," referring to the initial state of chaos before creation.</note>, by comparison to the great world <note>The Macrocosm or the universe.</note>; concerning the four elements and the four primordial main principles: and concerning all things, by reducing them through the great form of the world to our mastery, which is the minor form, just as a minor world <note>The Microcosm, referring here to the alchemical work itself as a reflection of the universe.</note> through a miracle.*

## CHAPTER III.

**T**he natural principles, both primordial and those that follow in the work of nature, are universally all the extremes that can exist, along with their intermediate points. We shall declare the nature of these primordial principles under the power of nature and of God, the supreme king and celestial emperor, who alone in Trinity is without beginning and without a creator. He is superior to the succession of all the aforementioned principles, which are named "extremes" and "means" <note>The "extremes" are the pure elements or qualities, while "means" are the mixtures that form physical reality.</note> in the works of nature. This nature the supreme God first created from nothing, out of his pure generosity and will, in a certain pure substance which is called the **quintessence** <note>Original: "essentia quinta," the "fifth essence" or ether that transcends the four physical elements.</note>,

in which all nature is comprised. From the better and purer part of this substance, divided into three parts, the Most High created the **angels**; from the second part, he created the **heavens, planets, and stars**. And from the third, less pure part, he made the **lower world**. 

And this the "son of doctrine" <note>A traditional address to the student or initiate.</note> ought to understand, not exactly as we hand it down [in steps], but rather how the whole was created simultaneously by the will of the superior God, without any operation of succession and without any preceding matter that would look toward a succession of kinds. For otherwise, it would not be a creation, nor a divine operation, which regards the creation of a scientific entity coming into being through creation from nothing into a true, substantial entity. <meta>This page continues the "Theory" section from Chapter III. we shall say, and have already said, that you should seek to understand this with a scientific spirit <note>Original: "spiritu scientifico," referring to a systematic, rational approach to knowledge rather than a purely religious or uneducated one.</note>, and not a hagiographical or common one. This is because we are speaking in relation to the operations of nature, which you must learn to imitate in our mastery <note>The "mastery" (magisterium) refers to the alchemical process or Great Work.</note>. Therefore, we speak by way of examples, so that you may understand us well, as has been said, and not merely as it is written.

For the supreme creator divided this part into five. He created from the purer part the **quintessence** of the elements, which shares in the celestial nature, and which we represent by the letter **O**. From this quintessence, he made four parts: from the first and purest part he made **fire**, which is the first element. From the second part, which was also quite pure, he made **air**, the second element. From the third part, which was pure but followed air, he made **water**, the third element. From the fourth part, which was the least pure, he made **earth**, the final element. We wish the first to be signified by **P**, the second by **Q**, the third by **R**, and the fourth by **S**.

Insofar as nature is more perfect in elemental things, it is completed as a whole with little additional perfection. For one element is perfected by another through the harmony of their properties and those of the fifth instrument <note>The "fifth instrument" refers to the quintessence acting as the underlying medium for the other four.</note>, which participates in celestial things. In that substance which later descends from those elements—possessing a lesser nature through the perfection of generation and corruption—the process is reversed, because its instinct or "appetite" comes immediately from the creation of nature. Therefore, what nature does is not entirely perfect compared to the perfection that comes directly from the Creator, rather than through nature. For that which comes from the Creator is perfect without destruction. 

Indeed, that instinct or appetite of nature cannot make a thing perfect unless it is completed by divine intellectual science—much like human nature, which is corrected by divine intelligence, just as a beautiful and good work is completed by a skilled craftsman. Through this, the **son of the art** <term>son of the art: an apprentice or initiate into the alchemical mysteries</term> can understand the nature of the primary elements after the division of the third substance created at the beginning. However, he should not think that their substance is the simple fifth element itself, but rather the fourth, third, second, or first substances "elemented" <note>That is, formed into elements (elementata) from the primordial source.</note> from that fifth part, which we call the primordial element and simple substance. Through this, the four mentioned elemental substances are formed, each according to its own nature, as we have explained above. 

These four elements, thus created, remained pure and clear by virtue of the clear part of nature from their creation until the time of the elder <note>Original: "presbyteri." In this context, it likely refers to the "Ancient" or the first man, Adam.</note>, through whose sin nature departed [from its original state]. He was called "the race" <note>Original: "genus."</note>, and from him, from the time of his birth [came mortality]. But afterwards, humans, birds, beasts, fish, and various things born of the earth died...

...exemplary things <note>Original: "exemplarae." This word completes a thought from the previous page regarding how nature's works serve as models for the alchemist.</note> destroyed and burned, through the destruction of generation, which has turned from corruption into generation, and afterwards from generation into corruption. And similarly, from impure bodies the world is dissolved, and the elements are corrupted; through this corruption, all things made and living by nature exist, and they have been of short duration. This is because nature, in its coarse and corrupted matter, cannot make anything as perfect as it did in its beginning, for it no longer possesses what is needed to continue its first work. Instead, nature makes use of imperfection tending toward corruption, because day by day it finds the nature of the elements less pure; that which it has placed into a work, it cannot improve into a perfect work, but rather it always decreases little by little. 

Yet nature always composes according to its ability, and joins together the stronger parts of the bond. And through this teaching, the **sons of art** <note>"Sons of art" (filii artis) is a traditional term for alchemists or initiates into the "Great Work."</note> can understand the word of the Savior: that at the end of the world He will consume all things, when He comes to judge the age by fire. Namely, all that which is not of the truth of the aforementioned elements, and all that is composed and made of evil and impurity, shall be confounded and cast into the abyss. However, all that which the aforementioned celestial fire finds of the virtues and pure truth above its sphere shall rest vibrantly forever, and it shall come upon the happy saved; and the evil and impure falls upon the damned. 

Through this, the consideration can be clarified and declared: that in the end, every thing will go to its own proper place, from where it was first moved. It is also to be understood that this earth, which we inhabit, is not the **true element** <term>True element: In Lullian alchemy, the physical soil (earth) we touch is a "gross" or "elemented" mixture; the "true element" of Earth is a pure, philosophical principle or "simple" state of matter.</term>, but was formed into an element from the true fifth element; afterwards, through the fifth elemental substance of a well-elemented body, the earth of which was formed from the fifth cause. And then you will find a void of formative power, like a body without a soul, and like rot gathered together in one place in matter without form, composed of the aforementioned infection through the reciprocal action of the elements upon one another. 

In the center, however, is the **pure earth** and the true element, which fire will not be able to burn on the **Day of Terror** <note>Original: "die terroris," referring to the Day of Judgment or the apocalypse.</note>, and so it is with the other elements. The first radical and artificial principle is God, the creator of all things. The second, the exemplary principle, is moved by God Himself, and is called **Wisdom**. The third succeeding principle, however, is **Matter**, created through God—that is, through the Wisdom which is moved by Him. This is the primordial element which we call *hyle* <note>original: "hyle," from the Greek ὕλη, meaning wood or raw material; in alchemy, it refers to the fundamental, formless substance of the universe</note>. We have declared this to you—if you have understood well—but you should not presume to seek it in its simple form to begin our work. Although we could not know our work nor bring it to an end without it, we must instead seek it in its composite form. We must purge it and clear it by fire so that it becomes pure and bright, as we said above: that all elements are created from this substance and enlivened by it for the purpose of creation and corruption.

Because it is necessary—as it naturally appears—since every thing existing under the sphere of the moon <note>This refers to the "sublunary" realm, the physical earth where things are subject to change and decay, unlike the unchanging heavens.</note> is created and formed from the said matter called *hyle*, there is a greater influence of it in every elemental thing—more in one than in another, as we find through nature—and it rests therein. By this, however, you may be certain that no thing in the world can exist without this "created and non-generated" substance, because it is the collector and the bond <term>colligantia|a binding force or glue</term> of the whole elemental body in the work of nature. Therefore, we call this *hyle* <note>original Greek: ὕλην</note> "Nature," and the primordial principle of everything elemental—that is, of all elemental things—because in its substance, it is simple.

The elements, which are the matter of nature, were first created through divine separation: namely, **earth**, **water**, **air**, and **fire**. These are elemental bodies formed from the primordial principle and the simple element that exists within them. From this understanding proceeds the *Methanoftrica* chronicle <note>Likely a reference to a specific philosophical or alchemical text regarding transformation (from the Greek "metanoeo," to change one's mind or purpose).</note>, which says that the species of the elements are found within their own limits and in their said principle, which is the primordial principle of their things. 

Therefore, if you seek this matter, attend to this: it is the pure subject, which is the union and motion of forms, and in which every form is held in potentiality. It contains infinite flux and instability in its motion, according to the diversity of those forms—both the extremes and the intermediaries—which it receives into itself. And therefore, by analogy, it is named by some the **"receptacle of forms,"** which are born from celestial matter that exists above its own nature. By other philosophers, it was called the **"forest"** <note>original: "forestum," a term used by medieval philosophers like Bernardus Silvestris to describe the chaotic, raw state of prime matter.</note>, comparing it to a coarse and raw thing by reason of its potentiality. And by yet other philosophers, it was called **"potentiality,"** because it possesses no form in actuality, but contains every form within itself as if enclosed—like silence without hearing, or like those who do not see, nor can they be seen because of the darkness. And thus must this matter be understood,

## *On the minor form, and on the principles of simple mineral nature through extremities and means.*

### CHAPTER 4.

Since the major form has been determined, we will hereafter descend to determine the minor form. In this are the principles succeeding in the work of nature, more closely related according to the extremities and the means of their closer operations.

<image-desc>A diagram featuring a large inverted triangle with the words GOD (top left), Wisdom (top right), and Hyle <note>primordial matter</note> (bottom) at its vertices. And since we have said above that the principles are universally all extremities <note>the outer limits or pure states of a substance</note> and all their means <note>the intermediate states or connecting substances</note>, we say here that the first and principal mean, extreme, or extremity, are the four elements mentioned above, which are the elemented extremities, and are signified by B. All elemented bodies are resolved into these vapors to enter a new generation. You should wish to retain and understand this, because I speak to you generally so that you may reach the end of that which is sought. 

The third is clear water composed of the said vapors through the condensation of its nature, which enters into the said vapors of the four elements; and that is the thing most closely related to **quicksilver** <note>original: "argento vivo," or mercury</note>, which is indeed found running and flowing upon the earth. ...caused by hot and dry vapors, and this is signified by **D**. The fourth is a certain substance proceeding from its own mineral vein and located within it, closer to the nature of metals; it is called *calcantis* <note>original: calcantis; likely vitriol or copper sulfate</note> and glassy *azoth* <note>original: azoth vitreus; a term for the essential transformative mercury</note> by some, and it is the earth and mineral source of metals. In its dissolution, it is congealed into the form of a "lizard" <note>a metaphorical term for a volatile or poisonous mineral state</note>, in which resides the form and appearance of a "stinking spirit" in the mixture. Its mineral heat is multiplied, which is the very life of the metal; and this is signified by **E**.

The fifth extreme, or extremity, or intermediate state, consists of the vapors immediately generated by the dissolution and rarefaction <note>the thinning or expansion of a substance</note> of the said glassy vitriol. And this is the first and nearest matter for the generation of all metals, impregnated and seized by a natural life-giving heat, in the form and appearance of "living water" <note>original: aquæ vivæ</note>. All investigators of this art should understand that in the work of nature, this is the "living silver" <note>mercury</note>, but it is not the kind of mercury found upon the earth; nor will it be so until it is first turned into the "poisonous blood of abscesses" <note>a metaphor for a stage of putrefaction or intense chemical reaction</note>, and it is signified by **F**.

The sixth extreme are the sulfurs made through succession, immediately generated by nature from the living substance of the said water. From these vapors, all other mercury is coagulated; it acts as the proper vessel or restraint for those vapors within whichever metal the vapor belongs to. And this occurs according to the purification which the matter receives through nature, shaped in such a way as is required for the form and appearance of that specific metal. And such sulfurs are signified by **G**.

The seventh extreme are the metals generated from the said sulfurous vapors and mercury through successive "cooking" <note>original: decoctionem</note>. These are the true extremes, or extremities, or intermediate states of imperfect enclosure, and in every work of nature they are signified by **H**. 

But through corruption—as when they are extracted from their mineral veins—nature intends to redden and rust them, so that they may return through circular motions, corrupting them and generating them again. This continues until they are finalized into a new generation through "digestion" within their mineral veins. Enclosed within these veins are the vapors released from those corrupted things; due to the weight of their elements and natural instinct, they are digested there by their own motion until they result in a better species. This is much like how the generation of flesh occurs in the body of an animal through the digestion of food and drink, as is briefly declared in the **magical science and art**, which begins thus: *It is manifest concerning generation...*

A master of subtle and ingenious mind resembles the work of nature in his own work regarding the preservation of the mineral species; he forms a thing with such power that it overcomes the whole course of nature. And by this, you can recognize that a natural work can be guided by the science and art of the practitioner, according to the teaching of his own instrument. And know, my son, why men do not know how to use their memory while investigating changeable and convertible beings and entities, nor how to choose with their will—receiving the good and dismissing the evil things which are against nature. 

And because they do not know how to apply these powers <note>the intellectual faculties of memory, will, and understanding</note> into their crafts—which are their true instruments, and about which we shall inform you in our second, "artificial" part—so that you may reach the reality of beings in our mastery <term>magisterium</term> <note>the Great Work or the highest level of alchemical practice</note>. Through the activity of these powers, you will receive habitual knowledge with delight, through which the intellect reaches from one species to another, and from the order of one species to the order of another; thus you will have an ordered delight in understanding both the specific and the universal.

### *Concerning the principles of this mastery, and from what things it is made, and how many they are in number, and concerning their conversion.* CHAPTER IV.

The first radical principles in our mastery are primarily three: namely, living water <note>original: "aqua viva"; often referring to mercurial water or a solvent</note> and stinking spirit <note>original: "foetens spiritus"; likely referring to unrefined sulfur or the "breath" of the mineral</note>. From these is created sulfur, which is our stone. But since these principles do not exist in their pure action upon the earth as we would require—but rather in a terrestrial action, in the form of metal, wherein their potential lies—we have therefore taken the extremities of their nature through the means of our art. We do this by recurring to one substance within its own mine <note>or ore</note>, namely **D**, **E**, and **H** <note>Lull uses letters as variables to represent specific qualities, elements, or stages in his alchemical system</note>. 

And since these are remote and contrary through the extremes of their nature, distinct science shows us that we should take **F**, which is the middle disposition of the extremes of its nature. This disposition is chosen from **D**, as appears through Figure **A** (declared below in the second part of the subsequent chapter), so that through **F**, **D** may be converted into **E** so that all things are turned into **B**; and that **B**, through circulation, may be reduced into **E**. From this you shall extract **F** in our mastery in the place of living water and stinking spirit, because in this way **F** has the power of converting **D** and **H** through the preservation of their forms. To this [substance] shall actually belong all that which was in potential in the work of nature, by means of better causes and reasons of the extremes; for in **F** and **D** there are actually **F**, **G**, and **H**, cooked and pure, and strongly digested by the ingenuity of wise nature. 

Therefore, it is necessary only to remove and separate one part of **D** and one part of **E**, and then you will have **F** in the work of art, to be assimilated to nature in all the best ways through the help of **C** and **D** which came from **H**, and **F** which descended from **H** into **B**, from which is made **F**, which is converted into **G** by the course of nature in our mastery. And that **G** is the first and nearest matter from which we create and make our perfect medicine, which is the ferment of the elixir <term>fermentum elixiris</term> <note>the substance that "leavens" or triggers the transformation of base metals into gold</note>.

...of the necessary principles of this science and divine art. Because when we told you that through careful consideration of these things—those which are natural, those which are not natural, and those which are against nature—you should have a material and essential knowledge of the temperament <note>The alchemical "temperament" is the specific balance of the four qualities: hot, cold, wet, and dry, which determines a substance's stability.</note> through all its substantial and even accidental parts. This knowledge allows you to guide yourself in our aforementioned mastery, once you have understood these principles. You must, however, intend to focus not on many things, but only on three, which stand alone by themselves. You can understand this from the previously mentioned chapter regarding the principles in our mastery, through which we comprehend this temperament.

And through this we say that there are three kinds of things: namely animal, vegetable, and mineral. The animal genus is multiplied within its species and divided into three differences: first, the active sperm, which is the "natural" sperm; second, the passive sperm, which is "unnatural"; and third, the menstrual blood, which is "against nature" <note>In alchemical philosophy, "natural" refers to the ideal state, "unnatural" to a corrupted or intermediate state, and "against nature" to substances that disrupt or dissolve the natural order, often used as solvents.</note>.

The vegetable genus is found in seeds and roots, which are natural but contain what is unnatural; because of this, their complexion is Hermaphroditic <term>Hermaphroditic: in alchemy, this refers to a substance containing both masculine (active/dry) and feminine (passive/wet) principles in one body</term>, with the masculine and feminine joined. This occurs according to the humor and humidity of the earth through the "menstrual" rain <note>original: "menstruo pluviali"</note>—the water-containing air—which is against nature.

The mineral genus is also divided into three differences, although all are metals and originate from a single matter; thus, they too have a Hermaphroditic complexion. The first difference is natural, such as gold and silver. This is because quicksilver <note>original: "argentum vivum"; literally "living silver," known today as mercury</note> contains within itself its own sulfur, which is congealed by its own power. One half is used for gold and the other half for silver, after its conversion into sulfur, both white and red. Because of this, gold and silver are the two natural "sperms"—speaking broadly <note>original: "largè"</note>—to distinguish them from that which perfects our elixir. 

The "unnatural" sperm is like lead and other impure metals, such as lead, tin, copper, iron, sulfur, and quicksilver. Those things which are "against nature" include vitriols <note>original: "atramenta"; literally "inks," referring here to metallic sulfates used as powerful reagents</note>, salts, alums, tutty <term>tutty: a crude zinc oxide collected from the flues of smelting furnaces</term>, marcasite, and arsenic. This also includes all things derived from other animal and vegetable types from which a "menstrual" moisture <note>original: "humidum menstruale"; a solvent or life-giving liquid in the alchemical process</note> can be made, tending more or less toward perfection or imperfection. Therefore, the mineral genus is added only as a general point of comparison between these natural, unnatural, and "against nature" states of the other two genera (animal and vegetable), because they receive a change into luminous clarity from the nature of those things closest to them. ### CAP. VI.

Since therefore it is clear and manifest that the property of the temperament in a metallic body is of the nature most closely related to it—as experience, which does not lie, affirms and demonstrates by the effect of noble resistance in a good fusion, and a fusion that remains stable during ignition <note>Ignition here refers to the process of heating a substance until it glows or undergoes a chemical change.</note>. When we say "all nature," we say this to distinguish between the natural, the unnatural, and that against nature, all of which are of one kind. And yet if we have said that the nature of a kind ought not to differ in its generation, you must understand this immediately for receiving the form of any living thing.

From these three things, my son, you shall extract the great <term>Dragon: "Draco," a symbol for the volatile or corrosive "spirit" of the matter, often associated with the initial raw material that must be "tilled" or tamed.</term>, which is the radical and principal beginning of firm alteration. ### C H A P T E R VIII.

This spirit we call in our *Testament* <note>Referring to the "Testamentum," one of the most famous works attributed to Lull.</note> the stony and rock-like spirit, because it has the power of holding stones against the fire, and of preserving and reviving the dead body from which it went out, whose virtue and property can be found in no other spirit. For the thickness of the fermentable spirit must surround the subtlety of the body and ascend over it, and this occurs through the property of entering which it carries within itself, which is a penetrative property. And therefore, no thickness of the body ought to or can remove its great and penetrative property through any hindrance coming from its opposite. ### *On the preparation of the stone.*
## C H A P T E R IX.

<margin>On the spirit and the soul</margin>
The preparation of the stony and fermentable spirit is this: that you take the juice of moonwort <note>original: "succus lunariæ"; while *Lunaria* is a genus of plants (moonwort), in alchemy this almost always refers to a "mercurial" liquid or a specific mineral secretion associated with the Moon (silver).</note>, and extract its sweat with a small and gentle fire. You will then have in your power one of our types of quicksilver <note>original: "arg. vivis" (argentum vivum); the living silver or mercury of the philosophers, distinct from common mercury.</note> in the liquid and form of "white water," which is the washing and the cleansing of our stone and of its entire nature. And this is one of the most principal secrets, and it is the "first gate," just as you are able to understand by the reasons spoken of before. In this liquid, the great dragon <note>The "dragon" is a common alchemical symbol for the volatile or raw matter that must be tamed or "killed" to be transformed.</note> is rectified, and it is cast out from the great desert of Arabia <note>Geographic locations like Arabia or Ethiopia in these texts often represent stages of color or chemical states; Arabia may refer to a dry, impure state.</note>, because otherwise it would be immediately suffocated by thirst and would perish in the Dead Sea; for you can already know that a great coldness extinguishes a small heat. Therefore, turn it and send it into the kingdom of Ethiopia <note>original: "Æthiopia"; in the "language of the birds" (alchemical code), Ethiopia refers to the *nigredo* or blackening stage, the first essential step of transformation.</note>, where it is naturally a native. For we say that unless it is turned and placed in its own land, it will depart and enter another region. Wherefore you should know for certain that every other climate or other region brings death to our stone—a fact hidden from the unskillful and the ignorant, but known by us.

This property comes into the said substance of nature through its "complexion" <note>The "complexion" refers to the specific balance of qualities (hot, cold, moist, dry) that defines a substance's temperament.</note>, by the action of the primary qualities of the elements, which are now transformed into the property and species of a metal that can endure the fire in its perfection. # THEORY

...again <note>original: *Iterum*; the OCR picks up the end of the word from the previous page</note> we say to you, and more clearly: that through the Creator—who did not cease from generating stones—it may cross the streams, because thus it is found exalted in the rivers; it is itself possessed of great power. And add nothing foreign of the world to it, giving to it only that which comes out and is born from itself; and for a truth, that thing came out from the dragon and from the stinking belly <note>The "dragon" and "stinking belly" are common alchemical allegories for the raw, chaotic state of matter (often lead or crude mercury) before it is purified</note>. For they are placed in the wave of water, of whom we are much afraid. For nothing suffices for them, except that they cause such evil and martyrdom to the people of peace, whereby the people are confounded, and they bring the whole world to confusion. Wherefore this secret was given to us by the one above, as if to be revealed by the Lord to one who is deaf, until it be made manifest to his sons through divine prudence and through their noble intellect. And therefore, sometimes chattering Clerics, Lawyers, Artists, or worldly physicians—and many others of whom we do not dare to speak—believe they can make the living water <note>original: *aquam vivam*; in alchemy, this refers to a potent mercurial solvent</note>, but the whole thing is not worth a single fig, because they believe they are plundering our philosophy, yet they find themselves plundered instead, and thus such men lose their lives therein. Keep, therefore, my sons, the fire and the governance of the spirit, and see that it does not vanish due to excessive heat, but retain it with love, and guard it from great heat. For if the soul departs, the spirit will not be able to bring the body to life, since it cannot give something that is not within itself.

### CHAPTER XI.

In all our mastery <note>The "mastery" or *magisterium* refers to the entire process of creating the Philosopher's Stone</note>, three principal spirits are necessary, which cannot be manifested without the completion of their resolution <note>Resolution here refers to the process of breaking a solid substance down into its liquid or spiritual components</note>. And they are named in another way: the "three living silvers" <note>original: *tria viva argenta*; likely referring to three distinct states or types of Mercury used in the process</note>. In these, our stone is dissolved and turned through the mutation of its nature, through a contrary and diverse digestion, which occurs through the circulation of the elements and through reciprocation into its primordial beginnings of generation. And because resolution is the condition of the entire "first gate" of our mastery, we wish to declare it according to the requirement of the reduction and conversion of the stone into three spirits. You must preserve each of these according to the specific property of the nature of each, as is required in the ultimate perfection of our mastery, through the said resolution divided into three principal parts. The first is bodily, and is called in the Oritan language <note>The "Oritan language" is a mystical or invented language Lull frequently cites to give his terms an air of ancient authority</note>, *Recfage* <note>A technical term in Lullian alchemy, often signifying the first stage of the work or the "matter" of the stone</note>; the second is spiritual...

### RAYMUND LULLY

*The first part of the Recfage solution is nothing other than the reduction of the coarse parts into the smallest and most subtle parts, or the reduction of the thick into the simple, by changing the specific form into a contrary and corrupted form, remaining in its own body—not in the form of water falling from the clouds, nor in the form of metal valued at various prices, but in the form of watery earth and subtle mineral water, sitting in the vessel of the deep hell.* <note>The "vessel of the deep hell" refers to the bottom of the alchemical flask or furnace where the initial "blackening" or decomposition takes place.</note>

You must then guard these very diligently if you wish to enter through that small gate. For it is necessary for you to know well how to govern yourself, and how to bring back that which can enter and exit, if you desire to pass to the second solution, **Agazoph**. 

Therefore pay attention here: the menstrual fluid <term>menstruum: in alchemy, this is not biological fluid but a "solvent" or base liquid used to dissolve and "fertilize" the metals</term> of the seeds is condensed from its airy state into a thick wateriness through the resolution of the feminine seed. This seed is in the menstrual fluid, embraced by the vapor of raw substances, which takes the form of water derived from a more crude vapor. And all of this is nothing other than air and radical humidity <note>original: *humiditas radicalis*; the essential life-giving moisture believed to exist within all matter.</note> generated from the heat and nature of the supreme metal <note>original: *supremi metalli*; usually referring to gold.</note>. The other raw nature, which is the cause of the menstrual condensation and remains below, is the cause, the joining matter, and the gathering-place of the **royal stone**. This stone has turned toward a cold nature because it lost its hot nature through resolution.

...divided operations doubling in the generator. This heat is the instrument with which the *formative power* <note>original: *virtus informativa*. Because the elements—converted by the power of natural heat (which is in the matter excited and hastened by the temperate heat of the sky)—mix themselves in the smallest parts, altering and corrupting while preserving the species governed by a non-burning heat. This corruption is the generation of our mercury, as we shall declare in the second part and the *wheel of the circle*. Because there we shall determine its principal colors, as well as its flavors, odors, thickness, simplicity, subtlety, and weight.

## *On the dissolution of the stone in its specific form, and on the change of its name.*

### CHAPTER XII.

By philosophizing in this way, you can understand that the first and principal intention in our mastery is to dissolve the stone by changing its nature into mercury. This is the first element in approaching its mineral nature; because of this, it is the root and the first element composed of all liquefiable bodies, and the father of the two luminaries <note>original: *luminarium*. In alchemy, the "two luminaries" refer to the Sun (gold) and the Moon (silver).</note>. Therefore, they are converted in this alone through a solemn resolution, and afterwards they are converted into **sulfur**. Because mercury by nature contains its own sulfur within it by means of a vapor, by which it congeals itself into the **philosophical stone**, which afterwards has the power of congealing all other mercury through our mastery. And this stone is called sulfur, and the matter brought near to the perfect nature of metal, through which nature is considered noble and most worthy among the wise. From this, the philosophers make a strong and very solemn medicine, and they call this the **elixir of life** <note>original: *elixir vitae*.</note>, because it is the superlative and ultimate consolation in the human body. 

And we shall provide knowledge of this intention of its composition in the second part of this book, through which we shall conclude the entire course of the said medicine, maintaining our speech in a middle way so that we may be better understood, according to the method and the "middle life" of nature. And so it appears that the intellect is instrumentally directed and led by reason through a "middle form" in this present art and science. Therefore, it is not fitting, nor is it necessary, that the mind be led too subtly, nor that one be too subtle in discerning real beings, lest it be turned toward fantastical things, for which neither art nor nature has any concern. 

If indeed the stone I have described to you becomes red and clear, and within it there is the power of a simple, non-burning fire, you shall do great things; from it you can compose the **elixir for gold**, which is a medicine preserving all active powers in human nature and restoring strengths diminished by nature’s defect. And briefly, if you possess this medicine in this world, you possess an everlasting treasure.

### CHAPTER XIII.

You can understand, my son, that a transition from one extreme to another cannot be made except through a medium <note>In alchemy, a "medium" is an intermediate state or substance that bridges two different conditions.</note>, and we have explained by the logic of nature that the extremes of our stone are, in the first degree, mercury <note>original: *arg vivum*, literally "living silver."</note>, and the second is the perfect **elixir**. But the mediums of these two extremes are ointments and oils, some of which are more "cooked," more pure, and more digested than others; these we call "the medicine to be perfected" and "the ferment of the elixir." You shall learn the preparation of those oils and ointments in the second part of this work. Through this, the good operator and son of learning ought to make **white sulfur** for silver from "black" mercury, and afterwards **red sulfur** for gold. For no sulfur can be made red unless it is first white.

Nature does not allow a transition to be made from the first to the third unless the transition is made through the second. This is apparent through the definition of the elements, which distinguishes that the earth is first black, then water <note>The author is describing a sequence of elemental transformations linked to colors: Earth (black), Water, Air (clear), and Fire (red).</note>, and that the air is more intensely clear, and that the fire is red. For this reason, it appears that earth cannot be converted into air unless it is first turned and changed into water, nor can water be converted into fire unless one of them is first converted into air.

Therefore, you, my son, have much to note within yourself, considering with a philosophical mind the nature of the coloring mediums in the mutation of the mineral nature. For in them lies much of the science of those who strengthen themselves to transmute metals from species to species. And now we have told you—if you have understood us—that it is necessary for you first to transmute the "bodies" <note>In alchemy, "bodies" usually refers to solid metals like gold, silver, or lead.</note> with a natural reduction into that medium through an artificial alteration (imitating the natural one), in which the species of gold or silver can be preserved without the imbalance of individual parts which are of the same kind. And this is the "near matter," which greatly aids the bonding of nature by reason of the first conjunction, by which the stone is dissolved through the alteration of its cooked and raw nature. This nature is very weak, which is the conversion of the "body" into mercury; and through its reduction, it is afterwards converted into **white sulfur**, then into **red sulfur**. And so, from degree to degree, the fallen matter gradually approaches the matter and nature most closely related to metal through an altering resolution. Through this, the matter can more promptly and better receive the "form" of gold or silver through multiplied science and art, as we shall say below in

### *On the gradual transmutations of the stone, so that the matter*
### *becomes fit for creating the elixir.*

### CHAPTER XIV.

After this, my son, we say that our stone is varied and changed by three gradual mutations before it becomes the matter for creating the **elixir** together. And these mutations are performed through the "third digestion" <note>In alchemy, "digestion" refers to the process of exposing a substance to gentle, continuous heat, similar to how a body processes food.</note>. One mutation is into a liquid, by way of a homogeneous oil. And just as this occurs in the cavity of the heart <note>Lull frequently uses "organic alchemy," comparing the stages of the work to the functions of human organs.</note>, so the first digestion occurs in its own vessel by the action of heat, which remains united to the matter. 

Another mutation is in the four humors—that is, when the luminaries <note>original: *corpora luminativa*. In alchemy, the "luminaries" are the Sun (Gold) and the Moon (Silver).</note> have already flowed into corruption. For it is necessary for their nature that their "bad" alteration be converted into "good," and once the bad is made good, they can consequently resist the corruption of all infirm bodies <note>Base metals were often described as "sick" or "infirm" versions of gold.</note>. Blessed be that sweet and just *Jesus Christ, Son of God*, who came to earth for sinners, and because it pleased Him to endure death and pour out His blood high upon the cross, and to be exalted upon it for us and other sinners, to redeem us from the death of hell and from torments. 

By this figure <note>A "figure" is a symbolic or spiritual analogy.</note> I admonish you: the presence of these four humors of the two luminaries—from which the royal medicine is made and established—was necessary. And just as this digestion is performed by living beings in the cavity of the liver’s structure <note>original: *fabricæ epatis epapanticæ*. This refers to the hepatic system as a "factory" of the body.</note>, so the second digestion occurs in the head of the **Alembic** <note>The cap of a distilling apparatus.</note>, descending into the receiver—specifically in the manner of water with the liquor of the air—possessing all the virtues of the mineral elements. 

The third digestion occurs through the mutation of the said humors into pure **sulfur**, just as in living beings where heat and primary humidity are converted into blood, and afterwards into the essence and substance of the limbs, according to the order of nature. Therefore, my son, you must understand that the first digestion occurs when the conjunction and "coitus" <note>The "chemical marriage" or union of the volatile (spirit) and fixed (body) elements.</note> is made for the love of nature, which is a libidinous and desired lust. Then the first mixing occurs through the conjunction and assimilation between the body and the spirit, so that the whole may arrive together at unity and a loving, united concord, joined by the bond of their qualities (now mixable and composed) and by their elemental virtues, one to the other, by virtue of the conception of two in one. And if you never perform this conjunction and coitus, you will never achieve a conception. And unless you achieve a conception, you will never have a pregnancy; and if there is no pregnancy, you will have no fru- <note>The text cuts off here; the catchword indicates the next page begins with "ctus," completing the word *fructus* or "fruit."</note>

Son of peace and truth, in our stone, my son, the spirit remains and moves as if in its own operating body. This happens through the attractive power of our stone, which the said spirit (along with the whole substance of our stone in its aforementioned first mixture) has universally acquired by way of exuberance. This is aided by a more immediate power, namely the natural heat of the stone, which regards nature in a closer proximity of genus and metallic nature. Likewise, it is aided by the power of our imperfect, perforated, and porous stone, which was caused in it through a certain operation—the continuous, insensible, and untouchable dissolution of its body. We shall speak of this more specifically in the second practical part.

## CHAPTER XVI.

Therefore, most dear son, you can be certain that without digestions or decoctions <note>the process of heating or "cooking" the substance</note>, our stone cannot be improved in its own nature. The other we call **optesis** <note>original: "Opteſis," a term for roasting or baking</note>, which is between *scaopteſis* and *scateſis*. Through this, the heat dries the spirit better while resolving it; this resolution we call *Adulphuch* <note>an Arabic-derived term used by Lull to describe a specific purification or distillation</note>, and it is signified by **L**. The third, which is the final stage of the consummation of our earth or threefold dissolution, is the digestion made when quicksilver is converted into the essence of pure sulfur; we call this **scaopteſis**, because it is between *opteſis* and *escateſis*, and it is signified by **M**. ->THE THEORY.<-

Through the first digestion we extract the elements and place them in harmony. Through the second, we dissolve the spirit, shaping its vessel, where it must be converted with the heat of roasting <note>original: "optesi," referring to cooking or roasting over heat</note> after the digestion of cooking. In the third, we create and form our stone from the matter itself immediately, just as the spirit departed from the vessel with the soul of the body, which is the perfection of the stone. In the fourth, we create our royal and true elixir.

H — Pepantic <note>mellowing or ripening</note> or stomach-like digestion.
I — Hepatic <note>liver-like</note> or Ephesus, which is the bath.
K — Solution of Periminel, that is, ashes.
L — Opfesi or Adulphuc, that is, ashes and sand.
M — Optesi, that is, flame.
N — Eschatesi, that is, the secret furnace.

## On the division of the stone into three main causes, on its change, on the principal colors, and from what matter it is specifically extracted.

### CHAPTER XVII.

**By** the doctrine already declared, it must be noted that three principal things are necessary for us in this part: namely the **body**, signified to us by N; the **spirit**, which we signify by O; and the **soul**, which we wish to be signified by P. Always, my son, in the change of the stone you will understand three principal colors.

The first color, therefore, is **black**, and it begins to appear at the end of digestion I, and lasts until the end of M. When our quicksilver <term>quicksilver: original "arg. vivum" (argentum vivum), or mercury, the liquid metal central to alchemy</term> is congealed into sulfur, then a **white** color appears in it, subtle, whiter than snow; and this is the second color. The third, however, will appear in a very **red** heat, like blood, through continuation upon the white stone. 

My son, when the blackness appears to you, it will be a sign of a very strong and noble corruption <note>in alchemy, "corruption" is not bad; it is the necessary decay of the old form so a new, perfected form can be born</note>, because no thing is animated by nature without putrefaction <term>putrefaction: the chemical breakdown or "death" of a substance, which alchemists believed was the first step toward purification</term> having occurred. Make it pass, therefore, through K and L until O becomes well-whitened, which may whiten N through M. After these things, you will redden it with the fire of the stone in the successive digestion of N. 

However, all craftsmen must work patiently in this whitening until the black is perfectly whitened, as we will show through the properties of the elements in Chapters 22 and 23 of this first book. For yellow <note>original: "citrinum," the citron-yellow stage often following the white</note> cannot be made from black until it is well-whitened. Because yellowness is essentially caused by a very white thing and a small amount of clear red. Similarly, the transition from yellow to white cannot occur except through black. Nor can gold be made into medicinal silver unless it is first destroyed and becomes black and corrupted. Nor can a better thing be made from a worse thing, except through its own corruption. Because that white sulfur, which through the digestion of N <note>original: "N," referring to the secret furnace</note> can quickly become red sulfur for gold—this should be understood as using only the fire of the stone, excited by M <note>original: "M," referring to the flame</note>. For within the substance of this stone is a natural heat of goodness and magnitude, and of the other parts of its noble substance. 

And because there is a substantial majority in this, which belongs to its own essence, it therefore possesses natural fire and the property of multiplying its own kind with its heat, digesting itself into the other elements which are capable of being heated, so that the fire may use its heat and multiply it within them through the path of composition and generation, with the continuation of M; for the heat of M is stronger than the digestion of L <note>original: "L," referring to the use of ashes and sand</note>. 

And so, my son, you shall know that this "reddening" <note>original: "rubificatio"</note> is nothing other than completed digestion. For when I rise in the morning and see my urine white and undigested, it is a sign of little sleep. Therefore, I rest and sleep, and I find the urine almost lemon-yellow <note>original: "citrinam"</note>, and I perceive that the sleep is perfect. But when the morning urine is lemon-yellow, then the heat of nature's fire has been spread through all the urinary parts; through this, nature clearly teaches and shows that "citrination" <term>citrination: a stage in the alchemical process where the matter turns a golden or lemon-yellow color, signaling proper digestion</term> is completed through total digestion. 

And therefore, you can understand that white and red sulfur come from only one matter of metals—namely, from fine silver with the fire of fine gold. But first it is necessary that the said matter be strongly purified and cooked in a "differential" manner, as is declared in the following chapter regarding its mixtures. 

My son, such sulfur cannot be found upon the earth, except for that which is in these two bodies <note>gold and silver</note>. Nor is every sulfur white, or red, or perfect for the Great Work <note>original: "magisterium"</note>, except for that which is in the said bodies. And therefore these bodies must be nobly prepared, so that such sulfur and quicksilver <term>quicksilver: mercury, or "argentum vivum"</term> may be obtained upon the earth, from which gold and silver were created beneath the earth. 

With these bodies, quicksilver is mixed in a subtle way. And therefore, if you know how to mix quicksilver with the bodies, you will come to the great secret which we call **white sulfur**, or the **blessed stone**, which afterwards is made red and is called the **royal crown**, and it is the completed stone. 

It is extracted only from these two bodies; the sulfurs for the white and the red have been extracted when the better and purer substance of sulfur has been found in these two bodies, purified to the highest degree by the ingenuity of nature. And this thing is better, higher, and more subtle, in which art cannot follow nature, because in all cases it is not assimilated to it. For if art wished to begin in the first nature or matter...

# THEORY.

...according to the likeness of nature, it would be very long and restless, and would be without end; nor would anything be more base, and many and infinite miseries and expenses would be incurred. And through this, the art—by purifying the primary matter—would be baser and weaker than nature, and thus could never follow nature with all its strength for several other reasons contained in the "tree of questions" <note>original: "arbore quæstionaria," likely referring to Lull’s *Arbor Scientiae*, a systematic diagram of knowledge</note> of this science. And therefore, this science chose gold for the father, and silver for the mother. Because from these two bodies, in their prepared sulfur and arsenic <note>In alchemy, "sulfur" and "arsenic" often refer to the soul and the volatile spirit of the metal rather than the common chemical elements</note>, our medicine is drawn out, and clarified from gold as the most precious of all metals. Therefore, the tincture <note>The substance used to "dye" or transform base metals into gold</note> is of redness, and is reflective and resplendent, tinting and transforming every body to perfect clarity. Silver, however, is the tincture of whiteness, tinting every body with imperfect clarity. With these bodies mix mercury, yet not such as is common mercury, as we shall say in the second part of this book. Wherefore you should know that quicksilver <note>original: "argentum vivum"</note> in its nature is not miscible with bodies.

*How the Artist must be virtuous to seek the first knowledge of the stone, and from what matter it is made, and strongly constant to maintain the second intention through the experience of the art known in the matter of nature.*

## CHAPTER XVIII.

Son, seeker of this science, it behooves you to be firm, and not to search after this or that: since in many things this art is never perfected. And therefore we say to you, that there is nothing but one single stone, namely sulfur, and one single medicine, namely the composition of sulfur, to which you must add nothing, except to remove superfluous earthy and phlegmatic <note>original: "fleumatica," referring to the "phlegm" or cold, watery impurities that hinder the work</note> parts. For these are and ought to be separable, and separated from our quicksilver, which is more common to men than common quicksilver, and is of greater price, merit, and stronger union of nature. From this quicksilver and its first forms, it is necessary to separate everything that does not belong to the harmonic sequence <note>original: "armoniaca," implying a musical or mathematical order</note> of metals, through known and recognized degrees of separation, until it approaches and becomes close to the first thing—namely, of its nearest kind. Insofar as it is possible with real concord, it must be incorporated with fire and earth. And then it is found multiplied with many noble virtues, and is very heavy. No one should ask from nature what she does not have...

For if you do the opposite, it will immediately be worsened and corrupted, and you will not reach your goal. And because the transition is easier in things that share a common symbol <note>A reference to Aristotelian physics, where elements with shared qualities—like heat or moisture—transform into one another more easily</note>, therefore in all bodily things—and those more suitable and similar to the nature of metals—it is necessary for you to take the medicine of diminished bodies <note>original: "corporum diminutorum." "Diminished bodies" refers to base metals like lead or tin, which alchemists believed were simply "sick" or "incomplete" versions of gold</note>. Since the work must have a greater affinity with them in its nature, so that it might embrace [the metal] better and more deeply, with the adherence and fellowship remaining perpetual; so that every body diminished in its nature might be perfected and completed even more perfectly in its nature through the collected abundance. And further, toward the end, [it is necessary] so that the Mercury might be mixed naturally through the smallest parts in those same metals before it takes flight <note>Alchemists used "flight" to describe evaporation or sublimation, where the spirit of the metal escapes the heat of the furnace</note>. And therefore, a substance more subtle and of easier melting in its liquidity is necessary for you to compose our medicine than the actual bodies of metals are, and of a stronger fixing retention than natural or composite quicksilver is in its own nature.
