<meta>This page continues the theoretical instruction on the preparation of the alchemical Stone. While the previous page established that the matter must be "noble" (gold and silver) and found in "deserted lands" (the raw state of matter), this page explains the process of reducing these metals back to their primary components—philosophical sulfur and quicksilver—through controlled operations and moderate heat.</meta>

### THEORY.

For this reason, we choose two luminary bodies <note>In alchemy, the "luminaries" are the Sun (gold) and the Moon (silver).</note>, which fix everything that is not fixed. And therefore it is necessary that those luminary bodies be reduced to their first nature through elementary retrogradation <note>Retrogradation here refers to the process of breaking a substance down into its original, simpler components.</note>—namely, into sulfur and quicksilver <note>original: "argentum vivum," the alchemical term for mercury</note>—by means of contrary operations: which are solution, refinement, sublimation, and coagulation. These are not common, everyday methods, but Philosophical ones. For we tell you that nothing is secret in this science except the method of work and operating, which we shall clearly show to you in the Practice in the second part of this book, provided you are willing to understand our theory, which advises you that you must be willing to be somewhat troubled or labor in the aforementioned operations. 

Because the bodies are of a strong composition, they require a long separation and a contrary operation: namely, that they first be Philosophically calcined <note>Calcination is the process of heating a substance to a high temperature to reduce it to a powder.</note>, and afterward they are also Philosophically dissolved, just as nature requires under a preservation that looks toward generation. For when they are calcined, they are more easily dissolved; because the heat of the fire penetrates the body, and by penetrating its parts, it allows the water to enter after it. Thus, the body is more susceptible to dissolution. And when it is well dissolved, the spirit is congealed; and when the spirit is congealed, the body is dissolved. Because without the coagulation of the spirit, the dissolution of the body does not occur, nor does the dissolution of the body occur without the coagulation of the spirit. 

In this deed, my son, be long-suffering, slow, sweet, and mild, and do not be hurried in anything. Permit all things to be perfected by a slow fire. For the first error in this art is to cook too much, because the fire burns everything and carries it to the region of perdition. Understand that every delay and slowness in this art are chosen for working patiently; do not begin the journey without patience. When it happens that you know many things through study, retain your patience, always working directly, and thus you will have philosophy as a habit; and as you offer your virtue, patience is given to the work. Indeed, patience of character is always the greatest thing, and a majority <note>In this context, "majority" implies a position of superiority or the most essential part.</note> in our great and secret work, which indeed allows one to penetrate it and to know the great secret—yet this is through experience with the "erective instrument" <note>This likely refers to an alchemical apparatus such as an Athanor (furnace) or a specific still.</note> which nature has shown, directing and rightly leading the intellect toward philosophy. 

Therefore, advise yourself that you do not make the fire too great at the beginning of the mixing, because corruption would immediately come upon the tincture. Therefore, in their first calcination, in which the tincture is to be preserved, you will go to the digestion of **L**. From that, you will safely extract **F** from **E**, in the manner that we shall tell you in the Practice. And afterward you will put **D** joined with **H** into **F** in digestion **I**; and there they will immediately be calcined with the form preserved in them, and there through...

THEORICA.
C 3

...[are junc]ted, they are not converted: but their individual parts, in which their simple mineral elements are bound together by the ingenuity of nature, are most excellently converted through that binding while this species is in actuality. And because of this, they are called the "principal mediums" in our <term>mastery: the Great Work or the alchemical process</term>, because they can be changed, cleansed, and purified while their species is preserved. This is done in such a way that the first species, which was in a manifest state of action, is made concrete within the essence of those concrete things found in created beings that do not convert. And since the species consists of those things—which exist in a state of truth, goodness, and magnitude within created beings—they do not convert; for if they did convert, real beings would be thrown into confusion, and art and science could not follow the path they know, nor could nature multiply any thing into the likeness of its preceding kind. 

And therefore, it was placed in the power of nature by the Creator that only the individuals—in which real beings exist, drawn from their species without corruption or the separation of their genus—are transmuted under the preservation of those species in order to achieve multiplication. And from this, our fire is created; it leaps, and from it comes light and clarity. And this light is our heat, which is multiplied by "unnatural fire" and "fire against nature" <note>In alchemical theory, "fire against nature" often refers to external heat or corrosive chemical agents that mimic the transformative power of natural heat.</note>. 

This occurs in the individual parts of mineral nature, as experience will make manifest to you, if you can be imbued with this practice through our art. For the figurative heat of our **red stone** <term>red stone: the Philosopher’s Stone in its final, most potent state</term>, which possesses the fire of simple ignition, is a part of the created fire and is separated from it. With this, we "tinge" <term>tinge: to transform or dye the internal nature of a metal</term> **quicksilver** <term>quicksilver: mercury (argentum vivum)</term>, until it becomes a fire of a greater composition. 

And therefore we call it a "composite fire," because the heat of simple fire is subtly fixed within it—a heat that is fire-making, fire-receptive, and fire-transformed <note>original: "ignificativa, ignificabilis, & ignificata." This is a Lullian logical triad describing the active, passive, and resulting states of the element of fire.</note>. And thus fire, being passive in its individual parts, moves the power to multiply its effect, action, completion, and end. This does not mean that the power, insofar as it is passive, moves the active power; rather, they are known likenesses to real beings intended to be penetrated, cooked, and transformed into a better nature, just as the nature of air is moved into the nature of fire. Thus it moves the power and its objects toward completion and ending, just like fire moves oil to give light and clarify the place in which it is. 

Nevertheless, my son, hold this as a general rule of nature: that always and at all times the object, insofar as it is desirable, moves the power to attract that desired thing to itself—just as a thing desires to be perfected by its own kind and no other, so that it may, according to its completion...

## How the whole making of the stone consists in the knowledge of the elements and in their conversion.

### CHAPTER XXII.

If you understand these elements and know how to convert them through certain operations, you will possess both the making of the stone and the understanding of it. For according to their proportion, we have their forms appearing in various species; and through various proportions of the mixture, a different form is given to the generated compound. A different proportion of mixing exists in metals, as is apparent from their forms. From this arises a part of the secret: we advise that unless you know stones and their virtues in all their natures, you should not approach our stone. My son, the form and species manifest to you the goodness of the matter, or its impurity, its utility, its coarseness, or its simplicity. For a certain form and species, according to its own property, is given to its own proper matter; and according to the flow of the matter, the forms are infused, just as gold and lead manifest to you. And insofar as the matter is more noble, so much more noble is the form of any mixture. And insofar as the form of a pure element is more noble, so much more noble is the form of the body which has been purified from all corruption.

### CHAPTER XXV.

Through this it appears that the celestial virtue acts for the sake of formation—that is, so that it might be able to perfect and shape matter—it performs all the aforementioned things, and thus it is declared how nature moves through its means to its extremes. It is also declared through this that no matter can be perfected unless it **suffers** <note>original: "patiatur." In alchemy, "suffering" refers to the matter being acted upon or undergoing a passive transformation through heat or chemical change.</note> for a long time. And therefore it is necessary that in your matter this virtue be infused, which is the **soul of the stone**, because the soul of our stone is of the nature of stones, just as the <term>vegetable soul: the basic power of growth and nutrition found in plants</term> is of plants, and the <term>vital soul: the animating force that provides movement and sensation in animals</term> is of beasts.

However, do not understand this to mean that it is "vegetable" in the same way as plants, but only that it follows an order in its progression, according to its own power, and according to what its matter can sustain of the power of its most noble celestial virtue; and to the degree that its matter is more <term>subtle: refined, thin, or purified</term>, the virtue works more or less upon it at its will. Not that it is like the vital soul, which is the action of organic and philosophical members <note>original: "organicorum, & philosophicalium membrorum." This refers to the functional parts of the alchemical "body" or apparatus, compared here to the organs of a living being.</note>, having in itself the power of life—because the matter of its own terrestrial nature, being hard and dry, does not permit this—but rather it is like an art, with which the Artist works in his craft. And therefore it is necessary for you to know that every such virtue, which shapes matter according to the kind of nature, requires two proper instruments through which it might shape its work according to the diversity of its matter; we shall speak of these instruments in the second part of the second chapter. Because here we still wish to inform you about the said virtues and to clarify them through examples, using the often-mentioned "vegetable" things <note>Things that possess the power of growth, like plants.</note>.

->*Concerning the death of the stone, and certain causes, and things hindering generation and multiplication; and how they are removed by the demonstration of an example with respect to common nature.*<-

# THEORY

[...the] course of nature, nor of multiplying itself, except by a certain resolution and thinning through the simplicity of its own hard substance. In this hard substance, the heat existing within is frozen and enclosed; this substance is limited and **mortified** <note>original: "mortificata." In alchemy, mortification refers to the "death" or chemical inactivation of a substance, often associated with it becoming black, dry, or solid.</note> by reason of the dryness and hardness in which the matter is confined, and in which the heat of nature is held back. This is because extreme dryness and coldness cause a mortifying quality. 

Through this, even a **peasant** <note>original: "rusticus." Alchemical authors often used the "simple peasant" or "common man" as an example of someone who observes the basic truths of nature, such as seeds growing in soil, without needing advanced philosophy.</note> can recognize that such dryness, which causes hardness and mortification, requires an airy moistening so that the natural heat can be resuscitated and extended into the simple matter of the air, which is its material food. However, to bring this density or hardness of coarse parts back into a state of simplicity is not granted to nature, except through the **subtiliation** <note>original: "subtiliationem." The process of making a substance thinner, more refined, or more spiritual/gaseous.</note> of its dry parts. This is achieved by a resolution made through the **re-incrudation** <term>re-incrudation: (Latin: *reincrudatio*) the alchemical process of returning a "ripe" or "cooked" substance to a "raw" (crude) and moist state so that it can be transformed anew</term> of the wet and heavy material moisture, which had been limited in the "cooked" state during perfect digestion—much like the subtle white substance from which the bread you eat is made. 

And the **re-incrudation** of the said seminal moisture, which was confined in the dry, is caused by the subtle, cold, and raw moisture which it receives during its dissolution. For this reason, it is necessary that the dry matter be limited or converted into **airy moisture**, which is the friend and food of fire, which by its own virtue shapes all things being born. 

But since "dry" and "moist" are opposite qualities by the difference of their contrariety, it is necessary that through the **difference of concordance** <note>original: "differentiam concordantiæ." A Lullian philosophical concept where a middle term or "bridge" is used to harmonize two opposing elements.</note>, the elements be transmuted from quality to quality: that is, one quality into another—namely, **dry into cold**, and **cold into moist**, and **moist into hot**—so that the matter may be properly prepared and joined through fire, by means of this "difference of concordance." 

This is to say that the dry matter of the grain is converted into material moisture (in which the natural heat resides) through the difference of concordance, which has the power to receive the **formative virtue of heaven** from it. Wherefore it appears that nature does not pass from one contrary to another without a medium, through which the "difference of concordance" is caused; it is through this that matter is transmuted from nature to nature, and this is the special distinction which it must preserve. 

For **Water** is the friend of **Air** through moisture, and neighbor to **Earth** through coldness. From water—through rarefaction, lightening, and refinement—comes the **re-incrudation** in things that are and have been cooked, condensed, and limited by both nature and art. And **Earth** is neighbor to **Fire** on account of its dryness, and **Fire** is neighbor to **Air** on account of its heat; from which earth—through rarefaction, and lightening or refinement—the **re-incrudation** occurs in things...

In alchemy, putrefaction is a necessary stage of decay that allows for new life or a higher form of matter to emerge.</note>.

A classic concept where the four elements (Earth, Water, Air, Fire) constantly cycle into one another.</note> is rotated by nature entirely and in a circular path, and it shall be so until it comes to its own determined point. Afterward, let its proper food be administered to it, which the aforementioned virtue has the power to transform into itself. 

And by this method, the mineral matter will be assisted by the industry of the Alchemist. It is done in such a way that, before every man, the matter will manifest its effects and powers through a clear light, not needing any logical proof. ### THEORY.
<margin>4. Vol. D</margin>

...and **putrefaction** and **mortification** <term>mortification: in alchemy, the "death" or breakdown of a substance, often associated with a blackening color (nigredo)</term>. Because then the nature of matter is changed from one nature into another, like a fragile thing and matter that has not yet attained the fulfillment of its perfection.

Therefore, draw the form from its matter through its corruption, so that the matter itself, once separated from its corruption, may be perfected in its **sublimation** <term>sublimation: the process of purifying a substance by heating it into vapor and then condensing it back into a solid</term>. Son, in every material there is a certain active power—as has been said, if you have understood us—which is called "incomplete form." By reason of its imperfection, it is common to two opposites, which are, so to speak, its formative influences, according to its instinct and institution. For when this power is led from potentiality into the act of some form by the formative virtue, it immediately possesses an appetite to exist under the contrary form. Consider this power which is common to both the cold and the moist; for while it exists under one of them, it immediately desires to be under the contrary form—that is, the contrary quality. 

Because no form of a corruptible or generatable body can ever sufficiently fulfill the active power of its matter, since it desires to be fulfilled under another form; nor can this form (being desperate) introduce itself into matter except after the corruption of the first form. And thus, according as the active virtue of the form to be introduced corrupts the present one, so is the active form excited and accelerated toward the contrary form. It grants gradually that it might be more and better completed toward a greater fulfillment, until it is made complete under the action of that form; for without its properties, it cannot exist, nor is it the whole of the matter. 

Therefore, son, when you wish to corrupt **our stone** <note>original: "lapidem nostrum" — likely referring to the Philosopher's Stone in its developing state</note>, do this through dry fire, so that what is dry may be converted into cold. And when you wish to approach generation <note>the act of creation or growth</note>, cause the moist to be converted into heat through coldness. And when you are at the point of generation, place the cold-moist with the hot-dry of its own nature. And when you wish to cool water with heat, heat it more. And when you wish to kindle fire, let it be bathed within with cold water. And if you wish to dissolve snow through coldness [F.] <note>likely an abbreviation for "Fire" or a specific degree of heat</note>, congeal it better; and thus they are turned. You will find the gradual mutations of nature according to the steps of the **ladder of nature** <note>original: "scala naturæ"</note>, which is circular and rounds the elements, as has been said. 

If, therefore, you convert dry into cold, cold into moist, and moist into hot, you will possess the **mastery** <term>mastery: (Latin: magisterium) the successful completion of the alchemical process or the production of the Philosopher's Stone</term>. For in this way, nature departs from an "evil" nature and is converted into a good one, and a good one into a better. And therefore, in this art, we understand "nature" in a twofold way. First, we take it for the "retained," as is the **fire of nature**. Second, we take it for its "container," as is the **air**...

# THE WRITINGS OF RAYMOND LULL

...in which fire is compelled to move in order to form the things of nature. And because air cannot exist unless it possesses the nature of fire, and no one can form any material species in its own likeness except within a closely related nature, it is clear that our **Stone** is composed of the matter of air. For if it were not a material **tincture** <term>tincture: in alchemy, a substance capable of infusing others with its color or properties, often the final stage of the Stone</term>, it could not manifest fire in its effect or action; nor could fire burn without the "food" of air. Nor would fire give off clarity by itself without air. 

Because in every composite there is the **fire of nature**; and that fire is moved by a certain internal shaping, and by moving itself, it moves the matter, always and at all times defining its limits. It is necessary that by this movement it leads toward some specific form, according to how well the "shaper" knows how to inform it—namely, toward that form for which the matter has an affinity according to the course of nature. For this reason, it has been declared that you should not work with anything except the **noblest matter** you can obtain, because a thing is only created according to the nature that is refined within it.

->*Concerning the humidity of our Stone, and how it is "permanent water," and concerning the diverse actions of fire, and the refinement of the gross elements, and concerning blackness.*<-

### CHAPTER XXVIII.

Our humidity, my son, is **permanent water** <term>permanent water: "aqua permanens," a central alchemical concept referring to a solvent that does not evaporate and survives the fire</term>, because it does not lose its **radical moisture** <term>radical moisture: the essential, life-sustaining fluid thought to exist in all things</term>. It is neither consumed by a burning fire, nor can the fire of "our sea" consume it; rather, it appears to change from one degree of heat to another—indeed, it is seen to increase, improve, and grow in its essential properties. 

For fire is its proper nourishment and the cause of its noble increase. Therefore, when you wish to begin the preparation of our **mastery**, take water proportioned in quality according to the nature of the body you wish to dissolve. Do this in such a way that the "virtue of fire against nature" does not overcome the "natural heat." 

For bodies are not of the same quality in their measure—even though they were all once of a single virtue in their measure within our Lord God—now they participate in a diversity of harmonies. For some of them are not of such a strong composition, nor is their **sulphur** <note>In alchemy, Sulphur represents the active, masculine, and combustible principle</note> so refined or tempered. And therefore, they can be dissolved by a more fragile power. 

Dearest son, the fire that warms a man chills a lion; and the fire that warms a lion burns and consumes a man. By this you must know the strengths of the virtues of our stones, to the end that the **quicksilver** <note>original: "arg. vivum" (argentum vivum), representing the volatile, feminine principle</note>, in respect to the power of the nature of sulphur, can be tempered through a certain knowledge of its graduation in its...

### THEORY.

...in the first resolution <note>or dissolution</note>, because in it lies all danger. And therefore I notify you that you should have the **sulphurs** destroyed by heat from simple **quicksilvers** <term>quicksilver: an archaic name for mercury, representing the fluid, metallic, and volatile principle in alchemy</term> in such a form that their active property is not destroyed by external heat, and so that they cannot be separated from their moist subject, which appears entirely black and full of a noble spirit. This **blackness** demonstrates the sign of the "first gate" for entering our **mastery** <term>mastery: the Latin "magisterium," referring to the successful completion of the Great Work or the alchemical process itself</term>. And without this blackness, nothing can be accomplished, because it is the **fire of nature**, which has the power to create the Stone; this Stone cannot be manifested without the corruption of its own body. And unless it is manifested in this way, it will never be in a state of action through which it might grow or generate. 

Since it has been revealed that the beginning of our operation is in the form of the **raven’s head** <note>original: "caput corvi"; a traditional alchemical term for the "nigredo" or black stage, symbolizing death and putrefaction before rebirth</note>, and all operations preceding the start of our work are entirely erroneous until the whole composite manifests as black: therefore, my son, do not think that our blackness comes suddenly or quickly. Instead, it arrives gently and gradually, because it is necessary that the heats pass through their various stages just as the elements do. Because the fire of nature, since it is enclosed in the deepest part of its body, cannot show itself immediately until that body is opened. 

For fire is enclosed and hidden within the coarse elements. And therefore it is necessary to refine the elements—namely, earth and water—through a weak **digestion** <term>digestion: a process of slow, consistent heating, similar to how the stomach processes food, used to mature the alchemical matter</term>. From this is caused **greenness** <note>original: "viriditas"</note>, which is the first color. This sign lets us know that the action of the released heat is still slight and slow, and consequently insufficient to dissolve and thin the earthy parts. Therefore, on the "skin" or surface, and indeed everywhere, the green color of nature is multiplied; however, because of the excessive moisture holding it back in a dull state, it cannot be fully manifested. 

But, as was said before, the natural heat is gradually strengthened by the help of the fire's heat, administered by the **Artist** and operator, who well knows how to arrange, shape, and cook his matter through his intellect until it appears clothed in black on the surface. For it is then that the natural fire fights against the moisture, and from this struggle the blackness is created. Therefore, when it begins to appear, increase it and multiply it through natural shaping, by which the natural fire must govern itself; it begins to digest the matter, as is apparent from the blackness. And from this it was declared that at the point of blackness, our fire begins to work, and not before. And therefore it is called the beginning of our mastery, because then the heat of our matter is awakened and accelerated, which has the power to **putrefy** <term>putrefaction: the alchemical stage of decomposition where the substance "dies" to its old form to be reborn as something more pure</term> all its elements until the end of this kind of digestion, which is the first [stage] of heat in...

...by our artifice, until the matter is completed, because the harsh <note>original: "humor ponticus"; referring to a sharp, bitter, or astringent quality of the matter</note> and earthy moisture, altered by its opposite and aided by its like, digests itself skillfully and aptly. And then, in the completed matter, through the degree of said digestion, the black color is multiplied—not only on the surface or the "skin," but through all the subtle and separated parts in the entire matter through multiplication, which is generated by natural heat within the radical moisture <term>radical moisture: the fundamental, life-sustaining fluid believed to exist in all things, which the alchemist seeks to purify</term>. From this, our **white tincture** <term>tincture: in alchemy, a substance capable of transmuting or "coloring" other bodies into a higher state</term> becomes as white as snow; and then we say that the body is fused and liquefied inside and out—not by the power or action of common fire, but by the power of the fire which is natural heat. For this fire seizes and impregnates our **Stone** with a stronger heat than elemental fire. And thus we see the powers and virtues of things, and their causes, and we know them through their effects. Keep this matter secret, my son: that natural heat, predominating after the lessening of the moisture that lifts up all coarseness and the earthiness of the substance, which previously it could not well dissolve. Afterward, through its stronger action, it resolves and digests so much that it comes to the final point of its action in the **first digestion**. And when the matter is thus digested, putrefied, and optimally cooked by the said digestion, nature separates the subtle from the dense, and the coarse is cast out to distant parts through the action of the **second digestion**. And as much as is necessary, it converts from the subtle into the substance of **sulphur**, created from **quicksilver** <term>quicksilver: an archaic name for mercury, representing the fluid, metallic principle</term>; according to this, the conversion is performed by the information given to the heat of nature in the **third digestion**.

*On the manner of philosophizing. And how this science and art is not given except to philosophers. And that the congealing of quicksilver is the principal and final secret. And on the patience of the operator, in passing through to the whiteness.*

### CHAPTER XXIX.

The books of this science speak through silent voices that must be strongly noted, to the end that the principal matter may be contained within them. And let it be known that this secret is not manifested except to philosophers and the sons of our philosophy, who are searchers and inquirers of truth and lovers of it, and not to sophists full of lies, nor to the greedy, nor to worldly lovers—such as usurers, merchants, money-reminting coiners, money-changers, and gatherers of treasures—who are condemned and enchanted by the devil. These men do not wish to labor or inquire except into palpable things, because they are soaked and intoxicated in worldly affairs, and cannot open their intellect to understand...

...while following our good teachings, through which they might possess an enduring treasure and salvation. Therefore, my son, I tell you to wisely contemplate the doctrines we give you in our books; take note of them and gloss them <note>original: "glosa fortiter"; to provide explanatory comments or interpretations</note> thoroughly through many considerations and repeated meditations if you desire to understand us. And when you do understand us, grasp the knowledge with both hands, yet keep it covered by your shirt—the garment of philosophy—and thus leave the teachings to others just as our fathers left them to us, and not otherwise. If you do the opposite, you shall be cursed, like one who shares in the world’s confusion. And do not reveal it by the living voice <note>original: "vocem vivam"; meaning oral transmission or plain, un-coded speech</note>, for no one ought to possess the art without labor, nor should it be manifested to anyone in practice without careful consideration, except through the veil of philosophy, and only to those who are enlightened and uplifted by intellect, and who possess the rectified instruments for penetrating the causes and secret things of nature.

And therefore, son, many considerations are necessary before you proceed to the formation of our **Stone**. You must be a seeker through the revelation of the noble intellect regarding those things we call true in our mastery: specifically, how the smoke of our fermented gold, after fixation and reduction into its earth, visibly appears in the philosophical fire. 

Know then, that the earth in which our gold must be sown and planted is first white before it can manifest the sight of our fire. At the start of our mastery, this is the congealing of our quicksilver in our magnesia through skill and a certain regime.

## *On the manner of proceeding in practice, and how great a thing is required in the magistery.*

### CHAPTER XXXI.

To instruct the "son of art" <note>A traditional term for an apprentice alchemist</note> on this matter, there is need of great knowledge—namely, through revelation or demonstrable teaching—so that he may be able to enter the practice of our magistery <note>The "Great Work" or the mastery of alchemical transformation</note>. He requires a strong and vast theory, which reveals the powers through the will of nature. And if you are negligent in thoroughly reading and examining what is contained in our books, you will go blindly into the practice like an ignorant man. And therefore, my son, you must think beforehand about which thing you must set your hand to work upon. You must know how many and which things are principally required in our magistery, or in the proximity of its operation.

And for that reason, son, I tell you that three things are required: namely, a subtle natural ingenuity <note>original: "Ingenium subtile"; innate intelligence and intuition</note>, not a false or artificial one; the work of the hands; and free will. And this further requires wisdom, wealth, and books. Wisdom, to know how to act. Wealth, to have the power to perform the work. Books, to open a diverse understanding, such as is found among many nations. For that which one person understands through the teaching of one author can never be fully grasped except through the teaching of another. And so the teaching of one will open the teaching of another, which was perhaps given through figures <note>Alchemical symbols, allegories, or coded diagrams</note> and according to a tradition of greater or lesser value.

But here, we shall reveal to you in a clear voice the hidden principle, so you may enter the "secrets of secrets" of nature. There you will see many beautiful wonders which are stored within the secrets of nature, and they shall be regarded almost as miracles through the secret of Lady Nature. In this, it is necessary that you begin to enter in this manner: Son, it is necessary for you first to have in your knowledge the formative virtue <note>original: "virtutem formativam"; the inherent power that gives shape and specific properties to a substance</note>, as recalled from what was said above, which depends upon our magistery known through certain science. Because art—that is, science—when it is truly known without any ignorance through the sense of intelligence that comes from the noble operator, informs the matter toward that existence to which the instrumental natural heat <note>original: "calor naturalis instrumentalis"; the heat of the furnace used as a tool to mimic nature's creative heat</note> is directed. In this heat, the active virtue flows from the formative virtue, and it is directed from its matter to work and form directly. Then it appears that the said instrumental heat is directed through...

...formative power <note>original: "virtutem formativam"; the innate capacity of a substance to take on a specific shape or quality</note>, and this formative power depends on the knowledge of the operator in guarding the course of nature within the magistery <note>The "Great Work" of alchemy</note>. Through this knowledge, the power is infused into the matter, because the excited and increased heat itself moves it. Just as in the nature of every other thing, the formative power is infused from the heavens and from the stars. For the heavens are the moving principle of all nature, just as the wise operator is in our magistery, through the teaching of his noble intelligence. 

Therefore, let it be revealed to you that two things are necessary in our magistery: namely, the informative power <note>original: "virtus informativa"; the guiding force that gives "form" or character to the substance</note> and the elevated instrument <note>Likely referring to the specialized alchemical furnace or vessel</note> through which our magistery must be formed. The informative power is governed by the four principal virtues, which are both convertible <note>Able to be changed into one another</note> and converting: namely, **heat**, **cold**, **moisture**, and **dryness**. This is done so that the matter may be treated with a direct instrument and guided and led to that act through which it must undergo its operation according to the intention of that which converts and that which is converted. In this action, the matter must be informed, so that through that very informing, its instrument may be governed toward the completion of its operation, corresponding to the will of the operator in the matter shaped by art according to the requirements of venerable nature—which is wise and intent on reaching and perfecting its work of perfection.

### *On the four natural changing virtues, and what they are called, and how they operate.*

## CHAPTER XXXII.

Understand, my son, that since the said formative power must govern itself through the four aforementioned elemental qualities, from these—without any intermediary and in succession—the four natural changing virtues <note>original: "virtutes naturales mutativæ"</note> are caused. Therefore, you must gradually divide the "informing" (which every good operator must infuse into the appropriate matter) successively into four parts: namely, into the **attractive** or **appetitive** nature, into the **retentive** and **coagulative** nature, and into the **expulsive** and **contentive** nature, and the **digestive** nature. 

The **attractive nature** operates through heat and moderate dryness; the **retentive nature** through dryness and moderate coldness; the **expulsive** through moisture and moderate heat; and the **digestive nature** through heat and moderate moisture. And in that action in which the matter operates best within its own complexion <note>The specific balance of the four qualities—hot, cold, moist, dry—in a substance</note>, you must assist it; because according to the greater or lesser strength of its complexion, the matter will show you its speed, its slowness, or the temperament of its difference.

### THEORY.

...of transmutation <note>original: "transmutationis"</note>, from which secondary effects arise. These are drawn from potential into actual existence <term>from potentiality into act</term>, such as weight, lightness, heaviness, hardness, softness, sweetness, bitterness, whiteness, and blackness, etc. Know then, my son, toward which power and which form you must guide your matter: either toward the **appetitive power**, the **digestive power**, the **retentive power**, or the **expulsive power** <note>These are the four biological "faculties" or "virtues" that medieval science believed governed how any body—be it human or chemical—absorbed, processed, held, or expelled substances</note>. It is necessary that the matter be "informed" <note>given a specific character or "form"</note> by a known and understood art. This must be done in such a way that the instrument used is moved and well-directed until the very end of its operation. This conclusion reveals a certain sign to the practitioner of his mastery. Therefore, if he keeps these signs in his memory, he will possess certain knowledge and the habit of correcting and improving both the strengthening and the weakening of the substance—which are the two extremes of natural operations.

Understand, therefore, that fire is the instrument of nature. Just as the hammer is the tool a blacksmith uses to move the iron into the shape he intends—the smith directing the hammer through a purposeful motion—so too does the heat of the fire work in our mastery. It is directed by the intention of the Artist according to the rules of the art. It may be directed toward destroying and corrupting, or toward generating, or toward binding, or toward other ends. 

It is therefore necessary for you, through this scientific knowledge, to have the guidance to choose and recognize the specific fire required. When this fire is shaped by the art, the matter must be changed from one nature into another, until the motion of the "supreme nature" within the fire can rest eternally in its own matter without any corruption, having terminated and expelled all foreign motions. This is the heat found in all things that are generated, just like the heat of the sun, which is the primary cause of all generation. 

Be certain of this: if the operator's skill is uncertain in preparing the matter, our **stone** <note>original: "lapis noster"; the Philosopher's Stone</note> cannot be formed. Within the potential of this stone, the entire course of virtues found at the heart of our medicine is naturally and formally included. Blessed be the glorious and almighty God, who gave to the human race the intellect to join and integrate the confused details of the whole of medicine into a single reality, through which they remain entirely rectified. 

And so, my son, we admonish you: if you desire to be a perfect physician, do not devote yourself to the mere "particulars" of medicine <note>Specific, isolated remedies for individual symptoms</note>, because they are confused and are not whole today. Nature cannot endure them because of this excessive confusion. Instead, find your satisfaction in the **unique medicine**, for there is only one cure for all malice, depravity, and sick-

### T H E O R I C A.

...by which the active virtue <term>active virtue: the inherent power within a substance to act upon other things and transform itself</term> exists, it may not be overcome by elemental fire. And in the first operation of its corruption <note>In alchemy, "corruption" is the necessary first stage where the old form of a substance is broken down so a new, higher form can be generated.</note>, you must observe that the fire against nature <note>original: "ignis contra naturam." This usually refers to external, artificial heat, like that of a furnace, as opposed to the internal "natural" heat of the substance itself.</note> exceeds the natural heat innate in the mobile subject by only one degree, and not beyond that number. For the individual spirit, which is the preserver of the species, desiring a similar generation by the right instinct of its nature, would be corrupted by the destruction of its essence, and then it would no longer have the appetite to create a similar generation. Because nature would depart through corruption and destruction—which are against nature—and would reach its limit and an end of consummation, because it would have no place in which to rest, nor air in which to breathe. 

And a vacuum must enter, where previously the place was full of an external nature. And you must have a large alembic <term>alembic: a distillation apparatus consisting of two vessels connected by a tube</term>, so that the matter can ascend more freely and be excited with a small fire, so that it may pass into the air. And it is not necessary that the air be greatly condensed into water by the excited fire, because the active virtue would be submerged and suffocated too much in the water, and the natural tinctures would be burned when the action of the heat of the elemental fire occupies the parts of the natural fire, or the place where it is carried. 

Just as it is seen that a large flame destroys a small one and converts it into itself, we do not want the fire against nature to convert the natural fire in the whole of its essential and accidental substance. Rather, we want the natural fire, by its primary power in the part already altered, to convert the fire against nature into itself. And therefore let it be revealed to you that two certain operations are necessary for you: namely, **corruption**, which should be performed under the preservation of its form, and is done by the fire against nature with the excitation of elemental fire, aided by the naturalness of the natural essence. 

The other operation is **generation**, which is done with the natural fire multiplied by the "non-natural" fire and the fire against nature. Because these two fires are converted into the proper natural fire—namely, the non-natural fire by itself and by accident, and the fire against nature by accident through the love of the attraction of the non-natural fire. And in that natural fire they are found and converted. Wherefore, between both, there are the warm and highly tempered instruments of nature, arising from a very strong virtue, which is high and most powerful for making a new regeneration or the binding of many virtues joined in one proper subject,

## *How the matter of our quick-silver is found. And it can be found in every elemental body.*

### C H A P T E R XXXIV.

If you wish, my son, to achieve the effect of our mastery <note>The "mastery" or *magisterium* refers to the successful completion of the Alchemical Work, resulting in the Philosopher's Stone.</note>, you must not be ignorant of the nature of our quick-silver <term>quick-silver: originally "argentum vivum," this refers here not to common liquid mercury, but to a philosophical "first matter" that resides within all things</term>, which is found in every elemental body. For every elemental body—in whatever form nature may have shaped it—is composed of the four principal elements, as is clearly evident through the revolution of the circle of nature. This circle shows that no thing created or generated by nature will ever be of such a diverse form or figure that we cannot find it, through natural principles, to be composed of one material genus: namely, our quick-silver.

Indeed, we wish this to be called the "proximate general genus" of nature, acting as its very own natural subject, in which Lady Nature paints and draws her diverse figures. And note: when we say "proximate," we say it to distinguish it from the "universal genus" from which this descends. And when we call it "general," we distinguish it from the even closer proximity of another genus which it has toward nature. 

Therefore, since it belongs to this genus, it is converted into it whenever it is brought close through art or nature. It belongs to the first form of the universal genus, from which all other genera descend, which are our "quick-silvers." And thus, since all genera come by a gradual natural succession from the first quick-silver—which is the most general substance, yet removed from the principal and more proximate means of nature—it is called "primary matter" <term>primary matter: or *materia prima*, the formless, fundamental "stuff" that exists before it takes on a specific shape or identity</term> for every succeeding genus. 

Nor do these things discord or differ in the nature of that first genus, which is called the "universal" or "most general" in our philosophy. On this point, the logicians and reasoners are deceived <note>Lull is critiquing scholars who only study the definitions of things (logic) without understanding their hidden, physical transformations.</note>, because they only consider things by their species or outward figure. Yet you see clearly every day that the genus of nourishment is converted into the genus of the thing being nourished. Nature could not do this unless the nature of the thing converting and the nature of the thing converted shared a harmony.

This harmony, my son, descends from the first genus of a thing, which is divided into three genera: namely, animal, vegetable, and mineral. 
1. From the first genus comes **vapor**, generated from the elements immediately and without a medium. 
2. From the second composition come **mineral bodies**.
3. From the third composition come **vegetables** (plants).
4. From the fourth are **beasts** and brute animals.
5. And from the fifth are **men**.

But all of these descend from the most principal of all principal genera, from which nature receives the nature of quick-silver to create every such compound. And every compound, by reason of the said matter, as if in the pri-

->T H E O R I C A.<-

[the] Mercurial matter is transmuted into something else, as has been said: into the nature and matter of another compound. Specifically, the Mercurial genus of the vegetable kingdom is transmuted into the animal and mineral genus, and the animal genus into the mineral. This occurs when it approaches a "retrogradation" <note>In Lullian alchemy, "retrogradation" refers to a reversal of the natural process of compounding, returning a substance to a simpler, more primary state of composition.</note> back to the second degree of composition, from which mineral bodies are formed. In this way, nature performs such a transmutation through a subtle separation of the pure from the impure—namely, of the homogeneous thing from the heterogeneous.

For nature’s intention is such that when it wishes to prepare its compound for destruction, it immediately considers separating the nature that participates with the **fifth thing** <note>original: *re quinta*, referring to the "Fifth Essence" or Quintessence, the pure spiritual core of matter</note>. In that essence, it saves and preserves the primary species, because it can receive no other counsel. And if it happens that, due to a cause of great excitation, nature cannot do this, it remains in a coarser matter, through which it transmutes said matter into the genus of another compound—be it vegetable, animal, or mineral. For according to how far the potential for corruption extends, and according to the material of the body, it is transmuted into that state, or another, or something similar. For instance, if the simple matter of the **fifth composition** <note>This refers to the highest level of alchemical refinement, where the substance is nearly spiritual.</note> is corrupted without the preservation of its form, it immediately seeks the matter of the **fourth composition** through its naturally coarse state.

But this division cannot be accomplished by art, nor by nature for the perfection of matter, unless the **active converter** <term>active converter: the agent or catalyst, often called the "philosophical fire" or "ferment," that triggers the transformation of the base matter</term> renders the whole matter **homogeneous**. This means that every part of it must be similar to the whole, whether the form is simple (like the form of the elements) or a mixed form (like the form of a stone or metals). This homogeneity is created so that the matter may be separated from all forms that do not result from the harmonious mixing of bodies, which nature or art intends to constitute from said matter.

Perhaps the aforementioned "converter" is natural, or contrary to nature. If it is natural, then **fusible stones** <note>original: *lapides fusibiles*; these are minerals or alchemical preparations that can be melted and shaped by heat.</note> will be created through heat and dryness. And if it is contrary to nature, then non-fusible stones will be created, in which no moisture remains to be shaped by the converting nature, except according to the continuity of the matter. Therefore, such stones cannot be melted, nor are they ever melted.

And when said matter has been broken down through the degrees of separation, it then nears the **First Cause**. The closer it is to that cause, the more it can be multiplied with the most noble virtues. This occurs when the body from which perfection comes—which we call the **fixed ointment** <term>fixed ointment: *unguentum fixum*, a stable, non-volatile substance that acts as the vehicle for the alchemical "tincture" or transforming power</term>—imprints its "figures" upon it. These figures are the multiplied tinctures of **goldenness** or **silverness** <note>original: *aureitatis aut argenteitatis*, referring to the qualities of gold and silver that can be projected onto base metals</note>. Through these figures, the virtue of the most noble matter completes its effects and duties, and its [own functions].

### *Concerning the supreme genus, from which all nature issued forth.*

## CHAPTER 35.

Therefore, my son, you ought to be sufficiently enlightened to see that unless there were a universal and supreme genus through which nature is governed, no thing that was to be created or generated by nature could exist. Nor could any animate thing live without the sustenance of this supreme genus, which is the very matter of nature; without it, nature would lose its being. 

Wherefore, since this supreme genus is potentially present in such a material state—though in a confused or hidden way—within the matter and substance of every genus, it is necessary for you to act. Through the transmutation of its form, following certain degrees of mastery, you must convert these matters from potentiality into action—specifically, into the **first matter** <note>original: *primam materiam*</note>. This matter is not far removed from the metallic genus, but is close and near to the lineage or type in which they existed at their beginning. From this matter or genus, nature begins to work before any other specific form of first matter is introduced or generated within that closer genus.

### *Concerning the matter which desires to have unity of form, so that it may be integrated by its perfection into the unity of the spirit of the fifth essence.*

## CHAPTER 36.

This **first matter**, Son, is a **subtle sulfurous earth** <term>subtle sulfurous earth: in alchemy, this is not common soil, but a refined, dry, and active principle that acts as the "soul" or "seed" of the metal.</term> which greatly desires to be made whole by the unity of the **spirit of the fifth essence** <note>original: *spiritus quintae essentiae*, the Quintessence or the most purified spiritual force in matter.</note>. Just as the first matter seeks its own proper form to reach completion, so too must the matter of **moist quicksilver** <note>original: *argenti vivi humidi*, or liquid mercury.</note> be prepared through seven distillations. This ensures the matter is pure, allowing a pure form to be obtained through resolution. 

This should be understood as applying to both dry and moist matter. The nobler and better the matter is, the more it desires a nobler form; and the nobler the form is, the more it ennobles its matter. However, the matter must be capable of receiving that form. When matter is brought close—either by the chemist’s art or by nature—to the action of the **First Cause** <note>In this context, the First Cause refers to the divine or primary creative power that initiates all change in the universe.</note>, it becomes highly capable of receiving the **golden mineral form** <note>original: *formam mineralem aureicam*</note>, which clarifies, illuminates, and utterly ennobles it. This <term>First Matter</term> <note>original: *prima materia*; the primordial, undifferentiated substance from which all things are created</note> has other properties, through which we know it to be of the nature of **sulfur** and **quicksilver** <note>original: *sulphur & argentum vivum*. In alchemical theory, these are the two fundamental principles—active/combustive and passive/metallic—that combine to form all metals.</note>. For it cannot be destroyed in fire, nor in air, water, or earth. And it possesses the properties of dissolving, congealing, drawing by desire, attracting, retaining, expelling, driving, and directing—which is the perfection and completion of an animated thing with contrary passions. Through these properties, it is most certainly established that it is of the nature of sulfur and quicksilver; since within them occur contrary operations which it could not perform unless it were of the nature of both and shared their properties. And since these stated properties cannot exist without a substance—just as no <term>accident</term> <note>original: *accidens*; a philosophical term for a property or quality that exists only within a substance, such as color or weight, rather than being the substance itself</note> can exist without matter—we say that this substance is nothing other than sulfur and quicksilver gathered according to their composition.

Through this, it is evident that **our Stone** is found in every place by reason of its properties, and from that experience we know that it is the first matter of all universal things which have been formed through generation and corruption according to their composition. Therefore, it has been declared to us that it is of the nature of sulfur and quicksilver. Because of this, it is not quicksilver in its entire substance, nor in its entire nature relative to **common quicksilver** <note>original: *argentum vivum communis*; the liquid mercury found in nature, which alchemists distinguished from their "philosophical" mercury</note>, but is partly made of it; and therefore it clings amicably to its own nature and is its perfector, by reason of its powerful <term>digestion</term> <note>original: *digestionis*; the alchemical process of slow, constant heating to mature a substance</note>, through which the raw is converted into the cooked. 

For then <note>original: *natura lætatur natura*; a famous alchemical maxim meaning "nature rejoices in nature," suggesting that like substances are naturally attracted to and perfect one another</note> **nature rejoices in nature**, and it is its mother and the dwelling-place of its nature through its harmony, which is moved by the First Cause; and one congeals the other, and they <term>fix</term> <note>original: *fixant*; the process of making a volatile substance stable so it no longer evaporates when heated</note> themselves perpetually and join without any separation. This could not happen unless the nature of one participated by affinity in the nature of the other, and this by the proximity and closeness of the first genus from which all things proceeded. 

And therefore we say it is clearly known that this first matter is of the nature of quicksilver and is close to it, since in its <term>projection</term> <note>original: *projectione*; the final step of the Great Work, where the perfected Stone is thrown onto base metal to transform it into gold or silver</note> it defends common quicksilver against the fire from burning without flight <note>meaning the mercury does not evaporate or "flee" the heat</note>, and congeals it, and wonderfully retains it after its perfect fixation. Whence it should be noted that the nature of the **Medicine** <note>original: *medicinæ*; another name for the Philosopher's Stone or the elixir of transformation</note> is nothing but quicksilver well-digested and cooked by the nature of its purified sulfur. And since the matter of quicksilver is of a metallic nature, it therefore penetrates the metal and mixes with it, because it is of the same substance and nature. Wherefore you must understand that quicksilver must be fixed, first in a certain decoction descending from one property—which is its digestion and perfection through the <term>ferment of the sun and moon</term> <note>original: *fermentum solis & lunæ*; "Sun" and "Moon" are alchemical code for gold and silver, used as catalysts to give the Work the "form" of a precious metal</note>—before you make a projection upon quicksilver... <meta>catchword: [ar-]gentum (quicksilver)</meta>

## *How our stone is found in every place. And regarding the skill by which it may be found.*

### CAP. XXXVIII.

Since, then, my son, we have told you that all things in the world receive their **substantial**, **accidental**, and **spiritual** form <note>In Aristotelian philosophy, the "substantial form" is what makes a thing what it is (its essence), while "accidental" forms are non-essential qualities like color or size.</note> from such materials, we say for this reason that you will find **our stone** in every place. Since all things in the world were procreated from it, once this is understood, see from what matter you desire to be a philosopher. For from every thing, or from some combination of them, you may extract the <term>first matter</term> <note>original: *prima materia*; the primal, formless base of all physical reality.</note>, even moving from potential into act, in deed and actually, as we have already revealed to you. From that matter alone—because only from it do they exist in truth—all things are procreated in greatness and power.

For example, when a blacksmith wants to make a nail, it is necessary that he takes the appropriate material, namely iron, because he cannot forge a nail without the matter of iron. Then, through his tools, he has to shape it, guided by the information coming from his intellect, until he reaches the desired end. It is the same with nature; when she wishes to begin shaping some thing into its **substantial form**, she takes the simple first matter which is without a completed form. In that matter, she begins to fix the **elements**, which are of diverse natures, according as they are purified and made more simple in their natural preparation through the action of temperate heat. 

Thus she shapes diverse forms, colors, odors, tastes, and diverse <term>complexions</term> <note>original: *complexio*; the specific balance of the four qualities (hot, cold, moist, dry) that determines the nature of a substance.</note>, according to the diversity of the <term>mixture of elements</term> <note>original: *mixtionum elementorum*; the way the four basic elements combine to form physical matter.</note> in this first matter—whether it be in animals, vegetables, or mineral things. For the said matter has a convertible respect for all things by reason of its lack of prior mixture. Therefore, it is able to be converted into everything, like a general seed of all things, according to the operation of the influences of things and joined causes, and according to the attraction of the place in which the matter resides. 

And therefore, the <term>most general genus</term> <note>original: *genus generalissimum*; a term from logic referring to the highest, most inclusive category of being that cannot be a species of anything else.</note>—which is similar to the first [matter] in which the matter is held through the individuality of the first kind—is drawn from that matter (already completely formed by nature and generation) through natural corruption combined with artifice. We then convert and congeal it into its own similar nature.

### *On keeping secret the discovery of the stone.*

### CHAPTER XXXIX.

Keep this secret: that in all things created and formed by nature, in their ultimate purification, there is found the **first matter** <term>materia prima: the formless, primordial substance that the alchemists believed could be stripped of its qualities and rebuilt into any other substance.</term> of all things and of each of them in the form of **Mercury** <note>original: *Mercurius*</note>. And we see this by noble experience, if you wish to perform it: this matter is called the "most general genus." However, do not take this as the laypeople do, who understand it only as a conceptual term or a phantasmal being, but as a real being, which is the material limit of nature, from which it receives its material principles in the act of generation, because it is the first being. This is the material limit in nature, and our philosophy, under a logical shadow <note>i.e., using the language of Aristotelian logic to hide the physical reality.</note>, proclaims it the "most general genus" because it is the subject of the first nature, which is divided into three, through which it is the genus of the mineral kind; likewise, it is the genus of the vegetable kind; and again, it is the genus of the animal kind. And therefore we wish our philosophy to be understood from these three principal genera in the art of experience: namely, the mineral, the vegetable, and the animal. Know, my son, that many will read our books and will not be able to understand them, because in them our principal terms of true understanding will be unknown, hidden, and covered—as will those of others. These people, through their ignorance and deficiency, will labor day by day to reject us because we tell the truth, and in the end all things will be known along with their rejection. Therefore, if you can obtain our books, keep them hidden from the hands of such people, and especially from those who [merely] trade in this art. In these books, we openly reveal the whole secret. And above all, guard the present book from the enemies of the world, because great wonders are and will be found here through certain experiences, as we shall say in the second part of this book.

### *How the stone, after its discovery, receives assistance from other things to produce a complete elixir.*

## CHAPTER XL.

Since we have told you further that the mentioned "genus" <note>Referring back to the "most general genus" or First Matter from the previous chapter.</note> must be protected from all **black combustion** <term>nigra combustione: a failure in the alchemical process where the material is charred or burned by excessive heat, ruining its transformative potential.</term>, this is necessary for you because, through that genus, you will complete your entire work with the help of the **tinctures of the sun and moon** <term>tincturarum solis & lunae: alchemical preparations of gold (sun) and silver (moon) used to "color" or transform base metals.</term>. However, it is necessary that you know how to extract this through the art and science of our mastery—as we shall tell you in the second part—and how to strip it of all its external forms which nature has placed within it, such as the forms of the various planets, different minerals, and various liquids.

And yet, in all of these things, this matter is found more closely in some than in others; it is found with greater abundance and a stronger bond to the substances and natures of metals according to how much they contain of the spirit of the **quintessence** <term>quinta essentia: the "fifth essence" or purest spiritual core of a substance, beyond the four elements of earth, air, fire, and water.</term>. Among **vegetables**, such things include the vine <note>original: *vitis*; the grapevine was prized by alchemists for producing "aqua vitae" (alcohol), seen as a concentrated life-force.</note> (called the masculine matter), and the great **lunaria** <note>original: *lunaria*; likely Moonwort, a plant believed to have a mystical connection to the moon (silver).</note> which is the vital juice, and the root of grain or straw, and leeks <note>original: *portis*; likely a variation of *porrum*.</note>, purslane, mallow, mercury-herb, celandine, and other trees and herbs of a hot and moist nature that bear flowers and gums from which oil can be made. The nature of these is closely joined to the matter and nature of metals and minerals, as are all other things that are naturally hot and moist.

Among **animals**, there is the species of the **basilisk** <note>original: *basilisci*; while a mythical creature, in alchemy it often symbolized the potent, transformative power of the Stone itself.</note>, and bees which make honey and wax. Among **liquids**, there are human blood, the hair of young men, urine, animal milk, and other viscous moistures. 

And among **minerals**, there are the **sun and moon** (gold and silver), because they are the "ferments" of stones. From these, the aforementioned genus emerged most closely, as it adheres better to the proper substances and natures of metals—namely, to gold and silver. From these you must create the "fermentation" of the stone through a natural conjunction; afterwards, it will have the power of **ingression** <term>ingressionem: the ability of the alchemical medicine to "enter" and permeate a base metal to transform it.</term> into every other metal by means of the ferment, which draws the metal into a nature close to the true medicine. This medicine participates in the essence of perfect bodies and the essential corruption of the perfected. 

Through this, it has been revealed to you that the more something gradually approaches nature, the better it participates in nature; and the more it participates, the more quickly it joins itself to it out of a "love of nature" and is converted into it. For wise nature rejoices and delights more quickly with its own kind than with something foreign. Thus it appears that, through the mediums of nature, you are able to pass smoothly to the extremes and draw our stone from **potentiality into act**.

*On the determination and the end of the stone in its various forms. And how it exists among stones, salts, and glass, all of which have departed from their own nature. And how it ought to be born.*

### CHAPTER XLI.

In this noble nature is determined and finished that "genus" (mentioned to you above) which we have drawn from stones, plants, and animals in the form of a clear water impregnated by the spirit of the **quintessence** <term>quinta essentia: the "fifth essence" or purest spiritual core of a substance, beyond the four elements of earth, air, fire, and water.</term>. Afterward, we congeal this water with the vapor of its own **sulphur** <term>sulphuris: in alchemy, Sulphur represents the active, combustible, and "masculine" principle of transformation, not just the chemical element.</term>, and then the stone appears, which was previously hidden from us within its liquid uniformity. My son, our sulphur is created among stones, and it grows among salts and among glass from the first substance—from the first thing, which is called the substance of **quicksilver** <term>ar. vivi (argentum vivum): literally "living silver" or mercury, representing the passive, fluid, and "feminine" principle.</term>. 

My son, from this substance of quicksilver we perform our entire work because it is incorruptible. We do not work with common salt that hardens into rock, nor with glass, nor the substance of any other common stone. Rather, we create our stone *among* them, because we believe these things to be the "vessels of nature" which the aforementioned genus has chosen. Therefore, when our stone is created, let it be born from its mother's womb. Do not add anything else to it from this point on, because it carries with it the power of its mother's womb—namely, that sulfurous nature which congeals all quicksilver. That is the "earth" in which we sow our **gold** <note>original: *aurum*; in this context, "gold" often refers to the perfected metallic seed or the Sun principle.</note>, because it has the power to retain it. You must hold such an intention when extracting the stone from the natural principles of both stones and plants; for glorious God placed many powers in stones and plants which, if they were well understood, would perform many wonders upon the earth—wonders that simple folk would undoubtedly judge to be miracles.

*On the great conjunction. And on the method of the male and the female. And on the eclipse of the sun and the moon. And on the second birth of our quicksilver, for the purpose of making the complete elixir.*

### CHAPTER XLII.

Now the place is revealed to you from which our **quicksilver** <note>original: *argentū vivū*</note> can emerge, which effects the conjunction of the female and the male. Do not believe that this occurs in the place of the female or the male alone in the "Great Work" <note>original: *magno magisterio*; the Great Work or *Magnum Opus* is the process of creating the Philosopher's Stone.</note>. Rather, it is like a mediator between the **sun** <note>Gold</note> and the **moon** <note>Silver</note>. Without this quicksilver, they would not be joined well in the perfection of the "Greater Stone." Because of this, when you subtly dissolve the sun with our quicksilver, you will see the **blood of man** <note>original: *sanguinem hominis*; a symbolic term for a deep red stage in the alchemical process, indicating life and vitality in the matter.</note>, which requires a suitable restraint—that is, a fitting **female** <note>original: *femellā*; likely referring to the receptive, cooling substance needed to stabilize the "blood" or red tincture.</note>.

*How generation cannot come from qualities that are too remote. And concerning the difference between the male and the female. And concerning philosophical heat.*

...of the generative [principle] should hold the formative virtue captured within itself—namely, a controlled and artificial heat governed by the Artist in relation to celestial power. This formative virtue (this stimulating artificial heat) should be held by its great temperament, which is created by coldness balancing and tempering the stimulating heat, and forcing the heat to remain in the deep composition of the compound. 

**Note** <note>original: "Nota"</note> that the **fire of the philosophers** consists of four things: namely, the unnatural fire applied to the proper subject of **quicksilver** <term>argentum vivum: literally "living silver," the fluid metallic principle</term> as the philosopher commands when he says that fire should be placed in bodies; the simple natural heat of that subject; the **informative virtue** <term>virtus informativa: the internal power that gives specific form to matter</term>; and the proportion of these three. For if one exceeds another, it overtakes it and diminishes its action. This is apparent through "digestible heat"—namely, so that the strength of the power can operate; if not, it should operate under the power of the informative virtue and its influence. 

And [ensure] that the subject of said power should not be excessive, neither in quantity nor heat, and this is achieved through **solution** <note>the process of dissolving a solid into a liquid state</note>. Hence, note concerning the temperament of fires in the likeness of the quantity of substance: that the power should not exceed the said virtue in such action, that the matter should not be diminished, and that it should not be in a contrary, repugnant quality. You must know this: that one of the elements must be placed into the other. And as great as the proportion of such power will be in its action, so much more will the active product have a greater operative virtue in its natural operations according to the course of nature. 

And because, my son, it will perhaps seem impossible for you to know how to perform the **Masterpiece** <term>magisterium: the "Great Work" or the process of creating the Philosopher's Stone</term>, we will declare it more clearly to you in the second part. For the sake of this performance, I have told you that you shall add the **Sun and Moon** <note>Gold and Silver</note> until they suffer an **eclipse** and are in the **Head and Tail of the Dragon** <note>In alchemy, this refers to the "conjunction" or union of the two principles, modeled on the points where the moon's orbit crosses the ecliptic</note>. Then, son, you have made a **unity out of plurality**, from which nature will make a new generation, since that unity contains within itself an essential plurality—not an **accidental** one <note>In medieval philosophy, an "accident" is a surface property like color, whereas "essence" is the core substance</note>, which comes from common Mercury, which is full of accidents. 

And therefore, the error of those who deceive men with their accidental **tinctures** <note>chemical washes or surface-level colorings that do not change the internal nature of the metal</note> arises; they believe that their product is our essential and substantial quicksilver. In truth, the essential has a hundred times more virtue than the accidental, because essential and substantial operations are nobler than accidental ones, and better for our Masterpiece. In that case, Art declines from the likeness of nature, because the matters of nature, compared to the matters of Art, are nothing but "accidents," philosophically or moderately speaking. Therefore, it is necessary for nature to form its creatures more subtly...

...all; and since the Art <note>The "Art" refers to alchemy, the human imitation of natural processes</note> cannot work with such extreme subtlety on its own, it must be supported and assisted according to its own capacity. This is why we do not provide it with matter that is already too refined; rather, we provide a "plurality" of essential and substantial matter through all its accidental properties. The more "essential" nature becomes through this unification of diverse parts, the greater and more significant its power becomes in both its active and passive essence. This power cannot operate or find a physical base to sustain itself without such action and passion. Therefore, such a plurality is naturally desired in our mastery.

->*How from the unity of our quicksilver, which is made from plurality, there emerges the simple assimilating power of the Stone.*<-

### CHAPTER XLV.

From this unity (my son) achieved within plurality, there emerges a certain noble power and a single, secret natural principle. Through its simplicity, this principle transmits itself outward from the first real entities toward the goal, so that its secrets may be manifested within them. Thus, through secondary simple things, the primary special powers are revealed, joined into one. We call this joined state <term>chaos</term> <note>the raw, unformed matter of the work</note>, nature, the origin, the <term>green lion</term> <note>original: "leo virdis"; a term for a potent, often acidic, mineral solvent or the raw state of the matter</note>, **quicksilver** <term>argentum vivum: the fluid, metallic principle of transformation</term>, ointment, oil, pasture, and a liquid of great value. This is because many virtues are united into one through the power of nature, governed by the art of our mastery. 

From this, secondary operations emerge that lead toward generation. For the goal of these real entities is found in the goal of the first simple elements; so it is in the whole course of nature, wherein one real thing possesses more or better virtue than another by virtue of its noble substance and dignity. The greater its virtue, the more powerful its operation. Therefore, in these alchemical operations <note>original: "sophisticis operationibus"; here meaning artificial laboratory operations</note>, the nobilities of these secrets can be revealed to any seeker of this science and searcher of nature’s secrets, provided they know how to observe them. Through this knowledge, one can arrive at our great secret, as long as they first understand the material substances from which real entities move from potential into actual existence.
