# RAYMUNDUS LULLUS

...afterwards the moon; and so, according to how the virtue is greater in one genus than in another, so its operation is more powerful in that one than in the other. And therefore, do not work except with the two aforementioned luminaries <note>The "luminaries" are the Sun and Moon, which in alchemical terms represent Gold and Silver.</note> and in their mediator, which is our **Mercury**, because their operation is nobler and of greater virtue in its own species than in any other. And when you see that the plurality of two is converted into unity, or the whole into a single genus through the power of the active principle and the simplicity of our said matter, then all things everywhere participate in the goals of the species; and in this principle of genus, and in this unity, the goals of the first individuals will begin, which nature will possess.

And therefore it is necessary that the corruption <note>In alchemy, "corruption" is the breakdown of a substance's old form so it can be reborn into a new, more perfect form.</note> of these things be initiated and started toward the dissolution of their own new genus, in which their prime matter or nature is preserved. Wherefore it is clearly manifest that without simplicity there would be no power or dominion in the course of nature; and without the *power to be* <note>original: "posse"</note> there would be no species; and without species, individual things would not exist, because it is necessary that they have existence under a single proper species.

And thus it is revealed to you, my son, that with intense simplicity all real beings and their natures move themselves—and even "imaginary" <note>original: "phantastica"; in this context, it refers to things that exist as concepts or forms before they are physically manifest</note> ones—and the greater their motion is, the better you can know that the natural virtue is of greater power, and consequently its operations. Therefore, in the greatness and virtue of motion, the greatness and virtue of its operation is multiplied. 

However, you will have knowledge of the greater virtue through the knowledge of more extensive motion, if you know how to recognize its greater goal; for motion comes from <term>potentiality</term> <note>original: "potentia"; the capacity of a thing to become something else</note>, and potentiality from simplicity—understand this both physically and naturally. And simplicity comes from subtlety, and subtlety comes from **solution** <note>the process of dissolving a solid into a liquid state</note>, which is the end of the corruption of old or ancient individuals. 

Therefore we say that through solution our **Stone** is drawn from potentiality into <term>actuality</term> <note>original: "actum"; the fully realized state of a substance</note>, since from that solution descend concrete real beings, which are the instruments of all natures—imaginary and real—through the "confusion" <note>In this sense, "confusion" refers to the thorough blending or fusion of substances into a single mass.</note> of a most noble mixture. From there come all noble agents, in which there are greater motions, and noble "patients" <note>original: "patientibus"; the passive substances that receive the action of the "agents"</note> in which their own agents are always moved. And when motions have greater virtues regarding agents—from which they receive their birth and origin immediately—than they have in patients, to that extent their operation is of greater virtue in active things than in passive things. 

And therefore the **sun** is of greater virtue, and has a greater instinct for generation and for more quickly creating its likeness—by reason of its motion—than the moon or any other planet in the whole course of nature; just as man has a greater appetite than woman, and the soul is better than the body. If therefore, my son, you know how to appropriate <note>The text ends mid-word: "appro-priare".</note> such a male...

### *When the Artist ought to consider the powers of the two quicksilvers after their conjunctions, and the differences of their effect in respect to their own effects.*

## CHAPTER 46.

Afterwards, my son, you must not be ignorant of the power of these two **quicksilvers** <note>original: "argentorum vivorum"; in alchemy, these represent the two essential aspects of Mercury—the "philosophical" and the "common," or the active and passive principles.</note>, namely when they are joined together through dissolution, since one is active and the other is passive. From these two, through a differential harmony arising from their united powers and virtues, come four principal natures, which are called in another way the four virtues of the governing nature. The first is named **attractive** or **appetitive**. The second, **retentive** and **coagulative** nature. The third, **expulsive** nature. The fourth, which is containing, is **digestive**. The attractive nature is produced by the mastery of heat through tempered dryness. The retentive is produced through the dominion of dryness. The expulsive is produced from the dominion of moisture and constrictive coldness. And the digestive nature is produced through <term>putrefaction</term> <note>The stage where matter breaks down, turns black, and "dies" before being reborn.</note>, which is produced by the domination of heat through a moderate and tempered moisture. 

The attractive nature is moved by the hot male, and the retentive by the suffering earth. The expulsive is moved by the humors of the parents, which mix themselves in the said genus, which we name <term>quicksilver</term> <note>original: "arg. vivum"</note>, which indeed descends more closely from the most general genus. And the digestive is moved by the quality of the fire of a tempered body with their humor, through <term>decoction</term> <note>A process of heating or "cooking" the substance to refine it.</note>, mixing all things together at once. Wherefore we call and say that every better part of the whole composite, once digested and separated, is the ointment, the soul, our gold, and the oil. It is an ointment because it colors and tints and melts, and makes all quicksilver flow by reason of its perfection, which it acquired through the said digestion; because in it, the cold is converted into hot, the dry into moist, and the heavy into light—each through its own means, and each through its own mover. 

Son, if you do not know the differences that exist between hot and cold, male and female, you will never know how to perform our work. Know that nothing can be born except from a female and a male, nor can any germ be generated except from heat and moisture. The appetitive strengths are masculine, hot, and dry, and belong to the coagulating fire. The retentive strengths are also masculine, cold, and dry, and are the earth. And the cleansing or digestive strengths—namely, the altering ones—are feminine, hot, and moist, and are the air. The expulsive strengths are similarly feminine...

<meta>This page continues the technical description of the four (and eventually five) alchemical powers or "fortitudes" that govern the creation of the Philosopher’s Stone. It picks up from the previous page’s discussion of the "quicksilvers" and the expulsive nature.</meta>

...of the cold and moist female, and these are water. And the **fifth strength** of life belongs to our "infant" <note>The "infant" is a common alchemical metaphor for the Philosopher's Stone or the perfected Elixir, as it is "born" from the union of various elements.</note>, which no longer possesses any single quality—such as coldness, moisture, dryness, or heat—because it is no longer merely hot, dry, cold, nor moist, and is neither female nor male. My son, our infant has two fathers and as many mothers; therefore, he is delicately nourished by their entire substance; he reigns and shall reign in the world, and he shall never die. 

My son, the **appetitive strengths** are hot and dry, and they are those which attract, dye, and color; they form colors without separation or alteration, and these proceed from the fire, which is their father. 

The **retentive strengths**, being cold and dry, are those which join the colors to the bodies and soften them, binding the aforementioned tinctures with a strong bond without any separation. 

The **digestive** and **cleansing strengths** are those which clean and wash away the impurities of the bodies; they extract from them the "first nature" and establish and ordain it as something burning, ignited, and illuminated, because they are hot and moist. 

The **expulsive strengths**, being cold and moist, are those which expel the vices <note>In this context, "vices" refers to chemical impurities or "accidental" qualities that hinder perfection.</note> of the world; when the work is performed, they transmute the bodies among themselves simultaneously, until they have passed into their crude nature; and afterward, when each of the elements has been turned into one, they shall never be separated or divided. And just as each of them was reduced entirely into a body, so also it is turned into a body; thus they compose themselves through art, and their natures are added and joined into one. 

But the **fifth virtue** is that which does everything, and leads and conducts all things to the end of their composition; it is the spirit of the <term>quintessence</term> <note>The "fifth essence," a celestial, incorruptible substance that Lull believed could be extracted from terrestrial matter to prolong life and transmute metals.</note> through the nature of its influence into the substances of the compounds, to the end that its virtue may be reflected and fixed in those very bodies through the art.

From this conjunction, the principle of the generation of the **stone** <note>The "stone" refers to the Philosopher’s Stone, the goal of the alchemical work.</note> is made clear. Thus, my son, you must work so that through the science and measure of the art, you add the natures until the bodies are turned into spirit by the accidental strengths introduced in the course of our philosophy through the art of mastery. Therefore, add two natures until you have drawn out the entire pure, shining, and clear nature; for from those two, one clear thing must be born, which must illuminate its entire kind. 

Yet guard the bodies in their liquefactions <note>The process of turning a solid into a liquid state.</note> when you are at work; do not exceed the measure that the signs of nature will show you in every decoction <note>The process of heating or boiling the substance.</note>, because nature is changed into nature until the bodies remain permanent in it for liquefaction and fusion. This is due to the permanence of the fixed materials, which are our well-tempered and moist secrets, into which the bodies are turned through the art of mastery. These are the ointments, oils, ferments, souls, and suns, which do not cease to shine upon our earth and to radiate. 

Therefore, you must labor in the thinning and refinement of nature to form the "body of philosophy" until it becomes clear water. This water is called the **water of wisdom**, for it is entirely gold and silver, brought into the action of spiritual elements, in which the spirit of the **fifth essence** <note>The *Quintessence*, a pure, incorruptible element above the four earthly elements (earth, air, fire, water).</note> rests and rejoices, which performs the whole work.

### *How the Artist and practitioner must guard the nature of the spirit of the quintessence as the form of forms. And how he should understand it. And concerning the measure of fire.*

## CHAPTER XLVIII.

Therefore, my son, it is necessary for you to guard the nature of the spirit of the **quintessence** <term>quintessence: From the Latin "quinta essentia" (fifth essence). In alchemy, this is the purest, most refined substance extracted from matter, believed to be the life force that binds all things.</term>, if you wish to achieve anything. This spirit depends indeed upon the **First Cause** <note>The "First Cause" refers to God or the primordial creative power of the universe.</note>, acting as the "form of forms." It has placed itself within the four "more honorable" natures <note>The four elements: Earth, Air, Fire, and Water.</note> and is named the **soul of the elements** <note>original: "anima elementorum"</note>, the clear light, and the spirit of the quintessence. And because every substantial thing that is formed descends immediately from this proximate fifth cause, we call her the "mother of mothers" of all other forms. 

My son, you must not think that this form and spirit is either hot, cold, dry, or moist, nor male or female. Instead, understand that the cause of its great perfection reaches into each of those four natures. For without this spirit, there would be no **constitution** <note>original: "complexio." In medieval science, this refers to the specific balance of qualities that makes up an individual thing.</note> in any composed thing, as we clearly recognize and see through certain experience in the binding and constitution of the four elements. These elements, by their contrary qualities, naturally resist one another; because of this resistance, the opposing elements could never agree to come together as one unless there were that most noble medium, which flows through all elements in a mingled way and participates in the quality of their natures. 

Therefore, my son, if you wish to know this, it is that which establishes peace between enemies. It is necessary to pay attention to this: for example, air and water stand between two enemies. Air stands between the hot and the cold <note>Air was traditionally seen as hot and moist, bridging the gap between hot Fire and cold Water.</note>, and water similarly stands between the moist and the dry—namely, between air and earth. Therefore, when we wish for the "dry" to be converted into the "moist," we take the instrument which is in the water. This water participates through its moisture in the **radical moisture** <term>radical moisture: The innate, life-sustaining fluid believed to be present in all living things; the alchemical "fuel" of life.</term>—that is, the vapor of aerial moisture that differs from its own aquatic **phlegm** <note>original: "phlegmate aquatico." Here used to describe the watery, thick residue or substance of the element.</note> in which the fifth spirit is carried. Without this vapor—which is the **matter of our seed** <note>original: "materia nostri germinis"</note> carried in its phlegm, descending from the most general of types—nothing could be congealed. 

Therefore, it has been told to you that you should know well how to arrange the "airy substance" of our stone, and the "earthly substance" of the same stone (which is its mother), until they are well-joined without any separation. My son, the airy substance is the matter of our seed, which in another way is named **permanent water** <term>permanent water: "aqua permanens," a central alchemical concept referring to a universal solvent or a stable liquid state of a substance that does not evaporate when heated.</term>. Its moisture is very hot because it is clothed in the property of the nature of fire; and therefore, it is necessary that you know how to arrange it...

...tution and to know it, you must gather it upon that earth. For there lies the whole power, and all the virtues of our Stone lie there. For if the substance of the seed were congealed and turned within the womb of its mother—which is the vessel of nature—once the airiness has expired (which participates in its essence through the power of evocative heat), the seed would remain without a soul; it would no longer have a pulse, nor the motion of any breath. And thus, in the manner of the earth, it would be mortified <note>mortified: In alchemy, "mortification" refers to the symbolic death or breakdown of a substance, often turning it black or making it inert, before it can be "resurrected" or refined.</note> into a colored white substance, which would lack the vivifying spirit—namely, air—in which every thing is brought to life and inspired.

Wherefore our earth, without that spirit, would not bear any fruit, for it is that spirit which perfects it. You should desire, therefore, my son, to congeal the volatile airiness in its own earth, by the loving nourishment of an appropriate fire, just like an infant held in the arms of its mother. That is to say, the said fire must be proportioned in such a degree that it does not overcome the power of the hot and moist spirit. For the hot nature of the spirit itself would be quickly dissolved by the flame of an improper fire, just as the power of a large flame annihilates the power of a small one. In this case, you must imitate nature; specifically, do not take more from elemental fire <note>elemental fire: Ordinary physical fire, as opposed to the "natural" or "secret" fire of the alchemist.</note> in the generation of the things of nature than you require for the proportioned excitation of the "fire of nature," which moves through the entirety of the matter. From such a likeness of nature, in which the generative power resides, she is your directress and mistress. Therefore, know how to understand her. For she, provided with great wisdom and with great care in her natural work, does not take from elemental fire except as much as she needs for the formation of her matter. 

Thus, my son, you must do: namely, fix the said moist spirit into its earth, and gently dry it through the heat which we call **escatesim** <term>escatesim: A term used in Lullian alchemy to describe a specific, gentle, and digestive degree of heat that mimics the natural warmth of the womb or an egg being hatched.</term>. For this heat undergoes the "feeling of nature" <note>original: "patitur sensum naturae"</note>, because it is sufficient for it that the dryness of the earth be sustained by the dryness of a very weak and thin fire. And when, through all this, its nature is excited within it by the subtle heat of the said fire—without any violation of that virtue—the hot spirit penetrates and enters into the deepest parts of the honorable matter, just as the soul enters the body of a man to give life. 

My son, this is the truest aerial substance, which you must compel through natural ingenuity and fix it in the body, lest it remain mortified. After this, you should cast off its **phlegm** <note>phlegm: In this context, the watery, tasteless, and useless residue or "superfluity" left over after the spirit has been fixed.</note> along with all superfluities, and then you will have the earthy substance well-disposed through moisture and heat, without the separation of one from the other. The whole is then converted to the nature of air. This bond was created through the said water, which is the medium between the dry and the moist, and the **inceration** <term>inceration: From the Latin "cera" (wax); a process of softening a dry substance until it reaches a waxy, meltable consistency.</term> of nature.

# THE WRITINGS OF RAYMUND LULL

<margin>¶ 3</margin>
...is called **subtle** <note>original: "subtili-", completing the catchword from the previous page</note>, or natural, because nature performs it through the generation and vivification of things that have been mortified <note>mortified: In alchemy, this refers to the symbolic "death" or chemical breakdown of a substance, often through darkening or rot, which must occur before it can be "resurrected" into a higher form.</note>, when through sublimation it joins the dry with the moist, and vice versa. For this mixture belongs to nature, because it occurs with fire, and not without it. Therefore, it is necessary that sulfur be composed of a very refined terrestrial part and a strongly digested and subtle aerial heat, as if in the vessel of nature; in which the said moisture and the said terrestrial matter are mixed together subtly, and by the **smallest parts** <note>per minima: An Aristotelian concept meaning mixing at the most fundamental, microscopic level so that the ingredients are no longer distinct.</note> and insensible pieces. This is done so that a minimum of dry earth and a minimum of moisture—to the quantity of a single grain of one and a similar quantity of the other—are gathered together in such a way that neither one nor the other can be separated from the parts of its own kind, as is clearly seen through their sublimation. In this, a certain and approved experience shows that the whole either flies and ascends, or the whole remains below. And thus it is found through art that none of the parts are separated from one another after nature has bound them together with greater and lesser [degrees], and with great and miraculous care. My son, all this occurs in the first creation of our Stone, and it is a mixture of different things, or rather a union of different **living silvers** <note>vivorum argentorum: Literally "living silvers," referring to different types or states of Mercury (Quicksilver) used in the Work.</note> which can be bound together in the essential unity of the spirit of the quintessence through alteration, so that they will never afterwards be separated from their own likenesses. This will be seen later through the experience of sublimation, which is able to unite things of the same kind. Furthermore, you must not be ignorant of the fact that it is necessary for our medicine to be composed, and that it must be composed, of one nature and one genus.

...subtlety, which you must understand from nature; for through its wisdom, nature takes great care in holding and carrying matter toward its perfection. Therefore, if you desire at all times to find the work through nature, always allow nature to arrange its matter with total science in the fire, according to what nature requires and demands for its arrangement. For then nature will perform its own duty, because it—and not you—forms, places, and changes the matter, provided it finds that the matter has been established and prepared through art in respect to the natural principles appropriate to it. Then nature, through its care and intelligence in the matter that obeys it, perfects the whole material. And just as you have nothing to do except provide for nature, so no form except the **soul** <note>original: "anima". In alchemy, the "soul" refers to the animating principle or the volatile spirit of a substance.</note> is what moves matter according to its own proper act, and without motion a thing cannot be generated. And therefore the entire effect proceeds from the soul. 

Not that you should understand this to be in the way a philosophical organic body is made, or that it has the power of life as found in animals, but rather as a worker is active in his craft. And therefore this soul is not a sixth virtue, but is the **fifth virtue** <term>virtus quinta: also known as the Quintessence, the purest and most essential part of a substance, distinct from the four physical elements</term> of the four elements, which results from them and is of the purer essence of the four elements. And therefore it rests in the sphere of fire, and lives there through continuous motion; and the cause of its motion is its natural heat, excited by simple elemental fire, as if in the same degree. Guard it, therefore, lest it escape due to excessive heat, and hold it in love.

They are joined by such a league that they are never separated from it until the end of the term of their mixing—either by themselves or by an accident—until, through the corruptive separation of the said virtue, it comes to the end of its mixing, and becomes totally separated, dissolved, and unbound from the whole composite. And then the elements have no power to hold themselves together, but they remain separated and unbound elementally from one another when their bond—that is, the aforementioned **fifth virtue**—is separated and dissolved from them, like a confused and desolate thing which [loses] its governance...

<margin>Chapter 51</margin>Before you perform the union of the spiritual elements, my son, it is necessary to know that by the intention of fixing them, you wish to unite them to the end that this unity may be fixed until it can resist the war of fire. ### CHAPTER LIII.

It is certain, my son, that a certain power is flowed into all bodies composed of elements, because without it they could not exist; but in homogeneous, finished things, the said power remains in perpetual **minerality** <term>Minerality: the essential, enduring nature of mineral substances</term>, and it is that which must endure all heat, by reason of its perfect **decoction** <term>Decoction: the process of refining or "cooking" a substance through heat to reach maturity</term> in the form of liquid humidity. These four raw elements are impregnated with a similar power, but are more raw through the matter of their vessels and by reason of the power of their raw nature; you ought to attract the nature that is more cooked, hot, moist, and subtly airy, which by the ingenuity of nature is congealed into the species and nature of metal, flowed into its own mineral. ...receive it with all its substantial parts, because this is the true species and pure nature of true clarity; and you should wish to strengthen it by new means, or increase its powers through the administration of **celestial influence** <term>Celestial influence: the medieval belief that the movement and "rays" of stars and planets directly shaped the growth and qualities of minerals and life on Earth</term>. As we have said, the power of the male, tempered in heat and moisture, tempers and strengthens the passive power [of the female] to retain the **germinous virtue** <term>Germinous virtue: the reproductive or "seeding" power within a substance that allows it to grow or multiply</term>. Therefore, my son, note these three virtues. For the first descends from the **First Mover** <term>First Mover: the "Primum Mobile," the outermost sphere of the heavens that sets all other things in motion</term>, or from the motion of the stars and their figures. And this, in our testament, we name the **First Form of Forms** <note>original: "primam formam formarum"</note>. This is the primary form through which inferior matters are transmuted from form to form only through the course and institution of nature. And from this form, nature has enough to shape and bring her first compounds into **act** <term>Act: the state of being fully realized or functional, as opposed to "potential"</term> from the power of the matters of the elements. And this form cannot be obedient to Art <note>Here, "Art" refers to the work of the human alchemist</note>.

The second virtue is the virtue infused into composed elemental matters, which it is necessary for you to draw from those matters in which it resides. This is done by way of converting its genus to its first nature, or approaching as much as is possible to its first thing; and this is sufficient for Art, because it is material. And at this point, Art cannot be compared to nature, because it cannot give **substantial form** <term>Substantial form: the core essence that makes a substance what it is (e.g., what makes gold specifically gold)</term> to things, as nature does through the ingenuity of its noble and intentional operation. And therefore it is necessary for Art to return to nature to obtain those substantial forms which nature has already created, in order to form one body with such power that the "male" may never leave it. This is to teach you how you might draw that body from its created compounds, and to show you its creation—how it converts matter from potential into the act of generation. 

Therefore, my son, the subtle artist must look closely at how nature operates, so that through Art he may be able to resemble her, and follow her as much as is possible. And that which is not possible [for nature], he should know how to supply through intellectual ingenuity in respect to nature, if he desires our thing.

And therefore you can know that sharp things, among other flavors caused by heat, are hotter than others, because the others can make no such impression as that which proceeds from an excellent heat. The animal nature, which is in our **menstruum** <term>Menstruum: A powerful alchemical solvent, named after the "menstrual" cycle because it was thought to provide the "blood" or nourishment for the growing Stone</term>, is such that it mortifies and darkens everything; it casts a shadow over and blackens all our airy things, and corrupts every animated thing; it dries up green and natural moist things which are generated or in the process of generation; it sours things that are sweet and dissolved, and it makes raw again <note>original: "reincrudat," meaning to return a substance to its "crude" or unripe state</note> things that are cooked and finished; and it makes the hot cold, the dry wet, the hard soft, the heavy light, and the coarse thin. And it does all these things from its own first nature through certain operations. 

Likewise, it has other better powers, because it gives life to everything dead. It whitens everything black, generates every animated thing, and moistens dry things; it preserves these things from burning, sweetens wild things, and softens moist and cold things. It softens dry, bitter, and hot things, and brings them into a tempered **complexion** <term>Complexion: The specific balance of the four primary qualities (hot, cold, moist, dry) that determines the nature of a substance</term>, and leads what was raw into a greater **decoction** <term>Decoction: A process of heating or "cooking" a substance to refine and concentrate its virtues</term>. It makes the cold hot, the dry a tempered moist, and the light heavy with moderation; from the thin it makes the coarse, which participates with the simple; it condenses the simple, thins the thick, and thus it has contrary operations which are the operations of nature. 

For when it is frozen, it freezes; when it is dissolved, it dissolves what is frozen. It is no wonder then, my son, if such a menstrual power be placed in your heart and diligently sought after, since it is the generator and governor of all nature. And this is a vile thing, which by itself is turned into a most noble, wonderful, and precious thing—a thing we would not have believed unless we had seen its effect. Note that this power receives animation and its end from its own element. And regarding this, you may see the chapter in our practice, when we shall speak of the body and the spirit, while giving an example of the generation...

# RAYMUND LULLY
<meta>catchword: Concerning</meta>

In its own mineral vessel, there is generated and created—specifically, in the bowels of its earth, or in mineral veins—a certain smoky substance, very subtle, which is joined together as a vapor, and there it is cooked and highly purified. Afterward, a sulfurous mineral virtue comes upon it in the form of a dry vapor, which penetrates it and congeals it with such a **bond of love** <note>original: "amoris ligamine"; a common alchemical term for chemical affinity or the strong attraction between substances</note> that they shall never be separated. 

While the virtue of the male <note>the sulfurous principle</note> overcomes the virtue of the female <note>the mercurial principle</note> through the **coequality of the fifth thing** <term>Rei quintæ: Likely referring to the Quintessence or a balanced state of the four elements</term>, they then remain as one fixed thing through the art [of nature] by the tempering of natural **decoction** <term>Decoction: A process of heating or "cooking" a substance in a fluid to extract its essence or mature it</term> which the matter possessed in its mineral form. Thus, the Mercurial moisture shall never be separated from the sulfurous dryness, nor the sulfurous dryness from the Mercurial moisture at any time, because they are united through action and passion into that material medium in which the form of the metal is fully established. 

This is not to say that it remains **quicksilver** <note>original: "argentum vivum"</note> in its total nature, since part of its nature is already altered by the compulsion or constriction which its subtle parts received by way of the binding of the sulfurous vapor; nor, by this, is it sulfur in its total nature. For if it were sulfur, it would burn the substance of the quicksilver through the excellence of its dominating action. And therefore, because the virtue of sulfur does not dominate over the virtue of quicksilver, nor can it consume its specific metallic clarity, but only congeals and fixes it to the degree of its own virtuous power, it preserves the species of the metal which the quicksilver holds materially according to its nature. 

Such a proportion of sulfur and quicksilver specifically constitutes the form and species of that metal, from which the vapor of sulfur and quicksilver will become the body of gold, or silver, or another metal. All of this results from the diverse purification of the said vapor by the digestion or decoction it received in its own proper mine. 

And for this reason, the good Artist takes metals as intermediaries in the work of the **mastery** <note>The "Magisterium" or the process of creating the Philosopher's Stone</note>, and especially the **Sun and Moon** <note>original: "solem & lunam"; Gold and Silver</note>. This is because these two have reached a tempered coequality and are highly purified of the substance of sulfur and quicksilver, being cooked, pure, and well-digested by the ingenuity of nature.

### CHAPTER LVII.

Son, this is the metallic matter in which our proportioned **sulfur** <term>Sulphur proportionatum: A balanced or "proportioned" state of the sulfurous principle, refined by nature for the alchemist's use</term> is found, which wise nature has prepared for us, as we have said. By its mediation, we perform our entire secret **magistery** <term>Magisterium: The "mastery" or the completed alchemical process of the Great Work</term>. Therefore, do not be ignorant of the fact that what is called the "second extremity" in the work of nature, we call the "middle" in our philosophical work. For it is necessary that what nature has left behind be supplied by art; for nature does not have the power to move through its own motion beyond the generation of metal, because it has completed its circulation. After this, the cause and the perfecting thing should shine clearly for you and assist you, as is manifested by all experience: that the **moisture of metals** cannot be consumed in their **calcinations** <term>Calcination: The process of heating a substance to high temperatures to reduce it to a powder or "calx," usually to remove impurities</term>, nor can it be separated from them, by reason of the homogeneity of the union of their elements, which are bound and joined together little by little. 

But the moisture of stones is separated—as is evident in their calcination—simply by fire without any medicinal application. And this is because the moisture in the coarse, earthly substance of stones is not bound by dryness in the smallest parts of one and the other, but in large and numerous parts of the moist and the dry. The opposite is true in the matter of **glass**, through which the art of glassmaking is made subordinate to this art. This is why the Philosopher says that glass should be your example in our magistery. And this is the cause why the moisture of stones and "middle minerals" are **inks** <note>original: "atramenta"; often referring to vitriol or metallic sulfates used for making ink</note>, **vitriols**, **quicksilver-like substances** <note>original: "azoquea"; related to 'azoc', a term for quicksilver or mercury</note>, **Marcasites**, **Alums**, **Salts**, and **borax**; these do not have their moisture fixed in their nature by material dryness, but it is volatile and fleeing from the fire. However, the moisture of metals is fixed and permanent in the fire. Therefore, with such a water, we **fix the little birds flying in the air** <note>original: "aviculas in aere volantes"; a common alchemical metaphor for volatile spirits or gases that are stabilized or "fixed" into a solid state</note> by the power of our stone, which is created from their own proper substance. 

It appears, therefore, that our **quicksilver** <note>original: "argentum vivum"</note> is the material substance and the **radical moisture** <term>Humiditas radicalis: The "root moisture" or fundamental life-force/fluidity inherent in a substance</term> of all liquefiable bodies. Therefore, make the bodies become the "water of liquefaction" by making and pouring them into quicksilver. For since it is the principal element of the said liquefiable things, when they are liquefied, they are resolved into it. And sulfur is the father. And so it is called the "middle" in the work of nature, but quicksilver and metals are called its "extremities," because they are the matter of the beginning and the matter of the end. And therefore it can appear to you, since we are held—

...of quicksilver <term>original: arg. vi., argentum vivum; mercury</term> there are two proper metals, and their nature has the capacity to be converted into the **stone of virtue** through the art of alchemy. This is due to the density, hardness, and compactness of the mercurial moisture, which has been fixed and thickened by the vapor of its own sulfur and natural heat into the form of a metal—just as the sun <note>gold</note> and moon <note>silver</note> were created from the subtle substance of their own specific intermediates by the power of its first circular work.

Therefore, in this case, we supplement the weaknesses of nature; specifically, by making hard bodies soft, and coarse bodies fine through the aid of nature, which does not deviate from this path. We liquefy them through processes of putrefaction <note>the breaking down of matter through warmth and moisture</note> until they are returned to the nature of quicksilver <term>mercury</term> by the sublimation of the coarse into the simple, the reduction of the "cooked" into the "raw," and the resolution and dissolution of the dry into the humid. It is necessary to do all these things completely until the end, so that the simple matter may better and more fully obey the digestive power of nature.

For it is now clearly manifest to every wise man—as was shown at the beginning regarding natural things—that a substance of subtle essence, which is similar to its whole (like a simple homogeneous body), is more quickly changed and generated by the power of its nature than another substance that is hard, coarse, and thick. Therefore, we dissolve gold and silver in radical substances of their own kind: namely, in the liquor and through the liquor of their own quicksilvers. The first of these is the **stinking menstruum** <term>menstruale foetens: a sharp, fundamental solvent used to break down metals</term>, which enters into the "first matter" of the two aforementioned luminaries <note>gold and silver</note>, as you can understand through natural principles in their own mineral source.

And so we tell you that they are immediately resolved and dissolved into that substance; indeed, before your very eyes, they are resolved into that from which they were originally made and are converted into the **stinking menstruum**. It would have no way of acting or being acted upon except through the harmony and agreement of nature that exists between one and the other.

Also, remember that you should place nothing with the menstruum except that which was born from it at the beginning of its mixing. For if you add a foreign thing, it will immediately be corrupted by that foreign nature, and you will never obtain what you desire. Gold, silver, and mercury are dissolved in our menstruum because it shares a close proximity and kinship with their primary nature. From this, you will extract a "white smoke," which is our **sulfur**; and the **green lion** <term>leo viridis: a term often referring to raw mineral salts or vitriol that acts as a powerful transformative agent</term>, which is our ointment; and the "stinking water," which is our quicksilver. However, the work requires that the **green lion** be dissolved by the stinking water in a formal dissolution, before...

Many say and affirm that **strong waters** <term>original: aquas fortes; typically corrosive acids like nitric acid or aqua regia</term> are the corruption of our Stone, and they do not lie. For someone who does not understand the corruption of a thing will find it difficult to understand its generation, since creation cannot occur without the corruption and transmutation of individual parts. These parts are the real, material beings of our Stone in its proper nature, which certainly must be corrupted by the aforementioned **menstrual solvent** <term>original: menstruale; a solvent likened to the biological cycle, used to break down and "re-fertilize" the metallic body</term> with a pious love, yet without their total destruction; for a pious mother never wishes to kill the son she has nourished. My son, everything you add that is not of its own kind will resist its dissolution. But this substance putrefies because it is of a kind capable of receiving the entire nature with which it is joined. See to it, then, that you do not mix anything else with our water unless it is of its own nature. For the thing that best and most quickly putrefies the **perfect body** <note>the "perfect body" refers to gold</note> is our water, by reason of its bitter sharpness and crude nature. This is what consumes, burns, and corrupts everything that is combustible and corruptible through the annihilation of its own burning and fiery nature. And if an oily, impure, and greasy moisture exists in its compound—which it must corrupt through its own property and operation—it reduces everything to nothing. But that which is pure and clean, and better dissolved, remains whole and is protected from the fire, because it is pure nature itself. This is the proper essential matter of our Stone, by virtue of the aforementioned dissolved water, which can neither be burned nor consumed, but rather its moisture increases when it is in the fire. ### *On the nature of ferments, and of their waters, and of our living silvers, and of their earths. On the mastery, and on the knowledge of strong water, and of the things that ought to be joined to them through the concordance of contrariety.*

## CHAPTER LXII.

After these things, my son, we intend to speak in summary of the nature of ferments, and of their waters, and of our living silvers <term>argentum vivum; "living silver" or mercury, which alchemists believed was the fluid soul of all metals</term>, which are all one, since there is but one single nature, and of our earths. And we say that this whole is but one thing, which is varied into a triad through its operations; and by varying through a single decoction <note>original: decoctionem; the process of boiling or heating a substance in a liquid to extract its essence</note>, it is one thing of a single simple power. 

After this, by passing gradually to its formation through another digestion <note>in alchemy, "digestion" refers to the slow application of gentle heat over a long period</note>, it became another thing, which we call "living silver," the earth, the water, and the ferment-gum, and our second "false-salt" <note>original: falsaturam; likely referring to a corrosive or biting preparation used to "attack" the metal</note>, bitter and harsh, which dissolves the whole body by a composite virtue and a property acquired through the second digestion. And afterward, through another digestion, it possesses a greater power. 

And thus you can understand that in our mastery <note>original: magisterio; the "Great Work" of alchemy</note> there are three proper earths, three waters, and three proper ferments, three proper gums, three proper false-salts, and three proper congealing living silvers, just as you can understand through the operation of the triangular figure <note>Llull is famous for using geometric diagrams to explain the "concordance" or harmony between conflicting elemental qualities</note>, through which are constituted the three principal reductions which are the completion of our entire mastery, as we shall declare in our practice. 

Therefore, son, guard the living silver that is congealed, and in the mines of its earth. For that is our living silver, our gum, our earth, our salt—the bitter thing which is sweetened by the virtue of the third reduction. And it is our ferment, our elixir, and our medicine for all infirmities. This is our water, not the common mercurial water of phlegmatic types, but that which we have said is of a much hotter nature than fire itself. 

On account of this, Hippocrates, Avicenna, Averroes, Galen, and other philosophers called it "the urine of choleric youths" <note>original: urinam juvenum cholericorum; alchemical code for a sharp, acidic, or ammoniacal substance, often aqua fortis or distilled mineral spirit</note>, that is, sharp "strong water" <term>aqua fortis; a powerful solvent, typically nitric acid</term>. And from these things which we have spoken of above, it is drawn, converted, and congealed into the water of the ferment, just as we have said. 

And know, my son, that a choleric thing is nothing but fire, and this, son, is the exposition of our first and last water. Therefore, dissipate the thing first captured by a thing sufficiently apt, and with that which is the lightly extracted thing, thus grind the mass that has been made—namely, with the fire of the water; for the white of urine disposes the members to ruin <note>original: nam album urinæ disponit membra ruinæ; a mnemonic rhyme warning of the corrosive power of the distilled substance</note>. Because no thing in the whole world for the tincture <note>original: tincturam; the "Tincture" is the final state of the Elixir that can transform or "dye" base metals into gold</note>,

Specifically, this is the preparation which nature makes through the **dissolution of the body** and the **congelation of the spirit** <note>The process of turning the solid metal into liquid and the volatile spirit into a stable solid</note>. The craftsman should skillfully provide the matter to this simple nature in the manner that nature requires in its actions. And therefore it is necessary that the stone be divided through the four elements; this division is the "solution" made so that the substance of the stone becomes most pure, until the whole is nothing but pure Mercury, which carries in its nature the property of **fixing** <term>fixandi; making a substance stable and resistant to fire</term> and **melting** <term>fundendi; the ability to flow or permeate other metals</term>. 

Therefore, when you wish the body to be dissolved after its calcination, dissolve it with the "living silver" <note>mercury</note> which came out of it, well-purged and cleansed through a sevenfold distillation. For then the body is very much ready for dissolution, and the living silver is very effective at penetrating it and entering through the sponginess of its body. In that sponginess, the spirit is congealed by the benefit of the dissolution of the "fixed nature" of the body and its mixture with the living silver.

And for this reason, **Aristotle** and **Plato**, and all other Philosophers, left in their writings the teaching that the species of metals cannot be changed from one form into a specific metallic form while maintaining their current metallic state, unless they are first reduced to their **primary nature**—namely, into sulfur and quicksilver. This is what opens the bodies to you through resolution and the joining of natural humidities, which are the true elements. 

Men fail in this by reason of ignorance. They are utterly ignorant of the opening of the pores and the closed passages, and the stimulation of the active and multiplying power. For they believe that what they do not know is impossible; but they lie. The thing is not impossible, since it exists in real action and is achieved through the art and work of a certain practice. If this practice is not understood, it cannot be performed well by you. You might watch and see the work of distillation, redistillation, reversion, and reiteration, but you will never know how to recognize the **mastery** <term>magisterium; the successful completion of the Great Work</term>—even if you saw the work completed before your eyes—unless you understand nature and how it must be transmuted.

And you might believe you are doing well with it, but you would first consume the entire span of your life—even if you had a thousand years to live—and you would be forever distilling before you could bring the **four elements** <term>the classical elements: Earth, Air, Fire, and Water</term> to a good result, unless you first understand the virtues of each one by itself, and afterwards come to know well all their signs in their mutations. 1. First, **solution** <term>solutio; the dissolving of a solid into a liquid state</term>

### THE THEORY
<meta>The catchword "locatum" from the previous page matches the first word of this page.</meta>

[that which is] placed moves to its own proper place, just as it is moved and drawn by some power of that place. Son, the cause of the attraction of nourishment—insofar as it is toward the place to which it is drawn—is nourishment, strength, and the **generative power**; we also name this "natural heat" and the "Philosophical heat" in our secrets. Without this heat, no thing is created, as it is the very power and potential of nature.

Therefore, porosity <note>the state of being porous or having tiny openings</note> requires a natural airiness, which is the container and proper vessel for the aforementioned heat. This airiness is revealed in the color **black**, occurring when the elements are well-mixed and the body is burned and scorched. If the elements have not been well-mixed, you will not see this blackness, which is the outward sign of the heat. This is because blackness proves that the body has not been deprived of, nor driven away by, the **active power**.

The active power is its own heat, both in terms of its elements and its function as an instrument. It is this power that causes blackness when it works upon its own moisture. 

<margin>Moist and dry are strongly mixed with the hot moisture consisting of fire</margin>

And when it works upon its own moisture, it demonstrates that the elements themselves are strongly mixed; this happens when the "water" has well-penetrated the depths of the body and has released and dissolved the heat, which is bound to the **radical moisture** <term>the fundamental, life-sustaining fluid inherent in all matter, thought to be the "oil" that keeps the lamp of life burning</term> in the color black. 

Therefore, when the radical moisture (which is the fuel for the fire) is separated from the body during its **calcination** <term>the process of heating a substance to high temperatures to purify it or reduce it to powder</term>, the natural heat is suffocated and extinguished. This happens because it no longer has a substance to sustain it, and the body then appears in a **red color**. This is a "work without profit," for the natural heat has departed and the body remains without life. <note>In alchemy, while "Red" is usually the final goal, a premature redness caused by over-heating indicates the "death" of the matter rather than its perfection.</note>

Son, the humidity of which we told you is the matter of the spirit, in which the natural heat is kept and housed. In the process of heating, this heat works against its own moisture and generates blackness. Since it is separated from its true balance, it must necessarily act according to its nature as fire. And because it has no other substance to restrain its action through a contrary quality—as the water and earth (in which it was originally bound and tempered) did at first—and because it is hot, it burns intensely. It scorches its own proper substance in which it is held and turns the whole thing **black as coal**. 

Therefore, son, take care that this moisture, in which the natural heat resides, is not entirely driven out of the body by excessive, external fire during your natural and productive calcinations. For if it were, the body could not afterwards draw in or convert the nourishment of the **Stone**, because the primary driver of the work would be gone, and the ability to "multiply" the medicine would perish entirely. ### *On the effect of fire, and how we name it in our mastery.* <note>original: "magisterium" — the systematic practice and goal of the alchemical art</note>

## CHAPTER LXVII.

For the reasons previously mentioned, you can understand and clearly discern if such heat is the cause of all generative things. Since it has been seen that every generative thing contains within itself contrary operations, the said heat—captured in the manner described before as a natural heat and instrument—is not entirely uniform in form and virtue. Rather, it consists of many forms and virtues according to the force and power it receives specifically, and in particular through the determination of the subject in which it resides. Therefore, nothing prevents it from having many wonderful operations and notable forms, each of which is proper and natural to it.

Son, by the power of reason we have drawn out the power of nature, which was occult <note>hidden or secret</note> and concealed, into the manifest. We have sought out reason through the power of the senses and the intellect; for these are the primary ways of knowing substances and natural operations. All of this is directed and known through the instrument of experience. By its power, we show you—as we have seen—that each of these diverse operations occurs in different measures, being either stronger or weaker.

But this diversity is caused by the variety in the mixing of the elements. Of this mixing, there is in general only one type of action, namely: to distill and re-distill, and to dissolve and congeal. Because of this constant repetition, our mastery is considered by the ignorant people of the world to be "child's play" or "women's work" <note>a common alchemical phrase suggesting that while the work is repetitive and simple like household chores, it requires great patience</note>, or a monster lacking both head and tail. But he who feels little, knows little; and they only know that much.

We say further, assuming whether the said mixture is completed or not: the hotter it is with natural heat, the more it will heat and dry the **moisture of Mercury** <note>In alchemy, "Mercury" often represents the fluid, metallic principle of matter</note>. It will imprint its effects more deeply upon the said Mercury until the Mercury itself is converted into its own likeness, by reason of the power overcoming the power of the moisture. ->THEORY.<-

...is <note>The text continues from the previous page's sentence about why natural heat is the cause of generation.</note> that the works of nature are done with contrariety <note>opposition or conflict between qualities</note>, regarding the effective powers <note>original: "virtutum effectualium"</note> that are in the elements; and according to the matter or the nature of that matter, the said powers receive their determination. For the active power, when it is in a vaporous and volatile moisture, quickly penetrates all condensed moisture without the help of external heat. And since the moisture in which the said vaporous power existed is separated, and leaves its power in the detached body, it remains afterward as a vacuum of power without any impression. Therefore, we tell you that moisture is quickly recovered, and then immediately perishes.

But in the dry, the cause is the opposite, and this is due to the contrariety of the moist and the dry. For if the moist is for a certain operation, the operation of the dry is its opposite. The contrariety lies in this: the dry receives an impression with difficulty, and gives it up with difficulty. Likewise, the moist performs its action without accidental fire, but the dry does not. And therefore, since the dry requires fire to complete its impression, we refine <note>original: "subtiliamus" — to make thin or pure</note> that dry matter as much as we can, and mix it with the moist until it is truly tempered <note>balanced</note> and moderately refined, so that with the help of a little heat it may make a noble impression deep within its body.

Always, however, it is necessary for this work to have the heat of common fire which excites it, and the common heat of working nature, of which we have said enough that you can understand us. It is necessary for you, my son, to plant this heat and place it in the most refined earth, so that the coarse earthly part cannot hinder its impression. Take an example of this in the refinement of the moist. Son, the said heat is like the principal effective cause of everything you seek, because it brings that which is only potential into manifest action, with manifest experience, by reason of the bond joined by heat and the instinct of nature.

For fire, insofar as it is fire, can never do this. Indeed, the matter would sooner be turned to ash by it, because it would not work like an organic instrument <note>a tool that functions like a living organ</note>, as does the innate heat in the compound—which is flowed into it by the sun and the stars, and not by common fire, as many believe through their great ignorance. For when we say that the Stone is generated by fire, they see no other fire, nor do they believe in any other fire bodily, except common fire; nor any other sulfur nor any other mercury <term>argentum vivum|literally "living silver," the base liquid metal used in alchemy</term>, unless it be the common kind. ...indeed they have become sons of Hermes <note>Followers of the legendary founder of alchemy, Hermes Trismegistus</note>, and we likewise; just as has been declared in many words and places in our volumes, and especially in the *Compendious Art of our Mastery* <note>original: "arte compendiosa magisterij nostri"</note> to illuminate the evidence and the certification of all the sons of learning. Likewise, we and many others call it the "son of the sun." For first, through the influence of the sun, it was generated by nature without the aid of science or art. And for this reason, Aristotle called the sun the father and the earth the mother of all growing things <note>original: "vegetabilium"</note>, because the sun impregnates the earth with a life-giving heat, which it afterwards converts into natural heat, which is multiplied by the aid of the heat of fire in our mastery. 

Wherefore, it was afterwards proclaimed by the Philosophers themselves to be the "son of fire," as was said and shown above. Therefore, it is now manifested that just as the Philosophers gave it in great clarity, so they have hidden it with great obscurity. But for you, who have seen nothing nor searched through anything in Philosophy, how can you think that we can give you anything better? See and consider whether this which we now wish to give can suffice for you without any fissure <note>likely meaning "without error" or "complete"</note>: this is the natural fire, which is generated by the sun and multiplied with the aid of common fire and Philosophical disposition. 

For if any of the three fires were lacking in the art, the whole would be worth nothing. Therefore, it appears that it is the "son of the sun" when it is naturally generated through it. And after these things, it becomes the "son of fire," because through that fire it grew and stood multiplied with innate virtue. And again, it is the "son of the Philosopher," because through him it was directed and governed even to the end of its perfection. And so it is shown that it has three fathers. The first is the cause of its generation. The second is the cause of its perfection. And the third is the cause of its multiplication. 

Therefore, son, we say that you should take our earth impregnated by the sun, and sacrifice the boy well with the substance through subtle nourishment. For he ought to stand in the place of the sun, having and carrying the strengths of his father within himself, for the father granted his power to the son. This is our "infused gold" <note>original: "aurum nostrum influxum"</note>, or our sun, since it is our soul, and not in any other thing. Afterward, it is our bronze <note>original: "æs nostrum"</note>, in which the sun is said to be, and it is the leprous and black earth <note>A term for the raw, unrefined matter of the Great Work</note>, in which the common [metal] is corrupted. Honor, therefore, its nature, and keep its virtue in your knowledge, because the stone is honored, found in the houses of...

->*How the weakening of one is the strengthening of another. And how our stone is generated through the strengthening of the mineral power.*<-

### C H A P T E R  L X I X.

Son, every weakening of a body is a dissolution <note>The breaking down of a solid into a liquid state</note>, and every dissolution of it is a loss of its temperament <term>Temperament: the specific, balanced proportion of the four qualities (hot, cold, moist, dry) that gives a substance its identity</term>. And every temperament is the restoration of a lost thing. Therefore it is fitting, since our stone must be weakened through dissolution, division, and corruption, that the power of the water (in which the individual parts of nature flee, along with all their species and elemental powers) must strengthen itself to perform the conjunction and union of the things altered in a new generation of mixtures. 

This is so that by the help of this strengthening, the power of the strengthened waters can be better and more suitably applied against the onset of weakness. By a good overflowing, it can obtain the power to overcome the powers of our weakened stone, converting the stone into the water's own quality and nature. Through this conversion, performed by the weakening of one and the strengthening of the other, our stone is compared to a man submerged in the depths of a great gulf of water. By this method, set forth by clear reason, wise nature shows us that the weakened power of the stone can be strengthened by the weakness of the power of the water—which was itself strengthened in the manner of water—so that it will have the power to convert the water back to its own nature. And within those elements, that nature which is the homogeneity of metals <note>original: *homogenea metallorum*; the shared, underlying substance that is common to all metals before they are differentiated</note> rests in its entirety and is carried along.

And therefore, it overcomes every higher and lower thing with its great strength. It is a most secret and very wonderful thing in nature, which simple people hold and consider to be a miracle, or an incantation, or magic art, since their memory cannot enable them to understand our mastery <term>Mastery: the *magisterium*, referring to the completed Great Work or the process of creating the Philosopher's Stone</term>, which is done through nature, and in nature, and of nature.

### *On the recapitulation, how from one single nature everything that is sought is made.*

## CHAPTER 74.

In recapitulating, we say, my son, that since this thing is of one single nature, it is made from that nature alone—which all those who do not have it, or the powerful, or the givers, and even those who possess it and consider their riches, desire and ask for. Wherefore this nature, through a loving concord, and without violence or combustible strengthening, and without the grinding of hands, or through softening by its own heat without the sensibility of its own property of nature, is changed from one quality into another. <meta>This page continues the discussion from the previous page regarding the elemental transitions. Having established that dry earth cannot easily turn into moisture without a medium, it now explains how water serves as that bridge between earth and air, and air between water and fire, forming a continuous cycle of transmutation.</meta>

->T H E O R I C A.<-

[water] participates with air, and through its moisture it thins the earth, lightening it. And through its coldness it condenses the air by constricting it. Thus, when water converts the earth to its own nature, it can afterward convert it into air through the harmony of the moisture which the earth received from the water, and the coldness which the air received from the water, which constricted it. Consequently, air is the medium between fire and water, since air is moist and shares in the nature of water, and since it is hot, it shares in the nature of fire. Through its moisture, air condenses fire and turns it into the nature of air through thickening <term>inspissatio: the process of making a liquid or gas thicker or more dense</term>, and through its heat, it thins and softens water, turning it into air through lightening <term>levigatio: the process of making a substance lighter, smoother, or more subtle</term>. Therefore, when water is converted into the nature of air, the air converts it into the nature of fire. Alternatively, when fire is converted into a moist, airy nature, the moisture and coldness convert it into the nature of water, according to the intention of nature or of a good and perfect craftsman. For just as water is made of the matter of earth, so air is made of the matter <margin>of water and earth</margin> of air and earth. And one is the matter of the other.

### *How the elements are thinned and thickened through the circular wheel, which is called by the philosophers of this art the Golden Chain.* <note>original: "Cathena aurea"; the Golden Chain refers to the interconnectedness of all things and the cyclic nature of elemental transformation.</note>

## C H A P T E R  LXXIX.

Therefore, son, we tell you—if you wish to understand us—that when earth is thinned through its contrary, it is turned into the nature of water because of the quality of coldness, which participates between dryness and moisture. And when that water is thinned further, it is turned into the nature of air by fire. And when that air is thinned further, it is turned into the nature of fire. Consequently, by a backward movement <term>retrogradatio: the reversal of the process, moving from the most subtle element (fire) back toward the most dense (earth)</term>, when the nature of fire is thickened, it is converted into the nature of moist air; then the fire loses as much of its heat as the moisture can oppose through the dulling effect of its thickening. And the better this nature is condensed through thickening, the better it will be converted into the nature of water, which through its condensation has "killed" or neutralized the greater part of the heat. It also loses a great part of its moisture through the hardening of the nature of air as it approaches terrestrial qualities. When this water is thickened further, it is then turned into the nature of earth, and because of its coldness, it loses part of its moisture by circling back and carrying itself toward dryness. Therefore, if you wish to kindle our fire, administer to it food that is light and tender.

because its dulling and death <note>original: "hebetatio & mortificatio"; in alchemy, mortification refers to the metaphorical 'death' or breakdown of a substance before it can be reborn or transformed</note> come only through the roughness and coarseness of matter, as is evident in the aforementioned explanation. And through this final order, the secret of the composition of our water <note>“Our water” usually refers to the "mercury of the philosophers," a specialized solvent used in the Great Work</note> shines forth to understanding sons, since it clearly appears that a dry nature cannot be converted into a moist one until it is first converted into a cold nature. 

Son, we clearly open the door of nature for you to enter all her works, if you understand: because the superior elements are the cause of the thinning of the inferior ones. And thinning is the cause of vivification <note>giving life or activity to a dormant substance</note> and animation. But the inferior elements are the cause of the thickening of the other elements. And this is by reason of the attraction of the closer harmony that lies in their natures, as was recently declared through earth and through fire; and thickening is the cause of mortification and the dulling of animal heat. 

And we swear with a good spirit that thinning does not happen without thickening, nor thickening without thinning; nor does the dissolution of earth happen without the congealing of water, nor the congealing of water without the dissolution of earth. Son, in the spirit the congealed body is dissolved, and through the body the congealed spirit is constrained; because by congealing the spirit, we dissolve the body, and by dissolving the body, we congeal the spirit.

# THEORY

...similarly from the above, from one <term>handful of fire</term> <note>original: "pugillo ignis"; a 'pugillus' is a small handful or pinch, used here as a proportional measure</note>, and nine of water, ten parts of <term>dead air</term> <note>original: "aeris mortui"</note> are made, which is <term>living water</term> <note>original: "aqua viva"</note>. ### THEORY.

...joined or added with a coarse nature through condensation, it will be closer to heaviness and weight, and of lesser perfection. And thus, son, you can understand the multiplication or diminution of operative virtues. For the philosopher <note>original: "philosophus"; usually referring to Aristotle, the ultimate authority for medieval scientists</note> in the book *Meteorology* <note>original: "Meteororum"; Aristotle’s work on the formation of minerals and atmospheric phenomena</note> says that terrestrial nature, in the place where metals are generated, contains within itself celestial virtues. Through these virtues, its individual existence is converted into the form, nature, and species of metals, with the assistance of the power of terrestrial nature.

In another way, if the power of terrestrial nature should exceed the power of celestial nature in potency—which, in the specification of a metal, was characterized by great dryness and great coldness of a coarse nature—it would condense the moisture (which ought to receive the form of metal) into the nature and likeness of earth, rather than into the form of metal. This occurs because of a deficiency of the celestial virtues which are not present in the said nature. Therefore, the **sons of truth** <note>original: "filii veritatis"; a traditional term for those initiated into the alchemical arts</note> can understand that the form of a metal comes from and exists because of a celestial power, infused into the deeper parts of their matter. Thus, it is said through *Meteorological* reasoning that the soul is in the seed of nature, just as the master is in his craft.

Son, such celestial power is found in the proper place where metals are generated, and therefore it is the form of the metal. Act then, son, so that in the place of generation or conversion there is such celestial power that it can transform the moisture of the individual—while preserving the action that seeks this from terrestrial nature—into a transparent and most refined form and species, through the congealing of terrestrial dryness. This will be a thing of great power. Because the power of the earth, through a temperate cold and through a balanced dryness, has worked by congealing, thickening, and retaining. And the formative celestial power, infused with the power of the earth, forms the species in a celestial color when the matter is congealed, so that by congealing, the species is transformed, and by shaping it, the matter is congealed.

Therefore, son, scripture commands that you must wash the **quicksilver** <term>original: "argentum vivum"; mercury, the "living silver" considered the primary matter of all metals</term> so many times until it turns into a clear celestial color. And this is the earth in which we sow our souls, and in it is our **congealing** <term>original: "congelatio"; the process of a liquid becoming solid or stable, essential for "fixing" the elixir</term>, and in no other place. Through this, the simple **fugitive spirits of the fifth essence** <term>original: "spiritus quinti fugitivi"; the volatile, spiritual elements of the quintessence that tend to escape during heating</term> are retained. These spirits must and ought to form the clear earth into the power and form of the **elixir** <term>original: "elixiris"; the supreme medicinal and transmutative substance</term>, through a special difference that is moved by the mobile harmony of the "five things," as we shall clearly note in the second part of this book:

## *How the entire intention of the operator must be focused on preparing the matter of the stone and on its temperament.*

### CHAPTER LXXXIV.

Therefore, your intellect can perceive through rational consideration that the more the matter is properly prepared and refined <note>original: "subtiliata"; referring to the process of making matter "subtle" or pure by removing coarse impurities</note>, the more it will obtain and retain within itself the celestial virtues <term>celestial virtues|influences or "spirit" believed to descend from the stars and planets to give life and form to physical objects</term> of the higher nature; and the less it is refined, the less it will retain. Son, see therefore and take note how water is changed into air, and air into fire, if you wish to have the preparation of nature. If you wish to make fire from the matter of earth, it is necessary for you from the beginning that you refine it well, so that it may be transmuted into the nature of water and air; and when you wish to work in the opposite direction, once your intention is understood, you shall change the elements into their opposites.

Nevertheless, perform your work from a simpler thing, because the celestial virtue is appropriated to it just as the form of a simpler thing is, and this is according to the action of matter and the course of nature. And hold to this saying of the Philosopher <note>original: "philosophi"; referring to Aristotle, the primary authority for medieval science</note> in the 7th book of the *Metaphysics*: "That according to the property of the matter, a certain and proper form will be appropriated to it according to its action." Therefore, if the matter is simple, it will take for itself the most noble and very pure form, because of its simplicity and the likeness which is born from the property of the simple higher nature. 

For this reason, when you wish to balance <note>original: "contemperare"; to bring the elements into a perfect "temperament" or harmonic ratio</note> the substance of the stone, place it in the location of generation, or of conversion into the qualities through which you wish—by certain knowledge—your stone to be changed: namely, in moist heat. For this is the quality through which sweetness is caused in the bitter stone, by the preservation of the stone’s moisture in its fire, until it can endure the eternal fire <note>original: "æternum ignem"; a metaphor for the final, stable state of the Philosopher's Stone where it can no longer be destroyed by heat</note>.

Through this mixture it appears that there is a "medium" <note>an intermediate substance</note> between the stone and the metal, since the said mixture is made in the matter of the stone, and in the matter of metals and liquefiable bodies. For a medium is everything that in some way participates with the stone on one side, and in some way with the metal on the other side. And furthermore, the property of a stone is that it cannot be melted, while the property of a metal, which it holds from its matter, is that it can be melted by heat and dryness. Therefore, by these things you can note that stones are in the genus of dry earth, and metals are in the genus of moist water. 

A "medium" is therefore called everything that participates in the qualities of those two extremes. But there are some among them which participate more with dryness, and those contain heat and dryness, and consist of heat and dryness, such as Marcasite <term>Marcasite|a brittle, metallic mineral (iron pyrite), often used in alchemy as a "middle" substance</term>, Antimony, and so on. But there are others which participate better in the degree of moisture, and from those, water is distilled by heat and dryness, such as rock salt <note>original: "salgemma"</note>. 

By this, son, the doctrine declared before your eyes can shine through: that which belongs to the property of metal is an aquatic moisture, and quicksilver separated by the art of the mastery <note>original: "magisterii"; the "Great Work" of alchemy</note> revealed to you. Therefore, son, have knowledge of the nature of the mediums, because from them we draw our whole science, and the power of placing quicksilver into the work; and we draw quicksilver from its glassy caverns, and with them the stone is carried...
