## *Concerning softening, which gives the elixir its melting property and perfect stability.*
<term>inceratione; "inceration" or softening, the process of bringing a substance to a waxy, meltable state</term>
### CHAPTER XXVI.

When you have fixed the water upon the earth, and the air upon the water successively, as we have told you, take one ounce of the medicine and place it in an earthen crucible over a light fire. Immediately, as it feels the heat, add its "white oil" <note>likely a purified liquid or solvent derived earlier in the process</note> drop by drop. Know that the oil will penetrate all its parts; it will enter imperceptibly into the depths of the elixir and settle there, rendering it meltable <term>fusibilem; capable of being melted</term>, penetrating, and well-integrated. Then take a small amount of it and test its meltability upon a red-hot copper plate. If it dissolves like wax without smoke, the medicine is created; if it does not, and instead gives off smoke, return it to the softening process <term>incerandum</term> by dripping its oil over it drop by drop until it shows the aforementioned sign in the manner described. Afterward, allow it to cool: for the elixir is complete—a price beyond price—which converts every diminished and imperfect body into an infinite, bright <term>limificum; likely from "limidus" or "limpidus," meaning clear or bright</term>, true, and good substance. Therefore, cast one weight of this upon 1,000 weights of common quicksilver <term>argenti vivi; mercury</term> washed with salt and vinegar, and it will be converted into pure silver <term>lunam; literally "the moon," the alchemical name for silver</term>, better than that from a mine, approved in every test. Similarly, if it is cast upon any of the imperfect bodies <note>The "imperfect bodies" are the base metals, such as lead, tin, or copper</note>, it will be transformed into true silver immediately after the radical moisture is reached.

By its own nature, this water is fit and capable of generating phlegm; however, if it accords and delights in heat and dryness by its own temperament, it multiplies the life-giving spirit. Therefore, this water multiplies sulfur when it is cast into the "bellies" of **choleric males**. And when it is cast into the "bellies" of **choleric females**, the quicksilver is multiplied, being well-tempered and strongly enriched by heat and moisture.

->### PRACTICE.<-

...[nourishment], place upon the substance of the body from which you wish to extract the blood enough pure Mercury so that it exceeds five or six fingers' height in a glass vessel with a long and narrow neck. Apply a gentle fire beneath it until you see the blood rise above the Mercury. And set aside everything that has been dissolved through liquefaction, and add more Mercury. 

Continue this work until you have its blood dissolved in the liquor; afterward, distill it through an **alembic** <note>a chemical apparatus consisting of two vessels connected by a tube, used for distilling volatile substances</note>. And then you will find the **quicksilver** <term>argentum vivum; mercury</term> to be of greater heat than it was before its **exuberation** <note>original: "exuberatio"; in alchemy, this refers to a process of making a substance "overflow" with power or vitality by feeding it with the essence of other metals</note>. 

Likewise, if you seek to exuberate it further, place it in another body and do as we have said until it has drawn all the life-giving moisture from it. In such a way, our **Stone** <note>the Philosopher's Stone</note> ascends high to heaven and is carried in the belly of the wind—that is, in the quicksilver <note>This is a reference to the famous *Emerald Tablet* of Hermes Trismegistus, which describes the Stone as being "carried in the belly of the wind"</note>. 

Thus you can perform your accidental exuberation and multiply it always into another body at your will. And if you are ingenious and discerning, do not throw away the earths which are black and dry: for with them you can perform many things by instinct and instruction, and create many stones. 

If you are idle, my son, and do not know what to do, enter into our **Mastery** <term>magisterium; the Great Work or the highest level of alchemical practice</term>, and you will have enough to do—so much so that you will not value all the riches of the world at a single button. For you will know that all the precious things of the world proceed in full wagonloads from one vile thing. 

My son, this matter arises from an exuberated **fermentation** <note>the stage where the Stone acts like yeast, transforming base metals into its own nature</note>, performed by means of the distancing of the body from its true temperament, and the water returning to its **menstrual state** <note>original: "menstruale"; referring to the "Philosophical Menstruum," a universal solvent used to dissolve metals</note> and the appropriation of this to the metal. 

If, therefore, after the distillation of the dissolved body, you dissolve another body of new metal, that which is subsequently dissolved will approach a greater fermentation because of the impregnated and exuberated virtue, better proportioned by the nature of the metal, purified through the **radical moisture** <term>humidum radicale; the fundamental, life-sustaining fluid believed to exist within all matter</term>. 

And thus through extremes and means, you must perform the exuberation of our quicksilvers. For this reason, the second is more powerful than the first, and the fourth more than the third, and the sixth more than the fifth, provided that each preserves its perfection according to how its nature was exuberated. 

And this multiplication always takes place perpetually, and this is the cause and reason of the great and excellent mineral virtue which is in our water. Through this, the **stone which is not a stone** <note>a common alchemical riddle indicating that the Elixir is not a common rock, but a refined metallic spirit</note> is brought from hidden potential into manifest action, and from a distant and remote power into a near power through certain degrees of operation which occur within the range of temperament and imbalance. And thus nature appropriates itself toward its own perfection. Know therefore, my son, that in any form there are degrees...

## *On the composition of the red elixir.*

### CHAPTER XXVIII.

By following the practice in this exact manner, just as the white elixir was made, you shall make the **red elixir** <note>The red elixir was the highest goal of alchemy, capable of transmuting metals into gold and acting as a panacea</note>, because there is no difference in the practice, provided all elements are red; and just as you multiplied the white sulfur, you shall multiply the red, putting in fine gold instead of silver. And let the water of Mercury first be turned red with the fire of the stone through boiling alone, and let the medicine be composed of three parts of ferment, three of water, three of air, and one part and a half of fire. 

And when you come to the reduction of air, repeat the **sublimation** <note>the process of heating a substance until it turns to vapor and then solidifies again, used for purification</note> until the whole is fixed together; and afterward continue the three fires which we mentioned for the white elixir to the end, so that the elixir may be better fixed and purified through the digestion of **roasting** <note>original: "optesis"; from the Greek word for baking or roasting in a furnace</note>. 

Son, this roasting digestion gives the medicine its power and the action it must perform, because through it, the humidity is ended and the fire is digested. Afterward, withdraw your elixir, place it down, and **soften it** <note>original: "incera"; literally "to wax," a process of adding liquid to a dry powder until it reaches the consistency of wax</note> within a crucible with a gentle fire without fear of it fleeing <note>evaporating</note>, and feed it drop by drop with its red oil until you see it melt like wax, without smoke, like tin upon burning iron. Then it will be made into a single thing: stable, deep-reaching, penetrating, consolidating, tinting, and permanent. 

Of this, cast one weight upon 1,000 parts of **silver** <term>luna; literally "the moon," the alchemical name for silver</term>, or **quicksilver** <term>argentum vivum; mercury</term> washed with salt and vinegar, and it will be transformed into true and perfect gold according to every test—better than that from a mine in all its properties. Son, we tell you that our gold and our silver are not common gold and silver, because we add a great fiery supplement to their **tinctures** <note>the soul or coloring principle of a metal</note>, and we cause them to be given and granted great perseverance in the fire through the property of our known operations and many good benefits for driving away every infirmity.

## *On the perfection and improvement of all medicines.*

### CHAPTER XXIX.

**S**on, if after **projection** <note>original: "projectio"; the final step where the alchemical medicine is cast upon molten base metal to transform it into gold or silver</note> you see that the metal has been converted and transmuted into another metal by the medicine, but your medicine did not have a sufficient enough color, then more of the said medicine should be added to that metal. And if it should have too much red color—for it is not possible for the white to have too much—do not add so much of the medicine; and if you have already added it, add more of the metal to be transmuted and converted. 

And if your medicine does not remain, or does not fully resist the fire, the defect is one of **fixation** <note>original: "fixio"; the process of making a substance stable under heat so it does not evaporate</note>. Thus its **penetration** <note>original: "ingressio"; the ability of the elixir to enter into the "pores" of the base metal</note> is lacking and it requires help, either through the reiteration of **solution and congelation** <note>dissolving the substance into a liquid and cooling it back into a solid to purify it</note>, or through the **sublimation** of the non-fixed part over the fixed part, until it gains resistance against the harshness of the fire. 

And if you see that it cannot be melted except by the violence and weight of the fire, the defect is a lack of good **inceration** <note>original: "inceratio"; literally "waxing," the process of softening a dry or brittle substance until it flows like wax</note>. Therefore, restore and supplement it through the inceration of the oil of the stone, by projecting it drop by drop over a gentle fire in a crucible, as described above, until the "wax" flows. 

Son, when you wish to incerate, you should place more of the hot and moist substance than of the cold and dry. But when you work with the intention of fixing, then place more of the cold and dry substance than of the hot and moist. Understand what we say, because the perfection of this work is nothing other than the **changing of natures** <note>the fundamental alchemical principle of balancing the four qualities: hot, cold, moist, and dry</note>.

### CHAPTER XXX.

**W**hen you have perfected the said medicines and have performed a projection with them, you can artificially multiply their virtues in two ways. 

The first way is that you cause them to be dissolved in their own **Mercury water** <note>original: "aqua Mercurii"; a specialized alchemical solvent, not common quicksilver</note>, either white or red, from which they were first created, until they have become clear water; and afterward, in a gentle boiling, cause them to be congealed, and later incerated in their own oils. And do this over the fire often mentioned, until they truly flow upon a metal plate, as we have said. Because of this, their virtue will be doubled in **tincture** <note>original: "tinctura"; the coloring power that transforms the base metal's appearance</note> and in all perfections, as you will be able to see in their projections: for the same weight which was previously projected over 1,000 parts will now be projected over 10,000. And in this multiplication, there is no great labor. 

The second way of multiplying involves greater labor, because if you distill them after they have been turned into water...

The method of **multiplication** <note>the process of increasing the power of the alchemical medicine so that a small amount can transform a large amount of base metal</note> is as follows: you must dissolve each of their forms individually in its own water by means of **inhumation** <note>original: "inhumationem"; the process of burying a sealed vessel in warm horse dung or earth to provide a gentle, consistent heat</note>. If you prepare them a third time as has been said, one will convert 100,000, and so proceeding into infinity. 

Therefore, son, you must note that the more the medicine is refined—that is, dissolved, **sublimated** <note>vaporized and solidified</note>, and **congealed**—the more greatly and abundantly it works. For in every dissolution it gains and acquires ten weights in every **projection** <note>the act of throwing the medicine onto molten metal</note> because of the power multiplied within it. Therefore, son, do not let it weary you to repeat the solutions, sublimations, and coagulations; for by such operations the medicine is **digested** <note>matured by heat</note>, united, and its power is multiplied, and it works more perfectly and is made fixed. 

Wherefore, son, if you have dissolved and congealed well as we have said, and if you recognize the species with which you must work, you shall reach the perfection of our **mastery** <note>original: "magisterii"; the completion of the Great Work</note> by a high and brief secret. This secret is reserved so that no one can reveal it, just as we have told you. But if you are a good seeker and a son of subtle learning through those things which we have said and shall say in our book of this present **Testament**, and the **Codicil**, and others, you will find it in full and know the secret. And when you know it, we forbid you, under the penalty of **anathema** <note>a formal curse or excommunication</note>, to disclose it to anyone; for he who discloses it is cursed by God. And for this reason, the philosophers have hidden it, and, God willing, will hide it in future times.

...strengthens all spirits and preserves them in health. And therefore, do not wonder if this medicine has been sought and desired by man above all other medicines, since all others are universally reduced to it <note>original: "reductæ sint"; meaning all other medicines derive their power from the principles found in this one</note>. Because it is common to every body, it has the power of rectifying all parts that carry virtue and of fixing those virtues within them—in the manner we described in the **treatise on stones** <note>original: "tractatu lapidarii"; likely referring to a work on the properties of gems and minerals</note>. It also makes **malleable glass** <note>original: "vitrum malleabile"; a legendary lost invention where glass could be hammered like metal without breaking</note>, and performs many other great and weighty wonders in the three natures, namely: **mineral, vegetable, and animal.**

But he spoke with such hidden words that today they are not understood in the world, except by certain persons who can believe with a firm conscience that some of the philosophers have spoken about the above-mentioned medicine.

Having already spoken many times and more often, we recall the many and diverse ways of practicing upon the mastery <note>original: "magisterium"; the successful completion of the alchemical Great Work</note> of the precious Philosopher’s Stone. Now, however, so that you may weigh the truth in the light, know that three things are principally to be noted. First, you must know the matter from which the Philosopher's Stone and all other precious stones are composed. Second, you must know the instruments with which one ought to work. Third, you must know how the said matter must be worked and practiced with the instrument. You should know that our mastery revolves around these three.

->*What the matter of our stone is.*<-

First, therefore, most illustrious King, know that the matter of our stone—or of all the stones of the philosophers and the virtuous ones, which are generated or composed through the art—is the metallic soul and our rectified and sharpened menstruum <term>menstruum: A specialized alchemical solvent believed to dissolve metals into their primary components</term>, or celestial moonwort <note>original: "lunaria coelica"; here referring to a specific alchemical substance rather than the common plant</note>, which among the philosophers is called Vegetable Mercury <term>Vegetable Mercury: A vital essence derived from organic sources, such as wine, rather than minerals</term> originating from red or white wine. It is also found in our *Codicil* <note>original: "Codicillus"; a shorter manual or supplement to a larger work</note> sent to you by King Edward. The instruments are two glass cucurbits <term>cucurbit: A gourd-shaped glass vessel used as the lower part of a distillation apparatus</term> having seven or eight receptacles, as demonstrated in our *Testament* sent to you with the *Codicil*, in the chapter that begins, "Son, you [do] not," etc. But the method of practice is fully treated in the following sections. ### First part.

However, most serene prince, it is first necessary to extract our <term>menstruum</term> <note>original: "menstruum"; a powerful alchemical solvent believed to be the "mother" or base of the work.</note> through the mastery from the mother—that is, from the dregs of wine and phlegm—by the office of the <term>alembic</term> <note>original: "alembici"; a classic distillation apparatus consisting of a boiling flask and a cooling cap.</note>. On the other hand, let the menstruum itself be rotated continuously in a circulation vessel for the space of ten days in warm manure, grape skins, or a <term>bain-marie</term> <note>original: "balneo Marię"; literally "Mary’s Bath," a vessel of hot water used for gentle, indirect heating.</note>. Likewise, my dearest son, it is necessary to have the primary matter of the elements and the <term>sulfur of nature</term> <note>original: "sulphur naturæ"; a philosophical principle of heat and combustion, not necessarily common sulfur.</note>. And because <term>quicksilver</term> <note>original: "argentum vivum"</note> is the existing genus of metals, which we draw out by artifice and by the art of the mastery from metals through the division of elements, and their purification and fixation with agents—drawing it out through rarefaction and circulation on one hand, and on the other hand through the rectification of the elements of metals. Remember, O King, what we said in our little book which begins: "Son, I intend to tell you the matter of the ferments," for when we say "by one <term>decoction</term>," <note>original: "decoctionem"; the process of boiling or heating a substance in a liquid.</note> we mean another rectification of the menstruum. It has simple power; we mean the first rectification of the menstruum. And when we say "by transferring it gradually through another cooking," we mean another rectification of the menstruum up to the third or fourth. For the mastery of the stone is ennobled by it to such a degree that its abundance can in no way be expressed. The present reason is clear through those who corrupt metals with "waters outside of nature" <note>likely referring to corrosive mineral acids like nitric acid (aqua fortis), which Lullians often distinguished from their "natural" organic solvents</note>, because they are ignorant of our menstruum; for it happens that such dissolution somewhat opposes nature. But they do not know how to strengthen it with a natural thing. Therefore, their practice is finally deprived of its effect, and they blame the art for the defect which is actually their own. And these things which we have said concerning the knowledge of the menstruum—which is found in one of those things without which nothing can be done in the mastery of this art—let these suffice for you.

### *Concerning the seed of metals, which is the matter of our stone.*

Now you should know, most serene Prince, that the **spirit of metals** <note>original: "metallorum spiritus"</note> is the other part and matter of our stone, which it is necessary for you to extract from the bodies of all metals. And this extraction is done in two ways, as the practice will show below: because in the two **perfect bodies** <note>Gold and Silver</note> it is divided through **putrefaction** <note>original: "putrefactionem"; in alchemy, this refers to the breakdown or "death" of a substance so it can be reborn/purified</note>, the division of the elements, and their **fixation** <note>the process of making a volatile substance stable under heat</note>. But in imperfect metals, it is divided through purification and the **sublimation** <note>the process of heating a substance until it vapors and then solidifies again</note> of simple unity. And in this step, the ignorant err, thinking that the bodies of metals can be reduced into their own **prime matter** <note>original: "materiam primam"; the original, undifferentiated substance from which all things were made</note> using common strong waters—as I said above—with waters "against nature." And if they had read our books, they would certainly know that such liquids are contrary to the intention of the philosophers. And this which we have said is clearly demonstrated in our *Codicillus* in the chapter that begins, *Therefore gold and silver are dissolved in the radical things of their own kind* <note>original: "Ideo dissolvitur aurum & argentum in rebus radicalibus sui generis"</note>. For this is the water with which incurable illnesses are cured, while preserving their nature, as is evident in the *Codicillus* in the chapter that begins, *Son, the sublimation,* etc. <note>original: "Fili sublimatio"</note>. ### Concerning the Instrument of the Stones.

We have spoken, most serene Prince, of the matter from which the **Philosopher’s Stone** is composed. Now, however, we shall speak of the instruments with which the stone is composed. For these are the vessels, such as the furnace, dung <note>original: "fimus"; horse dung was commonly used in laboratories to provide a gentle, constant heat for digestion</note> or grape-pulp <note>original: "vindemia"; the residue of wine-making, also used for gentle heat</note>, along with the diligence of the craftsman. But before you come to anything else, you must know that the mastery <note>original: "magisterium"; the completion of the alchemical work</note> is divided into three principal parts: namely, **dissolution**, **separation**, and **union**. Through this it is shown to you that first you must dissolve the bodies in our **menstruum**, that you must divide the menstrua from the "luminaries" <note>original: "luminaribus"; referring to the Sun (gold) and the Moon (silver)</note> and purify and fix them, and extract the **sulfur of nature** from the imperfect bodies. Thirdly, you must unite elements with elements, or "mud with mud," or elements with the **sulfur of nature**. And this union is divided into as many parts as there are mixtures and unions of the aforementioned. The first way is to unite air with fire. The second way is to unite air with the **sulfur of nature**; and these ways are found in the elements of the two "luminary" bodies <note>gold and silver</note>. The third way is to unite the "mud" arising from air in fire with the "mud" arising from air and the **sulfur of nature**, each by itself. The fourth way is that fire is united by itself, and air by itself, with the **sulfur of nature** only. The fifth way is to mix the **sulfur of nature** with the two elements at once, namely...

...with fire and air. And these ways of mixing the elements with the **sulfur of nature** <note>original: "sulphure naturæ"; in alchemy, sulfur often represents the active, combustible, and masculine principle of a substance</note> occur in two ways: for they are done either with their own earth or with a foreign earth. Indeed, with a foreign earth, it occurs in many more ways—as many ways as there are for mixing the sulfur of nature when they come to the Artist’s disposal. 

For, most serene Prince, you will be able to practice many particular works with the intellect truly presenting them, which the human intellect could hardly describe, except for those expressed in the third part of this book, and in the *Magica*, and in our *Testament*, and in the *Codicillus*, and the *Vade Mecum* <note>"Go with me," a handbook</note>, *On the Number of Philosophers*, and in the third book of the *Fifth Essence*, and my other books. 

Who then, most serene Prince, could recount the particulars found within the breadth of the <term>magisterium</term> <note>original: "magisterium"; the completion of the "Great Work" of alchemy, or the mastery of the process</note> after the fixation and purification of the elements? Know then how to purify the elements and to divide them first from the metals, for in this lies the whole of the mastery. Thus, once the elements and the sulfur of nature have been divided from the metals, there is almost nothing else remaining in respect to the work. For the entire labor and exhaustion lies in this, namely, the division of the elements and the sulfur. 

This is indeed the point where Artists abandon the mastery, because their division is very tedious, and because the unskilled think that in the first distillation and those of the second degree, they can distill all the air, and that from the first distillation of the third degree, they can similarly distill all the fire from the earth. This, however, is impossible and against the course of nature. 

Indeed, most serene Prince, we propose to reveal the true word to you now: for the air cannot be divided from metals except in the 20th, or 24th, or 30th distillation. For however many distillations there are, there are just as many <term>putrefactions</term> <note>original: "putrefactiones"; the stage of decay or breaking down of the substance, often associated with the color black</note> and repetitions of the water and air—namely, the <term>menstrual water</term> <note>original: "aquæ menstrualis"; the philosophical solvent mentioned on the previous page, used to dissolve the "body" of the metal</note>—and in each putrefaction, it requires eight or six continuous days, so that the division of the elements lasts nearly a year; but we completed the division of the elements in seven months, and the fire cannot be divided from the earth except in the 40th distillation. 

For who is there who can endure such labor for a year or for seven months? There are few indeed. And therefore, those ignorant of natural principles think they are performing the true practice with metals without the division of the elements; they are deceived in this. 

Afterward, there are some who, when they do not suddenly divide their elements and the sulfur of nature according to their whim, refuse to attend to the natures of minerals; they make a confused mixture without any purification or <term>sublimation</term> <note>the process of heating a substance into vapor and back to solid to purify it</note> and refinement, and they do not arrive at the sought-after end. They assign no cause to their own ignorance, but instead place the blame on the art, which they do not understand, asserting that the art is false; regarding which—

### *Concerning non-natural principles, and how they are understood.*

But since these principles are not naturally produced in one individual thing, as many erringly think, saying that there was one thing in the world which has the power to transmute all metals on earth—which is false. P. which otherwise are not converted into G. in our work.

...[vessel]s: and then extract, and put that which has been dissolved into another vial; and over that which remained—once the solutions and distillations are finished—place more of the <term>menstruum</term> <note>original: "menstruo"; a universal alchemical solvent, not a biological fluid</note> again in an amount equal to the quantity of the earth <note>the solid residue or "dregs" remaining in the vessel</note>, and place it in digestion H for 4 natural days. Once the 6 distillations of the dregs are finished, do not concern yourself with the remainder. 

Place the distillations, liquefactions, or even the solutions into digestion H and distill all the water through an alembic <note>the "cap" or hood of the still that collects vapor</note>. Upon the dregs, you should place other fresh Water of Mercury <note>original: "aqua Mercurii"</note>, and place it in digestion for one and a half months. Afterward, take the vessel Q in which the putrefied gold was held, and distill the water therefrom in digestion H. Upon the dregs, send just as much fresh menstruum, and again place the vessel in digestion H for 6 or 10 natural days. When these are finished, place the vessel in digestion I and distill the air together with the menstruum. 

After it no longer wishes to distill, keep the distillate in its own vessel, and over the dregs send more menstruum. Place it in digestion H for 6 natural days, and again distill as before in digestion I. Upon the dregs, send more fresh <term>lunaria</term> <note>original: "lunaria"; literally "moon-plant," a poetic name for a specific alchemical solvent often associated with silver or the moon's cooling properties</note>, and place it in digestion I. Thus you shall reiterate the inhumations and distillations in H and I until the 20th or 25th distillation. 

But while you are at the 22nd distillation, place that water (in which there is some part of the "Air") together with the menstruum to be distilled in digestion H. The whole menstruum will pass over through that distillation or another; and if there was any "Air" there, it will remain at the bottom in the manner of resplendent or lemon-yellow water. If its quantity is no more than 2, 3, or 4 drops, do not repeat the inhumations and distillations. If, however, there is more, repeat the inhumations and distillations in digestion H and I up to the 26th or 30th distillation, so that the Earth may be well evacuated of its Air. 

In every inhumation, it requires at least 5 continuous days until you have distilled all the Air, which—without fail—will be entirely distilled through the said distillations, if you have regulated the mastery well. After this, you shall take the vessel in which all the distillations are kept, and distill them with digestion H. Then all the Air will remain at the bottom, because nothing [of the Air] will be strong enough to ascend together with the menstruum through distillation in H. When you have distilled all the menstruum, the whole of the Air will remain in the depths in the color of most beautiful resplendent water. Save that, because when you have the Air in this way, the process was excellent. 

Indeed, just as you have done concerning the Air, we teach you the same method for the abstraction of Fire from Earth, neither more nor less, except that the separation of Fire from Earth is done by "inhuming" it with the Air, and in each turn distilling in digestion K. Or it can also be done...

Upon the dregs, place as much of reagent C as there is earth, and place it in digestion H for one natural day, and distill again.

But, Most Serene Prince, it is done better and more safely with D. Place it in digestion H for 2 days; afterward, distill through the alembic in digestion I. Upon the dregs, again put reagent D (if you worked with D) or C (if you worked with C), and place it in digestion H, and afterward distill, and put this distillation with the other. If indeed the menstruum should fail, distill that which you extracted from the earth through distillation, and work with that. Indeed, you shall repeat the addition of D over the earth so many times, and you shall inhumate and distill, until the entire earth, together with D or C, has ascended through the alembic and descends into the receiver. 

This matter is indeed called by the philosophers "living silver" <note>original: "arg. vivum" (argentum vivum); often refers to mercury, but here indicates a purified, mobile state of the matter</note> according to the consideration of the Alchemists. Then extract the earth from digestion I, and place it in digestion K, and the earth will be <term>sublimated</term> <note>the process where a solid turns into vapor and solidifies again at the top of the vessel</note>, and the earth will be like living silver in the virtue of sublimation. 

But you, Most Serene Prince, when you have completed all that we have said above, know that you have all the elements which you need to compose the <term>philosophers' stone</term>. When you have <term>putrefied</term> <note>rotted or broken down through moist heat</note> the white compound, the purification of the elements is nevertheless better done with D itself than with C, since C retains something of superfluity; D indeed, since it is of a subtler nature, and through this that chapter of our testament is elucidated, which begins: *When you have divided the stone* <note>original Latin: "Quam tu auras divisa la, etc."; likely a corruption of "Quando tu aurum diviseris per quatuor elementa"</note>, etc., that is, When you shall have divided the stone into the 4 elements. Likewise in the purification of the earth, about which we spoke above in the final part.

### *On the sublimation of air.*

Take therefore, in the name of Christ, the air, and you shall place it in an <term>alembic</term> <note>the cap or hood of a still</note>, and you shall distill it seven or six times—the sign of which will be until nothing more wishes to be distilled. Likewise, if perhaps the air should be turned into powder, you shall distill and purify it with just as much of D <note>D refers to a specific reagent or stage of heat in Lullian alchemical notation</note>, and in the last stage you shall distill D, and the air will remain below. You ought to know, however, Most Serene Prince, that what we have said—the distillation and purification of air—is done with the <term>digestion</term> <note>gentle, continuous heating in a controlled environment</note> of I <note>another Lullian notation for a specific grade of heat</note>. Likewise, you are well able to purify the air with its own water, for just as you purified the air, so you should do similarly in all things regarding the fire, as we said of the air; except that the purification of fire is done with the digestion of K <note>a different, likely higher, grade of heat or reagent</note>, and the air with the digestion of I. Likewise, Most Serene Prince, that which we said concerning the purification of the earth, you will find in full in the *vade mecum* regarding the number of the philosophers, in the chapter that begins: "The birth, indeed, is made by the way of the invented sublimation," etc., throughout the whole chapter. 

When therefore, Most Serene Prince, you have completed these things mentioned above, then you will have all that from which the <term>Philosophers' Stone</term> <note>the legendary substance capable of transmuting base metals into gold and granting long life</note> is composed. You indeed must make the mixture of the elements and things pertaining to the composition of the Stone. Take therefore the purified elements—in which purification it is necessary for the <term>feces</term> <note>original: *feces*, referring to the solid dregs or residue remaining after distillation</note> to remain at the bottom of the vessel. Furthermore, keep the dregs of fire and air aside, and take the fire and the air—whichever of these—placed in its own vessel, and close the vessel with gummed wax, and place it in a clear location for three continuous days. When these are finished, take as much of the dregs of fire as of air, and of the dregs of earth as there is of air; and if there are not as many dregs of the elements as there is of the element of air, add purified earth up to the stated quantity. Put the whole amount, with the dregs of fire, air, and earth, into the proper vessel for air, and close the little vessel very well with wax, mastic, and <term>lute</term> <note>a tough, airtight paste or cement used to seal alchemical apparatus</note>. And one of these vessels—namely, the vessel of air—you shall bury in the earth, and the other, in which is the fire, you shall suspend above in the air in another part. And do so in such a way that no stone or anything else may damage the glass, and let the said vessels stand there for a continuous year. When this is done, you shall fashion certain molds or models of wax, in the form of which you wish the Stone to come out or be made.

Once these things are done, open the vessel which you placed in the earth for a year, and put inside two or three sponges <note>original: *mollas*; these are soft, absorbent materials like wool or sponge used to capture vapors</note> which will float; let them stay thus in the vessel and immediately close it. And when the time has passed, open the vessel and take the sponges or measures and hold them outside the vessel; fill them with the water which you suspended in the air for the space of one year, and once again place the measures in the first vessel where the terrestrial water is, and immediately close the vessel. You should know indeed, most serene Prince, that the water you placed in the earthen sponges you will find within as a solidified "regeneration" in the manner of gum: and this gem is indeed called by the philosophers the **Elixir**.

With such an invisible spirit of terrestrial water, we make pure silver from common <term>quicksilver</term> <note>original: *argento vivo vulgi*; common Mercury</note>, good for every test, just as if from a mine without the heat of common fire; by reason of its power, its scent will thus congeal ☿ <note>The astrological and alchemical symbol for Mercury</note> into the most proven silver, just as the basilisk <note>a legendary serpent-king whose gaze was fatal</note> kills every animal in an instant with its sight.

### *There follows the first decoction, which is done with the heat of the Sun.*

Take therefore your stones, and put them in a certain glass vessel, which is called the **perfectory** <note>original: *perfectorium*; a specialized vessel used in the final stages of the alchemical work to "perfect" the substance</note> by Alchemists, and which is an oblong instrument, thin in substance: and close the vessel very well with mastic and with rye flour mixed with threads of linen cloth, and place it in the Sun for nine days in Spring and in Summer, or in Autumn and Winter for eighteen days; when these are finished, the first decoction will be completed. Then it behooves you to direct yourself to the second, which is the middle between the first and third decoctions: the second decoction is that which is done otherwise with the first heat <note>i.e., solar heat</note>.

### *Concerning the second decoction of the stone.*

Most Serene Prince, the second decoction is called **Optates**, and it is done with the same heat, but differently: because you should take the thinnest glass vessel that you can find, and larger in quantity, and let it be filled with the clearest water, and let it be placed in the ray of the Sun, and in that lower part where it shines most, and where the fire is most received through the mastery of the common people <note>This likely refers to using the water-filled glass as a "burning lens" or "burning sphere" to concentrate solar rays</note>, and let the aforementioned vessel with the stones be placed in such a way that the brightness of the fire touches the vessel where the stones are, and let it stay there, until the Sun cannot be captured through the vessel full of water. And let this decoction be continued in Spring for eighteen days, and in winter for fifteen days, and in summer for eight; which being finished, the second decoction is finished, and it is necessary to administer the third, which is the final completion of the stone.

### *The third decoction, which is done with the heat of common fire.*

The third decoction indeed is done with the heat of common fire and is done in a certain furnace, which is called the **Tripod of Secrets** <note>original: *Tripes archanorum*; a specialized three-legged furnace or stand used for prolonged heating</note> whose figure is truly situated in the book of the <term>Fifth Essence</term> <note>The *Quintessence*; referring to another work in the Lullian corpus, likely *De Consideratione Quintae Essentiae*</note>, which we do not believe is hidden from you, and it is done in this way. Take therefore the stones, which you have in the **perfectory** vessel, and thus with their vessel place them in the **Tripod of Secrets** for the space of nine days, continuing for it the fire from burning coals: which being finished, the final decoction is finished, which is called by the Alchemists <term>Sulphur</term> or **Sulphur D. H.** <note>likely an abbreviation for *Sulphur de Hermete* or "Sulphur of the Wise"</note>. And in this, most serene Prince, you have everything which is desired by the world—a treasure incomparable and innumerable, with which one can follow toward the most perfect end. And it is one of the secrets to multiply those stones: but because the multiplication of the stones overflows into the third or fourth number, of which two modes are indeed very tedious,

Because these things occur through the reduction of the stones to the first principle, we explain one method here. But one method, most serene Prince, is very pleasing to the senses, and it is the one that follows: how the multiplication of the philosophers' stone is performed in quantity alone.

### *Concerning the multiplication of the stone.*

This multiplication is performed with common quicksilver <note>original: *argento vivo vulgi*; refers to ordinary mercury as opposed to "philosophical mercury"</note> in this manner. Take of the stones in the quantity of one drachm <note>original symbol: ʒ; a unit of weight approximately equal to 3.9 grams</note> and place it upon one hundred thousand parts of common quicksilver. So great is the fire of the stone, multiplied by celestial virtues, that it can reduce the whole of that mercury into powder, burning away all the mineral impurities existing in said mercury, just as the gaze of the basilisk <note>A mythical serpent king said to kill with a single look; here used as a metaphor for the instant and total transformative power of the Stone</note> burns every animal vitality in an instant and kills every living thing. Indeed, here you will have one hundred thousand and one weights of quicksilver converted into medicine. Of these hundred thousand, a single part placed upon another hundred thousand parts of mercury <note>original symbol: ☿</note> reduces it into powder. As was previously clear from that second powder, a third time place it upon one hundred thousand drachms of mercury, and it reduces it into powder, making a new multiplication from each, up to one hundred multiplications. 

Who then could describe the quantity of medicine produced by these multiplications? Therefore, most serene Prince, because you can multiply one drachm of those hundred thousand, and then another hundred from those multiplied drachms, you will know that for each new multiplication, one drachm is to be placed upon a hundred thousand of quicksilver, and the whole becomes medicine. Most serene Prince, let the projection <note>The act of throwing the alchemical powder onto a molten base metal to effect transmutation</note> of the medicine upon the mercury be continued until the fire of the stone is extinguished, the matter is converted into perfect metal, and no more powder is produced. 

There are, however, other multiplications: one is called "virtual" <note>referring to the *virtue* or potency of the stone rather than its physical mass</note> and "quantitative" at the same time, and each of these is done by reduction to the principle, as is contained in our *Testament*, in the chapter that begins: *When you have finished the said things...* <note>original: "Quam in auras cicabades les dictes coses..." – this is a Latinized Catalan phrase from Lully’s *Testamentum*</note>. When you have completed the said things and performed projections through the whole circle, even if not in this same book of multiplication, let it be continued as is shown in the chapter that begins: *Son, take one drachm of the said multiplied medicine, etc.* <note>original: "Fili tu prendas una ʒ. de la medicina decta multiplicata"</note>. You will find further information regarding the other multiplication in the third book of the *Quintessence*, in the chapter that treats multiplication.

### On another mixture.

And let another mixture be made thus: that you join three weights of P. and two of O., and make the whole a single body. ### On another mixture.

Likewise, let another mixture be made: take eight parts of P. and one of O. and join them together, and place them in the digestion <note>Slow heating in a controlled environment to mature the substance</note> of H. <note>In Lullian notation, H typically represents Fire or Heat</note> for eight days: and afterwards incerate the earth of this or of some metal or of that for the solution and the sediment <note>original: *limum*; literally "mud" or "slime," referring to the residue of the work</note>. Then incerate its earth or another, and with this medicine you will make perfect gold, making a mixture from opposites—namely one weight of O. of gold and eight weights of P. of silver.

### On another way of mixing.

Likewise, in another way: if you take from the fire of gold and from its O. to the half of P., and from the earth to the half of O., mix together with the seventh part of the pure essence, and distill the deserted sediment, with which you can incerate its earth or another, and the dregs that remain: and similarly the dregs of silver. Most illustrious Prince, the instruction for all precious stones is one and the same, and is performed in a single way. ### *On the Balas Ruby.*

### *On the Sapphire.*

The Sapphire is composed of the double nature of quicksilver: namely, from the ethereal water of silver, and from the ethereal water of tin in a fourth part of the weight of the silver. Similarly, use the hardening water of silver and the hardening water of tin of the aforesaid weight. It is hardened to the softness of wax and boiled just as was said above concerning the others.

### *On the composition of Turquoise.*

Turquoise is composed of the nature of two ethereal waters and two restrictive waters. Therefore, take 4 drachms <note>original: "ʒ. quatuor"; a drachm was a common unit of weight in pharmacy and alchemy.</note> of the ethereal water of Venus <note>Venus is the alchemical symbol for copper.</note>, and 1 drachm of the ethereal water of Saturn <note>Saturn is the alchemical symbol for lead.</note>. Place this to harden while in its "soft wax" state in the hardening water of Venus mixed with the terrestrial water of lead, according to the weight of the aforementioned ethereal waters, and provide it with the same shaping processes as the other stones.

### *On the composition of the Emerald.*

The Emerald <note>original: "Exmiraldi" or "Xmiraldus"; a common medieval spelling for the emerald.</note> is composed or generated from one nature of two ethereal waters and two restrictive ones. Take as many parts as you wish of the terrestrial water of silver, and mix with it as much as you wish of the terrestrial water of copper, until you see that it has an intense or pale color, according to your desire. First, place the "soft wax" in its proper terrestrial waters for the space of a fifth of an hour, so that it may be better filled with the hardening virtue; first fill the "soft wax" with the ethereal water of copper, and set it to harden for one part of an hour. Afterward, rotate the "soft wax"—as was mentioned regarding the Carbuncle—in such a way that the hardening or terrestrial water touches the congealed ethereal water. Let it stand thus for three continuous days in the strong summer sun; in the spring and autumn for six continuous days; and in the winter for twelve days. When these times are finished, extract the hardened stone and make it pass through three shaping processes or decoctions <note>original: "decoctiones"; controlled heating or "cooking" stages.</note>, just as we described regarding the philosophers' stone in its practical application. By "shaping processes," understand these three decoctions: the first is called *Optasis*, the second *Optatesis*, and the third is called *Sulphur*, as we have explained above. <term>Optasis|From the Greek 'optēsis', referring to a stage of roasting or baking in alchemical furnace work.</term>

### *On the composition of the Heliotrope.*

The Heliotrope <note>Also known as Bloodstone, a green variety of chalcedony with red spots of iron oxide.</note> is composed of the very same nature from which the Emerald is composed, using the same weights and mixtures of waters. However, before the water of copper comes to a perfect hardening—so that it is in thickness like an egg white—you shall take your "soft wax" with tongs from the hardening water, and place upon that half-hardened mass 4 or 5 very small drops of the ethereal water of iron. Then take the "soft wax" with silver tongs and place it in the hardening water for one part of an hour. Afterward, extract it and place it in the hardening water for the duration of one *I Believe in God* and one *Hail Holy Queen* <note>original: "Credo in Deum" and "Salve regina"; in the absence of clocks, alchemists used the recitation of standard prayers to measure precise intervals of time.</note>, and provide it with hardening through

### *On the composition of the Camapheus.*

The Camapheus <note>Likely referring to the Agate or Onyx used for Cameos, known for its distinct layers of color.</note> is a stone having many and varied colors: some are white, others black, others red, and others between black and sky-blue and white, like chalcedonies. Each of these has its own distinct nature and power in its composition; but among all lapidaries, the red is most praised, though each is good according to its own proper nature. The white variety is composed of the ethereal water of silver <note>The Moon</note>, the ethereal water of tin <note>Jupiter</note>, and the ethereal water of lead <note>Saturn</note>, mixed in equal parts and placed to harden into a mass having the shape of a man <note>original: "figuram hominis"; potentially a reference to a carved figure or the "human" scale of the stone.</note> in the hardening water of silver and tin in equal weights. The red variety, however, is composed of the ethereal water of gold <note>The Sun</note> and the ethereal water of iron <note>Mars</note> placed in equal parts to harden in the terrestrial water of gold and the terrestrial water of iron mixed equally; or it can be composed of the ethereal water of silver mixed equally to harden in the hardening water of gold and silver. Likewise, the black variety is composed of the ethereal water of lead, the ethereal water of silver, and the ethereal water of gold, hardened in the terrestrial water of lead by the weight mentioned before. Afterward, place them in the sun, and let them pass through all three shaping stages.

### *How the Topaz is composed.*

The Topaz is composed of the dual nature of quicksilver <note>original: "argenti vivi"; mercury</note> reduced into the form of air. Therefore, take the ethereal water of gold and mix it with a fourth part of the ethereal water of iron, and place it in the mold to harden in the hardening water of gold, and do as we have said concerning the others.

### *On the composition of Chalcedony.*

Chalcedony is composed of the terrestrial water of iron and the terrestrial water of silver mixed equally, and placed in the mold to harden in the terrestrial water of iron and the moon <note>silver</note> mixed equally. Let it pass through all three shaping stages just like the others.

### *On the composition of the Beryl.*

The Beryl is composed of the dual substance of quicksilver: one part is from the ethereal water of silver, and the other is from the ethereal water of tin, which are said to be mixed equally in an airy nature. Fill your mold so that it may be hardened in the terrestrial water of silver and tin. Then, give it the shaping stages as we have described for the others.

### On the composition of Pearls.

The composition of pearls <note>original: "parlarum"; an older form for pearls, often called margaritas elsewhere in the text.</note> is made from a threefold substance of mercury <note>original: "argenti vivi"; literally "living silver," the base of many alchemical operations.</note> converted into the substance of ethereal water. Therefore, take the ethereal water of tin, and the ethereal water of lead, and the ethereal water of silver, mixed in equal parts. Let it be hardened in a wax mold within the hardening water of tin, and in the hardening water of silver and lead mixed equally; and afterward, let it pass through the shapings <note>original: "informationes"; the finishing or refining processes.</note> which we have described above.

### On the composition of Pearls by another way.

Pearls are composed by another way as follows: Pulverize small, tested pearls <note>original: "probas minutas"; small pearls of proven quality used as a "seed" or base.</note> into the finest powder, and dissolve them in the same water in which you dissolved common silver. This should be done over a digestion of I <note>In Lullian alchemy, letters of the alphabet (like I and H) refer to specific stages, degrees of heat, or chemical apparatuses defined in the author's "Alphabet."</note>, adding enough of the said water so that it floats above the pearls to the thickness of a middle finger. After the dissolution, a certain sliminess will float on top like a kind of film <note>original: "tela"; literally a web or cloth.</note>. And that film, most serene Prince, is the transparent form of oriental pearls. By what we have said, that chapter of our testament is clarified, in that part which treats of the making of pearls, which begins: *The showing of the virtues of the overflowing liquor.*

Likewise, after you perceive that the pearls have been liquefied inside by the water M <note>Another reference to the Lullian Alphabet, likely denoting a specific solvent or vessel.</note>, you shall separate the water with the sliminess of the pearls into another vessel, tilting the vessel gently so that none of the dregs go with the slimy water. If, however, there should be any dregs with the slimy water, strain it through a very clean silk cloth. After this, place that water in which the sliminess of the pearls remains into a flask with a long neck, over a digestion of H for nine days. When these have passed, that water will become one single body with the sliminess of the metal. By this, that chapter of our testament is clarified, which begins: *When you have these said pearls, it is a sacred white paste that you will liquefy by the power of the water.* <note>original: "Quando tu neuras celt dictes parles est pasta blanc sacram liquefacies per la virtut de laquet." This is a passage in Old Catalan or Occitan, typical of the Lullian corpus, even when the surrounding text is Latin.</note>

Afterward, you shall have your molds made of pure gold, or of silver gilded on the inside, which should be shaped to the likeness of any formed pearls. Similarly, have a rod of gold or gilded silver, and ensure that all the molds are divided into two parts. If the molds are round, or made in any other way, and require holes, you shall pierce those mold parts where they join together. Fill your molds with the paste of the powder which remained from the slimy water, so that each part of the mold is full of paste. Through the hole of the molds, insert a gold wire; do this for all of them, and let the paste stand thus in its molds for one natural day <note>A 24-hour period.</note>. When this has passed, if you see that the molds can be separated from the paste, pull those grains from the molds; if not, let them dry until you are able to extract the grains.

<summary>This page details two methods for creating artificial pearls using "ethereal waters" of metals and the dissolution of real pearl dust into a "slimy" essence that is then cast in gold molds.</summary>

# RAYMUNDUS LULLUS

And when you have extracted those grains from the soft substances already mentioned, place them to dry on a marble tray <note>original: "filara"; refers to a flat slab or specialized alchemical tray</note>, or in a glass tray, or some glazed vessel that is wide and flat. And cover it with a glass vessel or something else, so that dust does not touch the stones themselves. Let them stand there until they are well dried. And through what we have briefly said, that chapter in our *Testament* <note>The "Testamentum" is one of the most famous works attributed to Lullus, dealing with the transmutation of metals and gems.</note> and in our *Magistery* is clarified, which begins: "besides, afterwards an artificial measure of gold and quantity shall be made," etc.

And after the formation of the pearls and their drying, you should take a long gold wire and thread it through the hole of the pearls. Be as careful as you can not to touch them with your hand, except with some tongs of gilded silver or of gold. While you have them thus, have a certain glass vessel made in the shape of a hen's egg, and you will plug <note>original: "cavillabis"; to seal or peg shut</note> it on both sides. That which is inside should be set down. 

Likewise, place the pearls suspended by the gold wire in the "water of sliminess" <note>original: "aqua limositatis"; likely a viscous or mucilaginous solvent intended to give the pearls their luster</note>, which you have put into a digestion of H <note>In Lullian alchemy, letters of the alphabet refer to specific stages, degrees of heat, or chemical apparatuses; "H" typically refers to a specific level of heat in the furnace.</note> for nine days, in such a way that they are submerged in the water. Immediately put on the cover and let them stand so for two natural days. When these are finished, extract your pearls from that vessel and place them in the shade, where the sun does not touch them, for three natural days. 

Then apply to them the formation of <term>Optasim</term> <note>A specific finishing or refining stage in Lullian alchemy, likely derived from the Greek word for "roasting" or "baking."</note> in this way: You, most serene Prince, shall place three "tests" <note>original: "probas"; sample or trial pearls</note> on the gold wire, then put them into an eggshell which covers all three pearls, or more according to their size. Then others according to the size of the egg which you wish to contain them. Place the glass vessel or egg, and so on until they are arranged. 

And if it is summer time, let them stand thus in the sun for three natural days. In spring and autumn, for six days; in winter, for nine. But we advise you not to perform any <term>Obtetic</term> or <term>Obtatent</term> decoction <note>Technical alchemical terms for specific types of slow heating or "baking" processes.</note> for anyone in winter. Each day you shall turn the eggs or the aforementioned vessels every three hours. When these days are finished, pull out your pearls; then apply to them the formation of <term>Inlfuldeth</term> <note>A specialized term in the Lullian corpus, possibly of Arabic origin, referring to a final polishing or "fixing" stage.</note> for three days while they are placed in the vessel called the "perfectory" <note>original: "perfectorium"; a vessel used for the final completion of the alchemical work.</note>. When these are finished, place your pearls on the tripod of the <term>Athanor</term> <note>The "Athanor" is the standard alchemical furnace designed to provide steady, uniform heat over long periods.</note>, and you will see that they do not envy natural ones in any perfection; then use them.

### ->ON THE MEANING OF THE<-
### ->Letters.<-

**A** Signifies **God**, who is the first cause of this work.
**B** Signifies the **four elements** mixed together <note>original: "confusa"; implying the chaotic state of elements before they are refined</note> within metals.
**C** Signifies rectified **lunaria** <note>original: "lunariam"; likely referring to an alchemical solvent or "moon-water" associated with silver and the cooling nature of the Moon</note> in which the metals are dissolved.
**D** Signifies the **quintessence** <note>The "fifth essence," the purest and most medicinal part of a substance</note> of wine, or the quintessence in its state of perfection.
**E** Signifies the **soul of metals**, which is called the **Sulphur of nature** <note>In alchemy, "Sulphur" represents the active, combustible, and masculine principle of matter</note>.
**F** Signifies the **metals themselves**.
**G** Signifies the **slimes** <note>original: "limos"; referring to the primordial or sedimentary mud of the elements</note> of the elements.
**H** Signifies heat of the **first degree**, namely that of a **bath** <note>original: "balnei"; the 'balneum Mariae' or water bath, providing the gentlest heat</note>.
**I** Signifies heat of the **second degree**, specifically that of **ashes** <note>original: "cineris"; an ash bath provides a steadier and more intense heat than water</note>.
**K** Signifies heat of the **third degree**, the **sublimation** <note>The process where a solid turns into vapor and then back to solid, used to purify substances</note> of sulfur.
**L** Signifies the **soul of bodies**, that is, the **calx** <note>original: "calcem"; the fine powder remaining after a metal has been heated or "calcined"</note> immediately produced through the dissolution of the **menstruum** <note>A term for a powerful solvent, historically likened to biological solvents</note>.
**M** Signifies the **spirits** of perfected bodies.
**N** Signifies the **water of metals**.
**O** Signifies **air**.
**P** Signifies **fire**.
**Q** Signifies **glass instruments**.
**R** Signifies the **Stone** itself <note>The "Philosopher's Stone," the legendary goal of alchemy capable of transmuting metals and curing all disease</note>.

This system was designed to keep alchemical recipes secret from the uninitiated while providing a shorthand for practitioners.</summary>

# THE PRINTER TO THE READER.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'N' depicting a seated figure, possibly a scholar or deity, within a square frame with floral motifs.</image-desc>

*They believe man to be a **political animal** <note>original Greek: "πολίτικον ζώον" (politikon zoon); a reference to Aristotle’s definition of humans as naturally social beings</note> by nature: I believe it is by weakness and by **choice** <note>original Greek: "προαίρεσει" (proairesei); referring to a deliberate moral or intellectual decision</note>: For when man noticed the defect of his own nature, he strove with all his might to cure this disease by taking help from society. Thereafter, as necessity urged them, the various talents of men invented diverse arts; as enmities arose, they designed cities to protect their own possessions. Finally, as malice grew or luxury reached maturity, chance discovered or ingenuity invented the remaining arts. The entire lives of studious men are spent in preserving, expanding, or reforming these arts; so that since appetites differ according to the perceived goal, and the true will is hidden, a thing is pursued as if it were the truth. Many decline into **vain crafts** <note>original Greek: "ματαιοτέχνιαν" (mataiotechnia); the pursuit of useless or frivolous skills</note> in a **masterly fashion** <note>original Greek: "ἀρχιτεκτονικῶς" (architektonikos); performing a task with the skill of a master builder but toward a flawed end</note> because the goal is not well enough known; and just as the suitors of Penelope <note>In Greek mythology, the suitors who could not win Penelope's hand settled for her maidservants; here, it is a metaphor for scholars who fail to reach the "Truth" and settle for lesser knowledge</note>, unable to possess the mistress, turned to the handmaidens, so it is with those to whom nature has not granted a happy enough genius to see the truth itself with their eyes. Certainly, when they have seen it but are frustrated in the hope of obtaining it, they accept whatever is at hand—though I know not if that is a safe enough counsel. Indeed, the difficulty of the work to be undertaken ought not to block the path for those in whom some greatness of spirit still remains. Truly, since many arts have been discovered both for the sake of others and for one’s own utility, those which will benefit the public interest more should be sought by men with greater zeal—if indeed there is any art which spends its labor on relieving the inconveniences of human nature, such as poverty and disease, which they call the **sacred and divine art** <note>original Greek: "ἱερὰν τέχνην καὶ θείαν" (hieran technen kai theian); a traditional way of referring to alchemy and medicine</note>. In this art, when men of a former age found something, they committed it to writing; whence so many distinguished volumes of this craft have reached our own times. I, following their example, as much as...*

# THE BOOK OF **ARTEPHIUS**
## BEGINS, WHICH IS CALLED THE
### **KEY OF GREATER WISDOM**
->so it is called.<-

<image-desc>A large decorative woodcut initial 'D' featuring scrolling floral motifs inside a square border.</image-desc>

**D**IVIDED indeed is this book into three chapters, and no one is complete without the others. For the first requires the second and the third; and the third requires the first and the second. The first chapter treats of the composition of the **elements** <note>In alchemy, "elements" often refers not just to earth, air, fire, and water, but to the fundamental qualities of matter.</note>, both superior <note>The "superior" elements refer to the celestial bodies or the macrocosm.</note> and inferior <note>The "inferior" elements refer to terrestrial materials or the microcosm.</note>, and of equal and unequal natures, and of their conversion into one another, and their generation. The second treats of the generation of mineral bodies, both natural and artificial. The third treats of the generation of plants and animals, and of the binding <note>original Latin: *adligamento*, a technical term for the chemical or spiritual joining of substances.</note> of the body with the **spirit**, and also of the **soul** <term>Anima/Spiritus: In this context, the soul (anima) is often the life-force or volatile principle, while the spirit (spiritus) is the intermediary that links the physical body to the soul.</term> of the animal itself with the animal.

Let us therefore praise God, who is the inspector of all things, and there is nothing that can be hidden from Him; for He Himself is bound to His creatures through His word, and yet separated from them insofar as He transcends them. Indeed, I do not think that He created anything similar or equal to Himself; and among His great benefits, the greatest is that He bound our body with the most subtle of all elements, namely the soul, which sees things hidden and manifest—provided, however, that the virtues of the body do not predominate over it. For the more the forces of the body are strengthened, the more the virtues of the soul must necessarily be weakened; and the more the body itself is altered <note>In this context, "altered" suggests refined or purified through asceticism or alchemical processing.</note>, the more the intuition of the soul is made subtle. And for this reason, our master **Belenius** <note>Likely referring to Apollonius of Tyana, a Neo-Pythagorean philosopher often cited in medieval Arabic and Latin alchemical texts.</note>, the Philosopher, said: "Place your light in a clear glass vessel," and note that all the wisdom of this world revolves around these three things: namely, the binding of the corporeal soul with the corporeal soul, and the spiritual soul with the corporeal soul, and the spiritual with the spiritual. But the binding of a corporeal soul with a corporeal one is closer and easier than the spiritual with the spiritual. Concerning this third kind, the ancient Sages wished to write very little; for they said that no one could reach its knowledge unless his nature were divine and spiritual, and his birth...

In the beginning of all things, without the utterance of speech, He said: "Let there be such a creature." Afterward, nature was created by God, or rather the "prime matter" <note>original: *materia prima*. ...of the four spheres, concerning which we spoke above. The first of these is of coldness and humidity, which the ancient sages called the **sphere of the spirit**. Above that is the nature of equality, which they named the **sphere of the soul**. After this follows the nature of heat and humidity, which they called the **third sphere**. Finally, at the highest point, is the nature of heat and dryness, which they called the **fourth sphere**, and here things become fixed. 

And because, as I said before, when those first two natures were mixed with one another, there was no longer movement from top to bottom and vice versa, but rather all the spheres moved in a circular motion. We have already said that for every thing, the opposite extreme is its contrary, and that the motion from top to bottom is not only opposed by the motion from bottom to top, but also by rest. 

Therefore, we said that one part of the heat which had not mixed itself with the nature of coldness for the generation of humidity remained below, mixed with coldness. Because nature does not allow for a vacuum <note>original: *non est dare vacuum in natura*. A fundamental principle in pre-modern science stating that "nature abhors a vacuum" and will always move matter to fill an empty space.</note>, a part of coldness equal to it came to fill the place of that heat which had descended. 

Now, therefore, it is clear that these spheres were connected to one another. For the lowest sphere is of coldness and dryness, in which there is no heat at all. After it follows the sphere of coldness and humidity, where three-fourths are coldness and one-fourth is heat. Afterward comes the sphere of equality, which is the **sphere of the soul**, of which half is from the nature of heat and the other half is from the nature of humidity. We have already said that in the sphere of humidity, half is from the nature of heat and one-fourth is from the nature of coldness. The supreme sphere, which is after this one, is of the nature of heat and dryness, nor is there anything of coldness within it. 

Thus you see how these spheres are ordered in relation to one another.

### Chapter Two: On the Generation of Minerals.

Let us therefore speak of the generation of minerals. Some have said that the nature of all minerals is quicksilver <note>mercury</note> combined with sulfur. They argued that because the root of these minerals is quicksilver and sulfur, we should therefore prepare the root until we reach the branches. The cause of this <gloss>opinion</gloss> is that they considered the natures of mineral bodies only on the surface; for in the depths, if they had looked into the secrets of nature, they would never have fallen into such opinions. We say, therefore, that even if quicksilver and sulfur are the <term>first natural principles</term> <note>original: "prima naturalia"; the fundamental building blocks of physical matter in medieval science</note> of mineral bodies before their congealing <note>solidification or fixation</note>, nevertheless, after they have congealed, it is impossible for mineral bodies to be generated from that quicksilver and sulfur [individually]. This is because the congealing agent has already altered the substance into its own nature. 

<margin>in the beginning</margin> An example of this is the composition of soap: if one takes water extracted from ashes <note>lye</note> and oil along with certain other things, and boils them in a specific way, soap is generated from them. But if one took each ingredient by itself and boiled it until it congealed, and afterward tried to compose soap from them, he would not be able to do so. 

As for sulfur, in the beginning its nature was water—cold and moist—and afterward it was converted into air, whose nature is hot and moist. Later, it became fire, whose nature is hot and dry; and finally, with that fire, the water tempered itself, and it was a composition of male and female <note>Alchemists used gendered language to describe the union of opposing forces, such as the "male" active sulfur and the "female" passive mercury</note>. We say, therefore, that even if the nature or root of minerals is quicksilver with sulfur, we should not take the quicksilver from which the mineral bodies are already [formed], but rather we should take that which...

-> ### ARTEFIUS <-

...from these mineral bodies themselves, an example of which is evident in plants. For we know that the generation of a plant is from water combined with a subtle earthy substance, as we said before; yet if we were to take raw water and earth, we would never generate a plant. Therefore, we do not take the basic materials from which a plant is made, but rather that which comes from the plant—namely, its "egg" <note>original: "ovum"; in this context, it refers to the seed or the reproductive essence of the organism</note>—because we know that this "egg" is generated from the subtle earthy substance mixed with that water. We then commit it to the earth until that which was lacking is made complete.

And we also say that the generation of metals in the womb of the earth happens in this way: when the sun acts upon these lower regions, it heats the earth through its warmth, and a part of that heat remains in the interior of the earth. When the sun rises over the earth and finds that there is heat hidden within the earth—a heat naturally like itself—it must necessarily ascend together with a part of the newly generated heat.

<margin>+ water; a portion of the water dissolves it and converts it into vapor</margin>

When it encounters some portion of water, it dissolves it and converts it into vapor. This vapor moves upward until a proportionate amount of heat runs over it. But when the sun descends toward the west, that proportionate heat is diminished until the vapor is condensed and descends by dripping <note>original: "distillando"; medieval science viewed the natural water cycle and metallic formation as a giant natural distillation process occurring within the earth's crust</note>. Then, when the sun rises again and its heat fails as before, it descends a second time by dripping. In this way, it does not cease to continuously refine <note>original: "subtiliare"</note> and drip until all the "oil" <note>In alchemy, "oil" refers to the flammable or essential soul of a substance</note> that exists in that water is dissolved and mixed with the water itself, and the whole is converted into oil. 

If it finds some portion of sulfur and is mixed with it—and if the quantity of water is equal to the quantity of that sulfur, or a little more (specifically as much as is sufficient to incorporate it)—gold or silver is generated from it, and so with others according to the amount of its "cooking" <note>original: "decoctio"; the process of maturation through steady heat</note>. But if the quantity of sulfur is greater than the quantity of the water, there will be generated from them a mineral body that will not be among the ores of the seven <note>The "seven" refers to the traditional metals associated with the planets: gold, silver, copper, iron, tin, lead, and mercury</note>.

We have already said that in the artificial generation of these mineral bodies, we do not seek the raw materials from which the bodies are made, but rather that which comes from them, just as we illustrated with the plants. For we said that we take the "egg" of the plant and consider what that egg is made of; and after we know it to be from a subtle earthy substance mixed with water, we commit it to the earth. In the same way, among minerals, we take the "egg" itself, and then we consider from where it is generated. After we know from where it is generated—for we know that it must be nourished by those same things—we know that the thing from which it is genera-
