## TREATISE V.
### On the generation of Stones of every kind.

<image-desc>A small hand-drawn manicule (pointing hand) in the right margin, pointing towards the first line of the new chapter.</image-desc>
The matter of stone is the same as that of other things, and they are born in this way according to the purity of the locations. When the four Elements drip their vapor into the center of the earth, and the Archeus of nature <term>Archeus: The "internal chemist" or vital force believed to govern the growth and metabolism of minerals and living things within the earth.</term> ejects and sublimates it, this vapor passes through the places and pores of the earth, drawing all the impurity of the earth with it up to the surface. This is then congealed by the air; for what pure air creates, crude air congeals, because air has entry into air and they join together—for Nature rejoices in Nature. Thus rocks and stony mountains are formed, according to the size of the pores. The larger the pores of the earth, the better the place is purified. For while greater heat and a larger quantity of water pass through such a "breathing-hole," the earth is purified more quickly; consequently, metals are later born more easily in such places. Experience itself testifies to this, for Gold is sought and found nowhere else but in the Mountains, which rarely happens in a plain. Most often, such flat places are damp, not with vapor but with Elemental Water, which draws that vapor to itself; they embrace each other so closely that they are not easily separated. Afterwards, the Sun of the heavens digests this mixture and turns it into the rich clay used by potters. In places where there is coarse sand, and the vapor contains no rich oiliness or Sulfur, it creates herbs and grass in the meadows. There are also other precious stones, such as the Diamond, Ruby, Emerald, and other gems:

This color—which improves as it stays with that spirit because it has been refined—is raised with the spirit through many distilled repetitions. The spirit then has the power of entering imperfect things, and thus it introduces the color, which is then joined to that Water which is then partly congealed; thus it fills its pores and is fixed with it in an inseparable fixation. For all Water is congealed by heat if it is without spirit, but it is congealed by cold if it possesses spirit. But he who knows how to congeal Water with heat and join the spirit with it, will certainly find a thing a thousand times more precious than gold and every other thing. Therefore, let him cause the spirit to be separated from the water so that it may putrefy <note>original: "putrefat"; in alchemy, putrefaction was seen as the necessary "death" or breakdown of a substance before it could be reborn as something more perfect.</note> and the grain <note>the fundamental "seed" of the matter.</note> may appear; then, having rejected the dregs, let him lead the spirit back from on high into the Water and make them join together: for that union will generate a branch unlike the parents in form.

# TREATISE VI.
## *Concerning the second matter, and the putrefaction of things.*

We have spoken of the first matter of things, and how things are born from nature or seed—that is, how nature receives the matter from the Elements from which it generates seed. Now, however, we shall begin our discourse concerning the seed, and things generated from the seed.

Every thing that has a seed is multiplied in it, but this does not happen without the help of nature. For a seed is nothing other than air congealed in some body, or a moist vapor, and unless this is resolved by a warm vapor, it is of no use.

Therefore, let the investigators of the art know what a seed is, lest they seek a thing that does not exist; and let them know that it is triple, which from the four Ele- <meta>catchword: mentis (elements)</meta>

# ON THE SECOND MATTER.

...is produced from the [elements]: The first is the Mineral, which is discussed in this place; the second is the Vegetable; the third is the Animal. The Mineral seed is known by the Philosophers <note>original: "Philosophis"; in this context, the term refers to alchemists and natural philosophers who studied the hidden workings of nature.</note>; the Vegetable is common and ordinary, as we see in fruits; and the Animal is known through the imagination <note>original: "ex imaginatione"; likely referring to the formative power or the "idea" of the species that guides development.</note>. The Vegetable kingdom shows us how nature creates things from the four Elements. For it must be understood that Winter <note>original: "Hyems"</note> is the cause of putrefaction <note>original: "putrefactionis"; the process of breaking down matter so that new life can emerge.</note>, since it freezes the vital spirits in trees; and when these are released by the heat of the Sun (in which there is a Magnetic power that attracts all moisture), then the heat of nature, stirred by motion, drives the subtle vapor of water to the edges. This opens the pores of the tree and causes drops to distill, always separating the pure from the impure. 

Sometimes, however, the pure precedes the impure. The pure part is given off and congealed into flowers, while the impure part turns into leaves. The coarse and thick part becomes the bark. The bark of the tree remains fixed, but the leaves fall due to cold or heat when the pores are blocked. The flowers are congealed by a heat appropriate to them and bring forth fruit or seed—just like an apple, in which there is the <term>Sperma</term> <note>original: "Sperma"; here referring to the fleshy pulp of the fruit which surrounds the actual reproductive grain.</note>. The tree is not born from this fleshy pulp; rather, within that pulp is the seed or grain internally, from which the tree is born even without the pulp. For multiplication does not occur in the fleshy matter, but in the seed. Thus, we see with our own eyes how nature creates seed from the four Elements, so that we do not occupy ourselves with this work in vain. For that which has already been created does not need a creator <note>The author suggests that since nature has already provided the "seed," the alchemist's job is to work with it rather than trying to create life from scratch.</note>. 

Let it suffice to have advised the Reader with this example, but I return to the mineral subject proposed. Nature creates the mineral seed, or the seed of metals, in the bowels of the earth. Because of this, many do not believe such a seed exists in nature, for it is invisible. But it is no wonder that the ignorant doubt it, since even that which is before their eyes is not perceived by them, much less that which is invisibly hidden. 

But it is a most true principle that "that which is above is like that which is below," and vice versa <note>This is a fundamental Hermetic maxim from the Emerald Tablet, suggesting the laws of the heavens and the earth are identical.</note>. That which is born above ground is born from the same source as that which is below in the bowels of the earth. And what special right do vegetables have over metals, that God should implant a seed in them while undeservedly excluding the metals? Are metals not of the same dignity before God as trees? Let this be established as certain: nothing grows without seed, for where there is no seed, the thing is dead. It is necessary, therefore, either that the four Elements create the seed of metals, or that the elements produce metals without any seed. If they are produced without seed, then they can never be made perfect, since everything without a seed is imperfect in the nature of its composition. He who does not give faith to this undoubted truth is not worthy to search out the secrets of nature; for nothing is born in the world that lacks a seed. The seed of metals is truly and really implanted within them. Generation...

### TREATISE VI.

...however, its <note>Referring to the metal or mineral substance mentioned at the end of the previous page.</note> process happens thus. In the first operation of nature, the four elements distill—through the <term>Archaeus of Nature</term> <note>The "Archaeus" is a term popularized by Paracelsus, referring to the internal "master craftsman" or vital force that directs the development of life and matter.</note>—into the center of the earth a heavy vapor of Water, which is the **seed of Metals**, and is called **Mercury** because of its fluidity and its ability to join with every thing, not because of its essential nature; it is likened to **Sulphur** because of its internal heat, and after it has congealed, it becomes the radical moisture.

And although the body of metals is procreated from Mercury—which must be understood as the <term>Mercury of the Philosophers</term> <note>The essential, spiritual substance of the metal, rather than the common liquid quicksilver found in shops.</note>—nevertheless, those people should not be listened to who believe that **common mercury** is the seed of Metals. Such people mistake the "body" for the "seed," not considering that the aforementioned common mercury also contains its own seed within itself. The errors of all these people will become clear from the following example. It is manifest that humans have a seed through which they multiply: a Human's body is "Mercury," but the seed is hidden in the body, and compared to the body, its quantity in weight is tiny. Therefore, he who wishes to generate a Human should not take "Mercury," which is the body, but rather the seed, which is the congealed vapor of Water.

In the same way, common chemists proceed incorrectly in the "regeneration" of Metals: they dissolve metallic bodies—whether **Mercury**, **Gold**, **Saturn** <note>Lead</note>, or **Luna** <note>Silver</note>—and they corrode them with <term>strong waters</term> <note>Acids, such as nitric acid.</note> and other heterogeneous things not required for the true art. Afterward, they join them and force them together, not knowing that a human is not generated from a dissected human body, because the corruption of the body and the destruction of the seed has already occurred in that process. Every single thing is multiplied into male and female, as I mentioned in the treatise on the dual matter. The division of the sexes creates or produces nothing, but their proper union brings forth a new form. Therefore, **seeds** or **sperm** are to be taken, not bodies.

Take <note>original: "℞" or "Recipe"</note> therefore a **living Male** and a **living Female**; join these together so that they may conceive a sperm between them to procreate fruit according to their nature. For no mortal should believe they can create the **First Matter**: the first matter of man is the earth, and no man can create a Human from that; God alone knows how. But from the **Second Matter**, which has already been created, if it is placed in the proper location, nature will easily operate to generate that thing whose form is in the seed. The Artisan here does nothing except know how to separate the subtle from the thick and place it into the proper vessel. For this must be considered: as a thing is begun, so it is finished. From **one** come **two**, from **two** comes **one**, and no further. There is **one God**: from this one God a son was born; One gave two, and the two gave one—the **Holy Spirit** proceeding from both—and thus the world was made, and thus shall be its end.

# ON THE POSSIBILITY OF NATURE.

Consider the previous four points most exactly: you have in them the father and the son, and finally the Holy Spirit; you have the four elements, and you have the four lights—two celestial and two central. ## TREATISE VII.
### *On the power of the second matter.*

But so that you may more easily understand what this second matter is like, I will describe to you the powers by which you will recognize it. First, know that nature is divided into three kingdoms: There are two kingdoms, either of which can stand by itself, even if the other two did not exist. There is the mineral kingdom, the vegetable kingdom, and the animal kingdom. The mineral can subsist by itself, even if there were no humans in the world, nor any tree or herb. Likewise, the vegetable kingdom can stand by itself, even if there were no metal or animal; these two were created from one through one. The third, however, derives its life from the two aforementioned, without which it could not exist; it is more noble and more excellent than the previous two, just as it is also the last among them and dominates them, because power is always completed in the third, and multiplied in the second.

See, for instance, in the vegetable Kingdom: the **first matter** is the herb or the tree, which you do not know how to create—Nature alone does this. In this kingdom, the **second matter** is the seed, which you see, and in this the Herb or Tree is multiplied. In the Animal kingdom, the **first matter** is the beast or the human, whom you do not know how to create—and if you boast of it, you are vain and a liar; nature has done this. And even if you possessed the first matter according to the Philosophers, it would still be impossible for you to multiply that <term>central salt</term> <note>A hypothetical universal essence or "salt" that alchemists believed resided at the heart of all matter, acting as a link between spirit and body.</note> without gold. But as for the seed of Metals, only the sons of doctrine have known it. In vegetables, the seeds appear on the outside; the "kidneys" <note>The author uses "kidneys" (*renes*) metaphorically to describe the organ or site of metabolic transformation and maturation.</note> of its digestion is the warm air. In animals, the seed appears both inside and outside; the kidneys of its digestion are the kidneys of the man. In Minerals, Water is the seed in the center of their heart and life; the kidneys of its digestion is fire.

# TREATISE SEVEN
### *On the power of the second matter.*

<note>original: "cujusque,"</note>

The receptacle of the **Vegetable seed** is the earth; the receptacle of the **Animal seed** is the female's <term>matrix</term> <note>While literally meaning "womb," in alchemy, a matrix is any environment—spiritual, chemical, or biological—that provides the conditions for a seed to gestate.</note>; the receptacle of the **Mineral Water seed** is the air. These receptacles of the seeds are the congealings of bodies. That which is digestion is also solution; that which is putrefaction is also destruction. Furthermore, the power of every seed is to join itself to each thing within its own kingdom, because it is subtle and nothing other than air, which is congealed by "fatness" <note>An alchemical term for a combustible or oily principle, often related to Sulfur.</note> in water. It is recognized in this way: because it does not naturally mix with anything outside its own kingdom, it is not dissolved but congealed, since it does not require solution but solidification. 

It is necessary, therefore, for the pores of bodies to be opened so that the <term>sperma</term> <note>The visible vehicle or "husk" that carries the invisible seed.</note> may be emitted, in the center of which lies the **seed**, which is air. When that seed reaches its proper matrix, it is congealed and it congeals that which it finds—whether pure, or impure mixed with pure. As long as the seed is in the body, the body lives; when it is all consumed, the body dies. Indeed, all bodies are weakened after the emission of seed. Experience also testifies that men who indulge too much in <term>Venus</term> <note>A common euphemism for sexual activity or lust.</note> become weaker, just as trees bearing excessive fruit afterwards become sterile. The seed, therefore, as has now been repeated many times, is an invisible thing, but the **Sperma** is visible, and it is almost like a living Soul; it is not found in dead things. It is drawn out in two ways: gently and with violence. But because here the talk is only of its power, I say that nothing may be born without seed; all things are made by the power of the seed. Let the <term>sons of the art</term> know that seed is sought in vain in cut-off trees, for it is found only in those that are green.

## TREATISE VIII.

### *On Art, and how nature works in the seed through Art.*

Every seed is of no importance by itself if it is not placed, either by Art or by nature, into its proper matrix. And although the seed is in itself more noble than every other creature, nevertheless its matrix is the life which causes the **Sperma** or grain to rot <note>In alchemy, "putrefaction" or rotting is the first essential step of transformation, allowing the life-force to be released from its old form.</note> and causes the solidification of the "pure point." Moreover, it nourishes that seed with the heat of its body and makes it grow; and this happens in all the three aforementioned kingdoms of nature. This occurs naturally through months, years, and seasons. 

Truly, that **Art** <note>Meaning Alchemy, the "Great Art" that seeks to perfect and accelerate natural processes.</note> is wise which can shorten the process in the mineral and vegetable kingdoms, but not in the animal. In the mineral kingdom, Art completes only that which nature cannot, because of the "raw air" which has filled the pores of the body with its violence.

# TREATISE IX.

## *On the mixing of Metals, or on the drawing forth of the Metallic seed.*

We have spoken of nature, of art, of the body, and of the <term>sperma</term> <note>The visible vehicle or "husk" that carries the invisible seed.</note> and the seed: now let us descend to practice—namely, how Metals ought to be mixed, and what their correspondence is with one another. Know, therefore, that the woman does not differ from the man; they are from the same seed and both are born in one matrix. Nothing was lacking except <term>digestion</term> <note>The process of "ripening" or "maturing" a substance through sustained natural or artificial heat.</note>, and that the matrix should be purer in blood and salt. In the same way, the Moon <note>Silver</note> is from the same seed as the Sun <note>Gold</note> and the same matrix; but the matrix had more water than digested blood, according to the time of the celestial Moon. 

So that you may more easily imagine how metals unite to emit and receive seed, look at the heavens and the spheres of the planets. You see that Saturn <note>Lead</note> is the highest, followed by Jupiter <note>Tin</note>, then Mars <note>Iron</note>, after that the Sun <note>Gold</note>, followed by Venus <note>Copper</note>, then Mercury <note>Quicksilver</note>, and in the last place the Moon <note>Silver</note> is stationed. Consider now that the virtues of the planets do not ascend, but descend. Experience itself has also shown that Mars is not made from Venus, but Venus is made from Mars, as it is one sphere lower. Likewise, Jupiter is easily transmuted into Mercury, because Jupiter is the second from the <term>firmament</term> <note>The sphere of the fixed stars, the outermost boundary of the visible universe.</note> and Mercury is the second from the earth. Saturn is the first from heaven, and the Moon the first from the earth. The Sun mixes with all, but it is never improved by the lower things. Do not let it escape your notice that there is a great correspondence between Saturn and the Moon, in the middle of which the Sun is placed, just as between Jupiter and Mercury, in the middle of whom the Sun also stands. In exactly the same way between

# TREATISE NINE

->*On the mixing of Metals, or on the drawing forth of the Metallic seed.*<-

...trix. Consider Mars and Venus <note>original: "Martem & Venerem"; representing Iron and Copper respectively.</note>, who both have the Sun between them. <term>Chemists</term> <note>original: "Chymistæ"; practitioners of the "Sacred Art" of laboratory transformation.</note> know how to change Iron into Copper, or Venus, without the influence of the Sun: they also know how to make Mercury from Jupiter <note>Tin</note>; and there are some who fashion the Moon <note>Silver</note> out of Saturn <note>Lead</note>. But if they knew how to manage the nature of the Sun in these mutations, they would surely find a treasure more precious than any other. Therefore I say, one must not be ignorant of which Metals are to be joined together, and whose Natures correspond to one another. Furthermore, there is one particular Metal that has the power to consume the others: for it is almost like their water and almost their mother. Only one single thing, the <term>radical moisture</term> <note>The fundamental "life-fluid" of a substance that cannot be destroyed by fire.</note>—namely that of the Sun and Moon—resists it, and is actually improved by it. To reveal it: it is called <term>Chalybs</term> <note>Literally "Steel" or "Star-Iron," often used in alchemy to refer to a magnetic agent that attracts the "astral seed."</note>. If gold is joined with it eleven times, the gold emits its seed and is weakened almost to the point of death. The Chalybs conceives and generates a son more glorious than the father; afterward, when the seed of the newborn is placed into its own matrix, it purges that matrix and makes it a thousand times more fit for bringing forth the best fruits. There is also another Chalybs, similar to this one and created by nature itself, which knows how to draw out from the rays of the sun—by a wonderful force and virtue—that which so many men have sought, and which is the very principle of our work.

## TREATISE X.
### *On the supernatural generation of the son of the sun.*

We have treated those things which nature creates, and which God has created, so that the searchers of the art might more easily understand the possibilities of nature. But so that I do not delay any longer, I proceed to the method and the art of fashioning the <term>Philosophers' Stone</term>. The Stone, or <term>tincture</term> <note>A substance capable of "dyeing" or transforming the inner nature of base metals into gold.</note>, is nothing other than gold digested to the highest degree. For the gold of the common people is like a herb without seed; only when it ripens does it produce seed. Likewise, when gold matures, it gives forth a seed or tincture. But someone may ask: why does gold or another Metal not produce seed? The reason given is this: because it cannot reach maturity due to the crudeness of the air. It does not have sufficient heat, though it happens in certain places that pure gold is found because nature wished to perfect it, but was hindered by the crude air. For example, we see that <term>orange trees</term> <note>original: "Arantiorum"; oranges were often used as an analogy for the "Golden Apples" of the Hesperides, requiring a warm climate to ripen.</note> grow here indeed just like other trees; but in Italy and elsewhere, where their native soil is, they provide and bear fruit because the soil has sufficient heat. In these colder places, however...

One only is truly natural; the second is violent, under which all others are comprised. 

The natural solution is of such a kind that the pores of the body are opened in **our Water**, so that the digested seed may be emitted and placed into its own matrix. Indeed, **our Water** is a celestial water, not wetting the hands <note>original: "non madefaciens manus"; a classic alchemical paradox describing a substance that behaves like a liquid but does not leave a wet residue, often identified with Philosophical Mercury</note>, not the common sort, but almost like rainwater. The **Body** is the gold that gives the seed. **Our Moon** <note>original: "Luna nostra"; refers to "philosophical silver," a refined state of the metal rather than the common silver used in coinage</note> is not the common silver, which receives the seed of the gold. It is governed afterward by our continuous fire, for seven months, and sometimes ten, until our water consumes three and leaves one, and this in double measure; afterward it is nourished by the **milk of the earth** <note>original: "lacte terræ"</note>, or its fatness, which is born in the breasts of the earth, and is governed or preserved from putrefaction by the **salt of nature**. And thus is generated that infant of the second generation <note>The "infant" is a common metaphor for the Philosopher's Stone or the Elixir in its early stage of development</note>. Now let us proceed from Theory to practice.

# TREATISE XI.

->by means of art.<-

The discourse has been scattered through many chapters using examples, so that the practice might be more easily understood, which must be performed by imitating nature in this manner. <term>℞</term> <note>The symbol for "Recipe," meaning "Take."</note>. First, the earth will be dissolved in water, which is called the **Mercury of the Philosophers**, and that water dissolves those bodies...

...of the Sun and Moon <note>original: "Solis & Lunæ"; Gold and Silver</note>, and it consumes them so that there remains nothing but a tenth part with one part, and this will be the **metallic radical moisture** <term>radical moisture: the essential, life-giving fluid or "soul" of a metal that allows it to be transformed</term>. If it stains the iron, have ready the water about which we shall speak later, and pour in as much of that water as there was raw copper <note>original: "aeris"; often used generically for base metal</note> that entered. Cook it again with the previous fire until it stains once more. Thus far my experience has reached; I can do no more, I have found no more.

Indeed, that water ought to be the **menstruum of the world** <term>menstruum: a solvent or liquid medium used to extract or dissolve substances</term> from the sphere of the Moon, rectified so many times that it can **calcine** <term>calcine: to reduce a substance to a fine powder or ash through heat</term> the Sun <note>Gold</note>. Here I wished to reveal all things to you; and if you understand my meaning—even if you do not understand every syllable—I have revealed everything, especially in the first and second work.

Regarding the fire, there still remains more to be said. The first fire, or the fire of the first operation, is a continuous fire of one degree which surrounds the matter. The second is the natural fire, which digests and fixes the matter. I tell you the truth: I have laid open the governance of the fire, if you understand nature. 

Regarding the vessel, there still remains more to be said. It must be the vessel of nature, and two suffice: for the first work, a round vessel should be made; in the second, a slightly smaller glass in the shape of a **phial** or an egg <note>original: "Phiolæ vel ovi"; referring to the "Philosophical Egg," the sealed glass flask used for the final stages of the Great Work</note>. But above all, know that the fire of nature is one; whatever different things it works, the distance of the locations brings it about. Likewise, the vessel of Nature is one, but we use two for the sake of brevity. The matter is one, but from two substances. 

If, therefore, you intend your mind toward creating things, first consider things already created. If you cannot understand these things that are before your eyes, much less can you understand things yet to be created which you desire to produce. For know that you can create nothing—which is the property of God alone—but to make hidden things lying in the shadow become apparent, and to lift the shadow from them: this is granted to the intelligent Philosopher by God through nature. Consider, I pray, the water that seems simple to us: who would now believe that it contains in itself all things that the world has—hard stones, salts, air, earth, fire—though the water appears simple in itself? What shall I say of the earth, which contains in itself water, fire, salts, air, and in itself seems but bare earth? O marvelous nature, which knows how from water...

->### ON THE PRACTICE AND PREPARATION OF THE STONE<-

...water to produce wonderful fruits in the earth, and to supply them with life from the air: All these things happen, and the eyes of common men do not see them, but the eyes of the intellect and imagination perceive them with a most true vision. For the eyes of the wise see nature differently than common eyes. For example: The eyes of the common people see the Sun as hot; the eyes of the **Philosophers** <note>original: "Philosophorum"; here referring specifically to alchemists and natural philosophers</note>, on the contrary, see the Sun rather as cold, but its motions as hot. For its acts and effects are perceived through the distance of places. The **fire of nature** <note>original: "Ignis naturæ"</note> is one and the same with it: just as the sun is the center among the spheres of the planets, and from this center of heaven it scatters heat downward by its motion, so in the center of the earth is the **Sun of the earth** <term>Sun of the earth: also called the "central sun" or "central fire," a theoretical heat source at the world's core believed to drive all geological and alchemical growth</term>, which by its perpetual motion drives heat or rays upward to the earth's surface. 

This **intrinsic heat** <note>original: "calor intrinfecus"</note> is much more effective than this **elemental fire** <note>the common fire we use in kitchens or furnaces</note>, but it is tempered by earthly water, which day by day penetrates the pores of the earth and cools it; in the same way, the air, which day by day flies around the world, tempers the celestial Sun and its heat. And were it not for this, all things would be consumed by such heat, nor would anything be born. Just as that invisible fire, or central heat, would consume all things if water did not intervene, so the heat of the sun would destroy all things without the intermediary air. 

I will say briefly how these elements act among themselves: In the center of the earth is the central Sun, which by its motion, or that of its firmament, gives great heat, which extends itself all the way to the earth's surface. That heat causes the air in this way: The **matrix of the air** <term>matrix: the source or "womb" from which an element is generated</term> is water, which gives birth to children of its own nature, but different and much more subtle. For where the entry of Water is denied, air enters; when afterward that central heat, which is perpetual, acts, it makes the water distill and heat up, and thus that water, by the force of heat, is turned into air, and in this way, it breaks out to the surface of the earth because it does not allow itself to be enclosed. 

Where it has cooled afterward, it is resolved into water in opposite places. Meanwhile, it also happens that not only air but also Water goes out, just as it appears when black clouds are lifted into the air by violence. Let this domestic example be a matter for you: if you make water boil in a pot, you will see with a gentle fire, gentle vapors and winds; with a more vehement fire, thicker clouds will appear. In exactly the same way the central heat operates: it elevates subtle water into the air; that which is thick from salt or fatness it distributes to the earth, from which various things are born. The residue becomes rocks and stones. Someone might object: if the matter were so, then it ought to happen continually, yet often no wind is felt. I respond: if water is not violently poured into the **distillation vessel** <note>original: "distillatorium"; an alchemical vessel used for heating and condensing</note>, no wind is made, for a little water [excites] a little...

...brings wind: you see that thunder does not always happen, even if there is rain and wind, but only when, by the force of air, turbid water is carried to the **sphere of fire** <note>original: "sphæram ignis"; in the ancient cosmological model, this was the region above the air and below the moon</note>, for fire does not endure water. You have an example before your eyes: when you pour cold water into a hot furnace, thunderous sounds are provoked. The reason why water does not enter those places and cavities uniformly is that there are many such vessels and locations; sometimes one concavity pushes the winds and water away from itself for several days or months, until a **recoil** <note>original: "repercussio"; a backflow or reflection of force</note> of the water occurs again, as we see in the sea, whose waves are sometimes driven for many miles before they meet a recoil and return. 

But to return to our subject: I say that fire or heat is the cause of the motion of the air, and the life of all things, and the earth is the nurse or receptacle of all these. But if there were no water to cool the earth and our air, then the earth would be dried out for two reasons: namely, because of the heat of the **central motion** <note>the heat generated by the earth's core</note> and the heat of the **celestial sun**. 

Nevertheless, this drying happens in some places when the pores of the earth are blocked so that moisture cannot penetrate. Then, through the correspondence between the celestial and central suns—because they have a **magnetic force** <note>original: "vim... magneticam"; an early reference to the idea of invisible attraction between celestial and terrestrial bodies</note> between them—the earth is ignited by the sun, and thus, sometimes even a grave **disaster** <note>original: "cades," likely a typo for "clades" (catastrophe or destruction)</note> befalls the orbit of the world. 

Therefore, see to it that such an operation exists in our "earth," so that the central heat can change water into air, that it may go forth into the open world and scatter the residue (as I said) through the pores of the earth. And now, in the opposite way, let the air be turned into water much more subtle than the first was. This shall be done thus: if you give gold and silver to our **Old Man** <note>original: "seni nostro"; an alchemical personification of the base matter or the "Old King" requiring rejuvenation</note> to swallow, so that he consumes them; and finally, as he is about to die, let him be burned, and let his ashes be scattered in water. Cook these until it is enough, and you have a medicine for curing **Leprosy** <term>Leprosy: in alchemy, "leprosy" refers to the impurities and "sickness" found in base metals like lead or copper, which must be "cleansed" to reach the perfection of gold</term>. 

At least take heed of this: do not mistake the cold for the hot, or the hot for the cold. Mix natures with natures; if there is something contrary to nature (since only one thing is necessary to you), separate it, so that Nature becomes similar to Nature. Do this by fire, not by hand. Know that if you do not follow Nature, all things are in vain. And here I have told you, by the holy God, what a father owes to a son. He who has ears, let him hear; and he who has senses, let him pay attention.

# CONCERNING THE STONE, AND ITS VIRTUE.

...the **second matter** <term>materia secunda: the refined substance or "seed" that the alchemist works with, as opposed to the raw, universal "first matter"</term>, concerning bodies and seeds, and concerning their use and virtue: I have also written out the practical method for making the **Philosopher’s Stone**; but concerning its virtue only, as much as nature has granted me and experience has revealed to me, I will now disclose. But so that I may first encompass the argument of all these treatises summarily and in few words—so that the God-fearing reader may follow my mind and my meaning—the matter stands thus.

If anyone doubts the truth of the art, let them read the copious writings of the most ancient Philosophers, verified by reason and experience; as they are worthy of trust in their own art, their faith should not be disparaged. But he who does not grant them faith—we know then that one must not dispute with someone who denies principles: for the deaf and the "mute-tongued" <note>original: "mutiloqui"; those who lack the proper language to discuss the art</note> cannot [participate]. I have said that the art is true, for what prerogative would all things in this world have over metals? Why should we undeservedly exclude these alone—through the denial of their seed—from the supreme Creator's universal blessing of multiplication, which the sacred scriptures affirm was bestowed and imparted to all created things immediately from the founding of the world? If indeed they possess a seed, who is so foolish as not to believe that they can be multiplied in their own seed? In its own nature, the art of **Chemistry** <note>original: "Chymiae"; used here in the traditional sense of alchemy</note> is true, and nature is true, but rarely is there a true Artist: there is one nature, and one art, but many artists. Moreover, whereas nature creates things from the Elements, it generates them by the will of God from the **first matter** <term>materia prima: the formless, fundamental substance of the universe known only to God</term>, which God alone knows. Nature creates those things and multiplies them from the **second matter**, which the Philosophers know. Nothing happens in the world without the will of God and of nature. 

For any element is in its own sphere, but one cannot exist without the other; one lives from the other, and yet even when joined they do not agree. However, **water** is the most worthy of all the Elements, because it is the mother of all things. The spirit of fire floats upon this; because of fire, water becomes the "first matter"—namely through the struggle of fire with water—and thus are generated winds or suitable vapors, so that it may be congealed with the earth by the **raw air** <note>original: "aerem crudum"</note> which was separated from it from the beginning. This happens without ceasing by perpetual motion, because fire or heat is not excited otherwise than by motion; this is easy to see at the blacksmith's forge when he grinds iron with a file, which by more vehement friction heats up just as if it had glowed white-hot in a fire. Motion, therefore, causes heat; heat moves the water, and the motion of the water causes the air, which is the life of all living things. Thus things grow in this manner, as I said above: namely from water. For from its more subtle vapor, subtle and light things arise; from its oil, heavy things and those of greater value; and from its salt, things far [exceeding] the former...

...more beautiful. Because nature is sometimes hindered from being able to produce hard things—seeing as vapor, oiliness, and salt are often stained and mix themselves into the places of the earth—experience has therefore taught us to separate the pure from the impure. Therefore, if you wish for nature to be improved in its action, dissolve any body, and separate that foreign matter <term>Heterogeneum: dissimilar or external substances that contaminate the purity of a mineral</term> which has attached itself to the nature of the thing. For know that the **central salt of nitre** <note>original: "sal nitri centrale"; likely referring to the "universal salt" or saltpeter, seen by alchemists as a vital celestial salt that acts as a bridge between the spiritual and material</note> does not accept more from the earth than it has need of, whether that earth be pure or impure. The oiliness of the water, however, behaves differently, for it is never found in a pure state; Art must purge it through a double heat, and then join it back together.

### EPILOGUE OR CONCLUSION OF
### *these twelve Treatises.*

I have written the preceding twelve Treatises, friend reader, for the sake of the **sons of the art** <term>filiorum artis: a traditional term for initiates or sincere students of alchemy</term>, so that before they apply their hands to the work, they might have knowledge of Nature’s operation—namely, how she produces things through her working—lest they attempt to enter the gate without keys, or "draw water with a sieve" <note>A classical metaphor for a futile or impossible task</note>. For he who stretches his hands toward these labors without a knowledge of nature labors in vain; in this most holy and true science, he wanders in the darkness of night. For such a man, the Sun does not shine; he dwells in a thick shadow, as if the moon does not appear at night. 

Nature possesses its own **light** <term>lumen naturae: the "light of nature," an invisible guiding intelligence or spiritual insight that allows the alchemist to see beyond physical appearances</term> which is not visible to our physical eyes. To our eyes, the "shadow" of Nature is the physical body; but if the light of nature radiates upon someone, the cloud is immediately lifted from their eyes. Without any hindrance, they are able to behold the point of our **Magnet** <note>original: "Magnetis nostri"; here referring to a central attractive principle or substance that draws down celestial influences</note> which corresponds to both centers of radiation: namely, that of the sun and that of the earth. For the light of Nature penetrates that far, and lays open internal things. 

Let this be an example for you: suppose a youth of twelve years and a girl of the same age are dressed in identical clothing. If they are placed next to each other, no one will be able to tell which is the male and which is the female. Our eyes cannot penetrate the surface; therefore, our sight deceives us and accepts false things for true. But when their clothes are removed and they are stripped bare so that they appear just as Nature formed them, each is easily recognized in their own sex. In exactly the same way, our intellect creates a "shadow of the shadow" of Nature. For the naked body in a human is but the shadow of the **layers of Nature** <note>original: "feminis Naturae"; possibly a corruption of "fimbriis" (borders/fringes) or referring to the "veils" of nature</note>. Just as the human body is covered by garments, so too is **human nature** <term>natura humana: the inner essence or "seed" of man</term> covered by a body—a nature which God has reserved for Himself to cover and uncover. I could here discourse at length and philosophically about the dignity of man, his creation, and his generation, but since such things are not...

# OF THE AUTHOR

Whatever is made, is made by fire, as has been sufficiently explained in the preceding sections, and is stated here in place of a conclusion.

Farewell, kind reader, and for a long time—to the glory of the Divine Name, the salvation of your soul, and the benefit of your neighbor—enjoy these labors, which have been verified through my own experience.

### BY THE SAME AUTHOR, TO THE SONS OF 
### *Truth; A Philosophical Enigma.*

Now to you, **sons of science**, <note>Latin: *filii scientiæ*. A traditional way for alchemists to address their students or fellow initiates.</note> I have uncovered everything from the bubbling source of the universal fountain, so that nothing further remains. For in my preceding treatises, I have sufficiently explained nature through examples: I have revealed both theory and practice as far as was permitted. But lest anyone should complain of **Laconism**, <note>original: *Laconismo*. A reference to the Spartans of Laconia, known for their extreme brevity of speech. The author is saying he doesn't want to be accused of being too brief or cryptic.</note> claiming I have omitted something, I shall yet describe the whole art to you enigmatically, so that you may see how far I have progressed under God’s guidance. There are infinite books treating this art, yet in hardly any of them will you find the truth revealed to you to the extent that I have wished to provide. I have done this because I have conversed with many who thought they understood the writings of the Philosophers well, but I discovered that they explained those same writings in a way far more complex and subtle than Nature—which is simple—required. Indeed, all my truthful sayings always seemed too cheap and unbelievable to those who think themselves "deep" thinkers. It has happened several times that I suggested the art word-for-word to certain people, but they could by no means follow it, not believing that there is **Water in our Sea**, <note>A common alchemical metaphor. The "Sea" is the mercury of the philosophers or the universal solvent; the "Water" is the life-giving spirit within it.</note> and yet they still wished to be seen as Philosophers. Since they could not understand my words when spoken aloud, I do not fear (as other Philosophers have feared) that someone might grasp this too easily; I say it is a **Gift of God**. It is true that if the **alchemical** <note>original: *Chymico*.</note> study required a razor-sharp, subtle intellect, and if the matter were of a kind that could be seen by the eyes of the common people, I would find their minds well-suited for investigating such things. But I tell you: be simple, and do not be over-clever until you have found the **Secret**, <note>Latin: *Arcanum*. The hidden "heart" or "mystery" of the alchemical process.</note> for once you possess it, wisdom will necessarily follow. Then you will not lack the ability to write infinite books, which will be far easier for one who is at the center and sees the thing itself, than for one who walks around the circumference and knows nothing but hearsay. You now have the **secondary matter** <note>Latin: *Materiam secundam*. In alchemical theory, *Materia Prima* is the universal raw substance of the universe, while *Materia Secunda* is that substance once it has been "specified" or prepared into a particular form (like a metallic seed) ready for the Great Work.</note> of all things most clearly described. But I commend this caution to you: if you wish to reach this secret, know that first God must be prayed to, and then your neighbor must be loved. Finally, do not imagine things to be so complex that Nature knows nothing of them, but stay—stay, I say—on the simple path of Nature, because in simplicity you will more quickly

->ÆNIGMA PHILOSOPHICUM.<-

...to touch [the matter], just as you will be able to see it in its refinement. Do not always cling to syllables when reading my writings, but in your reading, consider Nature and its possibilities. Before you gird yourselves for the work, imagine diligently what you seek, and what the goal and end of your intention may be: for it is much better to fail first in the mind and imagination than in reality, with your hands and your expenses. And I tell you this: you must seek a certain thing that is hidden, from which is made (in a wonderful way) a humidity that dissolves gold without violence or noise. Indeed, it does so as gently and naturally as ice melts by the benefit of warm water. If you have found this, you have the matter from which gold is produced by Nature. And although all metals and all things have their origin from it, nothing is so friendly to it as gold; for impurity clings to other things, but none to gold, therefore it is like a mother to it. 

And so I finally conclude: if you do not wish to be cautious through these writings and warnings of mine, hold me excused—I who wish you well. I have acted faithfully as far as was permitted, as becomes a man of good conscience. If you ask who I am, I am a **cosmopolite** <note>original: *cosmopolita*. A "citizen of the world." This was the famous pseudonym of the alchemist Michael Sendivogius.</note>. If you know me, and desire to be good and honest men, you will remain silent. If you do not know me, do not inquire about me, for no more shall be revealed by me to any mortal as long as I live than what has been done in this public writing. Believe me, if I were not a man of such state and condition as I am, nothing would be more pleasant to me than a solitary life, or to hide away like **Diogenes** <note>A Greek philosopher who famously lived in a barrel to demonstrate his rejection of worldly needs and social status.</note> under his barrel. For I see that all things that exist are vanity; that fraud and greed have prevailed where everything is for sale, and that wickedness has overcome virtue. I see better things before my eyes in the future life, and in these I rejoice. Now I do not wonder, as I did before, why Philosophers, having obtained such a **medicine** <note>The Philosopher's Stone, often described as a universal medicine for both metals and the human body.</note>, did not care to prolong their days; for the next life is so present before the eyes of every Philosopher, just as your own face appears to you in a mirror. If God gives you the desired end, you will believe me afterward, and you will not reveal yourself to the world.

There were indeed many who partly tried to lead the spring water there through channels, and partly also elicited it from various things, but the attempted labor was in vain, because in those places it could be had by no means; and if it was had, it was nonetheless useless and poisonous: unless it came from the rays of the Sun or Moon [☽], which few were able to provide; and whoever had favorable fortune in completing this, could never attract more than ten parts.

# THE AUTHOR'S 

...first: After the decoction <note>The process of boiling or heating a substance in a liquid to extract its essence or mature it.</note>, it is an immortal fruit, possessing life and blood; for this blood makes all barren trees bear fruit of the same nature as the apple. I asked: "Can it not be further improved?" He said, "According to the philosophical writings, it can be raised <note>term: **Exaltation** (exaltari): A process by which a substance is raised to a higher state of potency or "virtue."</note> to ten, then to one hundred, then to a thousand, and ten thousand, and so on." I pressed him: "My Lord, do many know this water, and does it have a proper name?" He cried out openly, saying: "Few have known it, but all have seen it, and see it, and love it. It has many and various names. But its proper name is the **Water of our Sea**, the **Water of Life**, which does not wet the hands <note>original: *Aqua maris nostri, Aqua vitæ, non madefaciens manus*. This refers to "Philosophical Mercury," a substance that behaves like a liquid but does not dampen surfaces like common water.</note>."

I asked again: "Do others use it for other things?" He said, "Every creature uses it, but invisibly." I asked: "Is anything born in it?" And he? "From it all things in the world are made, and in it they live; but strictly speaking, there is nothing in it, but it is a thing that mixes itself with every thing." I asked: "Is it useful without this fruit of the tree?" To this he said: "At this time, not at all; since it is improved only in the sun by this fruit of the Solar Tree." I began to ask again: "Lord, I pray you, name it for me with such a clear name that I can have no further doubt." But he, raising his voice, cried out so loudly that he woke me from my sleep; therefore I could ask no more, nor did he wish to answer me further. Nor can I tell you more; be content with these things, and believe that it is not possible to speak more clearly. For if you do not perceive these things, you will never master the books of the other Philosophers.

After Saturn's unexpected and sudden departure, a new sleep overcame me, and **Neptune** appeared to me once more in visible form. He congratulated me on the happiness I found present in the **Gardens of the Hesperides** <note>A mythological garden of golden apples; here, it symbolizes the stage of the Great Work where the alchemical gold begins to "ripen."</note> by showing me a mirror in which I saw all of Nature laid bare. After various words exchanged back and forth, I thanked him for the favors shown—namely, that by his guidance I had not only entered this most pleasant Garden but had also come into that most desired conversation with Saturn. But because some difficulties still remained to be sought and investigated due to Saturn’s unforeseen departure, I aske— <meta>catchword: vi enixè (strongly)</meta>

# PHILOSOPHICAL ENIGMA 507

...I asked him earnestly, so that on this desired occasion he might remove my doubt. I addressed him with these words: "Lord, I have read the books of the Philosophers asserting that all generation occurs through a male and a female, and yet I have only seen the fruit of the **Solar Tree** in my dreams, with **Saturn** <note>In alchemy, Saturn often represents Lead or the initial, "heavy" stage of the work (the Black Phase).</note> placing it upon our **Mercury** <note>The fluid, transformative principle of the work.</note>. I believe also that you, as the Lord of this Sea, know these things well; I pray you, answer my question."

But he replied: "It is true, my son; all generation occurs through a male and a female. However, because of the distinction between the three kingdoms of Nature, a four-legged animal is born in one way, and a worm in another. For although worms possess eyes, sight, hearing, and the rest of the senses, they are produced through **putrefaction** <note>term: **Putrefaction** (*putrefactio*): A central alchemical process where a substance is allowed to decay or "rot" in a moist heat, believed to be the necessary precursor to new life and purification.</note>, and their 'place'—the earth in which they rot—acts as the female.

"So it is in the philosophical body: the mother of this thing is your 'water' that has been mentioned so many times, and whatever is born from it is born through putrefaction, in the manner of worms. For this reason, the Philosophers have called it the **Phoenix** <note>The mythical bird that burns and rises from its own ashes; it represents the "Red Stage" or the final perfection of the Alchemical Stone.</note> and the **Salamander** <note>A legendary creature capable of living in fire; it represents a substance that has become "fixed" and can withstand the highest heat without being destroyed.</note>. If it were made from the conception of two separate bodies, it would be a thing subject to death; but because it revives itself—the prior body having been destroyed—another incorruptible thing flashes forth.

"For indeed, the death of things is nothing other than the separation of one part from another. And in this Phoenix it happens thus: that the life separates itself from the corruptible body."

I asked further: "My Lord, are there different things or a composition of various things in this work?"

But he said: "It is a single thing, to which nothing else is mixed except the **philosophical water** <note>The "Universal Solvent" or "Mercurial Water" used to dissolve and then nourish the alchemical matter.</note>, which was revealed to you several times in your sleep. This water must be in a tenfold proportion to one part of the body. And believe firmly and without doubt, my son, that those things revealed to you by me and Saturn through dreams on this Island—according to the custom of this region—are by no means mere dreams, but the purest truth. Only **Experience**, the mistress of all things, will be able to reveal this to you with God’s assistance."

As I sought to ask more, he departed without response after saying farewell. I was then awakened from sleep and found myself standing in the long-desired region of **Eutopia** <note>original: *Eutopia*. A play on words; while "Utopia" means "No Place," "Eutopia" means "The Good Place."</note>.

->And so, dear reader, let what has been said<-
->by me thus far suffice for you.<-

### TO THE BENEVOLENT READER.

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial 'Q' featuring floral and scrollwork patterns.</image-desc>

Whoever the Author of this little treatise <note>original: *tractatuli*</note> may be, dear Reader, cease to inquire; as for the reason he wrote it, let this be the cause. It is also not necessary for you to know who I am. But know for an absolute certainty that the Author of this small work most perfectly possesses, has made, and holds the **PHILOSOPHERS' STONE** <note>The legendary substance capable of turning base metals into gold and granting eternal life; in this context, it represents the pinnacle of alchemical knowledge.</note>. Since we are joined by mutual and sincere goodwill, I requested that, as a sign of his affection for me (as the title itself bears witness), he might discuss the three first principles—namely, **MERCURY**, **SULPHUR**, and **SALT**—and indicate whether the **Philosophers' Stone** ought to be sought in these common substances or in others, and that he do so in the simplest words and a very plain style.

After he had granted my request with this hastily written treatise, I became firmly convinced that by publishing it—even though I fear the Author will find little pleasure in its publication (for he is far removed from all ambition)—true lovers of Philosophy <note>In the 17th century, "Philosophy" often referred to "Natural Philosophy" or Alchemical science.</note> would think well of me. Indeed, I do not doubt that, once they have read and carefully considered it, they will suffer less loss, expense, and damage at the hands of imposters, and lose less time, reputation, and honor.

If I find the honest world—for "I hate and keep away the profane crowd" <note>original: *prophanum enim vulgus Alchymistarum odi & arceo*. This is a play on a famous line by the Roman poet Horace (*Odes* 3.1.1), here specifically targeting "puffers" or fraudulent alchemists.</note> of **Alchemists**—to be grateful for this kind intention of mine, I will strive to see that the remaining two principles, and many other works by the same Author, shall follow. In the meantime, enjoy this and farewell.

# DIALOGUE
## OF MERCURY, THE ALCHE-
### MIST, AND NATURE.

In that time the *Chemists* gathered and held a council on how they ought to make and prepare the **PHILOSOPHERS' STONE** <note>The legendary substance said to transmute base metals into gold; also called the "Lapis."</note>, and so they established that each should state his opinion by vote. This gathering took place in the open air, in a certain meadow on a clear day. Many agreed that *Mercury* was its first matter, others *Sulphur*, and others other things. But the greatest opinion among them concerned *Mercury*, especially based on the sayings of the *Philosophers*, since they hold it to be the true "first matter," and even the first matter of *Metals*: for the *Philosophers* cry out: "OUR MERCURY," etc. <note>original: "NOSTER MERCURIUS." Alchemists often used the term "Our Mercury" to distinguish their secret philosophical substance from common quicksilver.</note> And while they were contending thus among themselves with various labors (for each of them expected the conclusion <note>In alchemical texts, "the conclusion" refers to the successful completion of the Great Work or the final recipe.</note> with desire and joy), meanwhile a massive storm arose with squalls, clouds, and an unheard-of wind, which dispersed that gathering into various provinces, leaving each man on his own without a conclusion. However, each of them impressed upon himself what the end of that dispute ought to have been. Therefore, each began his labors as before, seeking the **PHILOSOPHERS' STONE** in one thing or another, and this continues until now without ceasing. 

But one of them, mindful of the dispute—that the **Philosophers' Stone** must necessarily be sought in *Mercury*—said to himself: "Even if no conclusion was reached, I will nevertheless work with *Mercury*, and I myself shall reach the conclusion once the blessed stone is made." For he was a man who was always accustomed to talk to himself, as *Alchemists* are wont to do. He began, therefore, to read the *Books of the Philosophers*, and happened upon the book of *Alanus* <note>original: "Alani." Likely referring to Alan of Lille, a 12th-century scholar to whom several alchemical works were apocryphally attributed.</note>, which treats of *Mercury*, and thus he became a "Philosopher-*Alchemist*," though still without a conclusion. Having taken some *Mercury*, he began to work; he placed it in a glass vessel and applied fire. The *Mercury*, as is its custom, evaporated. The wretched *Alchemist*, ignorant of nature, beat his *wife*, saying: "No one could have come here except you; you took my *Mercury* out of the glass!" The *wife*, weeping, excused herself, and said quietly to her husband: "You will make nothing but dung <note>original: "merdam." The text uses a vulgar term here to emphasize the futility of the alchemist's work and his domestic folly.</note> out of these things."

The Alchemist took the Mercury again and placed it back into the vessel; he guarded it closely so that his wife would not take it. But Mercury, in its typical fashion, evaporated once more. The Alchemist, remembering that the "first matter" of the Philosophers' Stone must be volatile <note>original: "volatilem" — meaning a substance that easily evaporates or turns into vapor when heated. Alchemists saw this as a sign of the substance's "spirit."</note>, rejoiced greatly. Convincing himself that he could no longer be mistaken now that he possessed this matter, he began to handle the Mercury boldly. He later learned to sublimate and calcine <note>To "sublimate" is to turn a solid directly into vapor and back; to "calcine" is to heat a substance until it turns to powder.</note> it in strange ways—now with salts, now with sulfur, now with metals, minerals, blood, hair, "strong waters" <note>original: "aquis fortibus" — early chemical name for concentrated mineral acids like nitric acid</note>, herbs, urine, and vinegar. But he could find nothing that suited his purpose; he left nothing on earth untouched that he might use to treat his good Mercury.

When he could make no progress at all, he stumbled upon the saying that the Stone "is found in the dunghill" <note>original: "in sterquilinio invenitur." A famous alchemical paradox suggesting that the most precious substance in the world is hidden within the most common or revolting materials.</note>. He began to treat the Mercury with various types of dung, both together and separately. When he had become exhausted and full of anxious thoughts, he fell asleep. 

And in his sleep, a vision appeared to him: an **Old Man** approached him, greeted him, and said: "Friend, why are you so sad?" 

He replied: "I would very much like to make the Philosophers' Stone." 

Then the Old Man said: "Friend, out of what do you wish to make the Philosophers' Stone?" 

**ALCHEMIST.** Out of Mercury, sir. 

**OLD MAN.** But out of what kind of Mercury? 

**ALCHEMIST.** There is only one Mercury. 

**OLD MAN.** It is true that there is only one Mercury, but it varies in different places; one part is purer than another. 

**ALCHEMIST.** Oh sir, I know how to purge it perfectly with vinegar, saltpeter <note>original: "sale nitro"</note>, and vitriol <note>original: "vitriolo" — a term for metal sulfates, often used as corrosive agents in alchemy.</note>. 

**OLD MAN.** I tell you, this is not a true cleansing, nor is that the true Mercury. For wise men have a different Mercury and another way of cleansing it. 

And with that, he vanished. Awakening from his sleep, the Alchemist wondered what that vision meant and what the "Mercury of the Philosophers" ought to be. He could think of nothing other than his "Common Mercury" <note>original: "Mercurium vulgi" — the ordinary quicksilver found in shops, which alchemists often distinguished from their secret "Philosophical Mercury."</note>. Yet he wished he could have spoken longer with that Old Man. Nevertheless, he worked diligently, now in the dung of animals and children, and later he even began to work in his own dung. 

Every day he went to the place where he saw the vision, hoping he might speak to that Old Man again. Sometimes he would fake sleep, lying with his eyes closed, waiting for the Old Man. But when the Old Man did not come, the Alchemist thought he was afraid and did not believe he was actually sleeping. He would swear aloud, saying: "My Lord Old Man, do not be afraid; surely, I am sleeping! Look at my eyes if you do not believe me." 

And that poor Alchemist, after so much labor and the wasting of all his goods, now fell into a delirium <note>A state of mental confusion or madness, often used here to describe the "puffers" or failed alchemists who lost their minds to the search.</note>, always thinking of that Old Man. And from that intense imagination, a phantom appeared to him in his sleep,

When Nature heard these things, she called Mercury to her and said to him: "What have you done to this man? Why does he curse me because of you? Why does he blaspheme me? Mercury promised he would provide it, saying: "Mother Nature, but who can satisfy fools?" Nature departed with a smile, while Mercury, angry at the Alchemist, also went back to his own place.

**MERCURY:** You sow me in dung, and at the time of harvest I vanish; you, however, are accustomed to reap only dung. 
**ALCHEMIST:** Nevertheless, the Philosophers wrote thus: that their matter should be sought in a dunghill <note>original: "sterquilinio." While literal dung was sometimes used for heat, "dunghill" was more often an alchemical metaphor for the "base" or "vile" starting matter of the Great Work.</note>.

**ALCHEMIST:** Now I see that you are perhaps Mercury; but you do not want to obey me.

...the philosopher wishes. **ALCHEMIST:** Are you an old man? **MERCURY:** My mother bore me, but I am older than my mother <note>original: "ego senior sum matre." A common alchemical paradox implying that Mercury, as the "First Matter," existed before the specific forms (mothers) that later contain it.</note>. **ALCHEMIST:** What Devil can understand you? Since you do not answer me to the point? You always speak in parables. Tell me, are you the little fountain <note>original: "fontina."</note> of which **Count Bernard of Treviso** <note>A famous 15th-century alchemist who wrote about a "Fountain" in which a King must bathe to be transformed.</note> wrote? **MERCURY:** I am not the little fountain, but I am the water; the fountain surrounded me. **ALCHEMIST:** Is gold dissolved in you, since you are water? **MERCURY:** Whatever is with me, I love as a friend; and whatever is born with me, I give nourishment to it; and whatever is naked, I cover with my wings. **ALCHEMIST:** I see that there is no speaking with you; I ask one thing, you say another. If you do not wish to answer well, I shall certainly go to work on you now. **MERCURY:** O Lord, I beg you, be merciful to me; now I will willingly say what I know. **ALCHEMIST:** Tell me then, do you fear fire? **MERCURY:** I myself am fire. **ALCHEMIST:** And why then do you flee from fire? **MERCURY:** My spirit and the spirit of fire love each other, and as much as it is able, one accompanies the other. **ALCHEMIST:** And where are you accustomed to go, when you ascend with the fire? **MERCURY:** Know this: every pilgrim always strives toward his own fatherland, and when he arrives there from whence he set out, he rests, and he always returns wiser than when he left. **ALCHEMIST:** Do you return again sometimes? **MERCURY:** I return, but in another form. **ALCHEMIST:** I do not understand what this is, nor anything about the fire. **MERCURY:** If anyone knew the fire of my heart, he would see that fire—the proper heat <note>original: "calorem debitum."</note>—is my food: and the longer the spirit of my heart eats the fire, the fatter it will be; whose death is afterwards the life of all things, whatever they may be in this kingdom where I am. **ALCHEMIST:** Are you great? **MERCURY:** You have me as an example; out of a thousand little drops I shall be one, and from one I give many thousands of drops; and such is my body in your eyes. If you know how to play with me, you can divide me into as much as you wish, and I shall be one again: what then is the spirit (my heart) within, which always brings forth many thousands from the smallest part? **ALCHEMIST:** And how then must one act with you, so that you are thus? **MERCURY:** I am fire within, fire is my food, but the life of fire is air; without air, fire is extinguished. Fire prevails over air, therefore I do not rest, nor can raw air constrain me; add air to air, so that they both may be one and hold their weight; join them with hot fire at the proper times; give it to the fire for safekeeping. **ALCHEMIST:** What will happen afterwards? **MERCURY:** The superfluous part will be drawn away; burn the remainder with fire, place it in water, then cook it; when cooked, you shall give it as medicine to the sick. **ALCHEMIST:** You tell me nothing in answer to my questions. I see that you only wish to mock me with parables. Wife, bring the **pig dung** <note>original: "stercus porcinum." The Alchemist returns to his crude methods out of frustration, failing to understand Mercury's spiritual/chemical metaphors.</note>! I will treat this Mercury in new ways, until he tells me...

### D I A L O G U E.

...provided that the **Philosopher's Stone** <note>original: "Lapis Philosophicus." The ultimate goal of alchemy, believed to transmute base metals into gold and grant long life.</note> is to be made from him. **Mercury**, having heard these things, begins to lament over the **Alchemist**, and goes to mother **Nature**; he accuses the ungrateful worker. **Nature** believes her son **Mercury**, who is truthful; moved by anger, she comes to the **Alchemist** and calls to him: "Hey you, where are you?"

**ALCHEMIST:** Who is it that calls me?

**NATURE:** What are you doing, you fool, with my son? Why do you do him such great injury? Why do you torture him? He who wishes to do every good for you, if only you were willing to understand?

**ALCHEMIST:** What Devil rebukes me, such a great Man and **Philosopher**?

**NATURE:** O fool, you dung of philosophers <note>original: "stercus Philosophorum." A harsh insult suggesting the Alchemist is the waste product of the true art rather than its practitioner.</note> full of pride! I know the **Philosophers** and all the Sages, whom I love, for they also love me, and they do all things for me according to my pleasure; and where I am not able to go, they help me. But you Alchemists—of whose order you also are one—work without my knowledge or consent; indeed, you do everything contrary to me. For that reason, the contrary also happens to you. You think that you treat my children well, but you accomplish nothing. And if you were willing to consider it rightly, you do not manage them, but they manage you: for you are able to make nothing from them, nor do you know how, but they, when they wish, make fools out of you.

**ALCHEMIST:** It is not true! I also am a **Philosopher**, and I know how to work well. I have been with more than one Prince, and I was a **Philosopher** among them—as even my wife knows! And even right now I have a manuscript book, which was hidden in a certain wall for several hundred years <note>Finding "hidden" manuscripts in walls or tombs was a common trope used to claim ancient, secret authority for alchemical texts.</note>. Now I shall certainly know how to make the **Philosopher's Stone**; and even in these days it was revealed to me through a dream. O, I am accustomed to have true dreams! Wife, you know it is true!

**NATURE:** You will do just as your other colleagues have done, who in the beginning know everything—or think they know—but in the end know nothing.

**ALCHEMIST:** Nevertheless, others are accustomed to make it from you (if you are the true **Nature**).

**NATURE:** It is true, but only those who have known me, and they are few. But he who knows me does not torture my children, nor does he hinder me, but does what is pleasing to me; he increases my goods and heals the bodies of my children.

**ALCHEMIST:** Yet I also do thus!

**NATURE:** You do everything contrary to me, and you proceed against my will with my children: where you ought to <term>revivify</term> <note>To restore a substance to its active or "living" state.</note>, you kill; where you should <term>fix</term> <note>To make a volatile substance solid or resistant to fire.</note>, you <term>sublime</term> <note>To heat a solid until it turns into vapor and then solidifies again.</note>; where you should <term>calcine</term> <note>To reduce a substance to powder through heat.</note>, you <term>distill</term>. **ALCHEMIST:** Then I shall proceed with him gently, through <term>digestion</term> <note>Gentle, prolonged heating, similar to how a body processes food.</note> only.

**NATURE:** It is well if you know how; but if not, you will harm not him, but yourself and your finances. For it is the same to him: he mixes himself with dung just as with gold. A gem is always good, and dung does not diminish it, even if in it—

### GREETINGS TO THE READER.

*It has pleased me, Candid Reader, to place at the entrance of this little work the Symbol of Saturn, since that <term>First Matter</term><note>original: "materia prima." The primordial, formless substance that alchemists believed was the starting point for creating the Philosopher's Stone.</note> is clearly and transparently explained through it. May you enjoy our study and fare well.*

**I**t happened once, as I was sailing for so many years of my life from the *Arctic* pole to the *Antarctic* pole, that by a singular sign from God, I was cast upon the shore of a certain great sea: And although I held the entrances and properties of that world-sea to be very well known and understood, I was nevertheless unaware whether in those shores that little fish, the **Remora** <note>original: "Echeneis." I asked again: "Sir, can this fruit not also be cooked in other waters, or is something added to it?" He answered: "There is none but this one water which is useful in this region or on the Island. No other water can penetrate the pores of this **Apple** <note>original: "pomi"; used here interchangeably with the Solar Fruit, symbolizing the concentrated essence of the work.</note> except this one; and know that the **Solar Tree** also arose from this water, which was extracted from the rays of the **Sun** or the **Moon** by the **power of the magnet** <note>A reference to the "Magnesia of the Philosophers," a substance capable of attracting the celestial spirit or "world-soul" from the atmosphere.</note>. For this reason they have a great harmony between them. But if anything foreign were added to it, it could not provide what it does by itself. Therefore, it must be left by itself, and nothing added to it but this apple. For after the boiling, it is an **Immortal Fruit**, having life and blood, because the blood makes all sterile trees bear fruit of the same nature as the apple." I asked further: "Sir, is this Water drawn in another way, or is it found everywhere?" And he replied: "It is in every place, and no one can live without it. It is drawn in wonderful ways, but that which is extracted by the power of our **Steel** <note>original: "chalybis"; in alchemy, "Philosophic Steel" is an agent used to attract or "cut" the spirit from the matter.</note>, which is found in the **belly of the Ram** <note>original: "ventre Arietis"; likely a reference to the astrological sign of Aries (Spring), the traditional time to begin the work, or a specific mineral associated with that sign.</note>, is the best." I said: "For what is it useful?" He answered: "Before the proper cooking it is a supreme poison, but after a suitable cooking it is a supreme medicine, and it gives twenty-nine grains of blood, and each grain [gives] eight hundred sixty-four..." <note>The text ends mid-sentence, likely referring to the "multiplication" or "projection" power of the medicine onto base metals.</note>

I began to ask again: "Lord, I pray you, name it for me by such a manifest name that I can no longer have any doubt." Be content with these things, and believe that it is not possible to speak more clearly: for if you do not perceive these things, you will never understand the books of other Philosophers.

# 1 PHILOSOPHIC ENIGMA.

...that I had come. But he said: "It is true, son, all generation occurs through male and female; but because of the distinction between the three kingdoms of Nature, a four-footed animal is born in one way, and a worm in another. For although worms have eyes, sight, hearing, and the other senses, they are nonetheless produced through **putrefaction** <note>original: "putrefactionem." Early natural philosophy held that certain creatures like worms or insects were generated spontaneously from decaying matter rather than through mating.</note>, and their place, or the earth in which they rot, is the female.

"Thus, in the **Philosophical Body**, the mother of this thing is your water, so often repeated; and whatever is born from it is born in the manner of worms, through putrefaction. Therefore the Philosophers called it the **Phoenix** and the **Salamander** <note>original: "phœnicem & Salamandram." These legendary creatures were symbols of the Stone because they were said to be born from fire or to regenerate themselves without a mate, representing a substance that has become incorruptible.</note>. For if it were made from the conception of two bodies, it would be subject to death; but because it only revivifies itself, once the prior body is destroyed, another incorruptible body shines forth. For the death of things is nothing other than the separation of one from the other. And in this Phoenix it happens so, because life separates itself from the corruptible body by its own power."

Furthermore I asked: "My Lord, are there diverse things or a composition of things in this work?"

But he said: "It is a single thing, with which nothing else is mixed except the **Philosophic Water** <note>original: "aqua Philosophica"</note>, which has been manifested to you several times in sleep, and which ought to be in a tenfold proportion to one part of the body. And believe firmly and without doubt, son, that those things which were shown to you by me and by Saturn through dreams on this Island, according to the custom of the region..."

My counsel shall not be lacking to you, which indeed I can provide all the more easily as I am familiar with these places, provided you do not refuse to obey sound warnings.

->ADOLPHUS<-
