You said, my son, that you are held by a desire to visit Rome; but rest assured that this Rome is a **Sodom**, and truly named so. I too have seen this "head of the world," but I was then protected by a more prudent age, being more attentive to its distinctions and dangers. Therefore, by my advice, do not set your mind on lingering long in these places. For truly, Rome is a perilous path of the world, an earthly paradise, a garden of venereal <note>Referring to Venus; meaning physical or carnal pleasures.</note> delights, and a place from which honesty, piety, and all shame are exiled—the palace of the vicar of the worldly prince. You will see in it all the allurements of this world, the fountain of pride, the filth of pleasures, and the fruits of the flesh, which are of no value, for it is the **letter without the spirit**. For the Spirit is not found in this place, but must be sought by a deeper investigation. Thrice and four times happy is he in whom God awakens this inner spirit, which even the blind Jews rejected, even though the veil of the temple had been torn asunder and the Lamb had opened the book of the seven seals and had said: *it is finished* <note>original: "consummata esse omnia," the final words of Christ on the Cross (John 19:30). But this displeases me greatly: that while I see you in the best of health, you complain of the length of time, even though, supported by your flowering age, you feel the force of no disease. Therefore, by a better calculation...

<page-num>527</page-num>
<header>PART ONE</header>

I would have you consider that these matters are to be weighed entirely by you; for you see that I have touched upon these things briefly rather than running a long course through this arena. Nor should the opportunity of time be passed by idly without labor and study; rather, one must insist accurately and diligently upon the knowledge of God and His works, and the powers of our senses must be exerted. For we were created for this end—in the image of God—not in the likeness of beasts, which were created rather for our use. Therefore, our eyes and ears must be sharpened and diligently pricked up for the praise of God, and leisure must be banished; no time should be passed without honest studies.

->ADOLPHUS<-

Indeed, my elder, I feel that I have long since grasped those things that could be of use to me. I have acquired a knowledge of the Latin language and a significant acquaintance with Aristotelian doctrine <note>Aristotle’s philosophy was the foundation of university education in the early modern period.</note>. Therefore, I see no benefit in wasting my life in these studies, especially since I hold the opinion that all things are imperfect and vain. Nor do I see any master or teacher of an art who arranges his actions without fraud and deceit so as to skillfully reach the desired end. The study of Astronomy, which above all others ought to be most certain and indubitable, is utterly uncertain, deceptive, and inconstant; the same judgment applies to medicine. No one fails to see what a <term>cacoethes</term> <note>original: "cacoethes," a Greek-derived term meaning a malignant habit, an uncontrollable urge, or a persistent "itch" for error.</note> of errors dwells in the sacred writings of the theologians, even though the ultimate certainty and constancy should reside in the Holy Scriptures. Yet, the Scripture is snatched by almost everyone into a different sense, and there is no end to controversies. In this life, one person lies in wait for another; one kills the very soul, while on the other hand, some lie in wait for the goods of fortune. There is no end to thefts, robberies, contentions, and fights—and anyone is accustomed to boast that these are the works of the highest learning, or prudence, or fortitude.

Being in my youth, I see that I can agree with these views, even if I do not devote my labor further to the knowledge of letters and studies—especially since I see that the true target is hit by almost no one. This was also suggested to me the other day by a certain peasant <note>original: "rustico"</note>, who remarked that the more learned are actually worse and more wicked than others. Some fear, and not without reason, that the learned will pay the penalty for this even by their own destruction. Nor do I see any reason why we should turn away from true and heavenly doctrine, since it was handed down to us from heaven through the Word born in the flesh <note>original: "Verbum in carne natum," referring to the Incarnation of Christ.</note>, as I heard from you before. Indeed, to put it in a word, hu- <note>The text breaks here; the catchword "mana" indicates the next page begins with the word "humana" (human).</note>

## T H E  E L D E R

This is true indeed; I claim for myself a knowledge of the Latin language to that same extent, but the knowledge of exotic languages holds no special place, nor do they seem necessary in the same way as a knowledge of Hebrew and Greek, in which the knowledge of all arts has been handed down to us from antiquity. But we see also that a knowledge of those exotic tongues is necessary, especially in the courts of princes because of various affairs, and it is a distinguished gift of God. This is clear from the example of those building the Tower of Babel <note>A biblical narrative used here to explain the origin of linguistic diversity as a divine act that eventually leads back to God’s glory.</note>, among whom various idioms of languages arose, specifically to the end that, being dispersed into different parts of the world, they might also be delivered into different sects of opinion. All these things, however, were so governed by God, the Best and Greatest <note>original: "Deo Opt. Max.," an abbreviation for *Deo Optimo Maximo*, a title frequently used in both Roman paganism and later Christian scholarship.</note>, that they might serve the honor of God. By the efficacy of the Holy Spirit, when the pious were collected from all nations, that insane structure of the tower was converted—through the ministry of the Apostles—into the most holy temple of God, in which the praises of God might be heard. 

For no confusion or dissipation pleases God; on the contrary, the Demon is the author of controversies and discords, while the Triune God demands peace and concord from us above all things. This peace is preeminent over all, in which this world was founded and the administration of kingdoms shine forth; in this matter, Christ the Savior and his followers have provided an example for us, which it is fitting to imitate with all zeal. 

And these things indeed concern the knowledge of various languages; but as for the care of souls, it is by no means necessary to wear away one's entire life in attaining the knowledge of languages. Rather, it is required that we listen to the sacred sermons of the ministers and apply ourselves diligently to the reading of Holy Scripture, just as that same doctrine from those three primary languages <note>Hebrew, Greek, and Latin were the "Tres Linguae Sacrae" (Three Sacred Languages) of the Renaissance and Reformation eras.</note> is set forth to everyone in the vernacular tongue. The same judgment applies to natural philosophy and the study of acquiring the goods of fortune. 

But the wise of this world and the crafty of this age follow various paths, and not content with the governance prescribed by God, they seek external things. From this, that precious treasure of time is squandered, and various dangers to souls arise, to which we are subject in this final age in which God is about to visit and judge that ultimate city of Jerusalem—namely, the entire world <note>The author uses Jerusalem as a metaphor for the entire world facing divine judgment.</note>. There shall also arise, by the same logic, those three capital enemies, and first...

He warns that the world is in its "final age," where human vanity and the squandering of time lead to spiritual danger.</summary>

->PART ONE.<-

[adver]saries, spiritual ones, just as they preceded the coming of Christ in the flesh and the final desolation of the same; but at His final coming, their plans will be rendered empty and deceptive before the tribunal of Christ. If, therefore, these should arrive in these latest times, we shall notice that the end of the world is near. At that same time, there existed the different sects of the Pharisees, the Sadducees, and the Essenes. But were not the Pharisees mere laborers, occupied with external works, literalists, not recognizing the spirit nor the coming of the Messiah? Did not the Sadducees utterly deny the resurrection of the dead? And the Essenes, driven by an Anabaptist spirit <note>The author uses "Anabaptist" as a polemical label for his own time, projecting it back onto the Essenes to describe those he considers radical or heretical.</note>, attacked the Holy Trinity: a first blasphemy against divine Omnipotence, a second against mercy, and a third injurious to the just and true Spirit of God.

Hence you see that men are always opposing the divine standard; and although they were many in number and of various sects, those previously named were the primary and chief ones. Each of these attacked the doctrine of the Holy Trinity, one arising after another with only the names changed, while their malice grew daily as they proceeded. For there were few among the Jews who, devoted to the true religion, lived a sort of hidden life and escaped the snares of this world with the greatest zeal.

Therefore, every spirit must be tested; indeed, each one of us should test himself by the divine word, as if against a touchstone <note>original: "lapis lydius," a Lydian stone used to test the purity of gold.</note>. If this is done, the Spirit itself, by searching the conscience of each person, will present them for examination. 

These things have been said concerning the knowledge of languages. But you should be persuaded that man’s natural, daily, and eternal preservation and knowledge are not to be sought in animal-like intellect alone—for to err is human—but must be sought in the Word of God on both sides, which the investigation of nature should follow. For drawing their origin from God, they return to the same, and establish their boundary and end in the same. For the Word is the only standard and scepter, and nature is the standard of all creatures, paving the way for the habitation of the soul and body. From all these things, the true Theosophist <term>Theosophist: here meaning one who possesses "divine wisdom" or direct knowledge of God, rather than the 19th-century movement</term> is recognized. 

However, the true knowledge of all these things was hidden from Aristotle; for one may see him blinking in the shadows, although he far excelled others in the sharpness of human reason. The same must be said of his followers, even though they possess great influence among the common people due to the authority of his name. Therefore, before all things, an exact account of the time must be considered, and the study of truth and justice must be pursued with every effort, and the [aid] of the Holy Spirit must be implored...

<summary>The Elder critiques ancient Jewish sects as precursors to modern heresies and argues that true wisdom (Theosophy) comes from the Word of God rather than Aristotelian logic or human reason.</summary>

# THE HIDDEN GOLD OF PHILOSOPHY
<note>original: "AURELIÆ OCCULTÆ PHILOSOPH."</note>

...help, who may bestow upon us the knowledge of spiritual things, and we must take care with all our strength that we do not become stuck in the vices of this world’s labyrinth. Instead, following what is good and just, and allowing no day or hour to pass by without fruit and labor, let us direct all our actions toward the glory of the divine name and the benefit of our neighbor.

->*ADOLPHUS*<-

You have discussed all these things so copiously, my old friend, that having understood only the smallest part of them, I cannot possibly respond to everything. I see indeed that the good must be pursued with all zeal, but I decide that one must not respond to everything at once, and that we must indeed make haste slowly. <note>original: "lente festinandum," a reference to the classical adage *Festina lente*.</note>

->*THE ELDER*<-

You must learn those things, O friend, which you confess you are still ignorant of. For I admit that this path was made ready and easy for me by the benefit of the elders and the ancients; do not despair that this same thing can happen for you, provided that your own will and diligent study are not lacking.

->*ADOLPHUS*<-

I truly desire to hear all these things from you, and I will never shrink from any labor that might allow me to satisfy this desire of mine, especially since I easily perceive that all these things are both honorable and useful.

->*THE ELDER*<-

Before all things, the nobility and excellence of those **seven dignities** <term>seven dignities: A set of virtues or conditions of life that the author considers essential for the philosopher's path, balanced between spiritual focus and worldly stewardship.</term> must be considered with the highest sharpness of reason. I shall soon reveal them to you in order: they are **prosperous health** and the **accurate stewardship of time** (which is threefold); likewise, the estimation of **human beauty**, **reputation**, and **authority** must be cast aside <note>The Latin *rejicienda* suggests these outward markers of success are to be discarded or viewed as secondary to spiritual progress.</note>, as well as **fortitude** and **power**, and even **wealth** and the **care of household affairs**. 

For these are four gifts which men are accustomed to use thoughtlessly. If God, the Best and Greatest <note>original: "Deus Opt. Max.," standing for *Deus Optimus Maximus*.</note>, did not visit us with the lashes of afflictions and temptations in addition to these, nor sometimes deliver us to unexpected death, nor cast a delay upon the human race by recalling us with that terrible trumpet (for before Him there is no respect of persons, nor consideration of dignity, and the mind of man is ignorant of what the late evening may bring), we would arrive at the contemplation and knowledge of such goods by a much easier way. But truly—

### PART ONE

Indeed, how few of us, alongside the salvation of the soul, 
also take care for that eternal and perpetual health, eternal peace, 
angelic beauty, heavenly strength and wisdom, and the treasures 
of glory? All of these things have been promised to us, and we 
expect to share in them through our Savior Jesus, but not in this 
decaying and rotten body—provided, of course, that we have 
persevered until the end walking in His ways and precepts, even 
unto the true Ark of the Covenant. <note>The Ark of the Covenant is used here as a symbol for the ultimate presence of God and the goal of the spiritual journey.</note> For whoever offers 
obedience to that divine will, revealed and demonstrated in the 
Book of Life, his name will not be removed from that Book of 
Life; for we have all been called. Even if there were some things 
to be said about the glory of this world—which is indeed true 
glory in its own way—yet it is nothing and clearly dead compared 
to that heavenly glory, even though this world’s glory may be a 
most precious treasure (for I too acknowledge it as such), yet it 
is fleeting and empty, not perpetual and immortal like that 
heavenly glory, Christ. But blessed and truly happy are those 
whose minds God illuminates through the shadows of afflictions 
and leads them to this point; for then that spiritual contest and 
struggle, and the weapons to be used in it, are revealed. From 
this it is clear that temporal things cannot provide such great 
efficacy, but that power depends on the Word of God alone 
and is granted to men at the moment of death. Yet these things 
are not granted to everyone; hence we, taking preposterous 
care and being less concerned about it, live a clearly idle and 
voluptuous life, thinking we only have to fight and struggle 
with nature alone, when in fact things are far otherwise. From 
this arises that false security which holds tyranny over almost 
the whole of a man's life. From this it also becomes manifest 
that even the spirit of man is subjected to passions and the cross, 
just as that first man <note>A reference to Adam and the Fall.</note> sinned, and through the secondary 
body brought sins to completion. In the same way, that spiritual 
anxiety and affliction precedes death, making it appear more 
horrible and terrible to man than all other things—especially 
to those who have spent their age in that false security and 
the swamp of pleasures. From this comes that worm of 
conscience <note original="conscientiae vermis">A common medieval and early modern metaphor for the persistent, gnawing remorse felt by the guilty.</note> gnawing at the souls of men in a thousand 
ways of temptation. Would that we might truly know the 
glory of God in the time of flourishing grace, and apprehend 
it with our eyes and hearing as if prepared in His word, more 
worthy than the past and the future, in which heavenly 
and eternal treasures lie hidden—treasures which remain 
even after the desolation and destruction of all other 
things. Although all things are full of the glory of 
the divine majesty, and regarding it all...

Creatures and the works of His hands in heaven, below heaven, on earth, and under the earth bear witness to Him. For in all these things, one may contemplate the Lord God in the power of His virtue and goodness. If we consider this more exactly, we will find such vast treasures of wisdom for our contemplation that—beyond the knowledge of His word—because of the weakness of our intellect, we can hardly ever hope to attain them, trembling as we do before the face of God. Yet we see that God, the Greatest and Best, created all things in a good and proper order out of love for us. For such a person truly contemplates God in spirit and can rejoice in Him, knowing himself to be the image of God in spirit and being bound to direct the actions of his life according to the pattern of the actions of Christ—the first Adam <note>Original: *Christi primi Adami*. While theology usually calls Christ the "Second Adam," the author here likely refers to Him as the "First" in terms of pre-eminence or the original spiritual archetype</note> and precursor—for the benefit of his neighbor. In the future and perfect life, however, we shall acquire full knowledge of Divine glory without any labor or weariness of learning, which we are forced to "swallow" <note>The author uses the verb *devorare* (to devour or swallow), suggesting the difficult and sometimes bitter process of studying and learning in this mortal life</note> in this life. In that life, the honor and glory of the divine name will be fulfilled, remaining for eternity. For we know His mercy is renewed daily and His glory cannot be sufficiently sung even by Angelic tongues; nor can we humans sufficiently search out and proclaim divine mysteries unless all these things happen by the gift of the Holy Spirit. 

But the wicked, who behave badly in managing that household <note>Original: *re familiari*. This is a metaphor comparing the management of one's soul and life to the administration of a family estate or household</note>, have before them the proposed eternal affliction of eternal fire, eternal thirst and hunger, the specters of demons, and intolerable cold and heat. These will even afflict the demons themselves, although they cannot feel elemental passions; instead, they will feel only eternal and spiritual punishments, about which we can say nothing certain except what we have drawn from the mysteries of the divine word. Furthermore, that eternity and duration of time lacking any end must be considered and examined, and at every moment of time, God must be entreated to free us from the enemy, who tries to oppress us with infinite temptations and evils in all our ways and paths. 

Just as other creatures and elements, celestial bodies, and spirits attempt to bring the same danger, God's help must also meet us in this regard. Therefore, a more fervent prayer is most necessary of all, by which we implore the help of the Holy Spirit, so that aided by His grace we may hear and learn the word of God without ceasing. Through this, we acquire that trust in God which is the rule and touchstone <term>touchstone: *lydius lapis*, literally "Lydian stone," used to test the purity of gold and silver</term> of our lives, since He Himself says: "Do this and you shall live" <note>A reference to Luke 10:28</note>; and elsewhere: "he who has sinned, let him do penance, and cease from sins," for He does not [desire] the death of a sinner...

### ADOLPHUS

I seemed indeed to hear the sermon of some pastor, although I cannot deny that these spiritual matters will be a burden to me; it does not please me to establish the actions of my life according to this standard. In the interim, however, I shall diligently strive to exercise the powers of my intellect and do all those things which may be done through the strength of our human weakness. ### SENIOR

Why should I not think you expect a fuller knowledge of it? Since even this entire world burns with the desire for its knowledge. In this context, it refers to the alchemical "Universal Medicine" or Panacea</note>, and indeed with such a medicinal potion by which men are liberated from insurmountable diseases—by the breathing of divine grace—for which no other physician can bring any other relief. Truly, this mystery, far surpassing all excellence of gold or silver, [surpasses human] reason...

->ADOLPHUS<-

Indeed, now at last I recognize and understand your words, although you have tried to cover them until now with a spiritual veil. For this mystery is truly that **Stone of the Philosophers** so often sung of in the writings of all the masters, composed of the **First Matter** <note>original: *prima materia*; the formless base of all substance</note>—namely, of **salt, mercury, and sulfur.** The books of everyone are full of this Philosophical Stone, and even more writings come to light every day. Indeed, I have even known some who were addicted to this art; they often spoke many things with me about it and used to show me writings, which I myself changed in certain places. Yet even if these works are sometimes accurately and skillfully labored over, they are nevertheless corrupted and ruinously altered by such people. Because of this, both the printer and the unskilled common people feel the sting of fraud, since the profit comes only to that **plagiarist** <note>original: *plagiarium*; in this context, someone who steals or "kidnaps" the intellectual work of others to sell for profit</note>. From this, I perceive a great scandal. Besides these things, we see the end and effect of the art almost nowhere; those who cultivate this skill and have attained its true use and effect are rare and **most similar to a black swan** <note>original: *rari nigroque similimi cygno*; a Latin idiom referring to something extremely rare or non-existent, as black swans were unknown to Europeans at the time</note>. Furthermore, in most schools, these precepts of the art are considered trifles and fables. I have heard this more than once from highly learned men who, having begun a discussion with the followers of this art, pronounced them to be plagiarists, impostors, and sycophants. They claim no constancy or certainty can be found in the art, nor will it ever seem credible to me that the initiates of this art can produce true gold and silver from other base metals. I think these things happen either by divine power or by incantations and the service of demons—especially since I have heard, not without reason, that many are suspected of familiarity with demons...

Do not be affected by weariness when you see me discoursing more at length than usual on these matters, for the logic of this art requires it; primary and excellent things must precede the earthly things that follow. As for the questions you proposed to me, I will respond more clearly below, and I will demonstrate more openly that I have spoken the truth.

## THE ELDER

I see that the opinion of the common crowd and of all the foolish pleases you—those who, with all their zeal for riches, seek only perishable treasures and the allurements of pleasures. But the mind and judgment of the **Philosophers** <note>original: *Philosophorum*; here referring to the "True Philosophers" or Alchemists who seek wisdom over gold</note> is far different. Indeed, those who pursue such trifles are not worthy of the name "Philosopher." Rather, that name belongs to those who diligently strive to achieve a full knowledge of the divine mysteries, and who devote all their study and labor to serving **God, the Best and Greatest** <note>original: *Deo Opt. Max.*</note>, and their neighbor. 

They set aside the pursuit of ostentatious titles, ambition, and the hoarding of earthly wealth—even though God, in His mercy, bestows upon them what is necessary for this life. The studies of this current age are one thing; quite another is the mind occupied solely with the laborious acquisition of money and the enviable display of wealth and status. It is out of a hatred for these vanities that the Philosophers are accustomed to hide the mysteries of this art, lest they feel the force and oppression of this **Nimrodic family** <note>original: *Nemroticæ familiæ*; a reference to the descendants of Nimrod, the biblical builder of the Tower of Babel, often used as a metaphor for tyrants or those who seek worldly power through arrogance</note>. 

This is the same reason why these secrets remain closed off from peddlers and charlatans. From the public disclosure of this art, great confusion and disturbance would arise in every rank of this world. Yet, this distinction of social orders was established by the highest counsel of God Himself, and it is most necessary for propagating harmony and peace among men. For **God, the Best and Greatest**, distributed these distinctions of rank and degree among those born of the earth so that one might serve another, and one might care for the harmony and peace of another, until they are again separated from each other by God. 

This is much like how the **practitioner of the Alchemical art** <note>original: *artis Alchymicæ cultor*</note> separates the soul, body, and spirit from each other, and joins them together in turn. But this divine separation, belonging to God, the Best and Greatest, is to be performed by no man, unless he has received the command to restrain the wicked through His Word, which alone is the unique truth and justice. Whatever is outside of this is blasphemy and abomination before God. Hence the magistrate, acting in the place of God, has received a plainly divine power; hence also comes the vengeance of the law against him who sheds human blood outside of this command, for not even with God [any...]

...there is no partiality toward individuals; however, this divine separation must be considered more carefully and held in the highest regard. Truly, these things may seem to be spoken outside the bounds of our main subject, yet they offer great benefit and usefulness to the human race; for that reason, it was decided to include them here. 

For indeed, in the book of the Prophet **Ezekiel** <note>original: *Ezechielis*; referring to the vision of the valley of dry bones in Ezekiel 37</note>, mention is made of the four winds that blew upon the dead bones, which were then clothed in flesh; mention is also made there of the spirit that took possession of them. In the same way, the dispersal and return of the winds are mentioned more frequently. 

We also see that in the final struggle of death, everything within a human being is separated from one another. For the four elements, along with the spirit and soul (both of which are known by the name **spirit** <note>original: *spiritus*</note>), are then sorted and depart from each other. In their place, that elemental water and earth are joined together, while a different air and fire are condensed. 

The **sidereal spirit** <term>sidereal spirit; a concept in Paracelsian philosophy referring to the "astral body" or star-derived spirit that mediates between the physical body and the eternal soul</term> of life, the internal and invisible man, returns to the stars and is elevated above the elements. The soul journeys to **Abraham’s bosom** <note>original: *sinum Abrahæ*; a traditional term for the place of rest for the righteous after death</note> according to God's promises, and rests beneath the altar until the consummation and reunion—that is, until the number and time of this world (our earthly mother) and of heaven (the parent of nature) are fulfilled. 

Moreover, we see how the earth supplies us with our daily food; within this food lies the spirit of the elements as nourishment, as well as a celestial essence. By the same token, we also have the nourishment of water and fire, by which we preserve our temperament within the earthly body; this body also contains spiritual fire and water to strengthen the inner spirit. 

Just as the earth contains both of these within itself, so too does the heavens, which is called the **fifth essence** <term>fifth essence; also known as the "quintessence," the purest, most incorruptible substance that makes up the heavenly bodies, distinct from the four earthly elements</term>. For this is far more noble than the Elements and is the nourishment of the spirit, just as the **Word of God** is the food of souls and was made flesh so that He might gift the body, soul, and spirit with heavenly bliss. Even though this is not a physical food or nourishment, it is the bond and seal of the record <note>original: *apochæ*; a Greek-derived term for a receipt or legal discharge of debt</note> and the Book of Life. This serves as a testimony of truth, because of our meager faith and our weak knowledge of the divine power. 

God pursues both natural and spiritual things with the highest love, and wills that His entire creation reside within man, and in union with Christ, so that those who have fallen may be raised up. Just as the Word of God is the beginning of all things, in the same way, it is also the beginning of the image of God. For from the hearing of the Word of God, that flower of the Holy Spirit—faith—arises; and from the seed of that flower, the tree of good works grows. ...[appearan]ce, our own being foolish and impossible. This word is that **magnetic love** <note>original: *amor magneticus*; a term describing the spiritual attraction between God and the faithful, or between souls</note>, through which He draws us, along with all the pious, toward Himself, and from which no one can be separated. In the same way, there is also a **sidereal magnetic love** and that **earthly nature**, all of which must be considered and weighed with a more exact balance. Just as it must be investigated, within the knowledge of nature, what the **internal man** <term>internal man; the invisible, spiritual aspect of a human being that persists beyond physical death</term> effects in nature—who is invisible and heavenly—while the soul is supernatural and super-heavenly; of all these things, we know nothing except what has been revealed to us by God. 

Nature indeed sets forth those natural limits, although they are of the highest order and require hidden contemplation. Yet the physical man does not understand spiritual things unless they are revealed to him by the King of spirits, that **Holy Spirit**, the spirit of truth. Through Him, all arts, wisdom, and science are weighed; this spirit excites and kindles the super-heavenly fire of love and the magnetic spirit of wisdom in Christians. He washes us with water and makes us white, so that we may do penance for our sins and die daily to our guilt. From this comes that frequent mention of water and fire, of blood and the water of the spirit. This is He who gives life, for our sin is of a blood-red color, but the wages of sin are black death, the cross, and affliction; whereas the robe of the pious is white, and their crown is one of glory.

Let these things, spoken more at length, suffice for the present. Let us descend to the **untying** <note>original: *enodationem*; literally the "untying of knots," meaning the clarification or explanation</note> of the questions proposed by you. I will reveal their explanation to you in order and demonstrate the certainty of this art through the thing itself, so that your faith may hereafter be made **perceptive** <note>original: *oculata*; literally "having eyes," referring to knowledge gained through direct sight or experience rather than hearsay</note>. 

As for the other objection—that most learned men have little knowledge of this science—know that this occurs by the singular will of God and for a specific benefit. For God rejects all pride and ambition, and He bestows this **treasure** <note>original: *thesaurum*; in alchemical and mystical literature, this refers to the secret knowledge of the Great Work or the Philosopher's Stone</note> upon the humble and the poor, rather than upon the powerful and the "sons of this world." According to the Lord's command, a man is bound to put this treasure to use—to "invest it at interest"—to extol the honor and glory of God and to relieve the poverty of the needy. We must not, you see, grow numb in idle leisure and abandon the duties of life, but rather perform the works of our calling according to God's will and pleasure. 

For if this treasure were granted to everyone, what confusion and discord, I ask you, would arise among mortals? Nor do I see how that saying of **Sirach** <note>original: *Syracidæ*; referring to the author of the Book of Sirach or Ecclesiasticus</note> could be proven true: *"My son, if you wish to serve and please God, prepare yourself for the day of afflictions"* <note>Sirach 2:1</note>. This saying indeed speaks of poverty, want, and human weakness, as you [can see] from yourself...

...you will be able to easily conjecture. Nor is it granted to men to use and enjoy this treasure according to the whim of their mind, for the nature of man is malicious and depraved. Therefore, reveal this **secret** <note>original: *arcanum*; a hidden mystery or specialized knowledge</note> to no one, nor give your hand to pride, greed, or ambition, for it belongs to God's honor and glory alone. Thus, if fortune favors you, beware of being lifted up; if fortune thunders, beware of being submerged, for God is the judge of both fortunes and moderates both according to His will. For it is no less a virtue to hunt for knowledge with all zeal before it is acquired than it is to cover it with silence after it has been gained. Truly, if you reveal it in a way other than how it actually is, that **<term>supreme art</term>** <note>The "supreme art" (*ars illa summa*) refers to the Great Work of alchemy, encompassing both the creation of the Philosopher's Stone and the spiritual perfection of the practitioner.</note> loses its name and dignity. Hence, one of the Philosophers said:

> Hide this work from the eyes of all, like a word on your tongue and fire in your eyes; indeed, do not even discuss this with yourself, lest the wind carry your words to another, which will certainly result in your disadvantage later.

I have faithfully forewarned you of these things; it is your duty to take careful heed, lest you pay the penalty in body and soul. Truly, there is a great abuse of these most excellent gifts of God, which God bestows upon us out of pure grace and liberality. With the greatest disgrace, these Philosophical gifts and sciences are trampled and cast aside, which are usually foully defiled by the ignorant; because of this disgrace, they will not even be able to see this light. 

But the crime of greed and luxury has so thoroughly grown into the children of this age that the faith of their households becomes slippery, and the fountains of justice and all laws are subverted. It pleases me to relate an example of this matter which I was able to see with these eyes of mine. 

There lived in a certain city an exceedingly wealthy man, overflowing with riches, the parent of many sons, greedy, stingy, and harmful even to his own body because of his avarice; he amassed great treasures for his sons. These sons, who were educated by their mother in every abundance of things, grew sluggish in luxury and idleness through confidence in their father's wealth. Dissolving into crimes, they increased in vice even as they increased in age. But when the father had departed from this **lodging of life** <note>original: *vitæ diversorio*; a metaphor for earthly life as a temporary stay or inn</note>, they daily **squandered** <note>original: *abligurientes*; literally "licking away," used to describe wasting money on fine food and indulgence</note> those paternal goods. Immersed in vices and crimes, they foolishly expected an increase in wealth and riches to continue as it had before. But in vain; instead, feeling the daily decrease of their family estate and wealth, and reduced to extreme poverty, they did not even abstain from committing the greatest crimes, exposed to disgrace and shame throughout their whole lives. All these things arose from a perverse method of educating and instructing children; for first in morals...

# THE HIDDEN GOLD OF PHILOSOPHY

...and they ought to have been instructed in the knowledge of the sciences. For it is God's will that there be distinct orders and ranks of men, and that one should serve another: indeed, all men in their **<term>calling</term>** <note>original: *vocatione*; the station or profession to which God has appointed an individual</note> and rank are servants and hired hands. For our Lord and Savior likewise performed servile works for others and washed the feet of his disciples; however, honor is lesser in some and greater in others—even supreme—just as there are different gifts and blessings. Hence that rule prescribed by God the Father Himself, the Greatest and Best: "In the manner you have served in your calling, so also shall I count out your reward to you." 

Truly, in a single day, God dispenses such vast treasures of riches that they far exceed the wealth of the most opulent kingdoms; yet He has no fear of future poverty. On the contrary, the more He gives, the more He abounds; and for this reason, God is to be loved and cherished above all things and before all else with the highest love. Regarding human wealth, however, we commonly see this happen: that a liberal dispenser follows the miserly, hoarding **Euclio** <note>A character from the Roman playwright Plautus known for his extreme greed and hoarding of a pot of gold; here used as a type for the miser.</note>, according to that saying of the more learned: *Riches add horns to the poor* <note>original: *Opes cornua pauperi addunt*; a metaphor suggesting that wealth makes the lowly arrogant or aggressive</note>, and they quite often hurl the possessor into extreme ruin and the eternal torments of **Gehenna** <note>A term for Hell or a place of fiery torment.</note>. 

For if anyone should abound in the riches and wealth of this world, he does not easily undertake a serious thought or care for true health and heavenly peace, nor does he strive to relieve the needy with liberality. Instead, he consecrates all his diligence and study to acquiring heaps of great wealth, meanwhile forgetting God and all piety. Therefore, young men live among these allurements of the world with the greatest danger, even if the prudence of age sometimes makes up for a lack of experience. The pious, however, are forced to drink the cup of afflictions, while the wicked are reserved for the eternal torments of Hell. Truly, all these things are an object of mockery and laughter to the "sons of this age," who busily strive to graft their children into powerful families and riches, paying no heed to the **sting of conscience** <note>original: *conscientiæ morsu*; literally the "bite of conscience"</note> which seriously dictates that divine wisdom must be sought before all things. Without this wisdom, nothing ever endures in this theater of the world. From this comes that **worm of conscience** <note>A traditional metaphor for the recurring, painful remorse that haunts the guilty, especially at the point of death.</note>, gnawing at the hearts of the wretched with various arrows of temptation in the agony of death; for men are not accustomed to seeking the salvation of the soul in true humility.

...should become known, since we see that almost all other arts are commonly known to the public; and this indeed sometimes moves one who considers it carefully to the greatest doubt.

### THE ELDER

Before this you heard from me that silence is imposed on all cultivators of this art, and the hiding of this science, on account of the power and outrages of the tyrants of this world, the fornicators, the proud, the usurers, the luxurious, and other wicked men. For all the **Philosophers** <note>In this context, "Philosophers" refers to alchemists or seekers of natural wisdom.</note> hide the true knowledge of this science with the highest art; indeed, some who attained its possession but dealt poorly in its administration lost its use and benefits; for some, too, it was snatched away by untimely death, or even a violent death brought on by others. For the student and possessor of this art ought to be humble, pious, silent, and upright. 

If, therefore, God should also grant you the knowledge and possession of it, you shall cover it in the same way, nor sell it to another; rather, with constant diligence, you should apply yourself zealously to further knowledge and the works of your **<term>calling</term>** <note>original: *vocationis*; the station or profession to which God has appointed an individual</note>. You should show kindness to your neighbor and even to your enemy, for to this the rule of the Christian religion binds us. But the enemies of the faith must be resisted with the greatest strength, and we must strive zealously in this, so that others, prepared for the praise of God, may sing of His mercy with us. Truly, on account of ingratitude many things lie hidden; for ignorance produces very many losses, while knowledge, on the contrary, increases good things, and is that ray of light.

Very many, however, find those who attempt to investigate this art, but they study neither silence nor the other virtues necessary to attain these things; they fall into the same destruction as that **Phaethon** of **Ovid's** <note>A reference to the Roman poet Ovid's story of Phaethon, who attempted to drive the chariot of the Sun but, lacking his father's skill, scorched the earth and was destroyed by a thunderbolt; a metaphor for those who seek power beyond their spiritual capacity.</note>, who did not know how to rule his father’s chariot of the sun. Furthermore, this treasure must be guarded and preserved with the greatest care. But if a man considers even the parables and mysteries alone, let him think himself abundantly satisfied when he sees the seal and image of divine goodness impressed upon nature. For nature completes all things accurately, and indeed more perfectly than man himself, who is nevertheless the noblest creature, and closer to God, rational and beloved by the Creator. From this the excellence of man with respect to other creatures is evident, for which reason also **God, the Greatest and Best** <note>original: *Deus Opt. Max.* (Deus Optimus Maximus); a title originally used for Jupiter but adopted by Christian scholars to denote the Supreme Being.</note>, set before him precepts and eternal life.

### THE ELDER

Indeed, before all other things, these are to be considered; and for this reason I have made such lengthy mention of them, whereas I have passed over almost everything else. For they are nearly infinite, yet not all are necessary. For he who knows the **<term>Work</term>** <note>The *Magnum Opus* or Great Work of alchemy</note> itself, knows by himself that no handle should be given to heresies. For certain **<term>smug know-it-alls</term>** <note>original: *nasutuli*; literally "those with a large nose," referring to people who think themselves clever or critical in a superficial way</note> sometimes attempt to hawk these things to the common folk under the sacred name of the Bible—people who are accustomed to receiving such things with open arms—even comparing another impious and blasphemous work to the Divine power. For the Word of God is **<term>Jacob’s ladder</term>** <note>A reference to Genesis 28:12; in alchemical thought, this represents the stages of ascent from matter to spirit</note>, and Christ alone is the mediator and the norm, to whom all things in the Book of Life are directed. 

By the same reasoning, in our work of nature, we see life and death, and resurrection, likewise the creation of the entire world, numbers, measure and weight, the increase, powers, and efficacy of the stars and the elements—especially indeed of the **Sun** and the **Moon**. For by the Sun, according to the good pleasure and divine ordinance, [life] descends, and for that reason it is compared to the Sun and called by its name. For **<term>as it is above, so it is below</term>** <note>original: *quemadmodum enim superius, ita & inferius*; the foundational axiom of Hermeticism from the Emerald Tablet</note>, by which miracles are perfected; it is also male and female, and the servant of the entire world, containing in itself the riches and wealth of the universe: a purple, reddish, and golden sun. 

In these matters, two things are to be noted, concerning the "one" and the "two." For God, the Best and Greatest, created something out of nothing; that "something" indeed became a certain "one" in which all things, both celestial and earthly creatures, were contained; for God said: "Let it be," and it was. Yet when all things had been created by His word, and universal nature stood before Him, and it was separate from the [original] thing, and good—it was in its essence before God, and it was pleasing to God, for it was "very good." However, something from it quickly perished, and it did not endure until the time of that great world. Therefore, besides this, something else was required, for it could not endure through the "one" alone, just as it had been established in the beginning on account of the weaker creature, which God likewise willed. And He said: "**<term>Increase and multiply</term>**" <note>original: *crescite & multiplicabamini*; the divine command from Genesis 1:28, interpreted here as the necessity of duality for reproduction and stability</note>; for then it was multiplied to such an extent that nothing should perish until the great age of the world's end. For this was the blessing of the Lord, which He imparted to man by His word; and all things are perfected with the highest obedience until the end, and are governed by the Holy Spirit. The same is also found in **Adam** and **Eve**, male and female. It must be observed here, by what rea-

...[distinc]tion, creation is perfected by the One, increase, multiplication, and preservation by the second, and administration by the third, as if by the spirit; for these things must be examined with a more precise **<term>balance</term>** <note>original: *trutina*; the author uses the metaphor of weighing on a scale to suggest careful intellectual and spiritual judgment</note>. Lastly, God also swiftly joined a command and a prohibition to man's essence, and subjected all things to him without any defect, giving him the power to eat from all the fruits of Paradise, except for that single tree of the knowledge of good and evil. The fruit of this tree had been forbidden to him, perhaps indeed on account of the malice of the demon; yet man was ultimately subjected to the demon's will through disobedience. For good alone is to be known, and evil to be shunned—a choice by which a path was prepared for the Enemy. For God alone is the Lord who administers all things, while all creatures are subject to Him. 

The commandment introduced sin because they failed to observe it—namely through the instinct of the demon and their own free will. For this was the first sin, blasphemous and idolatrous, wrapping all knowledge in the darkness of ignorance; nay rather, converting knowledge into the recognition and science of evil, even unto this very day, into all vices, outrages, and the demonic arts. These are the things we renounce in the sacred font of baptism, specifically in the regeneration and renewal of our life in the **<term>New Adam</term>** <note>A traditional title for Jesus Christ, who is seen as undoing the damage caused by the "Old Adam"</note>. He is, as it were, the tree of life which was taken away from our first parents in the earthly paradise of terrestrial life. 

Yet this was promised again in the "seed of the woman," Christ, who is the tree of life—both spiritual and corporal—by whom not only the soul but also the body might receive life. For just as Adam, cast out from Paradise, was sent into the world—a garden of darkness, afflictions, and the **<term>mortification</term>** <note>original: *mortificationem*; in both theology and alchemy, this refers to a process of "dying" to one state to be reborn in another</note> of blood and flesh—in the same way, if we listen to the **<term>manna</term>** <note>The "bread from heaven" mentioned in the Bible, here signifying spiritual truth</note> (that is, the heavenly bread, the word of God) and if we establish the actions of our life according to His commandments, and if we, believing, partake in the Word which was made flesh, we shall resume life through Him. We shall be transferred from the house of ignorance into the celestial paradise. 

And just as death snatched Adam away, so too is it compelled—even against its own will—to present us to liberty through the Word of God alone: Christ, in whom all things exist. For in the Old Adam we die, but in the other and New Adam we rise again, just as He precedes us. Wherefore He is the tree of life, from which we must eat while we live as exiles in this house of afflictions. Indeed, just as a certain kind of fruit in Paradise was forbidden to the first Adam, so by equal reasoning let us devise no other norm, commandment, or path—neither to the right nor to the left...

# THE HIDDEN PHILOSOPHY OF AURELIA.

...besides the Word of God, contained in the **<term>Book of Life</term>** <note>original: *libro vitae*; a biblical concept (Revelation 20:12) representing the record of those saved, here used to represent the ultimate source of divine truth</note>, which was closed with seven seals and which Christ opened. But if we desire to know other and greater things beyond this, and to eat from the fruit of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, we are said to wish to serve two masters—that is, God and the devil—embracing a lie in place of the truth, and rejecting the truth as if it were a lie. Furthermore, we shall receive the reward worthy of our works. And it first happened to our parents that they were cast out from the sight of the living God; for God is not like man, but men are created in His image, so that they might obey His commands and neither take away from them nor add to them. Since the wisdom and knowledge granted to us for food are offered to us from the Word of God—by which man lives—and are plucked from the Book of Life, that spiritual garden; for from this comes every good, and through the Word all things were created, whatever may be grasped by the eyes and hands. For from the invisible the visible was made; so also from the hearing of the Word of God faith takes its origin, and from faith, good works. That is, from the invisible the visible is made, and from the Word the Christian is generated.

These things, however, are such that a man should act and work by a similar reason, rather than following idle and vain little questions about divine omnipotence. For this is the ordination and omnipotence of God, who also provided a similar example to man. But that **<term>doubting Thomas</term>** <note>original: *Thomas ille incredulus*; a reference to the Apostle Thomas who required physical proof of the Resurrection (John 20:24-29)</note> was not able to attain this, since he only recognized human nature and science and the lower elementary heaven, and especially those things that are internal, like water and earth, which are nevertheless the receptacles and prisons of death. This, moreover, is that philosophy rejected by Paul, in which there is no perfection; but only that **<term>celestial philosophy</term>** <note>original: *Philosophia coelestis*; here refers to a divine wisdom achieved through faith rather than worldly logic or elemental study</note> is perfected through faith, charity, and hope.

In this place, it should be noted that just as all things are preserved through the Word of God, and it is necessary for us to have faith in the Word that proceeds from the mouth of God, so also Christ attributed this honor to the Father: that without faith, nothing is acquired. But the greater part of men do not believe those things they do not see, nor do they consider that God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Spirit cannot be seen by our eyes, which are subject to sin. Just as men were not able to see the rays of His face—which far exceed all the brilliance of the sun—while He still moved among them in visible form, because of the defect of their sinful nature. This is true even though Christ himself is still present with us today in a bodily way, and is at the right hand of God—that is, in that most sacred purity and **<term>Godhead</term>** <note>original: *Deitas*; the divine essence or nature</note>, just as He also fulfilled every will of the Father, and [created] all things from...

### PART ONE.

...traversed from the abyss to the highest point in both flesh and spirit, and even now fulfills all things in all. But who among men can investigate that highest height and wisdom of God? For we know that **heaven is his throne, and the earth is the footstool of his feet.** <note>original: "caelum esse sedem illius, & terram scabellum pedum eius"; a reference to Isaiah 66:1 and Matthew 5:34–35</note> We cannot, therefore, inquire into those celestial things, nor know them, except for those which are handed down to us in the Word of God, which St. Paul saw but was not able to speak; instead, he transmitted the Word, that **<term>celestial bread</term>** <note>A metaphor for Christ or divine wisdom that sustains the soul</note> to us as a seal, in which the salvation of our souls consists: namely, the will of God, the true **<term>Tree of Life</term>**, so that we may drink his blood and eat his flesh, and firmly believe that these things are exactly so whenever the words of institution are recited. In this way also, perfected nature shows many miracles in a single mirror, which it suffices to have touched upon here briefly, since these things, granted to the Holy Scriptures, are sufficiently revealed by them; moreover, one who relies on such a will of God sees all things and holds them as known, just as even some of the wiser **<term>Pagans</term>** <note>original: "Ethnicis"; referring to pre-Christian philosophers like Hermes Trismegistus or Aristotle who were thought to have glimpsed divine truths through nature</note> recognized.

->ADOLPHUS.<-

You have led me away with such a lengthy speech of yours that I have even forgotten the greater part of it; but I desire to hear this from you: does not this **<term>work of nature</term>** <note>Refers to the alchemical process of transformation</note> have a spirit within itself which introduces change? For I see you made mention of the **<term>second number</term>** <note>original: "fecundi numeri"; likely referring to the alchemical duality of sulfur and mercury or the process of multiplication</note> which is multiplied, for a vital spirit is required for this.

->SENIOR.<-

Truly, a **<term>mineral vital spirit</term>** <note>The "spiritus vitalis mineralis" is the animating force within matter that the alchemist seeks to isolate and use for transformation</note> is within this, which completes its course in it after it is prepared by the craftsman according to its own dignity. For God, out of sheer goodness, appointed man as its master, so that from it he might form something else—namely, a **new world**—through the power of fire, according to the order and precept handed down by God. For without this, man will achieve nothing at all; and it is absolutely required that all these things be performed in the fear of the Lord, with an honorable purpose and a pure conscience. If, therefore, someone from the dregs of humanity does not attain the end of this art, it shall be a scandal to no one; for even though it is placed before the eyes of men and is generally used for other purposes, very few are ignorant of its true use, not knowing that this noble treasure is clouded over by those shadows. Hence, for the most part, this **purest gold** is left behind, hedged in by dense darkness and rust, and submerged in mud and filth—all of which, by the right order of nature...

### THE AURELIA OF OCCULT PHILOSOPHY
<meta>catchword: then</meta>

...thus they are made. But the wiser Philosophers, having heard only the name of **Mercury**, recognize this treasure and keep it before their eyes; although it becomes invisible and spiritual, it is nonetheless material. It is a most chaste virgin who has not known a man, a fragile substance—hence its names: **virgin’s milk** <note>original: "lac virgineum"; a common alchemical term for a white, caustic liquid or a specific stage of the work</note>, **earthly mountain honey**, **milk**, **infants’ urine**, and the like. For in all these things, craftsmen have sought it until now but have not found it, because it is prepared from a metallic matter, and indeed the best kind.

->ADOLPHUS.<-

Is this treasure not gold, then, since gold is such a noble metal? For I see you have already hinted at this for some time.

->SENIOR.<-

Least of all. You must first learn other things from me, for you still gape too greedily after the treasures of earthly gold. Truly, you have not yet sufficiently perceived these things; and indeed, I shall hand over to you the final and chief mystery of this art, committed to writing. Although certain doubts may seem to exist in my present speech, it will not be necessary to explain them more clearly. 

This treasure is not that worldly gold, nor silver, mercury, sun <note>original: "sol"; often used as a synonym for gold in alchemy</note>, antimony, nitre, sulfur, nor anything like them. Instead, it is the **spirit of gold** and **mercury**, which is called by the Philosophers the **<term>first and second matter</term>** <note>The "prime matter" is the raw, unformed substance of the universe; the "second matter" is that substance after it has been partially refined by the alchemist</note>. It is of a peculiar and singular nature and property, having experienced no force of fire. It is **purest eastern gold** <note>original: "aurum obryzum orientale"; refers to gold refined to the highest possible standard</note>, the most excellent of all, softer than that other gold and molten; it is that true mercury of gold and antimony, drawing its qualities from bodies if it be liquid. 

Its preparation is nothing other than that it be washed pure and cleansed with water and fire, just as most other things are prepared in the same way to please God and men. Therefore, one must exactly understand **sublimation**, **distillation**, **separation**, **digestion**, **purification**, and **coagulation**, along with **fixation**. One must also more diligently investigate that **<term>egg of nature</term>** <note>A symbol for the sealed alchemical flask or the primordial container of life</note> sought by so many from the very beginning. On this subject, the writings of many exist, including among others those of **Count Bernard** <note>Bernard of Trevisan (1406–1490), a famous Italian alchemist known for his search for the Philosopher's Stone</note> and others, which I will show you at the conclusion of our talk, and I will add many parables to them.

->ADOLPHUS.<-

Since I see that the use of this art must be obtained with much sweat...

->## PART ONE<-

...and its possession being joined with danger, and the duties of my **<term>calling</term>** <note>original: "vocationis"; the specific spiritual or professional duty assigned to an individual by God</note> being entirely necessary to undergo, I see that the joy which I previously took has become somewhat diminished, and that I have been deluded by a vain hope.

### SENIOR

Consider this as if spoken from a tripod <note>original: "è tripode dictum"; a classical idiom meaning an oracular or certain truth, referring to the priestess at Delphi</note>: you must labor strenuously and practice the duties of beneficence toward the poor—yet not just any poor, but those who are truly impoverished—taking up also the care of orphans and widows for the glory and honor of the Divine name. However, let the honor proper to God be given to no other; then, let consolations be sought from the Divine Word. For the Word of God precedes Nature by a long order, just as the servant follows the master, and the father surpasses the mother in dignity.

In all things, we must act as if we knew nothing certain about this, but rather we must apply ourselves eagerly to the labor of our calling, to procure the utility of our neighbor and the benefit of the **<term>Commonwealth</term>** <note>original: "Reip."; the Respublica or general community</note>, and to drive out the evils of ignorance. For without intermission, both the reason and the body must work for the good (for idleness is the pillow of **Satan**, and is prohibited under heavy penalty; from this, indeed, all other crimes arise: luxury, greed, homicide, lies, impostures, and frauds).

In this, we are imitating Nature herself. Our **Work** <note>The alchemical "Great Work" or "Opus"</note> never rests at any time, but operates without intermission, every day and hour, until its sixth period of weeks is completed and its **Sabbath** <note>original: "sabbatum"; the final stage of rest and perfection in the alchemical process</note> approaches. For then it rests and honors its master—man—whom it must serve according to God's ordinance, obeying his commands. In like manner, men must also labor and work without any intermission until we enter into the eternal kingdom of God. 

Yet truly, all these things happen as if against our nature, and we bear it with annoyance when we hear that our living must be sought through constant labor until we return to the earth from which we were made, since idleness and the lust for power appeal equally to everyone. In the same way, we are also sluggish in prayers and supplications, although all things must be obtained and requested from God through prayer. We despise others who act as healers <note>original: "medicantes"</note>, though we ourselves are supported by a meager income; meanwhile, we remain greedy, even though we are obligated to do good even for our enemies. Indeed, countless other outrages hold dominion among us, such as anger, greed, hatred, enmity, and mutual distrust. Because of these things, this most excellent good is taken away from us, as is that most illustrious knowledge of the **physician** <note>original: "medici"; here referring to the spiritual or alchemical healer who possesses the true medicine</note>.

-># THE AURELIA OF OCCULT PHILOSOPHY<-

...re, which lies hidden in this, unknown to other medical doctors; for this treasure is not handed down in the schools of physicians, but remains concealed before their eyes, in the same way that the internal spirit of the Holy Scripture was hidden from the Pharisees. That spirit was the true Messiah and the medicine of the soul, yet even though He walked in their midst, they did not see Him. For this reason, He gives thanks to the Father for closing off this treasure from the "wise men" of this world and revealing it to the simple and the foolish. In this same way, it is said of our **<term>natural medicine</term>** <note>referring to alchemical or spiritual healing rather than standard pharmacy</note> that the will of God must come first, which is to be sought through ardent prayer, just as this Divine will disposes all things in all other worldly matters.

From this, the vanity of those **<term>simples</term>** <note>original: "simplicium"; medicines made from a single constituent, usually a herb</note> and syrups is made clear—those which are commonly offered by the ointment-sellers <note>apothecaries</note> to the great loss of the physicians' reputation and the expense of the sick. Indeed, they are offered to the patients' most certain ruin and death, and the costs paid by the suffering are turned into nourishment for pride and luxury. Just recently, a certain country man complained that he had been so deceived by that art that he had lost nearly his entire substance and the support of his family, had not a man of small fortune quickly brought him aid.

For we see that most people care only for this: that, being gifted with a famous name and celebrity, they might sit among the **<term>gods of the higher nations</term>** <note>original: "majorum gentium diis"; a Roman idiom referring to the highest-ranking deities, here used to describe the social elite or academic "gods" of the medical world</note>. Meanwhile, they utterly neglect that care and diligence by which the benefit of their neighbor and those specific studies are supported—indeed, they neglect the acquisition of that very universal knowledge itself.

Therefore, everyone must strive with the greatest zeal to separate the good from the evil. That is, they must recognize the virtue and the fruits of the "good tree" with its triple root: gentleness, modesty, and patience. In the same way, they should cultivate the fruits of the soul—Faith, Charity, and Hope—so that we may know what Truth and Justice are, and what will become of both the soul and the body (that is, the celestial and the bodily good).

To achieve this more easily, **<term>Theological science</term>** and **<term>Juridical science</term>** <note>the study of Law</note> have been handed down to us by God; for in these consist the purity and holiness of nature. Indeed, virtue, the works of one's **<term>calling</term>** <note>original: "vocationis"; the specific life-path or duty assigned by God</note>, and singular justice are wisdom, light, and **<term>Philosophy</term>**, in which **Solomon** far excelled all other men. Truly, God Himself has assigned to each person the works of his calling, and He has commanded each of us to establish our actions wisely, piously, and justly within our calling and duty of life, according to the rule of the Divine Word—as a servant of God who must render an account of all things before the tribunal of the **Judge** of all...

...of the nations, before whom all the deeds of men shall be revealed. All good descends from God; likewise, from Him come the wise and the wealthy, the poor and the foolish, the beautiful and the weak. He who despises the poor and the weak scorns Him by whom he was created, for all good is from God, whereas evils have descended from the Devil, as if from the fount and origin of all evil. By the singular counsel of God, evil even in this life acts as a tyrant and causes trouble for the pious, although the Demon, out of sheer malice, tries to direct it toward the harm and destruction of men; for all evil serves God and the pious for their ultimate good—nay, even the demon himself is forced against his will to serve the divine glory. 

Our sin alone is the cause for evil being mixed with good in this life, while the divine kindness and mercy sustain us in the meantime. To that end, the precepts of the **<term>Decalogue</term>** <note>The Ten Commandments</note> were handed down to us by God, so that we might separate evil from good to avoid the cost of eternal damnation. 

But what the face and pursuits of the world are, anyone easily sees. Those greedy plunderers, having professed the name of Christ in the sacred font of Baptism, now imitate the perfidy and rapacity of the Jews with their excessive demands of **<term>usury</term>** <note>original: "usurarum exactionibus"; the practice of lending money at unreasonably high interest rates</note>. They wickedly believe they have complied with the divine will as long as they have seized the goods of the **<term>Ethnics</term>** <note>original: "Ethnicorum"; a term used here for non-Christians or "heathens"</note> and foreigners (by which name they are accustomed to call Christians), even though the Savior threatens eternal punishments to those who, hurting their neighbor with usury and extortions, devour their goods. This also applies to those who, giving themselves over to gluttony and luxury, intercept the property of orphans and widows. Indeed, these two types of men—the greedy and the luxurious—are to be joined together and judged by the same measure. 

In contrast, the lives of those wealthy **<term>Patriarchs</term>** <note>The biblical fathers of the faith</note>—Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, and Job—were precious and just, full of modesty and obedience toward God. For they placed the worship of God before all other creatures, and walking in purity of life and justice, they poured out ardent and effective prayers to the Lord. Just as in the Old Testament great riches were found among many, yet were joined by a great bond of constancy; so in the New Testament, poverty presses upon many worshippers of Christ. Nevertheless, a similar constancy, fear, and love toward God is required of them. 

From all these things, I think you have understood quite fully the reason why this **<term>mystery</term>** <note>referring to the "natural medicine" or alchemical secret mentioned on the previous page</note> has been so hidden and secret until now before the eyes of many. It is because the demon can, with easy effort, point out another way—one that wanders from the right path—through the vain pleasures of this world. For here, in the know—

->S E N I O R.<-

Do you not know that power has been given to the kings and princes of this world so that, in the place of God, the Best and Greatest <note>original: "Dei Opt. Max."</note>, they might restrain the malice of men, and cultivate and propagate justice, truth, piety, and obedience, so that all things in this state of life may be done decently and in good order? But just as the political magistrate is accustomed to punish the wicked with the secular sword <term>gladio seculari</term>, so also those spiritual fathers and ecclesiastical magistrates rule the life of the Christian people with the sword of the spirit <term>gladio spiritus</term>, and by the word of God and His commandments. After the wounds inflicted by the curse of the law, they anoint and heal with the oil of justice—unless the transgressors themselves reject the health and care of their wounds. Yet these wounds of conscience are not to be healed by the churchmen with a temporal sword, just as we see that Aaron, Moses, and Joshua <note>Biblical figures representing the distinct roles of Priest, Lawgiver, and Military Leader</note> held distinct offices until they had entered the promised land. 

The subjects are also commanded to show obedience and honor to the magistrate ordained by God, lest, puffed up with ambition, they thrust themselves into the duties of the magistrate and snatch away the functions of high office by bribery, deceit, or power—unless they are legitimately called to this. For he who exalts himself above others shall be humbled, since this arises from ambition and pride, which God resists above all else. Indeed, pride is an abominable idolatry <term>idololatria</term> above all others, since God alone is the highest and most powerful. He institutes and governs all orders and ranks of secular power according to His own will and good pleasure, seeing all things in light and in darkness. He is the creator and author of every order of justice and of all creatures; He forbids the trees and the mountains from mingling with the heights of heaven, restrains ravenous beasts, and represses the force and cruelty of giants and tyrants. For all who resist God and oppose His beloved, even good things turn into evil and poison; though the common sun may rise for them, God wonderfully overthrows the tower of their power with a whirlwind <note>original: "ventorum turbine"</note>, of which thing daily examples provide testimony.

<header>THE GOLDEN SECRET OF PHILOSOPHY</header>

Besides these, there are certain people to be found who, being somewhat steeped in the knowledge of mediocre and minor arts, put on great airs. ->ADOLPHUS.<-

You are wandering too far from our intended purpose into the explanation of spiritual questions. The knowledge of divine and human goods must be sought with equal steps. From this meditation, the salvation of the soul <term>animæ salus</term> arises. Thus, a man learns that all things must be demanded through prayers from Him, the fountain of all good things; he learns that the cares of the earth should be cast aside, and that the gifts bestowed upon us must be guarded with humility and modesty. For it is in this [pride] that the devil’s greatest power and cunning shines through, and none of us would ever escape his force and cleverness unless the mercy of God protected us. Truly, what happiness, profit, or excellence can a man have, even if he abounds in all the pleasures and riches of life, unless the diseases of his soul are cured and removed? For this was the greatest benefit of all, when Christ our Savior always joined the forgiveness of sins to the healing of physical diseases.

->ADOLPHUS.<-

These things are true indeed, but they are not examined with a sufficiently proper balance by most people—a fault which I clearly cannot deny is present in myself, since my mind has for a long time clung more than is right to worldly desires and pleasures. # THE SECRET PHILOSOPHY OF THE GOLDEN VEIL #

[...of the path of] errors, since the way of this world is very slippery and dangerous. King Solomon also pleaded with God for wisdom, so that he might govern God’s people to His honor and praise, and from Him he received immense treasures of riches—just as the same Solomon says: wisdom calls out at the crossroads <note>A reference to Proverbs 8, where Wisdom is personified as a woman calling out to humanity</note>, inviting us to embrace her love and study. For the divine glory is great and distinguished, showing itself to us everywhere and inviting us, yet few of us consider these things attentively in this mortal life—which, though it flies away quite swiftly, nevertheless seems to pass slowly for most people. However, the mystery of God is great among those who fear Him, and light arises in the darkness for the pious, from a merciful and just God. <note>original: "Psal. 112"; Psalm 112:4: "Unto the upright there ariseth light in the darkness: he is gracious, and full of compassion, and righteous."</note> Therefore, let us not consume that precious treasure of time, the sharpness of the mind, and the strength of the body in acquiring and amassing worldly riches, nor let us imitate the ambitious and the proud; but rather, let us direct all our efforts toward the advantage and utility of the pious—even if they are simple—in the fear of the Lord.

->A D O L P H V S.<-

Though I confess these things are true, a certain doubt still gnaws at me, since I hear it is the opinion of the Philosophers that this treasure must be pleaded for and requested from God through prayers.

->S E N I O R.<-

You have already heard from me several times that the kingdom of God must be sought above all things, and from this, God will add all things to us; nor can man live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God. <note>A reference to Matthew 4:4, emphasizing spiritual sustenance over material gain.</note> By the same reasoning with which the demon tempted our Savior, he is still accustomed to tempt us today in times of necessity. For where faith and the word of the Lord are not present within us, we despair in afflictions and lose heart entirely. Indeed, the same thing happens to us when prosperity blows our way: we follow even the demon himself, the author of all evil, and seek help from him. He, however, promises us things that are not his own, and casts us into the furthest shadows of ignorance. Let us, therefore, prefer the heavenly bread and manna to earthly things by many <term>parasangs<gloss>An ancient Persian unit of distance, roughly 3.5 miles; used here to mean a vast distance.</gloss></term>. As for the fact that the Philosophers say God must be prayed to while investigating this treasure, this is rightly and truly said; for God alone grants it to us, provided we do not set fixed moments or methods for Him...

<meta>catchword: provided,</meta>

<summary>The Senior uses the example of King Solomon to explain that true alchemical wisdom and material wealth are gifts from God, granted only to those who seek spiritual virtue first. He warns that seeking the "treasure" through worldly ambition or during times of desperation leads to demonic temptation rather than divine enlightenment.</summary>
