...is nothing other than the extraction of water from the earth, and the release of this water back upon the earth until the earth itself rots <note>original: "putrescat"; the stage of putrefaction where matter decays to be reborn.</note>. This earth rots with the water and is purified: when it has been purified, with the help of God, the whole mastery <note>original: "magisterium"; the completion of the alchemical Great Work.</note> will be finished. For if there is no rot, the matter cannot be melted or dissolved; and if it is not dissolved, it will return to nothing. Therefore, you must acquire the method of solution, because this whole process consists in sublimation <term>sublimation: The process of heating a substance until it turns into vapor and then solidifies again, used here to purify the "spirit" of the material.</term>. Therefore, understand this sublimation well: and guard the spirit that ascends so that it does not flee; and what you do for the white stage <note>Albedo, the second major stage, resulting in silver.</note>, you must also do for the red stage <note>Rubedo, the final stage, resulting in gold.</note>. For this medicine is one in essence and similar in its way of acting. There is, however, an addition of a lemon-yellow color <note>original: "citrinitatis"; a transitional stage between the white and red work.</note>, which is perfected by the purest substance of our fixed sulfur.

There is, however, a difference between the Lunar medicine <note>The recipe for making Silver.</note> and the <margin>The difference between Lunar and Solar medicine.</margin> Solar medicine <note>The recipe for making Gold.</note>: because the latter contains the former within itself, but the former does not; since the one requires the purest white sulfur, just as the other requires red. Let these two bodies suffice for you, because they resemble what is sought: but you must labor in solution and refinement <note>original: "subtiliatione"; making the matter "subtle" or spiritualized.</note> so that you dissolve the entire matter. Afterward, congeal it, and calcine <term>calcination: Reducing a metal to a powder through intense heat to remove impurities.</term> it, and dissolve it again: and keep repeating this until you achieve a perfect fusion. Therefore, since this is difficult to accomplish, it is altogether better to dissolve the bodies through water alone, without calcination: because this is safer, although it is slower in operation.

Be patient and gentle, then, and do not be hasty in extracting the tincture <term>tincture: The soul or essence of the metal that carries its color and power of transformation.</term>: do not seek to finish quickly, for excessive heat burns everything and leads it to a remote region <note>An alchemical metaphor for ruining the work or driving off the volatile spirits.</note>. For if you use too much fire at the beginning of its mixing, know that corruption will occur in the tinctures: because medicines are burned by excessive heat. Therefore, cook gently, until the "whiteness of urine" <note>original: "album urinæ"; likely a reference to a specific cloudy appearance or sediment in the vessel used as a visual marker.</note> arranges all the parts. Wait patiently, then: and through grinding and roasting <note>original: "contritionem & assationem"</note>, which are the same thing, let the parts bound by the viscosity of the water within the bodies be divided by the fire. For the dissolved bodies are reduced to the nature of a spirit: and they are never separated, just as water mixed with water is not.

Therefore, dearest son, you must labor in the solution of the Stone: and separate its purer parts from the impure and heavier ones: and finish the work with the lighter parts, having cast away the heavier ones. Thus, once the form of the bodies is first dissolved into our Mercury <term>Mercury: Not common quicksilver, but the "Philosophical Mercury," the fundamental fluid substance underlying all metals.</term>, a new form is immediately introduced; the old form having been destroyed, which form is at first black in color <note>The Nigredo stage.</note>, foul in smell, and subtle and broken to the touch. Now let us move on to other things. Sky-blue <note>original: "caelestis"</note> is generated from white and black in due proportion: green, violet, and camel-colored <note>original: "camelinus"; likely a tan or brownish-yellow</note> are procreated from black, white, and red joined together in due proportion, according to more or less, and so with others. If, however, you labor without putrefaction, you will see a reddish oil swimming on top like fruit: and this is a sign that you labor in vain. But if you dissolve your matter with putrefaction, you will see it black: afterwards green: then saffron-colored <note>original: "croceam"</note> and reddish, and of various colors. This whole thing, however, is perfected through true decoction <note>A technical term for the process of heating or "cooking" the substance in a vessel</note>. For there are two: one which ascends, and the other which does not. This whole thing, however, is done through melancholy.

<margin>Melancholy.</margin>
Melancholy is an unstable thing, and is a smoke <note>The author equates melancholy with the volatile vapors or "spirits" released during heating</note> that quickly ascends: namely, to the higher place in which it is, that is, in the head: and if it evaporates, it makes a man sad, shadowy, and dark throughout his whole life. And if that melancholy—that is, that smoke—should remain and return to its own proper place, it renders the man humble and peaceful: because he then knows himself. On account of this, the mountain in which the tabernacle is situated cries out, saying: "I am who I am <note>original: "Ego sum, qui sum"; a reference to the divine name in Exodus 3:14, here applied to the alchemical matter</note>: and I am the black of the white, and the white of the black: my own proper color." By God, I speak the truth, and I do not lie. O blessed nature: and blessed is your operation: because from the imperfect you make the perfect, with true putrefaction, which is black and dark. ...so that your whole intellect should be focused on cooking green things <note>In alchemy, "green" often refers to the raw, unrefined state of the material, sometimes called the "Green Lion."</note>: if you wish to have fruit, cook, grind, repeat, and let it not weary you even though the work is long: because it dissolves and joins itself: it whitens itself, and adorns itself with redness: it makes itself yellow and black. Furthermore, it weds itself and conceives from itself: because there is both male and female within. Likewise, there is cold, that is, water: and heat, that is, fire: and moisture, that is, air: and dryness, that is, earth. And similarly there are various colors: because of which the Philosophers <note>The "Philosophers" refers to the long lineage of alchemical authorities.</note> gave it diverse names: because water is clear and bright: fire indeed is red and bright: air is also white and bright: <margin>The Hope of the Philosophers.</margin> earth is black, foul, and dark. Know however, Son: that the hope and estimation of all Philosophers consists in two things: yet a triple root pursues it: namely, the exaltation of water, which, if it stops proceeding as a liquid, then the exit of the oil will be revealed: and these are the two signs. Because of this the Philosopher says: "He who has whitened me, he shall make me red." <note>Original Latin: "qui dealbavit me, ille faciet me rubeum." This refers to the progression from the Albedo (white) stage to the Rubedo (red) stage.</note> The Philosophers have called our Stone <term>Lapis Philosophorum|The Philosopher's Stone, the legendary substance capable of transmuting metals and granting longevity.</term> by many names, and have shown many things for making the white and the red. Wherefore I tell you, that you do not need those names: nor those diverse things, except for one name, and one thing, namely, the water which is administered: and one action, namely, cooking. Therefore, I advise you, Son: that you do not approach the work unless you begin to try and cook the waters, which are thickened by putrefying: and to note the humidity and dryness of that putrefaction. Its kind are two Stones from the genus of Stones. For it is extracted from Stones that are generated in any time of the year; and one has wings, and the other does not. Wherefore, Son, if you desire to have the true mastery, it is necessary for you to burn those wings. <note>In alchemical symbolism, "wings" represent volatility—the tendency of a substance to evaporate. To "burn the wings" means to "fix" the substance so it remains stable under heat.</note> Likewise, know that it is not made white without combustion. But the combustion is of the moisture: for unless it were, it would never be whitened. Therefore it is necessary that it be cooked in its moisture until it parches and dries out: then let it be ground with sublimated water, and cooked again until it is dried again: and let this be repeated in turns until, by God's favor, it is whitened. And it must be noted that, even if all principles are understood by you, if you are ignorant of the whitening <note>Original: "dealbatio," the Albedo stage of purification.</note>, you lose the joy set apart for you: for by grinding and by salt it is refined: it casts out the dregs and loses its foulness: then, it receives the color of gold, and is fixed in a spiritual order. **DISCIPLE.** Most sweet Preceptor, I beseech you to explain this dryness and combustion to me, which you have repeated twice above: and whether they are one thing, or two? **MASTER.** For it is necessary that souls be deprived of their bodies, and this is done by combustion, after mortification <note>Mortification is the chemical "death" or breakdown of the initial substance.</note>. <margin>What the difference is between...</margin> **DISCIPLE.** Master, tell me, what the difference is be[tween]—

<margin>through combustion and mortification.</margin>
...through combustion and mortification: and whether they are one, or two: and from what source combustion proceeds. **MASTER.** Son, I have already told you that it is necessary for the whole Elixir to be burned and mortified because <term>Azoch|A term for the 'universal spirit' or alchemical Mercury</term>, or <term>Zericon|Often refers to red lead or the 'raw' mineral state of the matter</term>, or the divine water, does not become red except through mortification <note>In alchemy, 'mortification' refers to the symbolic death or breakdown of a substance, often resulting in a black color.</note> and roasting: however, the whitening <note>The 'Albedo' stage of the work.</note> does not happen except through combustion. Behold now, Son, for I have shown you, and I have demonstrated both mortification and whitening, and I have shown the red by distinguishing them from one another. From which you should know, that each of them is first whitened, and afterwards it becomes red: and all of this proceeds from the benefit of the water. That water is the thing which whitens and makes red. It is the water which dissolves and congeals: it is the water which putrefies, and afterwards makes diverse and new things sprout.

Wherefore, Son, I warn you, that your whole intention should be in the cooking of the water: and do not let it weary you, and do not care for other things, except for the water. Cook it little by little, until it changes from color to perfect color: and beware, lest in the beginning you burn its flowers, nor its greenness <note>The 'flowers' and 'greenness' represent the volatile, living energy of the substance that can be destroyed by too much heat.</note>: and do not be in a hurry to finish your work. Also, see that your door is well closed <note>A reference to the 'Hermetic Seal,' ensuring the vessel is airtight so no vapors escape.</note>, so that he who is within cannot fly away: and thus, God granting, you will come to the result.

Also, note Son, that to dissolve, to calcine, to sublimate, to tint, to wash, to cool, to water, to extract, to coagulate, to moisten, to soak, to wash, to cook, to fix, to grind, to dry, and to distill, are all one: namely, they denote extracting the soul or spirit from the body, and they signify the application of the truth, which is that the fire should be gentle. For this fire separates the Elements, and joins them together again. For this reason the whole art consists in converting the elements, that is, making the moist dry, and the fleeting <note>Original Latin: "fugiens." This refers to volatile substances like Mercury that evaporate or 'flee' the fire.</note> fixed.

Also I tell you, that the Elements are divided into four parts: of which two have the nature of earth and grant an appearance to the sight, which are earth and water. The others, however, are neither seen, nor touched, nor do they grant any appearance, nor is their place seen, nor their work, nor their power, except within the prior elements, namely earth and water. Wherefore many are deceived regarding the Elements: because it is not necessary that we divide the Elements: because every Being is a composite: and it is not possible for every composite to be divided. Therefore it is not necessary for us to make such a division. And similarly in creation, it is not necessary to divide, but rather to conjoin, and to follow nature. Therefore it is necessary for us to conjoin the Elements, namely, earth and water, so that they become one: and so that they cannot be divided: and in these two the other two consist, just as do air and fire. When, however, the four Elements are not conjoined, so that dry with moist, and cold with hot, become one without any division: nothing of this art will be perfected for men—

## RECAPITULATION OF THE WHOLE WORK.

Having discussed the discourses of this our <term>magistery|The completion of the Great Work or the technical mastery of alchemy</term> according to the requirements of its order, along with its sufficient causes: it remains now that our entire magistery be briefly held in memory, under a complete recapitulation in a brief discourse.

<margin>1. Disposition</margin>
We say, therefore, that the entire intention and the sum of this our work is nothing else but that the <term>Philosophical Stone|The transformative substance sought by alchemists</term> be taken: and with the persistence of labor, let the work of <term>sublimation|The process of vaporizing a solid and cooling it back into solid form to purify it</term>, <term>solution|Dissolving a solid into a liquid</term>, and <term>distillation|The heating and cooling process used to separate or purify liquids</term> of the first degree be applied to it, so that it may be cleansed from corrupting impurity.

<margin>2. Disposition</margin>
Then let it be <term>fixed|Rendered resistant to heat so that it no longer evaporates</term>, so that nothing ascends. And when it has been fixed, dissolve what will be soluble in it, and preserve it in the temperament of fire, until through the manner of sublimation, solution, and distillation, that which can be elevated is raised: when it has been elevated, preserve it in the temperament of fire, until the whole is fixed, and rests in the severity <note>Resistance to or endurance of high heat.</note> of the fire. And this is called the second degree of preparation, and in this indeed consists the one goal of preparation and perfection.

<margin>3. Disposition</margin>
In a similar way, let the Stone be administered in the third degree: which through the whole beginning, middle, and end consists in the completion of the preparation. And it is this: that you make the already fixed Stone volatile <note>Easily evaporated or moved by heat.</note> through the administration of fire, by the modes of sublimation: and make the volatile fixed: until it rests in the severity of the fire, and nothing is seen to ascend. And this third mode is complete.

<margin>4. Disposition</margin>
The fourth administration truly is, that you dissolve the Stone, and make it volatile by way of distillation, and when it has been so, fix the whole with a fire appropriate to it, until it rests, without the matter having any separation.

<margin>5. Disposition</margin>
The fifth administration is, that you dissolve the congealed Stone: and that which you have already fixed, make it volatile with the administration of fire: and again make the volatile fixed, until it remains in the battle of the fire <note>original: "pugnā ignis"; a technical term for the intense trial or testing of the substance’s stability under high heat.</note>: and when it has been so, keep it: until a greater quantity of fire can be administered to it: and thus you have seen the fifth circle <note>Likely referring to the cycle of alchemical operations, often depicted as a wheel or series of concentric circles.</note>.

<margin>6. Disposition</margin>
The sixth separation <note>Though the margin says "disposition," the Latin text here uses "separatio."</note> is, that you take our Stone—so dissolved, sublimated, congealed, <term>calcined|Reduced to a powder through intense heat</term>, <term>waxed|Softened into a wax-like state, also called inceration</term>, distilled, and fixed—and join it by a subtle ingenuity with the part that was saved and not fixed: and through the manner of solution, sublimation, and distillation, make it volatile, with the greatest ingenuity of fire. And when it has been so done, fix the whole, until it rests in the severity of the fire: and that nothing is seen to ascend. And thus you have governed the sixth disposition.

<margin>7. Disposition</margin>
But, because the entire <term>arcanum|A profound secret or mystery of the art</term> consists in the seventh preparation, we say to you, Dearest Son, that we have scattered this arcanum in various places, and likewise hidden it. Where we have spoken more openly and clearly, there [we have spoken] more obscurely: and where more hid-

...where we spoke obscurely, there we have shown it more openly. Therefore, do not despair, Son of Doctrine: for if you seek it, you shall find it: not through doctrine alone, but by the investigation of the movements of nature herself. But he who only follows the pursuit of books shall arrive most slowly at this most precious art. 

We say, therefore, that the seventh operation is: first, to <term>dissolve|The process of liquidizing a solid</term> the Blessed Stone; second, to <term>distill|The process of purifying a liquid by heating it into vapor and condensing it back into a liquid</term> it; third, to <term>sublimate|The process of heating a solid until it becomes a vapor and then collects again as a solid</term> it; fourth, to <term>incerate|To bring a substance to a soft, waxy, and fusible state</term> it; fifth, to <term>descend|Distillation "per descensum," where vapors are forced downward into a collection vessel</term> it; sixth, to <term>calcinate|Reducing a substance to a dry powder or ash through intense heat</term> it; and seventh, to <term>fix|To make a substance stable and resistant to fire so that it no longer evaporates</term> it. 

Behold the whole <term>magistery|The complete mastery or finished product of the alchemical art</term>, and what we have said is nothing else but this: to dissolve and congeal; to fix and make volatile, and to make the volatile fixed, and the fixed repeatedly volatile, until it flows and transforms in a certain <term>silver-making|Original: "Lunificum"; the power to transform metals into silver, associated with the Moon</term> or <term>gold-making|Original: "Solificum"; the power to transform metals into gold, associated with the Sun</term> completion. From the repetition of the preparation in the medicine, there results its goodness and the multiplication of its power to transform. From the diversity of repetition upon the Stone, according to its degrees, results the quality of its multiplication and the diversity of the transformation: so that of the medicines, some transform a body into twice its weight, some tenfold, some sevenfold, some a hundredfold, some a thousandfold, and some into an infinite gold-making—and a true perfection of silver-making transforms the body.

<margin>The cooking of mercury and sulfur.</margin>
Wherefore I notify you, that unless our Stone at the beginning of the cooking becomes water without any crushing by hands, you have not yet found the work. Therefore this magistery is nothing else than to cook <term>mercury|Original: "argentum vivum," literally "living silver" or quicksilver</term> and <term>sulfur|The active, combustible principle in alchemy</term> until they become one. Mercury protects the sulfur from burning if it has been well sealed: so that the mercury cannot vanish; and in that way, the sulfur cannot be burned nor destroyed.

<margin>Why mercury is said to be water.</margin>
For this reason, mercury is our water: and we see an example in common water, that everything cooked with it is not burned as long as the water is present, no matter how strong the fire is; but when the water is consumed, that which is in the vessel is burned. And therefore the Philosophers commanded the mouth of the vessel to be closed, so that the <term>blessed water|The purified alchemical solvent</term> would not exhale <note>Original: "exhalaret"; to escape as vapor.</note>, and would protect that which is in the vessel from burning. Indeed, the water placed with those things prevented the fire from burning them: and those things, the more they are occupied by the flame of the fire, the more they are hidden in the water, lest they be harmed by the heat of the fire. The water, however, receives them into its belly and repels the flame of the fire from them. I command you, however, in the beginning to make a light fire, until a patience <note>A state of equilibrium or endurance where the ingredients no longer react violently to the heat.</note> is established between the fire and the water. And after you see the water fixed, without any rising up, do not care what kind of fire it is. But it is good to rule with patience, until the spirit...

# HERE BEGIN THE ES-
## SENTIAL AS WELL AS
### accidental questions of Master Arnald to Boniface
### the Eighth.

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial 'I' containing floral motifs and architectural scrollwork.</image-desc>
Here begin the essential and accidental questions of Master Arnald of Villanova addressed to the Reverend [Pope], set down in a suitable form of composition. He asked, therefore, in the first place: Can the work of the stone <note>The "stone" refers to the Philosopher’s Stone, the legendary substance capable of turning base metals into gold.</note> be accomplished from the luminaries and "water of life" <note>original: "aquæ vitæ"; in this context, it refers to a potent solvent or "philosophical mercury" rather than brandy.</note> alone? And the answer is yes. Or from one luminary <note>original: "luminari"; the "luminaries" in alchemy are the Sun (Gold) and the Moon (Silver).</note> alone? At the end of the questions, it is shown that this is also the case.

->I I.<-
It is asked: Can it be made from the water of life alone? The answer: No. Because quicksilver <note>original: "ar. vi." or "argentum vivum," meaning mercury.</note> performs nothing unless it is cast into the womb of the woman, or the "fixed lime," so that she may nourish it; and our "earth" is the woman, and the mother of quicksilver. <note>Alchemists used gendered metaphors: the "woman" or "womb" represents the receptive, solid material (earth/salt) that hosts the "male" volatile spirit (mercury).</note>

->I I I.<-
It is asked: Can it be made from the luminaries alone, and why is an "imperfect body" added? The answer: Because the work is completed more quickly. Furthermore, the colors which the philosophers described appear in a more orderly fashion and according to the sayings of the philosophers.

->I V.<-
It is asked: Do the colors appear in the work of the luminaries? The answer: They appear, but they do not keep the same order.

->V.<-
It is asked: Should the Sun and Moon individually, or both together once a solution is made, pass through the alembic? <term>Alembic: a distillation apparatus consisting of two vessels connected by a tube.</term> The answer: The safer and better way is for each to pass through by itself; some can pass through together, but with greater difficulty. He requires them to pass through the alembic first separately, then joined together. For in this way, the craftsman can be certain when the luminaries have been reduced to the "first matter," that is, quicksilver.

->V I.<-
It is asked: Why is it necessary for the luminaries to be reduced into ☿ <note>The symbol for Mercury.</note> that is, quicksilver? The answer: Because quicksilver is the "seed" <note>original: "sperma"</note> of all metals. Without it, a perfect generation of metals could not be immediately produced by art from them, nor could their multiplication be achieved.

->VII.<-

The question is asked: Whether our **water of life**, which is called the **water of damp dew**, <note>original: "aqua roris madidi"; a poetic alchemical term for a purified mercurial solvent, often thought to be collected from the atmosphere or distilled to extreme purity.</note> ought to be **Mineral** or extracted from lead or tin. For the Philosophers say that water made from lead does not enter our **masterwork**, <note>original: "magisterium"; the Great Work of creating the Philosopher's Stone.</note> but only mineral water. This is because lead is "unclean," while our mineral water is "clean." Furthermore, lead causes **vitrification**, <note>original: "vitrificat"; the process of turning into glass, which alchemists sought to avoid as it "locked" the metals and prevented transformation.</note> whereas our water preserves the material from vitrification. Therefore, it ought to be Mineral.

->VIII.<-

The question is asked: How is mineral water recognized so that it may be distinguished from the water of lead? **Response:** If you fear **sophistication**, <note>In an alchemical context, "sophistication" means adulteration or counterfeiting.</note> make it pass through an **alembic**; <note>A specialized apparatus used for distillation.</note> and if no dregs remain in the bottom of the **gourd**, <note>original: "cucurbitæ"; the lower, flask-like part of the distillation apparatus.</note> the mineral and natural water is good. If, however, dregs remain and they return into a Metallic body, then the **quicksilver** <note>original: "arg. viv." for "argentum vivum," or mercury.</note> has been falsified according to their kind.

->IX.<-

It is asked ninthly: If mineral water ought to be purged, or how the water may be **amalgamated** with the body. **Response:** First, the water ought to be "mortified" with common salt until it is converted into the appearance of **celestial ashes**. <note>original: "speciem cineris cæleſtinam"; likely referring to a light blue or shimmering grey powder resulting from the chemical reaction.</note> Then it ought to be dried in a **urinal** <note>In alchemy, a "urinal" refers to a glass vessel shaped like those used by physicians for uroscopy, used here for sublimation.</note> for **sublimating**, and pure, clean, and "living" water will ascend. Afterward, it ought to be cooked out slowly with vinegar over a gentle fire for one hour. Then it must be dried again as before. After this, it must be passed through **leather**, <note>original: "corium"; mercury was often strained through chamois or soft leather to remove physical impurities.</note> and thus it can be safely placed into our masterwork.

->X.<-

The question is asked: If the **perfect bodies**, which are called the **luminaries**, <note>The "luminaries" are Gold (the Sun) and Silver (the Moon).</note> ought to be prepared before they enter our Masterwork. **Response:** Gold ought to be purged by **cementation**, <note>original: "cementum"; a dry refining process for gold using salts and heat.</note> and silver by **cupellation**. <note>original: "cinericium"; a refining process where silver is heated in a porous cup made of bone ash (cinder) to remove base metals.</note> Then they ought to be made into **foils**, just as casting-foils are made by art, or else finely filed. For the more they are refined and thinned, the more quickly they are converted into quicksilver. Once perfectly refined, they can enter our Masterwork—that is, they may undergo our "subtiliation."

->XI.<-

Eleventhly it is asked: If an **imperfect body** <note>Base metals like copper, tin, or lead.</note> ought to be prepared, and how one should proceed with it. **Response:** It must similarly be melted and purged. And if it should be **copper**, it ought to be purged and refined just as it is purged and refined for making **cauldrons**, <note>original: "caldariis"; indicating a high grade of industrial purity.</note> then filed most finely, and afterward subtly amalgamated. Then it can be placed into our operation.

->XII.<-

The question is asked: How many parts of water ought to be placed in the first con-

### XIII.

The question is asked: How many parts should there be of water, and how many parts of the amalgam, so that the entire body is converted into **quicksilver**, <note>original: "arg. vivum" for *argentum vivum*, mercury.</note> and so that the whole may pass through the leather, i.e., <gloss>chamois leather</gloss>. <note>original: "Sämisch leder"; a soft, porous leather used to filter impurities from liquid mercury.</note>

### XIV.

The question is asked: Once the imperfect body has passed through the leather and been converted into quicksilver, in what vessel should it be placed?
**Response:** In a perfect glass vessel shaped like a side-dish, <note>original: "parobsis"; a shallow bowl or platter.</note> and it should be covered with another similar but wider one. ### XV.

The question is asked: How will the blackness appear, and how is the blackness to be removed? **Response:** On the first day, the blackness will appear only on the surface, like a certain black mist, and it must be removed very skillfully with a clean stone or glass spatula, after first uncovering the vessel; separate the blackness, which among the Philosophers is called the <term>dark garment</term>. <note>original: "vestis tenebrosa"; a metaphorical name for the initial impure state of the matter.</note> Likewise, once the vessel is covered, the fire should be continued until the blackness appears again. And let that blackness be removed again, and kept cleanly in a glass vessel with the aforementioned material; and let this be done continually until no blackness appears on the surface, and the stone remains clear and clean, for truly then the water is purified from its earth, and then you have the two elements of the stone, namely earth and water.

However, when the blackness has totally vanished, it is a sign of the "dew of putrefaction" and the dissolution of the stone. Now, [these things] last...

### XVII.

The question is asked: When the earth has been separated, what must finally be done with the water? **Response:** The water is to be placed in a **urinal** <note>original: "urinali"; a round-bottomed glass flask used for boiling and distillation, named for its resemblance to a vessel used for medical examinations.</note> with an **alembic** <note>term: "alembic" - a capped lid or "still-head" with a beak that allows vapors to condense and flow into a separate container.</note> placed on top with its receiver; as is the custom, place it securely among the ashes in the distillation furnace, and it is distilled with a slow fire. And be attentive during the distillation, so that between one drop and the following drop there are 40 moments. This is what the **Philosopher** <note>Alchemists often referred to Aristotle or Hermes Trismegistus simply as "The Philosopher."</note> means by 40 words with a distinct pause in the middle, dividing one thousand, one hundred and thirty-three spoken words. And this is the order and method to be observed in distillation. However, that which you find in the bottom is distilled with new water, using triple or quadruple its amount, until it is entirely dissolved and converted into **quicksilver**. <note>original: "argentum vivum", literally "living silver" or mercury.</note> And distill as before and let it stand as many times as necessary until the dregs are utterly removed. And when the water itself has been distilled, you then have the quickened water.

### XVIII.

The question is asked: For how long does this distillation last? **Response:** There is no determined time whether for a greater or lesser period, but it depends on the greater or lesser quantity of the water, provided a uniformity of the fire is maintained.

### XIX.

The question is asked: Once the distillation is finished, what is to be done then with the water? **Response:** Take the earth which you separated and saved above, pulverize it, and place it in the aforementioned glass vessel with the joints of both sealed with clay; <note>original: "lutatis juncturis"; using "lute," a clay or paste used to hermetically seal laboratory apparatus.</note> and give to it some of the aforementioned distilled water until it floats on top, and with a light fire—just as was the fire of **putrefaction** <note>The "fire of putrefaction" refers to a very gentle, steady heat, often compared to the heat of a fermenting dung heap or a brooding hen.</note>—for 4 days or until the water is dried into the earth. And so again give it some of the aforementioned water until it dries. And so on, until the earth is white and clear and purified. When it has been purified, with the help of God, the entire **Great Work** <note>original: "magisterium"; the "mastery" or the completed alchemical process.</note> will be directed toward its goal.

### XX.

The question is asked: What will have to be done with the earth thus purified? **Response:** It is to be placed in a urinal among the ashes in the sublimation furnace with an alembic placed on top, to which a strong fire should be given, until whatever water there is ascends into the alembic and the earth remains at the bottom. Then truly you have water, air, earth, and fire there. Because that earth is of a fiery nature.

<header>ARNOLD'S QUESTIONS</header>

### XXI.

The question is asked: What must be done, and what is the duration for the **putrefaction** <note>Putrefaction (decomposition) was considered a vital step to "kill" the base metal so it could be reborn as gold or silver.</note> and cleansing of the earth? **Response:** In 40 days, and sometimes more or less, depending on the quantity of the earth or the water.

### XXII.

The question is asked: Should the **luminaries** <note>term: "luminaries" - an alchemical term for the Sun (gold) and the Moon (silver).</note> be prepared in the same manner as the **imperfect body**? <note>term: "imperfect body" - the base metal (often lead or mercury) that the alchemist intended to transform.</note> **Response:** Yes, entirely so, because otherwise they could not take on the dignity of the **ferment** <note>The "ferment" acts like yeast in bread, a small amount of "perfected" material that catalyzes the transformation of the larger mass.</note> until they themselves have been dissolved, putrefied, distilled, and purified, just as was said regarding the imperfect body; and in the governance of this process lies the key and the secret of the first art.

### XXIII.

The question is asked: What should be done with the distilled waters produced from the luminaries and the imperfect body? **Response:** The water of the imperfect body is to be divided into two equal parts. One part should be joined with the water of the Sun (that is, with the water distilled from gold), and the other part with the water distilled from the Moon (silver). Then there are two types of **quicksilver** <note>original: "arg. viv." (argentum vivum); literally "living silver" or mercury.</note>. Truly, they are even created from a single seed. Then, the lunar water should be divided into nine parts. Each should be placed in a separate vial and kept among the ashes in a very slow heat, just as a hen nurtures her eggs.

### XXIV.

The question is asked: What must be done with these waters if you wish to aim for the **Moon**? <note>To "aim for the Moon" means to perform the *Albedo* or "White Work," the stage of the process that produces silver.</note> **Response:** Take 4 parts of the earth of the imperfect body, calcined <note>term: "calcined" - reduced to a powder through high heat.</note> and whitened, as has been described. Take also one part of the earth of the Sun, which is called the **solar ferment** <note>original: "fermentum solificum"</note>, and another part of the earth of the Moon, which is called the **lunar ferment** <note>original: "fermentum lunificum"</note>. That is, if the earth of the imperfect body is one pound, add three <note>likely three ounces or drachms, to maintain the proportions</note> of the solar ferment and the same amount of the lunar ferment. Let them be mixed well and finely, and place them in a round glass vessel with a narrow neck. Pour one vial of the lunar water over it, and then, having closed the vessel with a linen cloth, let it be placed in the **philosophical furnace** <note>term: "philosophical furnace" - a specialized oven designed to maintain steady, precise temperatures over many weeks.</note> among the ashes at the **second fire** <note>Alchemists used four degrees of heat; the "second fire" is a moderate heat, stronger than a lamp but weaker than a direct coal fire.</note>. Continue the fire steadily until the material is dried out. Then, give it another vial [of water] and continue the fire as before; let this be done until the material melts like wax. From that moment, the medicine for the **white work** is perfected.

### XXV.

The question is asked: How many **imbibitions** <note>term: "imbibition" - the process of a dry powder slowly soaking up a liquid until it is saturated.</note> are sufficient for the material to melt like wax for the white work? **Response:** At most seven, and at least five.

### XXVI.

The question is asked: How long do the imbibitions for the white work last? **Response:** If there was one pound of the imperfect body, it will be fixed...

# TO BONIFACE THE EIGHTH #

... [the material] is fixed with **imbibitions** <note>original: "imbibitionibus" — the process of repeatedly adding liquid to a solid substance so it "drinks" or absorbs the liquid.</note> in 90 days for the **white work**, and for the same amount of time for the **red work**. That is to say, it is sometimes fixed in a greater or lesser amount of time, depending on the skill of the operator and the greater or lesser portion of the pigment materials used.

### XXVII.

The question is asked: Once the **medicine for the white** <note>The "white work" or *albedo* is the penultimate stage of the Great Work, resulting in a stone capable of transforming base metals into silver.</note> is complete, how is it perfected for the **red**? <note>The "red work" or *rubedo* is the final stage, resulting in the most potent form of the Stone, capable of making gold.</note> **Response:** Take 1 lb. of the aforementioned white medicine. Let it be placed and held among hot ashes over the first level of heat until the medicine is dried and reduced to ash. Then, give it the first flask of **solar water** <note>original: "aqua solari" — water distilled from gold or associated with the sun.</note> to drink—that is, water distilled by the sun—and continue the second level of heat until the matter is dried. Afterward, give it another flask, and so let the imbibitions and desiccations continue successively until the matter turns red and melts like wax. Thus will the medicine be perfected for the red work.

### XXVIII.

The question is asked: Should the entire flask, or all the water of a single flask—whether **lunar** <note>Associated with silver.</note> or **solar**—be added all at once during a single imbibition of the solar or lunar medicine? **Response:** You ought to pour only enough over the matter so that the matter is just covered with water, and no more. Let it soak that up, and then pour on the next amount and dry it, and so on until the end.

### XXIX.

The question is asked: How is the **projection** <note>term: "projection" — the climactic step where a small amount of the Philosopher's Stone is cast upon a mass of molten base metal to transform it into precious metal.</note> of this solar or lunar medicine performed? **Response:** One part is to be placed upon ten parts of **imperfect metal**, or **quicksilver** <note>original: "arg. viv." or *argentum vivum* — mercury.</note>, and the whole will become medicine. From that medicine, one part is to be placed upon a thousand parts of an imperfect body. Finally, from that last medicine, one part is to be placed upon a thousand parts of a hot and clean imperfect body, and it will become a **silver-making** or **gold-making** body <note>original: "lunificum vel solificum"</note> according to the medicine, passing every test of the assay.

### XXX.

The question is asked: How is this white or red medicine **multiplied**? <note>Multiplication is the process of increasing the quantity and potency of the Philosopher's Stone.</note> **Response:** I told you, **Holy Father** <note>The text is addressed directly to Pope Boniface VIII.</note>, by word of mouth. For that reason, I will not say it in writing; for I told you, Father, what none of the philosophers have dared to reveal. Therefore, I beseech Your Holiness and adjure you not to reveal these things except to the sons of wisdom and those who labor faithfully in this art. The **Philosopher’s Stone** is increased through **putrefaction** <note>The stage of decomposition or "blackness."</note> and through frequent repetition.

# THE ACCIDENTAL QUESTIONS BEGIN.

## I.

To the accidental questions which you proposed to me, Holy Father, I will respond to you in order. First you ask: How many furnaces are necessary for the operation? I respond: There is one <term>furnace</term> <note>original: "furnellus"</note> for putrefaction, distillation, incineration, sublimation, imbibition, and fixation, as is evident from the figure.

## II.

How many vessels are necessary? Response: If you have a good understanding of the essential questions, this has been sufficiently determined.

## III.

Whether the vessels ought to be closed, and with what they ought to be closed. Response: The vessels for putrefaction should be closed with a tight linen cloth. The vessels for fixation, distillation, and incineration ought to be <term>luted</term> <note>original: "lutari" — the process of sealing joints with a paste called "lute" (often made of clay, lime, or egg whites) to make them airtight and heat-resistant.</note> with gypsum and egg white along the joints. The <term>receiver</term> <note>original: "receptorium"</note> of the distillation should not be luted to the <term>beak of the alembic</term> <note>original: "naso alembici" — the downward-pointing spout or "nose" of the distilling apparatus through which the vapor passes.</note>, but it should remain open.

## IV.

How many operating fires are necessary? Response: Four; read these verses and you will understand. "Let the first be named, in which the second is shown; nature rejoices in the second when the senses are balanced. The third exceeds, whose tolerance causes harm; the fourth—the second destroyer—knows not how to proceed." Or thus: "Let the first be formed so that sense is granted to it; nature rejoices in the second when the senses are balanced; the third exceeds, whose tolerance causes harm; once sense is destroyed, the fourth wishes to proceed." <note>These verses describe the four degrees of heat used in alchemy, moving from a gentle warmth (like a brooding hen) to the intense heat required for sublimation.</note>

## V.

How the fires are to be ordered in the operation. Response: [The first is for] putrefaction; the second for distillation and fixation; the third for incineration; and the fourth for sublimation—that is, the force of sublimation when the spirit is separated from the body, and it is called the <term>bird of Hermes</term> <note>original: "avis Hermetis" — a symbolic name for the volatile spirit or vapor that rises during the heating process.</note>.

## VI.

How many colors occur in the work of the operator? Response: There are three principal colors appearing in the work: <term>black</term> <note>original: "niger"</note>, <term>white</term> <note>original: "albus"</note>, and <term>red</term> <note>original: "rubeus"</note>. But there are many other colors appearing in our work, which occur in the work as follows: The first color is <term>silvery</term> <note>original: "argenteus"</note>, the second <term>black</term>, the third <term>violet</term>, the fourth <term>lemon-yellow</term> <note>original: "citrinus"</note>, the fifth <term>green</term>, the sixth <term>peacock-like</term> <note>original: "pavonius" — referring to the iridescent "Peacock's Tail" stage where many colors appear at once</note>, the seventh <term>bright silver</term> <note>original: "argentinus"</note>, the eighth <term>white</term>, the ni—

...the ninth citrine, the tenth saffron, the eleventh a perfect red. And there are many other intermediate colors, about which you need not be concerned.

### VII.

**How the colors appear in the amalgamation.** Response: The first color is silver. In <term>putrefaction</term> <note>original: "putrefactione" — the stage of decomposition where the matter turns black, symbolizing the death of the old form.</note>, it is black on the surface only. In the <term>conjunction</term> <note>original: "conjunctione"</note> of the ferment with the body, it varies with all colors imaginable. In <term>fixation</term> <note>original: "fixione" — the process of making a volatile substance stable and resistant to heat.</note>, however, it receives the supreme colors which are never destroyed by fire or any other means whatsoever.

### VIII.

**How the perfect red medicine gives weight to the Moon and to other bodies not having weight.** And the white medicine decreases the weight of lead, and brings it back to the weight of the Moon <note>original: "Luna" — the alchemical name for silver.</note>. Response: The red medicine constricts the parts of the Moon and other bodies that do not have the weight of the Sun <note>original: "Sol" — the alchemical name for gold.</note> until they are converted into the weight of Gold. And thus it turns them to its own specific form, which specific form it increases because of the deficiency and long perfection of its ferment. This ferment attracts and converts the imperfect body and the <term>water of life</term> <note>original: "aquam vitæ"</note> to its own nature and perfection. From these statements it follows that silver and copper are entirely converted into gold by the perfect medicine of redness; their weights increase by a greater or lesser degree, and they are diminished in quantity by this red matter. But it only stains them in perfect redness. Lead and <term>quicksilver</term> <note>original: "arg. vivum" or argentum vivum.</note>, however, when they are converted into silver by the medicine of whiteness, increase in quantity and decrease in weight. Tin, also, is not diminished in quantity and increases in weight. But it is whitened with a perfect whiteness according to every judgment and test, except for the <term>royal cement</term> <note>original: "regale cementum" — a harsh refining process used to separate gold from silver; the text claims the alchemical silver is so pure it might even "evaporate" in this intense test where standard silver remains.</note> in which all silver, even the best in the whole world, vanishes as smoke.

### IX.

**How it is possible that one part of one medicine converts a million parts of quicksilver, or of an imperfect body, into a gold-making body.** Response: The whole matter of this medicine has been converted through art and subtle ingenuity into a spiritual matter or substance, which among philosophers is called the <term>fifth essence</term> <note>original: "quinta essentia" — the quintessence or purest state of matter that transcends the four elements.</note>. Since in every way it has the nature of an informing and perfecting form. And therefore the form has an informing nature to infinity. Provided that the proper matter is brought near; for this reason, if it were possible that the whole water of the sea were quicksilver—a warmed world or a fused imperfect body—and if a little of this medicine were placed upon it, all that water would be converted into <term>Gold</term> <note>original symbol: ☉</note> or <term>Silver</term> <note>original symbol: ☽</note>. Because one part converts another and so on to infinity, and it would happen as quickly as <term>illumination</term> <note>original: "illuminationes" — likely referring to the instantaneous nature of a flash of light.</note> occurs.

He details how different metals react to the "red" and "white" medicines, noting changes in their physical volume and weight during the process.</summary>

### X.

**How should the saying of the ancient philosophers be understood: "There is one stone, one medicine, one vessel, one regimen for making the white and the red successively"?** Response: It was stated above that the nature of metals is one—that is, <term>quicksilver</term> <note>original: "arg. viv." or "argentum vivum"</note> thickened by sulfuric heat in the womb of the earth. Therefore, metals must not differ except in their degree of development. It was also stated elsewhere that these bodies must be reduced to the "seed" of metals; the means of doing this is through quicksilver—that is, to reduce the bodies into seed, which is quicksilver. Since all the <term>pigments</term> <note>original: "pigmentalia" — refers here to the chemical components or coloring agents used in the work.</note> of this work are reduced to quicksilver, and all are quicksilver for both the white and the red (depending on a greater or lesser <term>decoction</term> <note>original: "decoctionem" — a process of boiling or prolonged heating to extract or concentrate essences.</note>), it is therefore called "one stone" because of the quicksilver, which is the neutral seed of all metals. It is "one medicine," whether whitened or reddened. There is one vessel of <term>putrefaction</term> <note>original: "putrefactionis" — the stage of breakdown and blackening.</note> and, in succession, one vessel of distillation, one of incineration, and one regimen of <term>fixation</term> <note>original: "fixionis" — making a substance stable in fire.</note> for both the white and the red.

### XI.

**How should that saying in Aristotle's *Meteorology* be understood: "The power of non-burning sulfur congeals quicksilver and converts it into true silver. And the power of red non-burning sulfur congeals quicksilver and converts it into gold. And this is the greatest thing that Alchemists can acquire in this life"?** Response: In his book <term>*Meteorology*</term> <note>original: "Meteororum" — Aristotle’s work on natural phenomena. In the Middle Ages, an appendix by the Persian philosopher Avicenna was often included, which discussed metals.</note>, Aristotle demonstrates in his sayings the possibility and truth of Alchemy. He posits the final conversion by art, saying: "White sulfur is the perfect medicine for the white <note>the production of silver</note>, and red sulfur is the perfect medicine for the red <note>the production of gold</note>." And when Alchemists possess perfect whiteness and redness, they possess the perfect stone for both. This is the greatest thing they can acquire through their art. But if someone should ask, "Is this true? Why then did Aristotle say: 'Let the Alchemists rejoice, for one species of metals cannot be transmuted into another; they can only wipe away the impurities of true lead so that they look like gold, yet it remains lead...'" <note>This famous skeptical quote, "Scyant artifices alchimie..." (Let the practitioners of alchemy know...), was actually written by Avicenna but was long attributed to Aristotle, creating a major debate among medieval scientists.</note>

...remains, just as in its origin. Response: In these words, Aristotle shows a twofold mode of the operation of Alchemy: one <term>sophisticated</term> <note>In an alchemical context, "sophisticated" refers to "sophistry"—fraudulent or superficial methods that only mimic the appearance of gold rather than changing its nature.</note> and the other true. ->XII.<-

How should that saying be understood, which Pythagoras says: "Whoever does not coagulate silver into white, and does not join it with our silver, let him choose no other way for himself to work the <term>whiteness</term> <note>original: "albedinem" — the 'white' stage or 'albedo' of the Great Work, which produces silver.</note>, and let him not weary his body for those things which he cannot reach." And this is not joined to gold unless the gold is dissolved and reduced to ash with its own fixed water, from which it was created and composed. And then the Philosophers called that gold not "of the common people," but "their own," or "ours." Likewise, they say the same concerning silver. Therefore, if the quicksilver is congealed with the body as stated in our work, and through it and with it, it is fixed and congealed, and if it is joined with our prepared silver—as stated in our operation—with our white silver for the white work, and with our gold as stated in our operation for the red work, we shall have chosen that perfect way to the white and the red; otherwise, we would not be able to reach the perfection of this art. Many other paths of inquiry could be made concerning the aforesaid things, which are now made easier through what has been said...

*That most wise* Hermes Trismegistus, *when he was asked by* Poimandres <note>Poimandres, often described as a personification of the Divine Mind, is the figure who initiates Hermes into sacred knowledge in the "Corpus Hermeticum," the foundational texts of alchemy and Hermeticism.</note> *what he wished to hear and to learn, replied: "I desire," I say, "to know* God *and the causes of things." So much is the desire for knowing innate in noble minds, that it is their greatest consolation and pleasure to walk in the field of contemplation of the highest things. For the mind, drawing its origin from the fountain of eternity, always looking back toward its own beginning, and finding rest nowhere in fleeting and transitory things, by an innate instinct always desires to handle higher and loftier matters.*

*Hence the ancient sages were not content with the contemplation of the stars and heavenly spheres, or of other physical things contained in this sublunary <note>The "sublunary" sphere refers to the Earth and its atmosphere below the moon, which in ancient science was the only place where things grew old, decayed, and died.</note> world—all of which are fleeting and corruptible. But searching far more deeply into the most hidden secrets of nature, they discovered a most precious Gem <term>Gemma preciosissima</term> <note>original: "Gemmam reperêrunt preciosissimam" — This "Gem" is a poetic name for the Philosopher's Stone, the ultimate goal of the alchemical quest.</note>, which by a vast distance leaves behind everything generated and produced from corruptible elements. Which has rightly been held by all sages as a miracle of nature. For it exists as the center of all created things; indeed, in it all the powers and virtues of all the stars, plants, stones, animals, and minerals are essentially and truly, fully and sufficiently contained. So that among all the created things of this world, nothing more precious nor more useful than this Gem itself can be found. Which not only has a wonderful sympathy <term>Sympathiam</term> <note>In alchemical philosophy, "sympathy" describes the invisible, energetic resonance between different parts of the universe, such as a planet's influence on a specific metal or plant.</note> with all created things, but also with effective*

...it holds the power to remove corruption from all the aforementioned things, to restore them to their internal *Anatomy* <note>In this context, "Anatomy" refers to the essential, spiritual, and physical structure of a substance, which the alchemist seeks to restore to its perfect state.</note>, and return them to a youthful and flourishing state. Besides its immense and nearly innumerable virtues, this *Gem* has been called the *Secret of the Philosophers* <term>Arcanum Philosophorum</term> <note>original: "Arcanum Philosophorum"</note> by the wise. This secret is not only powerful and sufficient for curing diseases, but it also purges and cleanses all the "sick bodies" of metals from the leprosy of impurity and corruption, and reduces them to the complete and perfect form of gold and silver. Even if this appears ridiculous to the unskilled, its possibility can nevertheless be demonstrated by the clearest reasons.

...[to see its wonders] lie before him. Very few are those who understand its most profound mysteries. There are many indeed who, with Cyclopean daring <note>original: "Cyclopico ausu." A reference to the Cyclopes of myth, implying a blind, clumsy, or brute-force approach lacking intellectual or spiritual "sight."</note>, thrust themselves into these most high matters. Those who are steeped in good literature <note>That is, the "litterae humaniores" or classical education.</note> are terrified by the sublimity and difficulty of these things, so that they dread and neglect to touch the most healthy investigation of them. Meanwhile, the unlearned <term>Idiotæ: In this historical context, this refers to those without formal education or specialized knowledge, rather than being a modern insult.</term>, possessing not even a grain of salt <note>original: "micam salis"; a common Latin idiom for wit, common sense, or discernment.</note>, nor understanding the smallest spark of nature's possibility, wallow like swine in a most fertile field; they devastate and tear apart all the best things rather than building or erecting even the slightest thing in this noble Theater <note>The "Theater of Nature" was a common metaphor for the observable world as a stage of divine handiwork.</note>. 

They rely only on wavering opinions; since they are utterly blind, or at least one-eyed, in searching out the causes of hidden things, it is no wonder that if a question is raised merely regarding the subjects of this most noble art, how many myriads of disagreeing opinions emerge. What then will they say about the *preparation*, when the hinge of the whole business <note>original: "cardo totius negotii"; the central point upon which the success of the alchemical work turns.</note> rests upon it, and it is the most hidden thing of all in this sacred art? 

Therefore, there is no reason to wonder why so few out of such a great number of seekers reach the desired goal. And for that reason, the logic of those who inconsiderately deny the possibility of this most excellent art—simply because so few have found it—is very weak. For no one can obtain a fundamental knowledge of this art for himself except through constant "conversation" with the wise—those who have dedicated this hidden art to posterity under many enigmas and concealed figures. The best rule of all is to look for the consensus where all those authors agree; for there the truth is found, without ambiguity or sophistry <term>Sophismate: Deceptive or fallacious arguments intended to mislead.</term>.

Each author, however, used his own style according to his own pleasure; and what one has hidden, another has revealed.

...particles are scattered into this lower world. All herbs, all trees, sprout and bloom by its vigor and power: All metals and stones are produced into their being by its heat. This celestial Phoebus <note>A poetic name for the Sun, often used in alchemy to represent the source of spiritual and physical light.</note> has produced in this lower world a peculiar subject, to which, as if to a son, he has granted all the properties and virtues in a sensible form <note>A form that can be perceived by the senses.</note> which he himself possesses in a celestial form. 

But it is surrounded by a new, most strong body, and bound as if by adamantine <note>Unbreakable or diamond-like bonds; in alchemy, this refers to the hard, unrefined state of the raw material before it is processed.</note> chains; which, if you are wise enough to be able to loosen them, it will appear to you in most beautiful and very delightful clothing. Yet this is not yet enough, but it must be led to a new generation, it must die, and rise again from death; then it will appear in a new and incorruptible body, with a truly royal countenance, to whose scepter all things in the sublunary <note>The region below the moon, i.e., the Earth and its atmosphere.</note> world shall be subject, and all things shall be possible for it which are possible under the celestial Phoebus. 

And what is more: those things which the celestial Phoebus works through the succession and intervals of time, this Phoebus of ours <note>The alchemical agent or the Philosopher's Stone.</note> completes suddenly, and as if in a moment; just as the sun in the mines brings gold to its perfection only after a thousand years, our secret <term>arcanum|A hidden, powerful mystery or medicinal substance</term>, however, restores perfect health to the sick in a few hours, and in the space of half an hour converts the leprous <note>In alchemy, "leprous" refers to base or impure metals like lead or tin, which were seen as "diseased" versions of gold.</note> bodies of metals into perpetual gold <note>original: "solificum," meaning sun-making or gold-producing.</note>. Although this itself may be believed by many to be an empty figment: nevertheless, its probability can be sufficiently shown. # ROGER BACON, BOOK 2.
## *On the Mirror of Alchemy.*

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial letter 'T' featuring foliate patterns.</image-desc>

The **tincture** <term>tincture: a potent alchemical substance or "elixir" capable of transforming base metals or healing the body.</term> is generated solely from the **Mercury of the Wise** <note>Latin: Mercurius Sapientum. This is not common mercury (quicksilver), but a purified, philosophical substance believed to be the "soul" of metals.</note>, which is called the **first matter** <term>first matter: "prima materia," the original, primitive substance from which all things are created and to which they can be returned.</term>, **permanent water**, the **Vinegar of the Philosophers**, **virgin's milk**, and **corporal mercury**. Nothing foreign or strange is mixed with it—such as salts, alums, or vitriols—because the entire power of this **Mastery** <note>The "Magistery" refers to the successful completion of the alchemical Great Work.</note> is generated from this alone. Therefore, every thing is dissolved so that it may be **multiplied** <term>multiplied: "multiplicari," the process of increasing the power or quantity of the alchemical medicine.</term>.

The aforementioned Mercury is the root and the tree, from which infinite and many branches arise and grow.

The first labor for making the **elixir** is **sublimation** <term>sublimation: a process where a solid is heated into a vapor and then condensed back into a solid, used here as a metaphor for purifying the "stone" of its impurities.</term>, which is nothing other than the refinement of our **stone**, in which it is cleansed of all its superfluities.

The fixed and volatile parts are not separated from one another, but remain united and are **fixed** <note>In alchemy, "fixing" means making a volatile substance stable under heat.</note> together, so that both may have an easy fusion in the fire.

Take, therefore, the aforementioned Mercury, which you place in a sealed glass vessel into its warm bed for a **philosophical month** <note>Latin: mensem Philosophicum. Typically a period of 40 days, representing a symbolic cycle of time for the transformation of the matter.</note>, until it begins to putrefy and coagulate within itself, and all...

...that its own moisture may be consumed within itself, and even be turned into black earth. In this sublimation, the true separation of the four elements is completed. For the cold and watery element is changed into hot and dry earth, which is the **crow’s head** <term>crow’s head: Latin *caput corvi*, a symbol for the *nigredo* or blackening stage of the alchemical process, representing the "death" of the material before its purification</term>, the mother of the remaining elements. Furthermore, let the black earth be soaked with its own water in a slow heat and dried out until it is sufficiently cleansed and brought to whiteness.

When our fruitful earth is moistened with its own proper water in its thirst, it drinks it with great greed until it becomes pregnant and thereafter bears a hundredfold fruit.

Now proceed further with the white earth, for which you will increase the fire, until by the motion of continuous heat it is digested into an excellent redness, which is called **red coral**. Red Sulphur is blood, purple gold is burnt saffron. Repeat this three or four times with new material, and you will have the most perfect **red stone**, red as blood, with which you will tincture <term>tincture: the act of transforming or "staining" a base metal into a noble one through the power of the Elixir</term> Mercury and all imperfect Metals.

It is necessary, however, that you take three parts of the aforementioned Sulphur. Add one part of pure Gold—and this reduced into a subtle powder—and two parts of its water. Mix these three subtly until they become one inseparable thing. Let these then be digested in their furnace into a red stone.

...black like coal. And thus the common quicksilver <note>Latin: *argentum vivum vulgi*. Alchemists distinguished between the mercury bought from a merchant and the "Philosophical Mercury" they refined themselves.</note> is turned into a hot and tempered nature.

Therefore, the common quicksilver cannot be perfectly mixed with the metallic bodies unless those bodies are first reduced into the form and appearance of quicksilver. For this reason, when you wish to mix gold with common quicksilver, it is necessary that you reduce the body of the gold itself into the form of quicksilver through the bond of natural love. Then the Male shall be united with the female, because the quicksilver of the body <note>Latin: *argentum vivum corporis*, referring to the liquid essence extracted from gold.</note> is active, hot, and dry, but the common quicksilver is passive, cold, and moist. It is like a female who is kept in her chamber in a tempered heat until the **Eclipse** <term>Eclipse: Latin *ecclispsin*, used here to denote the *nigredo* or "blackening" stage, where the matter seems to "die" and turn dark before its rebirth.</term>, which is to say, the blackness. This is the secret of our true dissolution, because then the parts can be separated from one another, and they are converted into a powder whiter than snow.

Regarding what is said in the *Testament* <note>Referring to the *Testamentum*, a famous text attributed to the scholar and mystic Raymund Llull.</note> about the matter of our Stone, it must be known that we have introduced foreign things into this mastery only by way of comparison. In truth, only one single thing exists for our Stone: to which we neither add any foreign thing, nor from which do we take anything away. We have also described three stones—namely the **mineral, animal, and vegetable**—even though there is only one single stone of our art. This is because this composite consists of three things: namely **body, soul, and spirit**. The composite is called **mineral** because it comes from the mine; **animal** because it possesses a soul; and **vegetable** because it grows and multiplies <note>In alchemy, "vegetable" does not mean a plant, but rather anything that has the power to "vegetate" or grow and increase in volume or potency.</note>. In this lies every secret of our mastery: which is the Sun, the Moon, and the **Water of Life** <note>Latin: *aqua vitae*</note>. And this Water of Life is the soul and the life of bodies, through which our Stone is quickened and sustained. Therefore we call it "Heaven," and the **Quintessence** <term>Quintessence: The "fifth essence" or purest element, beyond the four physical elements of earth, air, fire, and water.</term>, and "Incombustible Oil," and by infinite other names, because it is almost as incorruptible as the Heavens in the continuous circulation of its own movement. Furthermore, there are many who go astray, believing that there is one individual thing produced by nature that has the power of transmuting metals. This is false, because the principles of our art are demonstrated in the *Book of the Quintessence*.

For Mercury, when extracted from gold, holding the condition of the male and aided by its essential form (which gives being to the Stone), is dissolved in the womb of the female, which holds the passive role. From these two—namely the mineral and the vegetable—the Stone of the Philosophers is composed. And nothing else ought to be mixed here except the male and the female. From this arises our "Heaven," or **Vegetable Mercury**, which is of the nature of heaven and is called the Quintessence, the Stone of Hermes.

...sublimation, calcination <note>Latin: *calcinatio*. The process of heating a substance until it is reduced to a powder.</note>, inceration <note>Latin: *inceratio*. The process of softening a hard substance until it reaches a waxy consistency.</note>, and fixation <note>Latin: *fixio*. The process of making a volatile substance stable and resistant to fire.</note>. The meaning of all these terms is simply **decoction** <note>Latin: *decoctio*. A long process of boiling or cooking, which alchemists believed was the primary way nature matured all things.</note>, because all these modes are perfected solely within our decoction. Truly, the method of our decoction is this: that you place the material of the compound, according to its measure, into its vessel, furnace, and fire, cooking it continually until it reaches the completion of its maturity. This is finished in ten months without any manual labor from the beginning to the end of the entire mastery. But by assigning these various names, the ancients wished to signify the sublimity of our art, so that the understanding of the foolish might be surrounded by a shadowy veil, lest the unworthy reach the peak of our secret hill. Instead, they are left in error until the **Sun and Moon** <note>Sol and Luna, representing Gold and Silver.</note> are reduced into a single globe—which is impossible to do except by the command of God.

### ARNOLD’S ROSARY

Without the Sun and the Moon, no "tinging body" <note>Latin: *corpus tingens*. A substance capable of "tinging" or transforming base metals into gold or silver.</note> is generated. Therefore, extract the tinging stone from gold and **quicksilver** <term>Quicksilver: Latin *argentum vivum* (living silver). While it usually refers to mercury, in this context, it often means a purified "philosophical" mercury.</term>, because they are of one nature. For gold provides a golden color, and silver provides a silvery color. He, therefore, who knows how to tinge quicksilver with gold and silver shall possess the art of the mastery.

You should not work, then, with anything except quicksilver and gold for the production of gold, because quicksilver is the father of all metals, and all things are dissolved back into it. For it is homogeneous and formless in its nature; through continuous decoction, it is purified and thickened. Then, by means of **white and red sulfur** <note>In alchemy, sulfur and mercury were the two primary components of all metals. "White sulfur" produced silver, while "red sulfur" produced gold.</note>, it is coagulated into a perfect metal. It is, by its very nature, transformative, becoming each of the specific things it embraces from the **planets** <note>The seven metals of antiquity were associated with the seven planets: Gold (Sun), Silver (Moon), Mercury (Mercury), Copper (Venus), Iron (Mars), Tin (Jupiter), and Lead (Saturn).</note>.

Therefore, the first task is that you take the "body" in which the red and fixed sulfur is contained <note>Referring to Gold.</note>, and reduce it into the **first matter**, which is to say, into quicksilver. For it is necessary that bodies become incorporeal and volatile; in this way, they are reduced into the nature of "spirit," so that the spirit may be sublimated with them. This is because the dissolution of the body occurs alongside the coagulation of the spirit, and the coagulation of the spirit occurs alongside the dissolution of the body, so that they become one and are never separated from each other again. For then all things have been reduced to their first homogeneous nature, which is quicksilver. When they are dissolved in that state of homogeneity, they are joined together at once, because each acts upon its companion which is similar to itself. Thus, the **Elixir** <term>Elixir: The "Medicine of Metals" or the Philosopher's Stone, capable of curing imperfection in both metals and the human body.</term> consists of these alone and no others. For if Mercury is joined with the rays of the Sun, it becomes a perfect elixir.

## THE SOUND OF THE TRUMPET
<note>original: *CLANGOR BVCCINÆ*, a famous alchemical text often attributed to various medieval authors.</note>

The **Sun** <note>representing Gold</note> does not heat the earth, nor does it impress its power upon the earth, except by means of the **Moon** <note>representing Silver</note>, which among the other stars is most receptive to the Light and heat of the Sun. In the same way, the Sun does not complete the Solar **tincture** <note>a concentrated alchemical essence capable of transforming or "dyeing" metals</note> except by means of the Moon, because the Sun has not yet reached that level of subtlety required to transform things. Therefore, the Moon is necessarily required there to make the Sun itself subtle, thin, and volatile. For this reason, **Hermes** <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of alchemy</note> says: "The Sun is its father, the Moon is its mother," and she is the field in which the solar seed must be sown. And thus we need nothing else from which our **stone** <note>the Philosopher's Stone</note> may be made, except the Sun and the Moon.

The Sun says: "In my sister the Moon, the degree of our wisdom grows, and not with any other of my servants." The Moon [says]: "I will give you my beauty—that is, the Solar light—when we are joined together through the smallest parts." The Sun is hot and dry; the Moon is cold and moist. The Moon receives the soul from the Sun, and the lamp of solar light is poured into the Lunar lamp, and a mixing of the **Luminaries** <note>the Sun and Moon</note> takes place. When my body is coagulated, I shall be the rising Sun at my birth, and my body shall be converted into Solar beauty.

The proper substance of living silver and **Sulfur**—smoky and most subtle, generated through our craft—in which the Spirit of the quintessence lies hidden and dwells, is the **Mercury of the Philosophers**. It is one thing composed of two: an oily vapor containing the nature of both within itself. One cannot be fixed <note>made stable in fire</note> without the other; that is the proper essential material of our Sulfur.

All metals are dissolved with **Mercurial water**, which cannot be dissolved in any other water. If, therefore, you seek a medicine that generates metals, its origin will be from metals: for nothing is suited to a thing except that which is closest to it in nature.

The entire benefit of this art lies in the Sun and Mercury. Indeed...

For indeed, these things joined into one constitute the **philosophers' stones**, and they possess an infinite **tincture** <note>original: *tincturam*, an alchemical essence capable of "dyeing" or transforming base metals into gold or silver</note>. For every elemental body has within itself a **radical or formal heat** <term>radical heat: the innate "vital spark" or fundamental energy believed to sustain the existence of matter</term> by which it persists and its seed is multiplied, because this heat digests the matter into its proper form and species. Then, whatever is superfluous and impure is gradually purged, matured, and improved through slow decoction <note>the process of heating or boiling a substance to extract its essence</note>. Moreover, the seed in Mercury cannot be extracted except by means of a **coagulant** <note>original: *coagulo*</note>, which is the **sulphur of gold**.

The **white** and the **red** <note>the two goals of the "Great Work": the white stone for making silver and the red stone for making gold</note> proceed from one root, with no other body intervening.

Our entire **mastery** <term>mastery: *magisterium*, the complete process of the alchemical Great Work</term> is achieved with **our water**, which has the greatest power of altering and penetrating bodies. For that reason, it dissolves bodies with a purely philosophical solution, so that they are converted into water as they were before; it extracts the soul from perfected bodies, and makes the living from the dead. This water is at first foul, thick, and fugitive, but through the operation and **sublimation** <note>the process of heating a substance until it turns to vapor and then becomes solid again</note> of the art, it is renewed, purified, thickened, and coagulated into white and red sulphur.

The **tinging spirit** is the **Mercury of the Philosophers** mixed with its own white or red sulphur; this Mercury is a permanent tincture, which is extracted from perfected bodies through dissolution, distillation, sublimation, and refinement. And such Mercury is called **incombustible oil**, the **Soul**, **air**, and the **splendor of bodies**, because it provides immortal life to dead bodies and illuminates them. Extract, therefore, this Mercury or stone as much from bodies as from **living silver** <note>original: *argento vivo*, common mercury</note>, because they are of one nature. For whatever truth consists of in this art is nothing other than joining the moist with the dry—that is, the liquid spirit with the pure, perfected body. Their operation is **dissolution** and **coagulation**.

To **dissolve** is to turn the body into spirit. To **coagulate** is to [turn] the spi[rit]...
