## THE LESSER ROSARY
<note>original: *Rosarius Minor*, a title often attributed to various medieval alchemical authors, emphasizing a "rose garden" of wisdom</note>

**Mercury** <note>referred to here not just as the liquid metal, but as the philosophical principle of fluidity and transformation</note> alone is the cause of perfection in metals; let us therefore choose it alone and strive to perfect it. For Mercury is the **stone** which the philosophers everywhere praise and honor. Within it is everything we seek. Nor did God create any creature nobler than it, except for the **rational soul**; for Mercury contains within itself the **soul**, the **body**, and the **spirit**. The soul gives life, the spirit tints <note>original: *tingit*, the action of the 'tincture' changing the color and nature of a metal</note>, and the body fixes <term>fix: to make a volatile substance solid and resistant to fire</term>. These three exist within the one Mercury, which has been congealed by the power of pure, non-burning **sulfur**. This Mercury is called "dry water," which has been uniformly thickened by the power of the aforementioned sulfur; and this is our stone.

All metallic bodies have their origin in Mercury; they are generated from it, and are eventually turned back into it. This is like **gold**, which is generated from pure and living Mercury, and is again converted into living Mercury; indeed, all bodies are converted into **quicksilver** <note>original: *argentum vivum*</note> solely by means of quicksilver and through no other thing. 

Nevertheless, this quicksilver that is made from gold possesses far greater power and fixes more quickly than that quicksilver which was never a body <note>meaning, mercury that has not yet been processed into a solid metal</note>. This is because the former far surpasses the latter in its "sulfurous strength." Quicksilver derived from gold is hot, masculine, and dry. Regarding their matter, these two have no difference; they differ only in their **digestion** <note>the process of maturing through heat</note>, in that one of them has been cooked by the natural heat in the "womb" of the earth. 

Therefore, our **tincture** is nothing other than **red sulfur** extracted from gold, because the pure substance of Mercury is coagulated and tinted by the power of non-burning sulfur. Consequently, all perfection lies in pure and fixed quicksilver and in no other thing. If you know how to cleanse and fix the quicksilver of the metals, you will have your heart's desire. The **sulfur** of the philosophers is a simple, living fire, giving life to and maturing other bodies so that it supplies what is lacking in nature. This is done without any mixing of foreign things, for these do not improve our stone, but rather corrupt it. This is because the medicine is a simple nature produced from Mercurial water. For putrefaction is the dissolution and separation of all natures or elements that were bound together; these are joined together once more through conversion, and are more strongly united in their nature than they were before. ### CALID REX.

This **Mastery** <note>original: *magisterium*, referring to the complete process of the alchemical art</note> of ours concerning the Secret Stone and its honored duty is the secret of secrets of God, which He has hidden from His people, nor did He wish to reveal it to any except those who have deserved it like faithful sons, and who have recognized His goodness and greatness. The composition in this Mastery is the conjunction or marriage of the congealed spirit with the leafy body; however, this is not completed except after putrefaction. For spirits are not congealed except by the **solution** <term>solution: the process of dissolving a solid into a liquid state</term> of the body. And likewise, the body is not dissolved except through the **congealing** <term>congealing: the solidification of a liquid or volatile spirit</term> of the spirit; and between the dissolution of the body and the congealing of the spirit, there is no difference in time, nor are they separate tasks. 

Instead, they have one single end, and one and the same operation moves upon both of them simultaneously. The Soul is not joined with the body except through the change of both from their own virtue and property, and after the conversion of their natures. And this is the dissolution and congealing of the Philosophers. The spirit will not linger in the body, nor will it remain with it in any way, unless the body itself possesses such subtlety and thinness as the spirit possesses. When it has been thinned and refined, and has left behind its density—departing from thickness, heaviness, and corporality toward spirituality—then it will be mixed with the subtle spirits and absorbed into them, and thus both will become one and the same, and they shall not be separated, just as water mixed with water cannot be. Therefore, whoever is able to refine and dissolve bodies, and to whiten and redden them, shall achieve the mastery.

Sf 3

Unless you make the body subtle until it becomes entirely water, it will not rust nor putrefy; because when the subtle is mixed with the thick, those things become one substance. For spirits are fleeting until bodies are mixed with them. Therefore, he who converts the soul into the body, and the body into the soul, will **tinge** <term>tinge: to dye or permeate a substance, fundamentally changing its internal nature and color</term> every body. Boiling <note>original: *decoctio*</note> generates things and changes them from their own substances and colors to other substances and other colors.

Our **Stone** <note>original: *Lapis*</note> is cold and moist in its manifest <note>outward or visible</note> state, and hot and dry in its occult <note>hidden or internal</note> state. Therefore, we must hide that which is manifest, and make manifest that which was hidden. Moreover, that which is hidden is a hot and dry oil. And this tinges, and nothing else. But that which is manifest is cold and moist, and it is a corrupting watery smoke. Therefore, this cold and moist aspect must be balanced with the substance. These weaknesses must therefore be destroyed in the fire and through the stages of fire. Heat and dryness destroy the cold, moist, and scorched watery nature by divine power. And then that spirit is changed into a most noble body, and will not flee from the fire, but flows like oil. This is the living tincture and the **permanent water** <term>permanent water: a fluid that does not evaporate when heated, a key alchemical goal signifying stability</term>, which always lives and remains, and the **vinegar of the Philosophers** <note>original: *acetum Philosophorum*</note> which rectifies and illuminates all the dead. And this hidden thing is of the nature of the sun and fire. Now, the perfect preparation of bodies and spirits is fulfilled through the practice of the four regimes. The first is resolution into water. The second is smoothing <note>original: *levigatio*, likely meaning sublimation or refinement</note> into air. The third is reduction to the nature of fire. The fourth is compression to earth. And Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary father of alchemy</note> hints at this when he says: "It ascends from the earth to the heaven gently with great ingenuity." <note>A famous quote from the Emerald Tablet describing the circulation of the work.</note> "The wind carried it in its belly," because through the wind—that is, the smoke—it is lifted into the air. For unless our stone is airy, it is not joined with the spirit permanently. And again it descends to the earth, when the spirit becomes a body, so that it may have perpetual endurance over fire and melt without smoking.

->AVICENNA.<-

**Gold** is the most perfect body, the King and lord of Stones, which is neither diminished in the air nor burned in the fire, but is improved by it; neither is anything superfluous nor lacking found within it. For it is created from the most subtle and clear substance of **Quicksilver** <note>original: *argenti vivi*, or Mercury</note> and from pure, red, fixed, and clear **Sulfur**, which tinges the substance of the quicksilver itself.

Gold is the body and the **ferment** <term>ferment: a substance that, like yeast in dough, triggers a transformation throughout the whole mass</term> of the Elixir, both for the White and the Red. For this reason, the philosophers have magnified it, because just as the Sun holds its place among the stars, so also does gold among metallic bodies.

646 THE SECRET

For the Sun <note>In alchemy, "Sol" or the Sun refers both to the celestial body and its terrestrial counterpart, Gold.</note> by its own light and splendor perfects all vegetation and germinates all fruits. Therefore Hermes <note>Refers to Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of alchemy.</note> says: a true **tincture** <term>tincture: a transformative essence or "dye" capable of transmuting base metals into gold or silver</term> is never made without the **red stone** <note>original: *rubeo lapide*</note>. If, therefore, gold is made "more than perfect"—whether by double, quadruple, a hundredfold, or a thousandfold—to that same extent it perfects the sick and imperfect bodies of metals.

But **Quicksilver** <note>original: *Argentum vivum*</note> is cold and moist as well as airy. And it alone is the "living spirit"; indeed, there is nothing else in the world like it which can perform such works as are performed through it. It penetrates all bodies; it is the ferment of bodies with which it is mixed, and then the whole will be an elixir for **whiteness** <note>original: *albedinem*, referring to the silver-making stage</note> and **redness** <note>original: *rubedinem*, referring to the gold-making stage</note>. It is the perennial water, the **Water of Life** <note>original: *Aqua vitæ*</note>, the **virgin’s milk** <note>original: *lac virginis*</note>, the fountain and the alum from which he who drinks does not die. When it is "living," it has certain operations; when it is "dead," it has other operations; and when it is dissolved, it has the greatest operations. The wise make it face the fire, and then it performs works and mutations: Because just as it is changed, so it changes; and as it is tinged, so it tinges; and as it is coagulated, so it coagulates. Therefore, among all the names of quicksilver, its "generation" is to be preferred. Water alone, through itself, does all things, dissolves all things, coagulates all things, and destroys all things without the help of anything else.

The changing of the body into water is the tincture of any body. And our intent should be nothing other than to choose the purest substance of Mercury from the bodies themselves.

<note>Bernard of Treviso, a 15th-century Italian alchemist famous for his pursuit of the Philosopher's Stone.</note>

Common metallic bodies, which nature alone completed in the mine, are "dead," nor can they perfect the imperfect. But if we take them before that stage and perfect them ourselves ten or twelve times over, they tend toward the infinite; for then they are entering, penetrating, tingeing, and "more than perfect." They are "living" in respect to the common metals. Therefore, these common metals, while they remain in their metallic form, are not our **Stone**; rather, it is necessary to change and renew their form. This cannot be done unless they are first reduced to **First Matter** <term>First Matter: the original, chaotic, and undifferentiated substance from which all metals are born</term>.

Now, the First Matter of metals is **sulfur** and **Mercury**, or the masculine and feminine seed. When these are united together in virtue, so that one has the power of the other within itself, that union is called the First Matter.

Every thing has its own proper and principal seed, from which its root is formed and multiplied. It also requires a thing similar to itself so that it may be generated and increased.

Our **medicine** <term>medicine: in alchemy, this refers to the Elixir or the substance capable of "healing" base metals into gold</term> is therefore made from two things of a single essence—that is, from a **Mercurial union** <note>original: *unione Mercuriali*</note>, both fixed and unfixed, spiritual and corporeal, cold and dry, hot and moist; it cannot be made from any other thing.

In the other seed, which is crude and imperfect in its nature, there are two other qualities—two others that are imperfect and less worthy—namely, **Water** and **Earth**. And so, in this art, there is nothing other than these two spermatic natures of the same root, substance, and essence: the substance of a single viscous and dry Mercury, which is joined to nothing in this world except its own body, as **Morienes** <note>Morienus, a legendary 7th-century alchemist and hermit of Rome who allegedly taught the art to King Khalid of Egypt</note> testifies. ### THE ASSEMBLY OF THE PHILOSOPHERS.

1. Take the **body** or **earth** and form it into thin plates; mix these with sea water, which, when it is governed <note>original: *regitur*; meaning properly processed or controlled by the chemist</note>, is called **permanent water** <term>aqua permanens: a symbolic alchemical solvent, often a refined form of mercury or an acid, that does not wet the hands</term>.

2. Fit this composition together well, and **join like with like** <note>literally: "join blood-relatives to blood-relatives"</note>, because the same nature that kills and turns a thing to nothing also brings life and renews. These natures embrace one another, and after their initial enmity, they become harmonious and friendly through a slow fire. Therefore, take **quicksilver** <note>mercury</note> and congeal it in the "body of magnesia," because it turns gold into a red fire; this is achieved through cooking and roasting.

3. The secret of the work consists of the male and the female—that is, the active and the passive agents. The male rejoices when the female is received and is helped by her; the female receives the **tinting seed** <note>original: *sperma tingens*</note> from the male and is colored by him. Mix them together, and you will have the **tinting spirit**, composed of male and female. Govern them according to the four seasons of the year: In **Winter**, dissolve, as it is of a cold temperament; in **Spring**, cook; in **Summer**, coagulate (this is when the "flowers" are produced); in **Autumn**, the fruits ripen. You cannot make the red substance, however, unless you have first made it white.

4. The foundation of this art is **very sharp vinegar** <note>original: *acetum acerrimum*; likely a metaphor for a powerful acid or a specialized solvent</note>. When it is mixed with the "body," it is contained and becomes one with it, turning gold into a pure spirit. If you place the body over the fire without this vinegar, it will be ruined. Therefore, cover these things gently until the **sulfur** becomes incombustible, because the moisture is initially cold, and an immoderate fire is its enemy. The vinegar burns the body, turns it into ash, and breaks down its density.

6. When the male is joined to the female, the female herself does not flee, and the entire composition becomes spiritual.

7. **Gum** is nothing other than the **permanent water**. Without gold, this Gum cannot be perfected.

8. In the entire process of ruling, nourishing, and grinding, you must use no other thing except that well-known **permanent water**. Its power is **spiritual blood**; when ground and incorporated with the "body," it turns the body into spirit, and the water itself is turned into a body. When mixed together and reduced to one, they transform each other.

10. This **permanent water** is called "the stone," and it is the pure **water of life**. It is also called Gum, poison, or vinegar. However, no **tinting poison** <note>In alchemy, "poison" often refers to a substance so potent it can "kill" the old form of a metal to allow for its rebirth</note> is generated without the **Sun** <note>gold</note> and its **shadow** <note>likely the "moon" or silver, or the dross left behind</note>.

13. There is a very great closeness between the **philosophers' brass** <term>æs philosophorum: a symbolic metal or alloy representing a specific stage of purification</term> and the **permanent water**, for each is naturally attracted to the other.

12. Whoever joins **quicksilver** <note>original: *Argentum vivum*; mercury</note> to the **body of Magnesia** <term>Magnesia: in alchemy, this is not modern magnesium, but a "primal" mineral substance or a stage of the base metal often associated with lead or the "mother" of the stone</term>, and the female to the male, draws out the hidden nature through which bodies are colored.

13. Because **quicksilver** is the fire that burns the bodies, killing them and binding them by its governance, which is one and the same.

14. And the more it is mixed with the body, the more the body is destroyed, ground down, and thinned. From this, the **tincture** <term>tincture: the potent substance or "dye" that transforms base metal into gold</term> results. And **Etholia** <note>original: *Etholia*; an alchemical term for a volatile spirit or "flower" that rises during heating</note>, not fleeing the fire, shatters all bodies and retains and colors all spirits. The body cannot tint itself unless the hidden spirit is drawn out from its **belly** <note>the inner core or essence of the substance</note>, and the body becomes the soul and spirit. For that thick, earthy part does not tint, but the thin part of nature does, which shatters the body itself. When you govern the **body of bronze** <note>original: *æris*</note> and extract the thinnest part from it, that thinnest part turns into the tincture and tints the condensed matter—that is, the dry is joined to the moist, and from this is generated the **unchanging tincture**.

15. This tincture is life to those things to which it is joined.

16. You must bear the long duration of the **cooking** <note>original: *decoctionis*</note> patiently, and you will have what you desire.

17. The **male**, having embraced his **female**, quickly passes into her body; he is liquefied, destroyed, and shattered, and thereafter the **redness** does not die.

18. Because these two share one nature, otherwise they would not mix so quickly, nor contain one another, nor become one.

19. **Nature is not improved except by its own nature**; therefore, do not introduce anything foreign to them, neither powder nor any other thing. Let the **conception** be sufficient for us, and the true son will be born: cook him gently.

20. Honor the **King and his wife**, and do not burn them with too much fire, but govern them until they become **black**, then **white**, then **red**, and finally the **tinting poison** <note>here meaning a substance so potent it "infects" and transforms everything it touches</note>.

21. The heart of the blowpipe <note>original: *Cor suffle*; likely a reference to the crucible or the focal point of the heat</note> is the whole composition, which must be roasted seven times; then it tints every body and is called **lead**, **tin**, **coin**, **flower of iron**, **flower of bronze**, and **flower of gold**.

22. The body and spirit must be turned into earth and ash. **Bronze**, when it is burned, becomes better than it was before, because by breathing in moisture it receives life and is increased, like other things. Therefore, our work is by no means a tincture unless it is diligently cooked until it becomes a powder and the **seed** <note>original: *sperma*</note> is spiritually produced through **putrefaction** <term>putrefaction: the stage of "rotting" or breaking down the matter, usually indicated by a black color, necessary for rebirth</term>. For in this way, and no other, will the color be found.

23. When **bronze** <note>original: *æs*; likely copper or a base metal alloy</note> falls into its own water, it is called the **ferment of Gold**, and then the **redness** <term>rubedo: the final, red stage of the alchemical work, signifying success and perfection</term> appears.
24. The heart was in the belly; the true nature was hidden, and this true nature is that **tinting Spirit** <note>original: *Spiritus tingens*</note> which it received from the permanent water. Therefore, grind the body, destroy it, and soak it; this makes the Spirit thin and impalpable. This happens when it is ground until it becomes dust, which is only achieved by the strongest **decoction** <term>decoction: the process of boiling or heating a substance in liquid to extract its essence</term> and continuous grinding.
25. For the Art requires two natures, because the precious is not made without the vile <note>the 'vile' refers to common or base metals like lead or copper</note>, nor the vile without the precious. These two are united together in **putrefaction** <term>putrefaction: the symbolic "rotting" or breakdown of the starting material</term> and decoction, and one contains the other so that it does not flee.
26. The Work, therefore, is made of two, and these two joined together they have called the **composite**.
27. For it is necessary that the body, which was not water, becomes water along with water; and water is mixed with water, and let them both become one and be turned into water, until the whole becomes water.
28. For by the heat of the water, the whole easily becomes water.
29. As man is composed of soul and body, so must we join two things together; this union is compared to **spouses**, from whose embrace the **golden water** <note>original: *aqua aurea*</note> leaps forth. Therefore, there is a war between the bronze and the **quicksilver** <note>original: *arg. viv.* (argentum vivum); mercury</note> until they come to their end and are corrupted; then the bronze, conceiving the quicksilver, coagulates it, and the body of both is destroyed and turned into dust by diligent and frequent soaking and boiling. For by this grinding, the spiritual, clean, and sublime soul is extracted from the body, which tints every body, and it is the **Sulphur of nature** <term>Sulphur: in alchemy, the active, masculine principle of transformation</term>.
30. That hidden tinting soul and sulphurous nature cannot be extracted unless the bodies become incorporeal—that is, a thin Spirit—through the continuity of cooking. This, however, is all done through **quicksilver**, because it is fiery, burning every body more than fire, and **mortifying** <term>mortifying: the "killing" or chemical breakdown of a substance's original form</term> the bodies; for every body that is mixed with it is ground down and given over to death.
<margin>37. Both become fleeing.</margin>
38. They become **fleeing** <note>original: *fugientes*; referring to volatility or the tendency to evaporate</note> again; through the intervention of fire, they embrace and contain each other. For when the four natures <note>the four elements: fire, air, water, and earth</note> have ascended into heaven, fire falls into air, air into water, and water into earth. Thus the earth is the container of them all, and the end of the whole work is dust and ashes.
39. The subtle Spirits have made the body itself a thin spirit, and have tinted the body into **poison** <note>original: *venenum*; in alchemy, this often refers to a potent, transformative substance</note>. Therefore, attenuate the things with fire until those things ascend as spirits.
40. The knowledge of this art is nothing other than the joining of **quicksilver** to the **body of magnesia** <term>Magnesia: a term for the "primal matter" or a specific stage of the base metal</term>, the sublimation of water, and vapor. No Sulphur is made without the **lime** <note>original: *calce*; the powder left after heating a metal</note> of quicksilver and the water of sulphur.

41. One **sulfur** <note>original: *sulphur*; in alchemy, sulfur represents the active, masculine, or combustible principle</note> is made from several sulfurs by the mixing of that which fights with fire and that which does not. This secret proceeds from two compositions: **sulfur** and **magnesia** <note>original: *magnesia*; not modern magnesium, but a term for a mineral "mother" substance or crude ore</note>. This composite, when reduced into one, is called **water** and **thick gold**. If these are turned into **quicksilver** <term>quicksilver: *argentum vivum*, or mercury</term>, they are named **sulfur water** and **fiery poison**, which, once truly whitened, has cast off its thick and heavy bodies.

43. By a slow fire, the humidity is first destroyed, and when all have become one, they are **bodiless bodies**. For every body is dissolved with the spirit with which it is mixed and becomes spiritual. And every spirit is altered and colored by the bodies. That which is mixed with the spirit as a **tinting color** and remains constant against the fire becomes **fixed** <term>fixed: *fixum*; the state where a substance no longer evaporates or reacts when heated</term> and incombustible sulfur, which was previously "fleeing" sulfur. He who can make the fleeing red spirit for the body joined to it, and then extract from that body and spirit its thin nature hidden in its belly, will complete the work.

44. **Quicksilver** <note>original: *Arg. vivum*</note> mixed with its own **tincture** <term>tincture: a substance capable of transmuting or coloring base metals into gold or silver</term>, tints. The vapor is contained by another quicksilver of its own kind so that it does not flee; this happens as soon as the quicksilver and **bronze** <note>original: *aes*; copper or a base metal alloy</note> are joined together. Thus, quicksilver is mixed with quicksilver until one and the same clean water is made from the two.

46. By the **soaking** <note>original: *imbibitione*; the process of a solid absorbing a liquid</term> of water alone, you will reach the true end of the work.

47. When the **bronze** is ground down and turned into water, it becomes "fleeing" and is turned into spirit; the spirit and the body are then bound to one another, and it is turned into a **tinting soul**.

48. **Quicksilver** is white to the sight, but when smoke reaches it, it turns red and becomes a poison.

49. Therefore, **quicksilver** is composed of many parts far and wide, so that two become three, and four become one, and two become one.

50. The entire perfection of sulfur consists in **boiling** <note>original: *decoctione*; long-term heating in a liquid</note>.

52. There are no other quicksilvers but these two: the **moisture of the Sun** <note>original: *Solis humor*; gold in a liquid or spiritual state</note> and the **spittle of the Moon** <note>original: *sputum Lunae*; silver in a liquid or spiritual state</note>. Join, therefore, the dry with the moist—that is, the earth and the water—and cook them with fire and air until the spirit is dried out within the soul, because the thin tinting substance takes its power from the thinnest part of the earth, water, and air.

->Bodies are tinted and fixed by bodies.<-

53. When the composition appears **red**, that **regimen** <term>regimen: a specific stage or controlled method of heating in the alchemical process</term> has been maintained by which bodies are turned into spirit and are bound to one another, possessing a tinting and germinating soul.

54. Through three multiplied boilings, our **vinegar** <note>original: *acetum*; often refers to a philosophical acid or solvent</note> is glued together and coagulated by the fire, and its nature is converted into nature; the **spittle of the Moon** joined to the **light of the Sun** is congealed.

# ARCANUM

55. Take a **white tree** <note>original: *arborem albam*; in alchemy, the "white tree" often symbolizes a purified state or the "Lunar" stage of the work, associated with silver</note>, build for it a house surrounded by dew, and place within it a man of great age, one hundred years old. Leave them in their home for eighty days. That old man does not cease to eat from the fruit of that tree, until his soul is transformed into a youthful body, and the **Father is made the Son**. <note>This is an allegory for the "recycling" of matter—breaking down an old substance so it can be reborn in a more potent, purified form.</note>

56. The Philosophers have put to death that **woman who kills her husband**.

57. For that woman’s belly is full of poison. Therefore, make a tomb for the **Dragon** <term>Dragon: *draco*; a common symbol for volatile or corrosive substances, often mercury or a crude mineral acid</term>, and bury the woman with him. The more strongly he is joined to that woman, and the more he binds her and coils around her, the more his body, mixed into the woman's limbs, sinks toward death. He is entirely turned into **Blood**, which is placed in the sun until the blood is consumed and dries up. Then the poison appears and the hidden is made manifest; and thus, nothing useful is made from the elements without the mixing of the male and the female.

58. This work, however, is guided by subtle meditation.

59. There is only one **tincture** <term>tincture: *tinctura*; the "medicine" or substance used by alchemists to transform base metals into gold or silver</term> of the Philosophers.

60. All our science is the nature of the male and the female. In the beginning of the mixing, it is necessary to combine the crude and pure elements over a slow fire, and to beware of the fire flaring up, until it is dried by that gentle heat. **Liquefaction** <note>original: *liquefactio*; the melting or dissolving of a solid</note> is the Head <note>meaning the "chief part" or "beginning"</note> of this art, because the moist becomes very thick, and the thick body becomes a spirit, and the fleeing spirit becomes strong, fighting against the fire. Therefore, invert the elements, and you will find what you seek. The composite generates itself, and nothing grows except from itself.

61. To burn is nothing other than to **whiten**, and to make **red** is to vivify <note>original: *vivificare*; to bring to life or animate</note>.

62. The definition of this art is the liquefaction of the body and the separation of the soul from the body, because our **copper** <note>original: *æs*; likely refers to "Philosophical Copper," a code for a specific starting material, not necessarily common household copper</note> has a soul and a body. It is necessary, therefore, for the body to be destroyed and the soul to be separated from it. The subtle body of nature penetrates, and it is the soul of **quicksilver** <term>quicksilver: *argenti vivi*; mercury</term> itself; in its fiery power, it perfects and gives life to the body.

63. The first sign of perfect **decoction** <note>original: *decoctionis*; a process of boiling or heating a substance in a liquid</note> is **blackness** <note>original: *nigredo*</note>, then **whiteness** <note>original: *albedo*</note>, and lastly the highest **redness** <note>original: *rubedo*</note>.

64. The Body must be destroyed until it dies; then you will be able to extract its soul, which is the **tinting spirit**.

64. The whole mastery is that the higher becomes the lower, and the lower becomes the higher; the composition is of a double nature: one is moist, the other is dry.

65. These, when they are cooked, become one. Seek out its partner, and bring nothing foreign into it.

OF THE PHILOSOPHERS.

## C O N C L U S I O N .

From the things stated above, it is therefore clearer than the midday sun <note>original: *luce meridiana clarius*; a common Latin idiom for something being self-evident</note> how firm the foundations of this **most noble science** <term>most noble science: *nobilissima scientia*; a traditional name for alchemy, reflecting its status as the pinnacle of natural philosophy</term> are. For nothing obscure or ambiguous is contained within them, although the writings of the Philosophers generally have this in common: they are not to be taken according to the **mere sound of the words** <note>original: *nudum verborum sonum*; this warns the reader that alchemical texts are allegorical rather than literal</note>. I have at least collected the very nucleus, as it were, and such things which confidently, according to the simple letter, report the genuine sense of the author; no other interpretation is to be sought.

I have gathered these things into such brevity that I know of no one who until now has either dared or tried to provide this.

This little work, although thin and small in appearance, is nonetheless rare in reality and of great value. For it contains the greatest and most hidden secret of the ancient Philosophers. If we look for the **medicine** by which the human body can be freed from all infirmities and enjoy the happiest health, it can be sufficiently obtained from here. If, however, we look for **riches**, which can be of great use in managing the greatest affairs, it is granted that those too may be found abundantly here by those who earnestly investigate the **mysteries of nature**.

Although the chief secret—in which the aim of the whole matter primarily consists—is kept in the **hidden school** <note>original: *schola occulta*; this refers to the tradition that the final "key" to alchemy is passed down through oral tradition or divine revelation rather than books</note>, nevertheless, the first beginnings and foundations are set down clearly enough. The rest is committed to the diligence of him who aspires to this
->greatest gift of GOD.<-
->Farewell.<-

SECRET

## THE TWENTY-TWO FOLLOW:
# PROPOSITIONS
### OR MAXIMS IN WHICH THE
#### truth of the entire chemical art is most briefly
#### comprised.

##### I.

The true **increase of metals** <note>original: *augmentatio Metallorum*; the process of multiplying the quantity or quality of a metal</note> proceeds from nothing other than its own **seed** <term>seed: *semen*; in alchemical theory, the vital, reproductive spark within matter that allows it to grow or transform</term>, which comes from the metallic root, as is clearly evident from the light of nature. Therefore, every intention concerning the increase of metals outside of this seed is false and erroneous.

2. Moreover, it is necessary that this seed first be reduced into its **prime matter** <note>original: *suam primam*; the original, undifferentiated state of a substance before it takes a specific form</note>, because without this reduction, no alteration of this seed can occur.

3. It is necessary, then, for this seed to die, and then tend toward a new generation; it is then improved tenfold, a hundredfold, a thousandfold, and is led to a state of "more than perfection," through which it can communicate perfection even to other **sick bodies** <note>original: *ægris corporibus*; a common alchemical metaphor where base metals like lead or iron are described as "sick" versions of the "healthy" or perfect metal, gold</note>.

4. This new thing generated is called the **Secret of the Philosophers** <note>original: *Arcanum Philosophorum*</note>, because that which was hidden and lay concealed potentially within the seed has now been made manifest and appears in actuality through the industry of the Philosopher, and it is of a heavenly nature. Therefore, it is powerful enough to alter metallic bodies into the new and incorruptible form of gold and silver.

5. Every work, therefore, that does not proceed according to the aforementioned order is false and contrary to the possibilities of nature.

6. For our art is not perfected from foreign or strange things. Therefore, to walk a foreign path, and not as nature requires, is vanity.

7. Indeed, all the resolutions, calcinations, sublimations, and distillations of the **Sophists** <term>Sophists: here referring to "false alchemists" or "puffers" who used harsh, literal chemical processes rather than the subtle "natural" methods of true philosophy</term> destroy our Philosophical work rather than bringing any utility.

8. No real transmutation can therefore take place in metals outside of the aforementioned secret.

9. Our **tincture** <note>original: *tinctura*; the concentrated essence or "Stone" capable of staining or transforming base metals</note> is made solely from the **Mercury of the Sages** <term>Mercury of the Sages: *Mercurius sapientū*; a theoretical "First Water" or universal solvent, distinct from common quicksilver</term>, which is composed of fixed and volatile gold and silver; for in these two the whole **mastery** <note>original: *magisterium*; the "Great Work" or the completed alchemical process</note> consists.

<meta>catchword: 10. And—</meta>

It warns against the literal chemical methods of "Sophists" in favor of a "natural" process using the Mercury of the Sages.</summary>

->OF THE PHILOSOPHERS.<-

10. Their union must be both formal and essential—a process by which the physical body is transformed into the subtle nature of the Spirit. Once this occurs, they can never again be separated from one another.

11. From this union arises a third thing, which is called the **water of life** <note>original: *aqua vitæ*</note>, the **quintessence** <term>quintessence: literally the "fifth essence," a purified substance beyond the four elements (earth, air, fire, water)</term>, the incombustible oil, the "heaven," permanent water, vinegar, and the **Mercury of the Philosophers** <note>original: *Mercurius Philosophorum*; not common quicksilver, but a refined, spiritualized metallic principle</note>. This is the first and most immediate material of our Stone.

12. And so, the Sun is the Father and the Moon is the Mother. This is because the Sun cannot impress its power upon other bodies except through the mediation of the Moon; it is she who dissolves the bodies through a true "philosophical solution" and extracts from them a permanent **tincture** <term>tincture: a substance capable of deeply staining or transforming the inner nature and color of a metal</term>. Both of these substances share a single, uniform nature.

13. Quicksilver <note>original: *Argentum vivum*</note> derived from gold is hot, masculine, and dry. Therefore, our tincture is nothing other than **red sulfur** <note>original: *sulphur rubeum*</note>, which is a "living fire"—a simple substance that brings life and maturity to other bodies. It is extracted from gold itself because gold has been perfectly "digested" <note>in alchemy, "digestion" refers to being matured or refined by heat over a long period</note> by nature.

14. If, therefore, this Gold has been made "more than perfect"—whether by two, four, a hundred, or a thousand times—it is able to bring the imperfect bodies of base metals to a state of perfection.

15. Our medicine, then, is made from two things of a single essence: that is, a union of Mercury that is both fixed and non-fixed, spiritual and physical, cold and dry, and hot and moist. It cannot be made from any other thing.

16. Thus, the secret of the work consists of two parts: the male and the female, the active and the passive. When joined, they are called the "composite." One is dry and the other is moist. 

And when all these parts become one, they are the incorporeal soul and the transforming <note>original: *tingens*; literally "dyeing" or "staining"</note> soul.

17. Through **attrition** <note>original: *contritionem*; the process of grinding or wearing down</note>, the soul is extracted from the body. It cannot be drawn out unless the body is first made into a thin spirit, which is achieved entirely through the use of quicksilver; indeed, no sulfur can be made without the **calx** <term>calx: the powdery residue left after a metal or mineral has been consumed or "calcined" by fire</term> of quicksilver. 

It is this thin part of nature that transforms (or "tinges") the substance, as it breaks down the body itself.

18. Although many different methods of preparation have been described by others, their true meaning is all contained within the single process of **sublimation** <term>sublimation: the process of heating a substance until it turns to vapor, then collecting it as it cools back into a solid; here used as a metaphor for the entire purification process</term>. In our unique sublimation, all these methods are perfected. This occurs in a "vaporous fire" <note>a gentle, indirect heat</note>, where our Mercury is placed in a firmly sealed vessel for the duration of a month within its furnace. It remains there until it rots (putrefies) within itself, then turns to a snowy whiteness, and finally is converted into a royal purple redness—the true sign of the celestial, fiery secret.

->SECRET OF THE PHILOSOPHERS.<-

19. Take, therefore, the **Body** <note>original: *Corpus*; the solid metallic base</note> and mix it with the **sea water** <note>original: *aqua maris*; a metaphor for the alchemical solvent or "mercury"</note>. When this is guided according to the seasons of the year, **permanent water** <term>permanent water: a stable alchemical solvent that does not evaporate when heated</term> arises. This is the **sharpest vinegar** <note>original: *acetum acerrimum*</note>, for it is the fire that burns and **mortifies** <term>mortification: the alchemical process of breaking down a substance's physical structure to "kill" its base form</term> bodies. It is also called the **water of life** <note>original: *aqua vitæ*</note>, **Gum**, and **Poison** <note>original: *Venenum*</note>, because it consumes the body and turns it into ash; its inner power is the **Spiritual blood** <note>original: *Spiritualis sanguis*</note>.

20. The perfect preparation is completed through the exercise of the **four regimens** <note>referring to four distinct stages of heat or chemical treatment</note> according to the four seasons of the year. In this way, it "ascends from the earth to heaven, and again descends from heaven to the earth," and receives the power of things above and things below <note>This is a direct reference to the *Emerald Tablet*, the foundational text of Western alchemy, describing the circulation of energy and matter</note>.

21. And in this manner is produced the **Potable Gold** <term>Potable Gold: *Aurum potabile*, a legendary liquid medicine made from gold, believed to be a universal cure</term> of the physicians. This is the most precious secret above every other mystery of this world. By it, all the most desperate illnesses of the entire human body are miraculously healed, and a truly whole life is preserved until the appointed time of death.

22. Thus, one can easily recognize the deceptions and false arguments of the ignorant, who—without our **Philosophical Secret**—childishly promise the
->alteration of metals into a<-
->nobler form.<-

# SECOND TREATISE

## THE GOLDEN TREATISE ON THE PHILOSOPHERS’ STONE by Johannes de Lasnioro, Disciple of Antonius of Florence.

> O God, reach out to help me, and open my understanding, so that I may know that there is no other besides You who might open the depths of my heart to me and give me the Spirit of truth, so that through my own natural talent <note>original: *ingenium*</note> I might be able to write down those things which are of the truth. For You alone are the truth, and whoever loves the truth, the truth follows them.

> Lord, I approach the door of Your Divinity, so that with Your Angel I might be able to recount the depths and the Secret of the Philosophers, though I am ignorant. But You, most holy Lord, help me; then all things will be in the open and easy to write, so that whoever reads this little book may clearly understand that I have set down the truth. Within the brevity of this speech is joy and gladness, and their [burdensome] thoughts shall be taken from them. And whoever understands this little book shall be delivered from poverty. But it is necessary for them to maintain a quiet discretion <note>original: *petulantiam*; here referring to the need for humble restraint to keep the secret safe</note>, lest they fall into the hands of tyrants, who might perhaps say: "Do my will, or sadness will follow you," just as happened to me. Nevertheless, in punishing, the Lord has punished me, but He has not handed me over to death; to Him be praise and honor forever and ever. And if there is anything beyond.

->*IN THE NAME OF OUR LORD*<-
->*Jesus Christ.*<-

Take our crude **Sulfur** <note>original: *Sulphur*; in alchemy, sulfur represents the active, masculine, and combustible principle of matter</note>, perfected in its own blood, either Red or White, according to the work at hand which required no [external] labor. That Sulfur contains within itself two bodies: namely, the imperfect body which we call the **ferment** <term>ferment: a substance, like yeast in bread, that transforms and "multiplies" the alchemical matter into the final stone</term>. Our Sulfur is not the sulfur of the common people <note>original: *Sulphur vulgi*</note>, as the ignorant imagine. For our Sulfur is made of a dual thing. And for this reason, some call it <term>rebis</term> <note>original: *rebis*; from the Latin *res bina*, meaning "double thing"—the union of opposites like male and female, or body and soul</note>, and they speak the truth, because it is made of body and soul. Therefore, it is necessary to draw out the ferment from our Sulfur for the white or the red work. For if the craftsman uses common Gold or Silver as a ferment, he is a liar and is found to be useless.

# THE SECRET
<note>original: *ARCANUM*</note>

Because **Our Gold** is not the gold of the crowd <note>original: *Aurum vulgi*; common gold used in commerce</note>, it is therefore not possible to draw our **ferment** <note>original: *fermentum*; a substance used to "leaven" or initiate the transformation of metals</note> from it, even though it is a perfect and well-ripened body. But what our gold requires naturally, common gold lacks; and thus it gives nothing that it does not possess. And if anyone should argue the opposite and say that it is impossible to complete the work without natural gold or silver—because the Philosophers speak, saying: "Gold is the ferment of redness, and silver is the ferment of whiteness"—then you would be contradicting the Philosophers. 

But understand, my son, the words of the Philosophers speaking thus: "Our Gold," they say, is not the gold of the crowd; rather, our gold contains two things within itself: namely, the gold which is the ferment of our art (either for redness or whiteness), and **Our Sulfur** <note>original: *Sulphur nostrum*; the active, masculine principle in alchemy</note> remains with it, and they assist each other, because one cannot be made or born without the other. And thus our sulfur is more perfect than gold. And truly I say that no Alchemist should intrude upon this divine secret <note>original: *arcanum*</note> unless he has known our gold with its sulfur; otherwise, he will be deceived. 

And this is the proof of the truth. Take natural gold and join it with natural **Mercury** <note>original: *Mercurio*; quicksilver</note>, as alchemists are currently accustomed to work, and let the work proceed either by making an amalgam or by soaking it with any oil or water, and let it be ruled by fire for its proper time, whether long or short, and a **tincture** <note>original: *tinctura*; the substance capable of transmuting base metals</note> will be made. Let it be projected upon some [metal] body and it colors it red. But let it be tested in the assay <note>original: *examine*; the trial by fire to test the purity of a metal</note>, and in the assay, the "perfect" will depart along with the imperfect. 

And this is the reason: because natural gold lacked our sulfur. Because our sulfur is dry and hot, enduring fire, and is never corrupted by fire; it fixes and retains every volatile thing from flight and makes it fixed <note>original: *fixum*; a substance that does not evaporate or change when heated</note>. And therefore it is necessary that our sulfur make both mercury and gold fixed and eternal in the assay. And if our sulfur did not exist, no mineral would ever have been procreated. 

For when it has reached the completion of the tincture, then our sulfur remains firm as that same perfect body. The Spirit—that is, the Mercury—colors and enters the dead bodies. The Soul—that is, **Our Gold**—visits and illuminates the darkness; that is, it repels the blackness or the stench. And thus these three resuscitate dead bodies from their tombs <note>This is a common alchemical metaphor for the transmutation of base "dead" metals into "living" gold</note>, as is well-evident to the wise. 

Let us return, therefore, my son, to the previous matters, so that we may draw out from that substance the sulfur which is secret and shining. Let it become a sulfur and a permanent ferment without any stain, because it is necessary for us to divide the pure from the impure if we wish to receive fruit from it. Take that sulfur and put it to be **calcined** <note>original: *calcinandum*; the process of heating a substance until it is reduced to a powder</note> in its own vessel in the strongest fire. For our preparation is very simple and cheap. When the calcination is done, let it be projected into our purified urine, and it will be dispersed into the smallest pieces; and thus you need nothing else except to remove the pure from the impure. And this can sometimes be done without fire,

# PHILOSOPHICAL TREATISE

...but with fire, its purification is better and more useful. Therefore, do not let the preparation weary you if you desire the fruit. And so after the separation, you will have clear **Sulfur** with its **ferment**, which will be more splendid than gems. O, how delightful is that nature, which is found everywhere and is sold for a low price. O, how very useful is this thing which contains within itself the most precious thing. Fools indeed value it cheaply, but by the wise it is greatly beloved, because fools do not know its virtue. 

Indeed, let this matter be composed with **Our Mercury**, so that it becomes one body retaining within itself three things, namely: body, Spirit, and soul; and this in the true matrimonial weight <note>original: *pondere vero matrimonificato*; referring to the balanced proportions required for a chemical "marriage"</note>, so that a true mineral may be produced, just as it is procreated in the bowels of the earth. Once the composition is made, let it be placed in **Our Gold** and let them be joined into a hard **Stone**, such that not even fire shall overcome them. 

O, how admirable is nature, which so languishes with love, because on account of her languor the woman kills her husband, and afterwards the husband also kills the woman, and thus they shall procreate infinite sons <note>This violent imagery is a common alchemical metaphor for the dissolution and recombination of chemical substances</note>. O, what great blindness there is among the workers of this divine work, because they do not follow nature, omitting extraneous things, knowing that the nature of **Our Stone** does not need those things which they use. Namely: **Arsenic**, **orpiment** <note>original: *auripigmento*; a yellow arsenic sulfide mineral</note>, common **Sulfur**, **Magnesia**, **Vitriol** <note>original: *Atramento*; literally "inky substance," used for metallic sulfates</note>, nor **Salts**—namely salt of alkali, salt of alum—and so on with other trifles. 

But it needs the natural thing which belongs to it by nature. My son, return to yourself and remember what is natural, and omit extraneous things, and for certain you shall rejoice. Do you not know that nature whitens nature, and nature reddens nature? Return, return, my son, and remember that it is impossible to make **Gold** or **Silver** from dung, but only from nature—just as a human comes from a human, and so with other natures. 

We have already made mention of the discovery of **Our Sulfur**, as well as its separation and composition, and of its **Mercury**. It is necessary that we proceed further, by **Philosophical labor**, so that our **Stone** may cast its seed <note>original: *spermatisset*; to produce the generative "seed" of the metal</note>, because if the seed has not been cast forth from it, our work would be destroyed. While the seed is ejected from it: know that it procreates infinite infernal sons <note>original: *filios infernales*; refers to the numerous mineral offspring or lower transformations produced during the process</note>. Because through its corruption the seed will putrefy and die. If, however, it has not died, it remains only in destruction.

And therefore it is written: *The corruption of one is the generation of another* <note>original: *Vnius corruptio est alterius generatio*; a standard Aristotelian principle used by alchemists to explain how one substance must break down to become another</note>. Note the example in man: A man performing the act with a woman emits seed into her womb, and if it has not "died" <note>in this context, "died" refers to the biological breakdown and transformation of the seed necessary for growth</note>, impregnation does not occur. And this happens sometimes when a man and a woman are not of one nature. Because the woman is cold and moist, and the man is hot and dry, and thus they differ in some respects, so that the seed cannot have the passage to receive putrefaction, or either the man or woman is "corrupt" <note>meaning physically imbalanced or impaired</note>, and therefore the seed is annihilated. In the same way it must be held concerning **Our Stone**, that its seed must die. And from then...

### ->ARCANUM<-

The impregnation will undoubtedly occur, unless the craftsman is ignorant in the composition of nature, and thus the work is destroyed. But if the work was composed with the proper thing—that is, the male and the female—it will without doubt reach this divine work. But how few true [philosophers] are found now! Many have become **Philosophers**, but not all are decorated by this divine mastery <term>magisterium</term> <note>The 'Mastery' or *Magisterium* refers to the successful completion of the Great Work, the creation of the Philosopher's Stone.</note>. The new **Philosophy** deservedly chooses new **Philosophers**, and thus the world is deceived. O, how holy it is to follow *Hermes* and *Thomas Aquinas* and other modern **Philosophers**, and to read their books so that they might acquire understanding of what this divine art is or can be made from; and to leave behind the new **Philosophers** who are accustomed to writing, *"Take, take,"* which is *"Deceive,"* and you will have a trifle <note>original: *trufam*; a mockery or a worthless thing.</note>.

Such men do not imitate nature, nor do they seek honor, but rather the confusion of the art. But because it is impossible for the art to be destroyed or remain in confusion through one fool, such men do not deserve the name of **Philosopher**, but of vain **Sophists** and deceivers.

Many torture **Mercury** with various pains, wishing to make it fixed <note>In alchemy, to 'fix' a substance means to make it stable and non-volatile so it does not evaporate when heated.</note>. But when they cannot achieve it, they say he is a fleeing thief. Rather, I say they themselves are more fugitive than the tortured **Mercury**. Therefore, when **Mercury** flees and escapes and enters into the craftsman, then both become fugitives. If they only knew nature, which when added to itself would not flee! Both the craftsman and the **Mercury** have need of **Philosophical Sulfur**, lest they be fleeing, but rather permanent, so that from them infinite sons might be procreated. Thus let us leave the lying sons in their errors, and let them be fixed forever in their wickednesses.

Return, my son, to the former sperm <note>original: *sperma*; in this context, it refers to the 'seed' or the primary material of the Stone, not biological fluid.</note> of our **Stone**. It is a thing most delightful and worthy of honor, because it is a perpetual thing and permanent water. Therefore let us hold fast to it, leaving behind the errors which have now been revealed.

Receive for your labor your sperm (not that which proceeds from your natural body) and proceed with it wisely, because our whole secret lies hidden there, and if you have worked otherwise, you will be found a liar and useless. And under oath I tell the truth and do not lie. Because our nature is one, one medicine, one mineral, in which the whole mastery consists, and also one fire, one vessel, one labor. He who has worked according to the rule of our nature shall truly reach the venerable **Gum** and the praiseworthy **tincture**. O, remember, son, how wonderfully nature proceeds, and how she will lead you to great honor if you have worked directly; with how much great honor you shall be decorated, provided only that you follow nature. Son, hear my commands and follow me, because I wish this divine work to be promulgated...

<header>PHILSOPHICAL [MATTERS].</header>

In brief speech, which will be well understood by the wise: Take our Philosophical vessel <note>original: *vas Philosophicale*</note> in which you must complete this divine work. This vessel must be made in the likeness of a woman's womb <note>original: *matricis mulieris*</note>; let the seed <note>original: *sperma*</note> be placed into it in our manner, and let it be positioned in our sun, so that it may follow the higher things. And infernal vapors and most subtle smokes will surround it, and thus it will be distilled and washed in its own blood, and there it will receive nourishment in its washing. Thus, that seed requires nothing but distillation and **calcination** <term>calcination</term> <note>The process of heating a substance to high temperatures in air or oxygen to change its state, often to reduce it to a fine powder or ash.</note>, and all of this is done in one work and one vessel.

### IN ITS DISTILLATION THERE ARE THREE THINGS
### to be considered.

<margin>*let him learn</margin>
First: How our **Sulphur** <note>In alchemy, Sulphur often represents the active, combustible, and masculine principle of a substance.</note> shall be converted into ash, and how it seeks the lower place so that it may be said of it: Do not despise the ash that is in the lower place, because it is the dead earth of its own body. Recognize, my son, and understand my words: that the dead body—that is, our **Sulphur**—seeks the lower parts specifically so that it might endure the fire, because the fire does not consume it due to its permanence. Second, it must be considered that the **Soul** <note>original: *anima*</note> seeks the middle, and for this reason: the **Soul** is **Gold** or our ferment, but it is not as fixed as the **Sulphur**. Thus, it cannot endure the fire so suddenly unless it takes up the assistance of the **Sulphur**; therefore, it seeks the middle ground. Third, it must be considered that the **Spirit** <note>original: *Spiritus*</note> is an impossible thing <note>Meaning it is highly volatile and difficult to "fix" or stabilize.</note>; therefore, it seeks the higher parts, as it is said: *The Spirit was carried upon the waters.* And this is the reason why it cannot endure the fire, unless it learns little by little from those other two. And so, through **calcination**, the fire is always increased for it, so that it may learn to endure the fire along with these two bodies.

And know that these three are not joined together so very easily, unless the dead body has been cleansed of its blackness <note>The *nigredo* stage, symbolizing putrefaction and the "death" of the old form.</note> and is revived. Then it receives the **Soul** and the **Spirit**, and in its union many colors will appear, and wonderful signs. And thus all things will be fixed and perpetual. For in the beginning of our art, the first sign is blackness, because the matter putrefies, and the volatile part strives to battle little by little against the fire, so that all things may be fixed. And thus there is a Philosophical proverb: *Unless the bodies die and the dead are revived and joined with the Spirits, the Mastery is nothing,* because nature now rules alone.

### NOTE.

After the blackness and its washing, the craftsman can rightly rejoice, seeing such great wonders; for what in the beginning was blackness has now been made into a great light. O venerable nature...

<header>THE SECRET</header>
<meta>catchword: happened [disse].</meta>

How many tribulations and anxieties you have caused in your art during your **blackness** <term>nigredo</term> <note>original: *nigredine*. The first stage of the alchemical "Great Work," representing the "death" or decomposition of the material.</note>. Behold how you now illuminate it with great light and perpetual joy. Where there is blackness, there is infinite love.

O, how delightful is the birth from the most base thing, procreated in the **Philosophical womb** <note>original: *matrice Philosophica*. A common metaphor for the sealed alchemical vessel where the transformation occurs.</note>! Its trees are decorated with various leaves and flowers. Its roots are made of precious stones, and the illuminating branch of the tree shines with a brilliant light. The herbs give off the scent of **Balsam** to the trees and expel all infirmity.

And truly I say: If a man were half-dead and saw the goodness and beauty of the Stone, all his infirmity would depart from him. And if he were in his death-throes and consumed but one flower, the entire plague would leave him.

Recognize, my son, how many virtues nature possesses; my senses fail me so that I might even be able to describe its powers. What we have seen with our eyes, we testify to; and what we have worked with our hands, we have written down.

It is necessary for us to proceed further, so that our stone may be further perfected and born from its mother's womb, and it will show us infinite wonders.

Therefore, proceed with it in our manner, so that it may drink the milk from which it receives nourishment, and it shall be converted into a **red color** and lack all whiteness. Let it be known that this shall be our second sign. Proceed further, so that our Stone may have all its members, and thus it is converted into blackness—so that every stain is cleansed from it—and then it shall be converted into a **whiteness** <term>albedo</term> <note>The second major stage, representing purification and the washing away of impurities.</note> ten times clearer than it was before. Proceed further so that you may make a **carbuncle** <note>original: *carbunculum*. Historically, a glowing red gemstone; in alchemy, this represents the final perfected state of the Stone, often called the "Red Work" or *rubedo*.</note> out of the crystal, and thus your whole art is completed, and your Stone shall be everlasting. Praise Jesus Christ when you have reached this point.

Here ends the universal way of Johannes de Lasnioro Lazon, in the year **one thousand four hundred and forty-eight** <note>1448 AD</note>. On the Friday in the Vigil of Vitus <note>The eve of the feast of St. Vitus, June 15.</note>. I, Johannes Lucianus, truly copied this with great diligence in the **four-hundredth year** <note>likely shorthand for 1400.</note>. Praise be to the nourishing Trinity and the indivisible Unity, without end. Amen.

This Johannes de Lazionoro, written above, was a disciple of that Antonius the Italian, originally from Florence, who was slaughtered here in Bohemia by impious men because of that chemical art; just as it is testified in the Bohemian writing concerning the Philosopher's Stone, it so **happened**—

<header>TREATISE III.</header>

# THE NOBLE CHEMICAL
## TREATISE OF JOHANNES
### TRITHEMIUS, ABBOT
### of Sponheim, easily the prince among Philosophers
### in our century.

->PUBLISHED NOW FOR THE FIRST TIME BY<-
->*an anonymous author for the sake of the*<-
->*sons of Hermetic Wisdom.*<-

**A**ll the most learned men of natural philosophy have decreed and established that the **Moon** <term>Luna</term> <note>In alchemical texts, "Luna" refers both to the celestial body and the metal Silver.</note> is closely related to the **Sun** <term>Sol</term> <note>In alchemy, "Sol" refers to Gold.</note>. In this elementary world, she changes and distributes the actions of men and the commerce of things together with her brother **Phoebus** <note>original: *Phæbo*. A poetic name for the Sun.</note> through a wonderful arrangement of variety. Just as in the heavens, that **Daedalus** <note>A reference to the mythical Greek master craftsman, used here as a metaphor for God or the creative force of Nature.</note>, the craftsman of nature and the maker of all things, ordained two most bright lights from the beginning of the rising world—one to preside over the Day, the other over the night. But since, according to the opinion of all those who philosophize, the earthly Moon lacks only a little **fixation** <term>fixio</term> <note>original: *fixio*. The process of making a volatile substance stable so that it does not evaporate when heated.</note>, I wished to bring forth into the midst of the sons of wisdom something hidden, secret, and most remote from the sanctuaries of Philosophy. By this means, the silvery **Phoebe** <note>original: *Phæbe*. A poetic name for the Moon (Silver).</note>, who has long been carried on two wheels, may finally be promoted to the four-horse rank of her brother Phoebus. Thus, being appointed not over the night but over the day, she may drench this world of ours in a golden brilliance.

Nor shall anyone persuade me that any other labor is easier or more certain than this very one. I also judge those men to have clearly wasted their efforts who have undertaken many labors in **coagulating Mercury** <note>Mercury was notoriously difficult to "fix" or solidify; Trithemius suggests starting with Silver is a much more efficient path to making Gold.</note>, since they already possess the Moon, which is nearly fixed and which they can most easily lead to a more subtle nature. By this same ingenuity, **Saturn** <term>Lead</term> and **Venus** <term>Copper</term> could also be easily carried to the nature of gold, although philosophers have mostly reflected upon the Moon and her defects.

The Moon lacks weight, which **Saturn** <note>Saturn represents Lead, which is heavy and associated with stability and "weight" in alchemical theory.</note>—who approaches the Sun in weight—will give to you most abundantly. For this reason, Gold is frequently described by Philosophers as "leprous." Philosophers and Astronomers attribute the "earthly" quality to Saturn. For what is heavier than earth, or what is more ponderous? Because of this, in the heavens, Saturn walks around his kingdom in a circuit of thirty years because of his slowness and weight. And since the Moon lacks...

**fixation** <term>fixio</term> <note>The process of making a volatile substance stable so it can withstand heat without evaporating.</note>, that is, a more complete **decoction** <term>decoctio</term> <note>A long-term "cooking" or digestion of a substance in alchemical heat.</note>, which fiery **Mars** <term>Mars</term> <note>In alchemy, Mars represents the metal Iron.</note> abundantly provides for you—both because it is closer to the heat of the **Sun** <term>Sol</term> <note>Gold.</note>, and also because it is less easily destroyed in our common fire. Truly, **Venus** <term>Venus</term> <note>Copper.</note>, the inseparable companion of the Sun, easily increases the color. While the natural magicians confess she is the Goddess of the most beautiful color, we philosophically assign both color and weight to Mars, in which you may conclude the fixation. But you will understand the required proportion and the necessary **mixture** <note>original: *mystionem*, likely a variation of *mixtionem*.</note> of these three bodies toward one another partly from the investigation of astronomical matters, and partly from the study of natural things. In astronomical knowledge, you must know how much they approach or stand apart from the **Moon** <term>Luna</term> <note>Silver.</note>. Specifically, **Saturn** <term>Saturnus</term> <note>Lead.</note> is sixth in order, Mars is fourth, and Venus occupies the second place. Naturally, however, if you consider their nature and qualities according to the three "defects" of the Moon, you will see which among them is greater, and what is owed to the Moon first, and what is owed last. For it would be of no small help to this matter if you were to examine precisely how much Saturn exceeds in weight; look upon the figure on the preceding page with your wits, and you will see that I have written of these things philosophically.

He who desires to bring anything from the most profound science of **Chemistry** to its end must well consider the celestial bodies, and diligently recognize their qualities, natures, and positions; if he does this, he will find, by divine grace, an inexhaustible understanding in them. Therefore, I have decided to lay open something of these matters for the son of wisdom. By considering these things, he will perhaps investigate many other, even greater things, by himself.

The **Sun** resides in the middle like an Emperor of the planets, most powerfully governing the whole world and the other planets. Three planets are placed above him and three below. Mars is the superior planet closer to the Sun; Venus is closer below. If, therefore, you desire to advance the **Moon** into the nature of the **Sun**, it is necessary that you extract the most subtle and tinting **Spirits** from Mars and Venus. However, because these are volatile, they cannot tint the Moon unless you first restrain and congeal them with the **ferment** <term>fermentum</term> <note>A substance, often gold or silver, used to "leaven" or transform a larger mass of base metal.</note> of the Sun, which is the most perfect of all. This is despite the fact that some pseudo-philosophers <note>original: *scioli*, meaning "smatterers" or those with superficial knowledge.</note> strive to coagulate those fleeing Spirits into a vegetable body.

Another point: If the Sun must become the Moon <note>original: *Si Sol Luna fieri debeat*. This may refer to the "white" stage of the work or a reduction to a base state.</note>, it is necessary that the two intermediate planets between the Moon and the Sun be first separated and set apart. (By the "entry" of Venus, understand the Moon; by **Mercury** <term>Mercurius</term> <note>Quicksilver.</note>, understand the evaporable moisture). Certain pseudo-philosophers have called these two obstacles by the names "grime" and "glue of the dregs" <note>original: *norem & gluten rambium*. *Gluten rambium* is a technical term in medieval alchemy, often referring to a viscous, impure mineral moisture.</note>, using inept and dull terms.

### *Of Hermes Trismegistus*
# THE GOLDEN TRACTATE
## *CONCERNING THE SECRET OF THE PHYSICAL STONE <note>The "Physical Stone" refers to the Philosopher’s Stone, the goal of alchemy.</note>, divided into seven Chapters: now truly illustrated with commentaries by a certain Anonymous author.*

### CHAPTER ONE

->❦<-

->HERMES<-

*For Hermes says: In so long an age I have not ceased to experiment, nor have I spared my soul from labor; and I obtained this art and science solely by the inspiration of the living God, who deigned to reveal it to me, His servant.*

->COMMENTARY<- <note>original: "Scholium." A scholium is a marginal note or explanatory commentary written by a later scholar to clarify a text.</note>

<image-desc>Ornamental woodcut initial 'T' with floral and foliate patterns.</image-desc>
Three things are most necessary for a disciple of the art or a "son of the teaching" <note>A common alchemical term for an initiate or student.</note>: Study, experience, and Divine Blessing. For whatever is first implanted and sown in our intellect through study and diligent meditation is afterward confirmed by experience—that is, by visual demonstration resulting from manual operation. Yet, you should not promise yourself successful progress in either action unless you have also first secured divine favor and blessing for yourself. For in the conduct of human affairs, the will and decree of GOD occupy the primary role; as it is written in Romans 9: *It is not of him that runs, nor of him that wills, but of God who shows mercy.* <note>original Latin: "Non est currentis, neq; volentis, sed miserentis DEI."</note> If you have Him favorable and well-disposed, you shall fear no obstacle, even though the whole world and the devil himself should oppose you; nevertheless, you shall happily complete your purpose. On the contrary, if you feel Him to be angry, all labor will be ineffectual, vain, and empty, according to that saying:
> *No effort is ever successful or useful,*
> *If God does not both grant counsel and provide help.*
Hippocrates <note>The famous Greek physician of antiquity.</note> contended that these seven things suffice for perfect medicine: Nature, instruction, a place suitable for studies, education from childhood, study, industry, and time. But because

The accompanying commentary emphasizes that success in alchemy requires a balance of theoretical study, practical lab work, and, most importantly, the favor of God.</summary>

### CHAPTER I.

<sig>Vu</sig>

...he omits what is most necessary above all others, namely the divine blessing: and this is either due to an ignorance of GOD, or out of contempt for his own Gods, an infinite number of which the pagan nations once worshipped. And although he might seem excusable for this reason—because he was a Pagan—a huge difference nevertheless appears between those Pagans who were skilled in Alchemy <term>Chymia</term> and those who were unskilled. 

But you will say that Hermes the Egyptian also originated from a pagan nation. I admit that; he was a pagan by nationality, yet in religion he came closest to the true and legitimate worship of God. The Magi, who came from the east to Christ, were not bound to the ceremonies of the Jews in worshipping GOD, nor were they from that same people, but were born of a Gentile family; nevertheless, they were illuminated by the singular grace of GOD: and without doubt, they would not have yielded even to the Jews themselves, or to many pseudo-Christians today, in faithfully and truly pursuing divine worship. 

But how does it happen that some Pagans, such as Hermes, Plato, the three Magi, and many more like them, seem to have had such distinguished knowledge of GOD, while others had so little or plainly none at all? Saint Paul solves this knotty question in the first chapter of the Epistle to the Romans. There he proposes a twofold distinction among the Pagans: some of whom he says indeed knew GOD, but did not glorify Him as GOD or give thanks; while others, through the opportunity of knowing GOD from nature, neglected Him by their own fault. 

Furthermore, if we run through the records of all ages, it can be clearly seen that those Pagan philosophers who simultaneously cultivated Alchemy <term>Chymia</term> shone forth with a greater brilliance of piety and virtues than the rest. But Peripatetic or pagan Ethics, in cultivating virtues, relies not on **GOD's** blessing but on its own strengths. This foundation is utterly false, and it looks toward an equally spurious and adulterated goal: namely, empty and vain glory. 

And what surprises me is that this paganism has not yet faded away in the schools of Christians, but is cultivated as if it were a most necessary part of Philosophy. If any benefit is gained from this, its Professors in the Academies gain only this: they write ethical theses which they force the students to defend, from whom they afterwards expect a generous fee. For instance, not long ago, someone disputing on the topic of "liberality" <note>The virtue of being generous with money</note> presented his presiding officer, in exchange for his chairmanship, with some twenty imperial thalers <note>A silver coin used throughout the Holy Roman Empire</note>. Just as the presiding officer highly praised this "liberality" in this case, he conversely criticized others who had offered less. 

This, of course, is the benefit that flows from the profession of Ethics: that Doctors now make a profit from it. But while they prescribe laws and precepts of virtue to others, they take no care for themselves, lest they meanwhile fall imprudently into horrific vices—specifically greed, and many similar things. 

But if anyone should try to force the argument—beyond the benefits already listed—that the precepts of Ethics are greatly useful for shaping the outward behavior of studious youth: then against this weapon, I oppose only piety, which is useful for all things, having the promise of both the present life and the life to come. If young people are well-instructed and make progress in this one thing alone, they will emerge most excellent in the refinement of both external and internal character, and in the integrity of their lives. 

Farewell, then, to that corpse-like and dead Ethics of the Pagans! May our Christian Ethics, having come forth from the living fountains of divinity, make us partakers not only of worldly happiness in this world, but also of eternal blessedness in the life to follow. For the virtues of this ethics arise from true faith in **Christ**, without which no human being will ever be able to please **GOD** or be saved. Literally "little big-noses," a Latin idiom for people who think they are clever or overly critical.</note> stand in the way, saying that although it cannot be denied that the word of the Lord is the cause and principle of all things, nevertheless that is only to be understood concerning the **efficient cause** <term>Efficient cause: The agent or force that brings something into being, like a carpenter making a chair.</term>, but not concerning the **material cause** <term>Material cause: The actual "stuff" or matter out of which a thing is made, like the wood of a chair.</term>. For they deem it absurd if anyone asserts that this **WORD**, which is nothing but the breath of the spirit and the essential inhalation of **GOD**, became corporeal and visible, passing into wood, stone, etc.

But how ridiculous and worthy of every rejection this objection is, is clear from the fact that this difference between the **formal** and **material** cause only holds place in artificial things: but not in natural things, and much less in the work of creation. In artificial things indeed, wood—as the subject matter from which a table is formed—is something separate and diverse from the joiner or craftsman, who performs the office of the efficient or formal cause. In natural things, however, matter and form do not exist as something separate, nor will anyone find any diversity in them, unless he also wishes, having abandoned the faithful testimony of the senses, to imagine those things which no mortal ever saw, or heard, tasted, smelled, or touched. For if this philosophical axiom of the same *Aristotle* is true—as I myself do not doubt it is most true—namely: "Nothing falls into the senses which was not first in the mind; and nothing truly existing in the mind is there which does not fall into the senses" <note>This is a variation of the famous Scholastic maxim "Nothing is in the intellect which was not first in the senses."
