->### Vol 4. Book Bbbb###<-

...ordering [the separation of] the subtle from the dense, beginning with a light fire and finishing in it, until the whole was transformed into a dense matter through the office of fire. In this way, I made the **elixir** <term>elixir<gloss>The "philosopher's stone" in liquid or powder form, capable of transmuting metals or healing the body</gloss></term>. Sometimes, however, I placed those raw materials before a lighter fire, using a method of **putrefaction** <term>putrefaction<gloss>A stage of "chemical death" where substances break down and blacken, viewed as a necessary precursor to rebirth</gloss></term> until the end of their death and tribulation; indeed, I even carried it out for a longer duration. I found this method to be shorter than the others, and therein I rested. 

Regarding all these matters, I taught this process more diligently to a certain man I found who was sick in spirit and mind—who for three years was a most devoted student—and to certain others. This man, not content with my demonstrations alone, exercised himself greatly in these things, and by varying the process in many ways, he did not fail in them. For when he saw his subtle confection turned into water, he struck it many times <note>likely referring to agitation or rhythmic grinding</note>, and dried it gently in **distilled vinegar** within a glass vessel. Then, in a stronger fire, he cooked it by **sublimating** <term>sublimation<gloss>The process of heating a substance until it becomes a vapor and then solidifies again, used for purification</gloss></term> and repeated the work so often until the whole resided as a liquid with **fixation** <term>fixation<gloss>The stabilization of a volatile substance so that it no longer evaporates when exposed to heat</gloss></term>, so that it might tint any body. 

He augmented it at times just as I did—by dissolving, coagulating, and dissolving purified **tinctures** <term>tinctures<gloss>The concentrated "spirit" or color of a substance used to transform the properties of another material</gloss></term>, then adding, coagulating, fixing, and melting—and he found a new way of augmenting. Because he dissolved and coagulated at his pleasure and varied the work in many ways, he most excellently perceived the nature, intention, and secrets of the Philosophers. I taught him three secrets in particular, which he diligently committed to memory: 

First, concerning the conversion of the entire compound into **salt** following the process of putrefaction, about which I had told him: "If you wish to be enriched, prepare the salt; unless you convert everything into salt, you will have nothing." 

Second, concerning its conversion through the preceding **calcination** <term>calcination<gloss>The reduction of a substance to a fine powder or ash through high heat</gloss></term> and liquefaction with a fire that is neither vitrifying <note>meaning a fire not hot enough to turn the substance into glass</note> nor too strong, but one that melts the matter with a light heat. Concerning this, I had told him: "Unless you have made the bodies spiritual, do not blaspheme the elixir"—that is, the Work—for it is necessary that the body becomes an impalpable spirit, and that all things are mixed in the smallest parts; this happens when it becomes a liquid and a **tinting poison**. For he who can turn <term>brumazar</term> <note>original: "brumazar"; an obscure Arabic-derived term for a primary alchemical substance or a toxic mineral state</note> into poison will find what he seeks and will not err. 

The third secret was about the **solution** <term>solution<gloss>The process of dissolving a solid into a liquid, often called the "key" to alchemy</gloss></term> of the entire compound, which is the "Treasure of the thing that lifts the poor man from the dung-heap" <note>A common alchemical metaphor for turning worthless matter into gold</note>, through which **Hermes** <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of alchemy</note> said he was exalted above all the circles of the world. This man is truly a son of our Philosophy, for he perceives the principal secrets; if someone is ignorant of these, he is frustrated in his purpose, but if he knows them, he will not err in the work. Therefore, let him approach the work with confidence, in whose mind various images and variations of the operation result. For his hand cannot easily run to the **Practice** when his mind is corrupted in the **Theory**—that is, the beginning. Indeed, such a man, in his operations, is at last overcome by weariness...

...left behind, I thought about that which has been handed down. Some used to dissolve bodies and fix the spirits bathed with the solution on high, a point about which I hesitated greatly and my mind wandered. For he <note>Referring to the student mentioned on the previous page</note> made **sharp waters** <term>aquas acutas<gloss>Corrosive mineral acids, such as nitric acid or aqua regia, used to dissolve metals</gloss></term> as he knew how, and as he wished he **calcined** and dissolved spirits and bodies. The composition which he had made, he afterwards purged with fire and congealed in a well-secured glass vessel. By gradually increasing the fire, he fixed the whole, which he brought to a state of liquefaction by continuing the fire. As a diligent investigator, he understood that this was the intention of the **Assembly** <note>original: "Turbae"; referring to the *Turba Philosophorum*, one of the earliest and most influential Latin alchemical texts</note>, since otherwise there is the labor of distillation and calcination, for which we require many different vessels. 

The Philosophers, however, required nothing in the whole work except one single vessel, and one regime—namely, cooking—and one thing by which it is administered: heat. For this reason **Hermes** <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure regarded as the father of alchemy</note>, the father of Philosophers, commanded us to contemplate for a long time until one might grasp the true path of the Philosophers in the operation, by the lawful way, as is testified in the book of the *Assembly*. Therefore, regarding the manner of the vessel and the fire, he wandered much; but after he knew the matter from which it is made, he persisted with constancy and patience until he grasped the desired end of perfection, and there, coming to a halt, he rested. 

But now the doctrine given, alas, languishes due to the disturbance of the mind; and though among all the prescribed methods these are truer and easier than others, we nevertheless require many vessels, from which comes weariness in the management because of the troublesome labors. Therefore, whoever wishes to be made equal to this son of mine in this work, let him accept this tradition of mine, in which I shall prescribe in order whatever he himself perceived in the **Great Work** <note>The "Opus Majus," the ultimate alchemical process of creating the Philosopher's Stone</note>—which is done in one single action—by drawing for a long time from the secrets of the Philosophers. 

I will say, therefore, that there are four principal things to be observed: **Matter**, **Manner**, **Place**, and **Time**. 
*   **Matter** <term>Res<gloss>The physical substance or "First Matter" used to begin the work</gloss></term>, namely that from which it is made, and the weights of the fire itself. 
*   **Time**, namely the duration in which the whole is finished. 
*   **Place**, namely where it is perfected by cooking. 
*   **Manner**, namely the way of acting. 

Concerning the first, namely the air, I have already given a sufficiently plain tradition in the preceding pages. Regarding the vessel, they have said it should be like an **eggshell**. Others say it is made in the likeness of a **human head**. Even the **envious** <note>original: "invidi"; a term used for alchemical authors who deliberately hid secrets behind metaphors to protect them from the unworthy</note> said it was finally a round, dark thing surrounded by dew, and these speak the truth. Even the envious said it should be in the manner of a half-moon. Others said that it should be in the likeness of a **dish** <term>paropsis<gloss>A shallow bowl or side-dish; in alchemy, this refers to the shape of the crucible or container</gloss></term>, and in this the envious spoke. 

We took two black substances, and we placed them in the dish which we have, and from there they will be eggs or salt. The Wise said that the vessel should be round, very thick, and made of glass. Concerning which **Arisleus** <note>A central figure in the *Visio Arislei*, an alchemical allegory where he is trapped in a glass house to undergo a symbolic death and rebirth</note> said in his vision: "They imprisoned me and my companions in their glass house, over which they built another house—"

# CONCERNING THE SECRET
<note>original: "DE SILENTO"; likely a variant of *De Silentio* (Concerning Silence) or a typo for *De Sigillo* (Concerning the Seal), both common alchemical titles referring to the preservation of secrets or the sealing of the vessel.</note>

->Bbbb 2<-

...[there] are, upon which a third [vessel rests], and thus we were enclosed in three houses <note>The "three houses" refers to a nested arrangement of vessels, such as a glass flask inside a ceramic pot inside a furnace</note>; the arrangement of these vessels a wise operator will be able to construct sufficiently through his own industry.

### On the manner of acting and the fire

Let us begin while the Sun is in **Aries** <note>The sign of Aries (the Ram) marks the spring equinox, the traditional beginning of the alchemical year and a symbol of renewal</note>. Some say [it should begin] in the drum, others from the humidity of winter; some said it should be done with a light fire, others with a fire of dung <note>A "fire of dung" (*ignis fimi*) refers to the gentle, steady heat produced by fermenting horse manure, used for long-term digestion</note>. Others said let the fire be in the beginning like the heat of spring; others like the heat of digesting food; others like the heat in an **Embryo**; others like the heat of a **hen sitting upon eggs**. Some performed it with humidity. Some with straw and ash. Some with a lamp-wick. Some with coals and moderate flames. The "envious" <note>The "envious" (*invidi*) is a term used for ancient masters who intentionally obscured their writings to prevent the unworthy from succeeding</note> said: "Let it be completed in a triple heat of fire, namely, Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius." <note>These are the three fire signs of the Zodiac, representing the increasing intensity of the heat</note> And these spoke the truth. 

I say lastly, that in the first regime the Philosophers wished to show the lightness of the fire, and afterwards stronger and stronger. (Wherefore **Arisleus** <note>A prominent figure in early alchemical literature, specifically the *Turba Philosophorum*</note> says:) "We remained in the darkness of the waves in the intense heat of summer, and in a disturbance of the sea the like of which never happened to us." I say, therefore, that these are the orders of fire among which experiment demonstrates the quantities. For this reason they said we know the science of fires to be wonderful. For fire in different ways works different effects.

### On the time

Concerning the time, some said that it is done in three days; others in seven, others in four, others in six, others in thirty days. I, however, say that all can be excused. For they added that general clause from which no one ought to deviate, namely: **until it is completed**. Because every natural action has one time in which it is perfected, and is terminated by a due continuation; however, the work is prolonged and shortened by the suitability of the things, vessels, and fires which are all composed together.

I command you, therefore, to take **quicksilver** <term>argentum vivum<gloss>Mercury; the volatile "spirit" of the work</gloss></term> and **sulfur**, for the universal work which I mentioned, in the due weight; let them be prepared true and sincere, and raw, just as the mine brought them forth, without any foreign liquid, incorporating them together. Let it be placed in a glass vessel, round and thick, having a long and narrow neck; close the orifice most excellently, lest the **vapor** <note>original: "humor"; refers to the volatile essence or "spirit" of the materials</note> breathe out. Place it in that perforated and fitted pot, or in an iron vessel, or with sulfur over the fire. If, however, you are bolder and instructed in the lightness of the fire, let the glass vessel be **luted** <note>Luting (*lutatum*) involves coating the glass with a mixture of clay, sand, and hair to protect it from breaking under direct heat</note> at the bottom. And then you will not need to surround it with liquid from wine. Let there be some obstacle, which may prevent its direct access to the fire.

# THE WORK OF PETER
<note>original: "OPUS PETRI"; This likely refers to a specific alchemical treatise or "Work" attributed to a master named Peter, possibly Peter of Ferrara or another medieval adept.</note>

And you should begin under a legitimate constellation of the heavens, which will greatly benefit your work. Then you must apply a very slow fire, for at least ten days, so that the heat is of such nutrition, and **putrefaction** <note>Putrefaction was considered the essential first stage of the Great Work, where the matter "dies" and decays to allow for rebirth.</note>, or **solution**, that it acts internally, so that some manner of separation is created in them; and you shall not liquefy it unless perhaps by a fire of liquefaction that is still light. Likewise, it is cooked until much fruit and the **stone** are produced, and all **blackness** <note>original: "nigredo"; the first stage of the alchemical process</note> vanishes—which is not the true color, or whatever intermediate color might occur—and through the lightness of the fire, a miraculous **whiteness** <note>original: "albedo"; the second major stage, representing purification</note> approaches. For the elements, when diligently cooked, rejoice and are converted into other natures. If all elements are not joined together, nothing of this art which is desired is perfected. But when mixed and alienated from their own natures, they become something new; and all of this, through the lightness of the fire, is nothing else but to extract the humidities of the bodies and consume them. Therefore, let the fire be light, which thins the natures and amends them, and sequesters the liquid from the turbid. Indeed, a light fire is that which the **magnesia** <note>In alchemy, "magnesia" does not refer to the modern element magnesium, but rather to a mystical "primary matter" or a specific mineral used to draw out the "hidden soul" of the metals.</note> does not flee. Let not the fire be kindled too much, lest the matter be deprived of sense and motion. For if the composite is ruled more than is proper, that which could have been beneficial is exterminated.

Wherefore, if anyone introduced to this art knew their natures, he would certainly endure the lengthiness of the cooking, by mixing the elements with **mercury** <note>original: "arg. viv." or *argentum vivum* (living silver)</note> at first over a light fire, which is called the fire or heat of **spring**, or the degree of **Aries** <note>The "degree of Aries" signifies a gentle heat, like the sun in March/April, used to sprout seeds.</note> in which the trees bud and turn white. When the whiteness is seen, it is certain that all things are now **fixed**; wherefore, as the fire is no longer to be doubted, you shall then give a fire of coals, increasing it by degrees, like the heat of **summer** or the degrees of **Leo** <note>The "degree of Leo" represents the height of summer heat (July/August), used to "ripen" the alchemical fruit.</note>, when the fruits ripen and the harvests are perfected. And let it be continued here until the mass is worn down in the fire—not by calcining it into ash with your hands—and it will become a strongly burnt ash. Then, in a convenient fire, if it should be for the **red**, let it be made red, and in the final fire it is liquefied and completed; and it is continuously liquefied until it reaches the heat of **Sagittarius** <note>The "heat of Sagittarius" (late autumn) often refers to a cooling or a final transition stage where the fruit is separated or the cycle is completed.</note>, by which the leaves and fruits are scattered. Therefore, first it becomes **black**. Secondly, **white**. Thirdly, **citrine** <note>original: "citrinus"; a yellowish color signifying the transition between white and red.</note>. Fourthly, **red**. Finally, it becomes a **tingeing poison** <note>original: "venenum tingens"; "poison" here is used as a term of power, meaning a concentrated elixir or "tincture" capable of transforming everything it touches.</note>, any body of which is called "good" by many names, with which, if you cook Mercury, you shall drive away poverty. This is the **Stone** created in the likeness of the **Greater World** <note>The "Macrocosm" or the universe at large.</note>. By the heavy and the light, the soft and the hard, the hot and the cold, the moist and the dry. Bound by nature in a firm peace, it is a perpetual fruit in the fire. It conquers every subtle thing and penetrates every solid thing, which the foulness of the earth cannot corrupt, nor the muddiness of water condense, nor the touch

### ON SILENCE.

...to overshadow the air, nor can the violence of fire overcome it. Therefore, hide this **stone** <term>Lapis Philosophorum; the Philosopher's Stone, the goal of the Great Work</term> from the powerful, and from the envious and the unworthy, lest they become stronger from that which is unworthily performed, and more ready for illicit deeds. I shall therefore relate certain general matters regarding the entire process, and I say: Venerate the **King** and his **wife** <note>Common alchemical symbols for Sulfur (the active, masculine principle) and Mercury (the passive, feminine principle).</note>, for you do not know their fury; fear lest it should perhaps rush upon you and they show their wrath.

Furthermore, **quicksilver** <term>argentum vivum; mercury</term> is fiery, burning every body more than fire; and every body that is mixed with it is worn down by it and given over to death before it is shattered. The **Dragon** <note>A symbol for the volatile, crude, or poisonous state of the matter, often associated with mercury or acidic vapors.</note> also does not die by one treatment alone; therefore, the Philosophers dug a tomb for themselves and buried a woman with him. For whoever was strongly joined to the woman—whose belly is full of weapons and poison—the more he is turned and rolled around her, the more his body is sequestered into many parts. But seeing himself overcome by womanly art, and mixed with the woman's arts and given over to death, he is entirely turned into blood. Therefore, stir up a war between the **earth** and the **quicksilver**, because both, having been corrupted, tend toward perfection.

Likewise, when they are diligently ground and exalted by fire, and not by hands, as is necessary, that **Kuhul** <note>original: "Kuhul"; an Arabic-derived term for an extremely fine powder, often associated with antimony or the blackened state of the matter.</note> is produced in nature, and a color that does not flee. For every body dissolved with the spirit to which it is mixed becomes, without a doubt, spiritual. And every spirit altered by a body will be colored, possessing the power of tinting and fighting against fire. Therefore the **copper** <term>aes; crude metal</term> is whitened and has become shadowless. Whiten the **latten** <term>lathonem; a term for a brass-like alloy representing the matter in its impure yellow state</term> and tear up your books, lest your hearts be torn <note>This is a common alchemical trope: the warning that if one follows literal books rather than the "truth" of the lab, they will suffer despair.</note>. The science of this art is nothing else than the **sublimation** of vapor and water, and the conjunction of the body of **magnesia** <note>In alchemy, magnesia refers to a specific "prime matter" or metallic starting material, not the modern element magnesium.</note> with quicksilver.

And it must be known that **Azoth** <note>The essential spirit or universal solvent, often depicted as the soul of mercury.</note> cannot substantially take away or change the color of the latten, except in appearance. But the latten can, both substantially and in appearance, take away its own whiteness. For there is within it a miraculous strength which appears above all colors when the colors have been washed; and when it takes away its blackness and impurity and becomes white, then it is latten, and makes it red. Care must be taken that the moisture does not leave the vessel; truly coagulate it in the vessel until it becomes **ash**. And know that you have then mixed it most excellently, because this ash receives the spirit and is soaked with that moisture until it is turned into a color more beautiful than it was before.

### THE WORK OF PETER

Look at how painters are unable to paint with their own pictures <note>original: "suis nequeunt pingere picturis"; likely meaning that just as a painter needs raw pigment rather than finished art to create, the alchemist needs raw material rather than a finished product to begin the work.</note>. So too do the **Philosophers** <term>Philosophi; here meaning alchemists, the "philosophers of nature"</term> treat their medicines until they turn their materials into dust. These materials should indeed be crushed, not by hands, but cooked by fire until they become a flowable ash. If you are unable to burn the body and reduce it to ash, you have accomplished nothing of value. For if you have governed it subtly as I have described, you will see many good results in effect. It is necessary, therefore, for the body to be prepared by the flame of fire. Let that which is occupied be broken down and made weak with water—namely, raw water—in which it resides, until the whole becomes as water. When you see **whiteness** <note>albedo; the second major stage of the alchemical process, representing purification and the "Lunar" state</note> appearing in the vessel and rising above all else, be certain that **redness** <note>rubor or rubedo; the final stage representing perfection, solar power, and the completion of the Stone</note> is surely hidden within that whiteness.

Furthermore, it is the duty of the fire to subsequently make the color red. First, **blackness** <note>nigredo; the first stage, symbolizing death, putrefaction, and the decomposition of the matter</note> arises from their death, and afterward whiteness succeeds it. Then the redness which is extracted from it corrects the blackness, putting to flight the raw state. He is therefore a true **Artist** <term>Artifex; the alchemist as a skilled craftsman of nature</term> who reduces these two into one: that is, the body into spirit and the spirit into the body. And what is more, he turns it into blood. When the Philosophers saw it turned into blood, they left it in the sun for many days until it became a poison. Then the lightness is consumed, and the blood increases. Whoever among you, therefore, knows how to make the fleeing spirit red by mixing the body with it—and then from that body, with that spirit, subtly extracts its thin nature hidden in its belly using a slow fire—if he is patient in the long duration of the cooking, he undoubtedly tints every body. And for this reason they said: "Look upon the wonderful strength, according to the nature of the stone, and do not despise it." Hence it is necessary that the body itself be broken down by a most subtle spirit—one lacking a body—until it flows smoothly. In this secret governance, the "fleeing" <note>volatile or easily evaporated</note> bodies become "non-fleeing" <note>fixed or stable under heat</note>, spirits are converted into bodies, and bodies into spirits. And there shall be one corporeal and one spiritual thing which is called the **Elixir**, that is, the medicine for curing all bodies and transforming them into true **silver-making** <term>lunificum; from "Luna" (the Moon/Silver), the power to transmute metals into silver</term> and **gold-making** <term>solificum; from "Sol" (the Sun/Gold), the power to transmute metals into gold</term> substances.

The **Envious** <note>Invidis; a common term for previous alchemical authors who supposedly hid their secrets from the unworthy using riddles</note> have summarized this entire work more briefly when they said: "He who does not corrupt, does not amend," meaning to **putrefy** <term>putrefactio; the breaking down of matter through rot or heat</term>; and "He who does not wander, does not perfect," meaning to roast or to process as a mineral. And "He who is not saddened, is not gladdened." But they spoke more truly when they said: "Nature contains nature," namely, in the first work of putrefaction. Nature...

DE SILENTO.
<sig>Bbbb 4</sig>

it destroys the nature <note>i.e., the original physical form of the base matter</note>, namely by **sublimating** it <term>sublimatio; the process of heating a substance until it turns to vapor and then solidifies again, used for purification</term>, through the froth <note>original: "per kymam"; likely referring to the "vaporous sprout" or the rising spirit of the chemical reaction</note>, or by reducing it to ash. Nature overcomes nature and conquers it <note>a foundational alchemical maxim: the transformation is not forced from outside but is a natural process where the "spirit" of the substance triumphs over its "body"</note>; specifically by turning it red, **fixing** it <term>fixatio; the stage where a volatile substance is made stable so it no longer evaporates under heat</term>, turning it white, liquefying it, and by creating the "poison" <note>in alchemical literature, "poison" often refers to a potent, transformative agent or the corrosive state that "kills" the base metal before its resurrection as a noble one</note>. And thus, my dearest son, you possess the entire Art. Here end the sayings of the excellent Master **PETER OF SILENTO**.

# TO THE MOST NOBLE,

## AND MOST RENOWNED MAN, and most experienced Doctor of Chemical Medicine, Lord BERNHARD G. PENOTO of Port-Sainte-Marie in Aquitaine, many greetings.

*“Owls to Athens,” <note>original: "Noctuas Athenas"; a classical Greek idiom similar to "carrying coals to Newcastle," meaning to give someone something they already have in abundance</note> you will say, most excellent and learned man, when you see these small pages about the **Philosopher’s Stone**, for you hold perfectly <note>original: "ad unguem," literally "to the fingernail," meaning with absolute precision</note> in your mind everything that all antiquity has committed to writing about it. But so be it! For just as this type of coinage was nowhere more common, nor more in use for buying and selling, than in Athens: so too are the arts nowhere usually held in greater price and honor than in Athens—among those, of course, who love, cultivate, and admire them. I have therefore inscribed this first treatise to your name, both for these and other reasons. For just as soldiers once used to hang up their arms in the temple of Pallas <note>Athena, goddess of wisdom</note> when peace was established: so I hang it up in your <term>chemical laboratory</term> <note>original Greek: "χημιατρείω" (chemiatreiō); a word coined to describe a place where chemistry is applied to medicine</note>, and I do not doubt that you will grant it a place even in your Library <note>original: "Museo," referring to a place of study or a collection of knowledge</note>. Furthermore, both your kindness and your generosity invite me; those who have known you intimately praise the former, while the latter is known to all the learned from your writings, which were published for the common benefit with the most ready zeal. For the ancient Philosophers shrouded the **Love of Chemistry** <note>original: "Philochemiam"</note> in riddles and parables; even if their volumes are unfolded diligently and attentively, the reader will depart from their reading more uncertain than when he first approached it. Therefore, those who love chemistry owe you immortal thanks for that transparent clarity, which these*

# *TO THE GENTLE*
## *& fair reader.*

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial letter D featuring floral scrollwork and foliage.</image-desc>

Kind reader, when these two treatises—written on ancient parchments—came into my hands through the favor of friends, I judged them worthy to be published for the benefit of the public. This was done especially for the sake of those who love and practice the <term>chemical art</term> <note>In this period, "chemistry" (Chemia) referred to both what we now call chemistry and the esoteric pursuits of alchemy</note> (for we do not concern ourselves with the ignorant or those who despise the gifts of **GOD**). These works are not at odds with the doctrines of the ancients; however, they require a discerning reader, just as all the writings of the philosophers do. I did not wish, nor ought I, to change anything in them; they are presented exactly as they were written. You should value the matter itself rather than the mere words. 

No name was attached to the first treatise, though from certain clues I suspect it is the labor of a certain monk. The name of the author is prefixed to the second work; however, who that Paul was is not clear to me, nor could I learn it from those who shared the manuscript with me. Fair reader, take this in good part and favor our efforts. Soon, you may expect from me things of no small use to <term>pharmacists</term> <note>original: "Pharmacurgis"</note>, <term>surgeons</term> <note>original: "Cheirurgis"</note>, and <term>alchemists</term> <note>original: "Chrysurgis," literally "gold-workers," referring to those who seek the transmutation of metals</note>. -> # PHILOSOPHICAL TREATISE ON THE RED <-
-> ## AND the White by an Anonymous Author. <-

<image-desc>A decorative woodcut initial 'P' featuring a square frame filled with intricate foliate and scrollwork patterns.</image-desc>

First, you shall prepare for yourself for the following uses two waters: one for the <term>Red work</term> <note>original: "ad rubrum." The *Rubedo* (Redness) is the final stage of the alchemical Great Work, associated with the creation of the Philosopher's Stone and the transmutation of base metals into gold.</note>, and another for the <term>White work</term> <note>original: "ad album." The *Albedo* (Whiteness) is the stage preceding the red, associated with the creation of a "White Stone" that transmutes metals into silver.</note>, in this manner.

### *Water for Gold.*

Take four pounds each of <term>blue Hungarian vitriol</term> <note>Copper sulfate.</note>, well-dried, and <term>saltpeter</term> <note>Potassium nitrate.</note>; and one pound of <term>sal ammoniac</term> <note>Ammonium chloride.</note>. Let <term>aqua fortis</term> <note>Literally "strong water." Because this recipe includes sal ammoniac, it creates Aqua Regia, the only acid known to early chemists that could dissolve gold.</note> be made in an earthenware vessel with a glass <term>alembic</term> <note>The top part of a still, used for distilling liquids.</note> well-sealed with clay. First apply a slow fire, then a moderate one, and finally a stronger one. Once the distillation is complete, collect what is in the receiver and keep it in a glass vessel well-stopped. Let it be labeled: **Water for Gold**.

### *Water for Silver.*

Take equal parts of saltpeter, <term>burnt alum</term>, <term>salt of tartar</term> <note>Potassium carbonate.</note>, and <term>rock salt</term> <note>original: "salis gemmæ."</note>; and half a part of blue vitriol, well-dried. Let *aqua fortis* be made in the same manner as before. Let it be labeled: **Water for Silver**.

### *Preparation of the Sun for the Work.*

Take <term>Spanish Gold</term> <note>The "Sun" (*Sol*) is the traditional alchemical symbol and name for gold.</note> purified seven times, either through a "great cementation" or by <term>Antimony</term> <note>Antimony was frequently used in the 16th and 17th centuries to purify gold by melting it with the metal, which would carry away impurities.</note>, as skilled goldsmiths know how to do. Let it be beaten into thin foils, like parchment. Cast it into double its own weight of "parting water" <note>original: "aquæ separationis." An acid used to separate gold from silver.</note> so that it is dissolved and remains at the bottom of the water like red sand. Evaporate the aforementioned water through distillation until only the gold remains at the bottom. Afterward, wash it with common, clear water until you perceive no taste of the sharpness of the *aqua fortis*. If it is not <term>impalpable</term> <note>A powder so fine it cannot be felt as individual grains between the fingers.</note>, dissolve it again in the aforementioned water, wash, and dry it as you did before, until you have rendered it impalpable.

### *How the Sun is calcined.*

Take your gold thus prepared to be impalpable, as described above, and grind it with double its weight of well-prepared common salt. Place it upon a true marble slab or (what is better) a glass plate, and let them be ground together until all the gold is well mixed with the salt. Then place it in a crucible in a strong fire and let it be <term>calcined</term> <note>The process of heating a substance to high temperatures in the presence of air to change its physical or chemical state, often reducing it to a fine powder.</note> thoroughly. Afterward, allow it to <insert>cool</insert>

### *Preparation of Silver.*

Let it be purified optimally through a <term>bath of Saturn</term> <note>original: "balneum Saturni." A process of refining silver by melting it with lead (the metal associated with the planet Saturn), known as cupellation.</note>, as is the custom; afterward let it be beaten into thin plates, as was said regarding gold, and placed in double its own weight of the aforementioned separating water. When you see that it is all consumed by the said water, evaporate the water by a <term>Bain-Marie</term> <note>original: "Balneum Mariæ." A water bath used for gentle, indirect heating.</note>. Then, use a stronger heat until only the silver remains at the bottom. Afterward, wash it with common water, and it will be sufficiently prepared and fine for calcining.

### *Calcination of Silver.*

Take your silver, now reduced to an impalpable powder, and grind it with common salt, just as you did in calcining your <term>Sun</term> <note>original: "sole." In alchemy, the Sun (Sol) represents Gold, while the Moon (Luna) represents Silver.</note> in every way, and you will have it properly calcined for the work.

### *How common Mercury is prepared, so that it becomes Mercury fit for this work.*

Take half a pound of common mercury and pass it twice or thrice through leather. Then take two ounces of pulverized sea salt and place it with your mercury in a wooden mortar, or a sufficiently large wooden bowl, and let them be rubbed together with a little of the sharpest vinegar using a wooden pestle, until your mercury has been <term>mortified</term> <note>original: "mortificatus." To "mortify" or "kill" mercury meant to break the liquid metal down into tiny, dull globules or a powder so that its metallic luster and fluidity disappeared.</note>. Afterward, take half a pound of <term>Hungarian vitriol</term> <note>Copper sulfate.</note> and two ounces of common salt; mix them together with your mercury and place them in a glass distilling vessel with its <term>alembic</term> <note>The upper part or "head" of a still.</note> well-sealed with clay. Distill off all excess moisture with a slow fire, and collect the water that comes out; for it will serve you in place of sharp vinegar to "fix" the mercury. Afterward, when your material is properly deprived of all moisture, place it in a <term>sublimatory</term> <note>A vessel used for sublimation, the process where a solid is heated into a vapor and then collected as a purified solid on a cooler surface.</note> well-sealed with clay, which ought to be two small fingers higher than your material. When it begins to sublimate, stop up the neck of the sublimatory simply with paper or with a small linen cloth filled with cotton. Once this is done, place your sublimatory upon the furnace, upon which has been placed another vessel full of ashes. Position your sublimatory upon the furnace in the said ashes so that they exceed your material by two fingers. Then make a small fire for six hours. Afterward, strengthen the fire gradually (little by little), and at first, you will see your mercury sublimate like a very white dew, and by the force of the fire, it will finally be...

->*Repetition of the sublimation.*<-

Take your sublimate and again add to it a little less <term>vitriol</term> <note>original: "vitrioli." In this work, it is necessary to have some material from which the vessels can be <term>luted</term> <note>original: "lutari." From the Latin "lutum" (mud/clay); the practice of sealing joints or coating glass vessels with a paste to protect them from breaking in high heat and to prevent "spirits" (vapors) from escaping.</note>, both so they can resist the violence of the fire and so that the spirits are retained, lest they evaporate.

->*The first, best lute, which the Philosophers call,*<-
->*the lute of wisdom.*<-

Take four parts of the best potter's earth that can endure fire, one part each of linen scrapings <note>Shredded linen served as a binding fiber, similar to modern fiberglass, to prevent the clay from cracking.</note> and common salt, and two parts of <term>Armenian bole</term> <note>original: "Boli armeni." ->*Another lute, with which the joints of the vessels are sealed.*<-

Take very finely sifted wheat flour, knead it with egg white and common salt, and you will have an excellent lute, with which you can smear a linen cloth to be placed on the joints of the vessels. You can remove this lute if you thoroughly soak the said linen cloths with warm common water.

->*The work for the Sun follows.*<-

Take one ounce of your <term>Sun</term> <note>original: "sole." The alchemical name for Gold.</note>, properly refined and calcined, and divide it into eight equal parts. Afterward, take three ounces of your <term>strong water</term> <note>original: "aquæ fortis." Usually nitric acid, used to dissolve metals.</note> prepared for the Sun, and place it in a glass flask; afterward, throw into it the eighth part of your Sun, and let it stand in a place as warm as smoke <note>Likely referring to a gentle heat, such as the upper part of a furnace or a vapor bath.</note>, until your Sun has been perfectly dissolved; once this is done, throw in another eighth part of your reserved Sun, and let it be dissolved in the aforementioned manner, and so with the other parts. Take care, however, that no part of your Sun is thrown into the aforementioned water before that which you previously placed there has been properly dissolved; and if perhaps you see your water is no longer able to dissolve [anything], pour it out by tilting into another vessel, so that your undissolved Sun remains at the bottom

In alchemy, the sun is the symbol for gold.</note> well and properly dissolved, and turned into water; which water you must carefully keep aside.

### *The Inspiration of Mercury.*

Afterward, take one pound of your water and four ounces of your <term>sublimated Mercury</term> <note>Mercury that has been heated into vapor and solidified again to purify it.</note>, well-pulverized; make from this also eight equal parts, just as you did with your gold, and maintain the same process as you did with your gold. When all the mercury has been dissolved, reserve it also separately.

### *Note.*

If the <term>calcined</term> <note>Metals reduced to a powder through heat.</note> metals cannot be dissolved by your waters, add as much <term>sal ammoniac</term> <note>original: "salis armoniaci"; ammonium chloride, used to increase the potency of solvents.</note> to your water (little by little) as necessity seems to demand, so that they may work.

### *The Waxing and Animation of Mercury.*

Take your mercurial waters and place them in an <term>alembic</term> <note>original: "alembico"; a classic distillation apparatus.</note> very well luted, with its receiver, and place it in a <term>Bain-Marie</term> <note>original: "Balneum Mariæ"; a water bath used for gentle, steady heating.</note>. With a slow fire, allow it to distill for as long as it takes for all the watery humidity to drip out, which you should keep separately. Then increase the fire, and the spirit of Mercury, or its <term>quintessence</term> <note>original: "quinta essentia"; the purest, most concentrated essence of a substance.</note>, will emerge. Toward the end, increase the fire further so that the entire essence is sublimated. However, take care that you are not harmed by the vaporous and poisonous exhalations. When everything has been sublimated, allow the sublimatory vessel to cool. Afterward, open your glass and collect all the sublimated mercurial essence; weigh it, and you will find it diminished by half an ounce or more.

Note that the dregs <note>original: "feces." The solid residue left over after distillation or sublimation.</note> must be saved, both from this action and from the others following.

### *The Second Operation.*

Dissolve it again in <term>aqua fortis</term> <note>original: "aqua forti"; literally "strong water," typically nitric acid used to dissolve metals.</note>, and once dissolved, distill the water and sublimate it by the same aforementioned process.

### *The Third Operation.*

Repeat a third time in the same manner, always reserving the dregs. Observe that while your Mercury is thus brought to an most excellent degree, it is nevertheless not yet entirely <term>fixed</term> <note>A "fixed" substance is one that has been made stable and will no longer evaporate or change when exposed to fire.</note>.

### *The Final Sublimation, which is the Beginning of Fixation.*

Dry the aforementioned spirit of our Mercury with a slow fire, or in a moderately warm oven, for two or three natural days. Afterward, let it be placed in a glass vessel having a long neck, properly stopped up with its alembic, and apply a slow fire like a Bain-Marie (little by little) until you see it ascend; then gradually—

<header>CONCERNING THE STONE</header>
<meta>catchword: fui pon-</meta>

Strengthen the fire until everything that is possible has ascended. However, take care that the work is not destroyed by too much fire. If any <term>dregs</term> <note>original: "feces"; the solid residue or sediment remaining after distillation or filtration.</note> remain, save them separately, just as was said before.

### *The second operation of the dregs.*

Take all those reserved dregs and add a triple amount of <term>strong water</term> <note>original: "aqua forti"; typically nitric acid, used by alchemists as a powerful solvent.</note>; let them digest in a glass vessel, very well sealed, in moderate heat, for as long as it takes for all the dregs to be dissolved. Then, by <term>decanting</term> <note>original: "per inclinationem"; carefully pouring off the liquid to leave the sediment behind.</note>, cautiously distill what you see to be clear and pure away from the impure. Afterward, if you see that they are not yet entirely dissolved, pour over them again as much of your strong water as you see necessary for dissolving, and you may repeat this three times until all that matter has been dissolved. After the third dissolution and the separation of said substance has been performed, if any dregs still remain, you should discard them without concern as useless matter. However, reserve those solutions which you separated by decanting for the following work, because it is a part of our <term>Mercury</term> which is now semi-fixed.

### *The third fixation.*

Take that water which you separated by decanting and distill it as many times as necessary until it is consumed, though its dregs remain. However, there must be such an interval between all the distillations until the matter has been dissolved into its own water. If the water becomes too weak to dissolve, you shall take new water so that the matter may be better dissolved. In the end, you will see it become white like ashes. Afterward, when the matter has been properly dried, then in the furnace—first with a moderate fire, then a strong one, and finally a stronger one—it is not only dried, but becomes more and more white and fixed. Save it in a clean place, well-sealed.

### *The moistening of the aforesaid Mercury.*

Take your aforesaid "inspired" Mercury and place it in a glass vessel, well-sealed, and bury it in <term>warm manure</term> <note>original: "fimo calido"; decomposing horse manure was used in alchemical laboratories as a source of gentle, consistent heat.</note> or in a damp place, so that it may moisten itself.

### *The waxing of the gold.*

Take your <term>gold</term> <note>original: "solem" (the sun). The sun is the traditional alchemical symbol for gold.</note> dissolved with strong water, as above, and evaporate all the water by means of a <term>Bain-Marie</term> <note>original: "balneum Mariæ"; a water bath used for gentle heating.</note>. Finally, your gold will remain at the bottom like melted wax. Pour over it other new water and evaporate it again, up to three times; and after the third extraction, you will have a very glowing <term>oil of gold</term> <note>original: "oleum solis"; a concentrated, liquid form of gold considered a high stage of refinement.</note>.

Take your aforesaid earth and weigh it, and for one part...

### *The final fixation follows.*

Afterward, take all of your very precious matter and place it in a glass <term>sublimatory vessel</term> <note>A vessel used for sublimation, the process where a solid turns into vapor and then solidifies again, often used to purify substances.</note>. Give it a slow fire at first, then a stronger one. If anything is <term>sublimated</term> <note>Refers to the material that rises and deposits at the top of the vessel.</note>, let it be cooled, and whatever was sublimated must be incorporated back with its "body" (the residue at the bottom). Sublimate it again until nothing more rises, even if you treat it with a very strong fire. However, do not remove your matter from the fire until you see it is thoroughly "cooked," possessing a purple color and being well <term>fixed</term> <note>original: "fixam"; a "fixed" substance is one that is stable under heat and will not evaporate or change further.</note>.

### *Projection.*

Afterward, take one grain of this substance and project it upon a hundred grains of heated crude mercury. Then give it a moderate fire, and afterward a strong one for about four hours; it will turn into a true "sprout" of gold, though it will be brittle and easy to melt. From this, take one grain and project it upon another hundred grains of heated crude mercury, and it will become the most pure and <term>malleable</term> gold, capable of passing every test.

### *The lunar operation.*

As far as the <term>lunar operation</term> <note>The process for creating silver.</note> is concerned, the process is the same, except that in place of gold you must use <term>prepared silver</term> <note>original: "luna præparata"; alchemists used the name "Luna" (the Moon) for silver.</note> in your work. You should work only with your aforementioned water and your <term>whitened mercury</term> <note>original: "Mercurio vivificato ad album"; mercury that has been processed until it reaches a white stage, suitable for silver-making.</note> until you have reached the true fixation and the whitest color.

It is necessary in all these works to be prudent, diligent, and patient, and to wait for the true fixations and colorings, which will infallibly follow in the course of time. Also, be cautious in your projections, and you will have an immense treasure in your hands. Use it to the praise of Almighty God and for the comfort of the
->poor, Amen.<-

# TO THE MOST EXCELLENT MAN IN NOBILITY
# and learned doctrine, MASTER NICHOLAS BERN-
# ARD of Crest-Arnaud, a Frenchman from Dauphiné,
# a most outstanding Physician
# and Chemist.

*What the reasoning for my plan was, most learned and dis-*
*tinguished man, so that I might send forth into public the*
*previous treatise on the Physician’s Stone* <note>original: "de lap. de Physico." In this context, "Physico" refers to the natural philosopher or physician's approach to the Philosopher's Stone.</note> *in the name of*

*the patronage of your name. For I have understood from*

*brought so much light and growth to the Love of Chemistry*
<note>original: "Philochemiæ." A term used by alchemists to describe their devotion to the "divine" art of chemistry.</note> *that those things which were previously more intricate and*
*obscure than the oracles of Apollo* <note>Reference to the Delphic oracles of the Greek god Apollo, which were famously difficult to interpret.</note> *have now become most*
*clear through your studies and explanations. Indeed, I do not*
*deny—rather, I gladly confess—that my mind has been freed*
*from many tangled labyrinths by the constant reading of your*
*writings; and those difficulties* <note>original: "scrupulos." Literally "small sharp stones," used here to mean doubts or intellectual obstacles.</note> *which other Philosophers*
*were unable to remove have been taken away and utterly*
*cleared by your help. To whom, therefore, ought I or could*
*I dedicate these treatises more than to the craftsmen*
<note>original: "artificibus." In alchemy, the "artifex" is the practitioner who works the materials.</note> *themselves? For since no one can judge the arts better*
*than the craftsmen, I wished to subject them to your refined*
*judgment. If you grant these a certain place in your Library*
*and number me among your friends, I have already attained,*
*according to my wish and my heart's desire, that which I have*
*most greatly hoped for. Leipzig, on the Kalends of April*
<note>The first day of the month.</note> *in the Year 1603.*

->Your Excellence’s<-
->Devoted Student,<-

Dissolve one *loth* <term>a historical Germanic unit of weight, roughly 15 grams or half an ounce</term> of silver <note>original: "lunæ," literally 'of the moon,' the standard alchemical symbol for silver</note> in two *loths* of aqua fortis <term>literally "strong water," referring to nitric acid</term>: Then take eight *loths* of living Mercury <note>original: "Mercurii vivi," meaning quicksilver or liquid elemental mercury</note>, and four or six *loths* of aqua fortis, pour them together into the dissolved silver, place in slow ashes <note>original: "cineres lentos," referring to a gentle heat provided by an ash-bath</note>, or entirely cold ones: In the beginning you will see wonders: which is the beginning of fixing or precipitating Mercury. Geber <note>An influential 8th-century Arabic alchemist (Jabir ibn Hayyan) whose Latinized works were foundational to European alchemy</term> says, fix one part, save one part for waxing <note>original: "incerandum," the process of softening a substance to a wax-like consistency, usually to prepare it for fusion</note>.

->*The properties of this operation.*<-

In the joining of the waters, the waters are at first somewhat disturbed: but afterwards, being well united, they become clear. Second, in cold sand the matter is raised into most delightful growths, little mounds and shrubs <note>This describes a "chemical garden," likely the formation of silver crystals known as "Diana’s Tree"</note>, and it suddenly moves and lives, and remains in the color of the metal, especially when you pour off the waters and pour simple water over it, after the shrubs have grown. Third, this matter is greatly hardened in three days and with slow heat. Fourth, the spirits are not separated nor do they ascend, because the water prevents the ascent. If indeed anything ascends, it is coagulated at the surface of the water, and descends again in the form of a thin plate. Fifth, the ferment is joined to the spirit through the medicine: the body is reduced into its first matter, that is into the nearby water, which is the beginning of the fixation of Mercury and the precipitation of Mercury. Therefore, let the water be poured off from the little mounds and let them be dried slowly, and ground and placed in a Wallenburg vessel <note>A specific type of alchemical flask used for distillation or sublimation</note> under the spout <note>original: "ducillo," a small pipe or vent</note> and throne <note>original: "throno," referring to the upper part or "head" of the vessel</note>, and first the superfluous common water will ascend. I opened it and wished to lead back the sublimated materials over the foundations: but I saw that it smoked upwards impetuously in the vessel together with the spirits of the aqua fortis: Soon I covered it again with the spout and throne and let it stand thus through the night, so that the sublimated materials might be fixed above by their own fire: And this was done on the following day. ### *On the total fixation of precipitated Mercury.*

Then the quicksilver is overcome by the upper substances and should not be put back in; continue this way until the ashes are dried in their entirety and fixed. From these, starting from seven loths of **silver** <note>original: "luna," literally 'the moon'</note> as mentioned above, I obtained seven pounds, as was said.

A great secret: when the materials are no longer increasing in volume, or you have increased and fixed them as much as you like, then save four pounds to use as **ferment** <note>In alchemy, a "ferment" is a small amount of a perfected substance used to transform a larger mass</note>, and revivify the rest again: afterward, <insert><note>The manuscript contains a manicule (pointing hand) here</note> fix</insert> it again. By iterating this way, set it separately for a "great sublimation" without any volatile matter, and **reverberate** <note>to heat intensely in a furnace where the flames are "reflected" back onto the material</note> the matter at the bottom; dissolve and coagulate and repeat, and save the ferment in which you fix the volatile parts, and they will be white. And when it then ought to become volatile, it does not ascend but flows at the bottom. 

Note: when you soak the ashes well in a proportionate fire with **strong waters** <term>acids, usually nitric acid, used to dissolve metals</term>, you can first dissolve clean mercury, **gold** <note>original: "solem," the sun</note>, and **silver** <note>original: "lunam," the moon</note> in them; or take strong water in which silver has already been dissolved. Behold, continue the fermentation and afterward these same perfected bodies in a "great sublimation" continuously become volatile, as described above, and you complete the work in three days. The great sublimation makes the fixed become volatile: In this process, three parts of the volatile are coupled with one part of the fixed, or more, depending on the nature of the ashes to be raised. What remains in the bottom and is not raised, you shall raise again with an equal part. And that which cannot be raised at all shall be saved as our "raw and dead earth." For the body is not sublimated without the spirit, nor is the spirit fixed without the body.

I took eight loths of the most highly fixed ashes—stable against any fire—and one pound of well-animated mercury, and I sublimated the whole amount except for two drachms; **Praise be to God.** For the "great" or "greatest" work, let one **mark** <term>a unit of weight, usually 8 ounces</term> of the fixed and two pounds of the volatile be taken for one container. The **Ferrarese** <note>original: "Ferrarieñsis." This likely refers to an alchemical method or substance associated with the 13th-century chemist Guido of Ferrara</note> flies with the flying, and rests with the resting.

# PHILOSOPHICAL.

<margin>Geee 4</margin>
<meta>catchword: Increase is better</meta>

### *The Revivification of Fixed Ashes.*

Finally, when you have as much **Water** as is required: Then take one **mark** <term>a unit of weight, usually about 8 ounces</term> of fixed ashes and two pounds of raw **Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurii crudi"</note> or well-animated Mercury, which is better, [placed] at the bottom then: Let one mark of fixed ashes be taken again and **sublimated** <term>the process of heating a substance until it vaporizes and then solidifies again</term> with two pounds of animated Mercury, as described above. By repeating this four times, two pounds of fixed ashes will be included in two pounds of mercury, totaling about four pounds. Sublimate these four pounds once more by themselves, and the Mercury will be well cleansed and animated. Place this Mercury over the fire of **decoction** <term>slow, steady heating to extract or concentrate substances</term> for one to three days, and new ashes will be generated—greyish-blue <note>original: "glauci"</note> and very open: **Fix** <term>to make a volatile substance stable so it no longer evaporates when heated</term> these in their proper time and fire, which you shall increase afterward in the [same] manner as above, forever.

### *Concerning the Animated Water.*

This is drawn out from the fixed ashes through a great sublimation, and it is necessary to have a large amount so that at last the undigested material is not added to the digested: But a great amount cannot be obtained without the **augmentation** <note>increasing the quantity or potency</note> of the ashes. Let the **animated water** <note>mercury that has been chemically "quickened" or prepared for alchemical work</note> be kept in Wallenburg jars <note>original: "pixidibus wallenburgensibus"; likely ceramic or glass vessels from the Wallenburg region</note> and note on every label how many times it has been animated: for the more it is dissolved and coagulated, the better and more animated it becomes. Let it therefore be animated at least four times. The best proof of a sufficient preparation of the water is when, in the great sublimation, no more [substance] proceeds; the water is best when, before the great sublimation, the mercury has been **fermented** with the ashes under a tube <note>original: "sub canna"; likely referring to a delivery pipe in a distillation apparatus</note> for 24 hours; then the spirit is first united to the body. Let the mercury be put in first, then the ashes; let the mercury first be incorporated with them, and afterward it is raised up.

### *The Augmentation of the Ashes.*

Take the ashes and add double or triple the amount of Mercury and place them under the **spigot and throne** <term>original: "ducillo & throno"; technical terms for specific parts of an alchemical furnace or ventilation setup</term> over a strong fire for a day and a night; then they will receive the mercury into themselves. Then, with a slow fire, pour off the remaining mercury and set it back to dry in its own fire—namely, so that it does not ascend <note>evaporate</note>, or only a little—until it is incinerated together; and let this be done for eight or fourteen days or thereabouts. Then let it be exposed until it is dried at the **fourth degree of fire** <note>the highest level of heat in traditional alchemy, often compared to a blast furnace</note>. Note that when the ashes are to be augmented with Mercury, they should first be well dried. Thus, they are its **ferment** <note>a starter material that triggers a transformation in a larger mass</note> forever.

**Sulfur** is contained by sulfurs; every dry thing naturally desires its own moisture: Let a fire of its own tolerance be given in the drying out of the Mercury: it is not separated from the ashes except for a little bit: because if it were separated, it would not be **fixed** <note>made stable against heat</note> with the ashes.

# ON THE STONE

It is made from animated Mercury collected from a great sublimation. Note: When the ashes no longer wish to take in the Mercury, let it be soaked once with **aqua fortis** <term>literally "strong water," the historical name for nitric acid</term>. Note: Under a high tube <note>original: "canna alta," likely referring to a chimney or a long glass neck</note>, Mercury animated two or three times is reduced back into ashes. Note: I increased eight **lotones** <term>a German unit of weight, usually about half an ounce</term> of ashes in eight days to fifty **lotones**, always in a great fire; this was done in November, in the year 1489.

Note well here, in the **inceration** <term>the process of softening a substance to a wax-like consistency</term>, it is necessary always to make a hole through the ashes with a wooden stick; otherwise, the whole thing is destroyed. In this way, the Mercury in the **decoction** <term>slow, steady heating</term> freely ascends and descends through that same hole and causes no violence, but instead infuses itself well into the ashes. Test with a marked rod whether the ashes are raised or not. It is good to apply a strong fire during the day and a weaker one at night, so that those things fixed in the "earth" <note>the solid matter at the bottom of the vessel</note> do not escape violently. Behold, it is good to begin the process of infusion toward nightfall, so that during the day he can have a strong fire for four hours for the infusion, and a weaker one through the night, so that it can be **fixed** <term>made stable so it no longer evaporates</term> proportionally by the fire. Note: I placed sixteen *lotones* of well-fixed ashes of Mercury and double that of animated Mercury—specifically thirty-two—to the fire of decoction for two days, and the whole was fixed except for six *lotones*; and if it had stood longer, the whole would have been fixed. It follows, therefore, that animated mercury thus placed in the fire of decoction is entirely fixed and turned to ash in three days. For since I increased it with much Mercury and with a small part—namely, half—it is not surprising enough, and this is true of that which is entirely fixed. Note: I placed one pound of fixed ashes with three pounds of raw Mercury, and on the third day we found a thick **amalgam** <term>a mixture of mercury with another metal</term> which no longer bubbled. This we placed back in alone and it was well fixed in three days afterward with a strong fire. Behold, in six days Mercury is fixed in such a manner with ashes, even when raw.

### *Extraction of the Amalgam.*

The **amalgam** is extracted from the fermented, well-fixed ashes with two and a half *lotones* of clean Mercury under a long tube with the fire of decoction for a day and a night. Once fermented, squeeze out the superfluous Mercury and wash it well with hot water after grinding, and **digest** <term>heat gently for a long period to mature the substance</term> it into **silver** <note>original: "lunam," literally "the moon," the alchemical name for silver</note>.

### *Conclusion for the increase of the ashes.*

Take one pound of ashes and three pounds of animated Mercury; let it be placed under a high vent <note>original: "ducillo"</note> in a furnace having six holes above <insert><image-desc>A small rectangular diagram containing six circles arranged in two vertical columns of three, representing holes (foramina) in a furnace.</image-desc></insert>. Let the holes be open, so that the coals may be frequently pushed down with a rod under the **capella** <term>a muffle or small vaulted chamber in the furnace</term> for four hours.

It outlines specific techniques for "fixing" mercury—transforming it from a liquid/volatile state into a stable solid—and concludes with a method for extracting a silver-like amalgam.</summary>

->**PHILOSOPHICO.**<-
Cccc 5

...small vessel <note>original: "capella," usually referring to a small vaulted furnace or a cupel</note>: in this way the whole may revive, which you will feel with the rod; then the coagulated substance will rise to the plug <term>original: "ducillum," a stopper or vent-plug in the apparatus</term>, which must be pushed down with the rod through the hole as much as possible, once every two hours. Then the Mercury descends again to the bottom and boils, just as it did at the beginning. On the second day, all four vessels that had been set out ceased to boil, and the matter began to **coagulate** <term>thicken from a liquid to a solid</term> and turn red, which I was able to see on the inserted rod. Thus, first the ashes are **amalgamated** <term>blended into a soft alloy</term> with the Mercury, then they coagulate and grow red; let them remain standing until they are completely **fixed** <term>made resistant to evaporation by heat</term> by such a great fire, and a small amount of Mercury will rise to the "throne" <note>original: "thronum," referring to the highest part or the head of the alchemical vessel</note>, which may be left there or put back in. Thus I let it stand for four days, and I found each part well executed; at the top, the matter stood hard and shattered under the plug, so that it could hardly be pushed down, and at the bottom, I replaced what was like an amalgam until it was sufficiently fixed. It seems better, as noted above, for it to be fixed entirely in three days with double the Mercury: where it is said, I put in 16 **lotones** <term>a German weight of about half an ounce</term> of well-fixed Mercury. 

Note: when the ashes are completely fixed in a great fire, they can no longer be "increased" (as mentioned above), but the method then requires that one part of these be **sublimated** <term>heated until it turns to vapor and collects again as a solid</term> with six parts of Mercury; and if anything remains, let it be sublimated again as above with its own Mercury. Then let only the sublimate be placed in a stronger fire under the tube <note>original: "canna," likely a long-necked glass vessel or chimney</note>, and let it be cooked again into ashes. Those can then be increased as before, and even more strongly; however, in white and grey-blue <note>original: "glaucis"</note> ashes, this hardness does not occur. 

I put in one pound of mercury that had been frequently **animated** <term>chemically "quickened" or purified through repeated processing</term>, specifically through three sublimations under the plug at a strong fire, and in one night it was entirely fixed and turned to ash. O, how much hope there is in the repetition of the works! For every repetition makes the operation more sublime. O, what glory there is in the Great Sublimation! 

Note: when the ashes are fixed under the plug at a strong or moderate fire, it is necessary that they have with them separate **living Mercury** <term>quicksilver in its fluid, metallic state</term>; otherwise, they will all become volatile <note>likely to evaporate or vanish into smoke</note> again. And it is quite a wonder to see it coagulate in its own "water," just as butter forms in milk, and yet the water retains the water. 

Note: in the fixation and augmentation of the ashes, the Mercury is put in first and the ashes afterward; however, in the Great Sublimation, it is the opposite. The drier the ashes, the more Mercury they incorporate into themselves in a great fire. And thus, in the cover of each vessel, a hole is opened, along with a hole in the upper door and similarly the large lower door, and that Mercury thus incorporated into the ashes is fixed. With those same ashes, it must not be continually ground or separated, as above...

# CONCERNING THE PHILOSOPHERS' STONE.

...as Morienus <note>original: "nus," likely referring to Morienus Romanus, a legendary figure in alchemical lore</note> did: the more Mercury is **animated** <term>given chemical "life" or reactivity through purification</term>, the more it is incinerated even by itself alone, as I have learned by experience.

### *Concerning the preparation of the earth.*

Collect all the "dead earths" <term>the solid residue remaining at the bottom of a flask</term> during **sublimation** <term>the process of heating a substance until it turns to vapor and then solidifies again, leaving impurities behind</term> which were in no way able to be raised, until you have one mark or a pound. **Reverberate** <term>heat in a furnace where the flames are reflected down onto the material</term> this to the highest whiteness for three days; then, in distilled vinegar, dissolve and **coagulate** <term>thicken or solidify</term> it four times; then you will have prepared it well according to Geber <note>Geber is the Latinized name of Jabir ibn Hayyan, the most famous of the early chemists</note>. Geber says: After a fourfold solution and coagulation, it is converted into the nature of salts; it melts without turning into glass and is cleansed from the "earth of the common people" <note>original: "terra vulgi," meaning crude, unpurified matter</note> and from superfluities. It becomes white, crystalline, fusible, and well-prepared. Morienus says: "Kill the earth, and it shall be turned into **calx** <term>a fine powder produced by heating a metal or mineral</term>; then revive that which has been deprived of all moisture by restoring its **Auxilem** <note>a corruption of an Arabic alchemical term, likely referring to the "moist" or "soul" component</note> and its humidity." Therefore, return its own water to the earth until it is **fixed** <term>made resistant to heat so it no longer evaporates</term> and mixed with it. When you have whitened that earth by fire alone, you have directed it sufficiently.

### *Concerning fermentation and projection.*

Take two marks of pure gold and melt them in a crucible; then cast in one **ferto** <note>original: "fertonem," a unit of weight; the text defines it here as a fourth part of a pound</note> of the said medicine, well-ground. It is immediately absorbed by the gold and becomes one with it. Then cast in another ferto of the medicine, so that the two marks of gold are consumed; then grind it and **digest** <term>heat gently over a long period</term> it with a stronger fire into a very red powder, in the manner of **minium** <term>red lead, used here to describe the specific vibrant red color</term>. Let one part of this be cast upon a hundred parts of pure **Luna** <term>the alchemical name for Silver</term>, and it will become the best gold.

If, however, the solution and coagulation are repeated through great sublimation, its power to **tinge** <term>to transform or dye the internal nature of a metal</term> increases unto infinity. For the "white work" <note>the process of making silver</note>, it does not require **fermentation** <term>the process of adding a "seed" of precious metal to the medicine</term>, and one part tinges 160 parts of purified **Venus** <term>the alchemical name for Copper</term> into the most perfect Silver.

The increase of the medicine's power through great sublimation is possible for as long as you wish—specifically, when it can no longer be sublimated, let it be increased with distilled Mercury every fifteen days, with one **loto** <note>a "Loth," a German weight approximately equal to half an ounce</note>, using a slow fire, just as in the "restoration of the soul"; thus it continues unto infinity. Believe that for each turn you can add more to the increase, provided that the **fixed** <term>the solid, stable part</term> exceeds the **volatile** <term>the part that easily evaporates</term> in both quantity and power. May praise be to ALMIGHTY GOD forever and ever,

->A M E N.<-
